requests.specific_A: Considering only customers who have placed at least one order, count each customer's orders, keeping their `gender`. Work out what share each customer has of all orders placed by customers of the same gender; customers with no gender recorded are left out. Which customers have a share above the average share across these customers? Show the customer id, gender, number of orders, share, and how far the share is above the average. Sort by that gap from largest to smallest, with missing values last, and keep the top 10. Don't round anything.
requests.specific_B: Considering all customers, including those who have never placed an order (counted as 0 orders), count each customer's orders, keeping their `gender`. Work out what share each customer has of all orders placed by customers of the same gender; customers with no gender recorded are left out. Which customers have a share above the average share across these customers? Show the customer id, gender, number of orders, share, and how far the share is above the average. Sort by that gap from largest to smallest, with missing values last, and keep the top 10. Don't round anything.
requests.open: Looking at customers' order counts, what share of all orders from customers of the same gender does each customer account for? Customers with no gender recorded are left out. Which customers have a share above the average share across customers? Show the customer id, gender, number of orders, share, and how far the share is above the average. Sort by that gap from largest to smallest, with missing values last, and show the top 10. Don't round anything.

readings.A: Only customers who placed at least one order are counted, both in the shares and in the average share.
readings.B: Every customer is counted. Customers with no orders have 0 orders and a share of 0, and they are included in the average share.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Orders"."customer_id" AS "e", "Customers"."gender" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "Orders" AS "Orders" INNER JOIN "Customers" AS "Customers" ON "Customers"."customer_id" = "Orders"."customer_id" GROUP BY "Orders"."customer_id", "Customers"."gender"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v" ORDER BY ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Customers"."customer_id" AS "e", "Customers"."gender" AS "g", COUNT("Orders"."order_id") AS "m1" FROM "Customers" AS "Customers" LEFT JOIN "Orders" AS "Orders" ON "Customers"."customer_id" = "Orders"."customer_id" GROUP BY "Customers"."customer_id", "Customers"."gender"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v" ORDER BY ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Customers and their orders. Each order is linked to its customer by `customer_id`, and orders are counted per customer id and `gender`.
Gender total: the sum of the per-customer order counts within each gender. Each customer is matched to their gender's total by exact text equality, so customers with no gender recorded drop out.
share = the customer's order count ÷ the total orders for their gender
Benchmark: the average share across all remaining customers, as one overall value.
Keep only customers whose share is strictly greater than the overall average share.
customer id
gender
number of orders
share minus the average share (not rounded)
Sort by output 5, descending, with missing values last.
Return the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: Include only customers with at least one order (Orders inner-joined to Customers).

B.requirement: Include every customer. A customer with no orders gets a count of 0 and a share of 0, which still counts toward the average share.

requests.specific_A: For each site code in `scanfeatures` (`zoneref`), total the artifact counts (`articount`) over its feature records, ignoring missing counts, so each site is one unit. Each unit's share is its count divided by the overall artifact total across all of `scanfeatures`; if the overall total is missing, return no rows. The average share is the mean of the units' shares (ignoring missing shares); if that average is missing, return no rows. For each unit show the site code, its artifact count, its share, and its share minus the average share. Sort by that difference from highest to lowest with missing values last, and keep the top 10.
requests.specific_B: Treat each individual record in `scanfeatures` as one unit, without combining records from the same site; its count is that record's artifact count (`articount`), and missing counts are ignored in totals and averages. Each unit's share is its count divided by the overall artifact total across all of `scanfeatures`; if the overall total is missing, return no rows. The average share is the mean of the units' shares (ignoring missing shares); if that average is missing, return no rows. For each unit show the site code, its artifact count, its share, and its share minus the average share. Sort by that difference from highest to lowest with missing values last, and keep the top 10.
requests.open: In the feature scan data, which 10 site artifact counts (`articount`, identified by site code `zoneref`) stand furthest above the average in their share of all artifacts? Each count's share is that count divided by the overall artifact total across all of `scanfeatures` (return nothing if the overall total is missing), and the average share is the mean of those shares (again return nothing if that average is missing). For each, give the site code, the artifact count, its share, and its share minus the average share. Ignore missing counts, and sort from the highest difference down with missing values last.

readings.A: Total the artifact counts per site, then compute and rank each site's share against the average site share.
readings.B: Treat each feature record separately, then compute and rank each record's share against the average record share.

requests.specific_A: Considering only constructors that have at least one constructor standings record, count each constructor's standings records. Compare each count with the average count over those constructors. Show the 10 constructors furthest above that average: the constructor id, its `nationality`, its record count, and the difference from the average (unrounded), largest difference first.
requests.specific_B: Considering every constructor, with a count of 0 for those that have no constructor standings records, count each constructor's standings records. Compare each count with the average count over all constructors. Show the 10 constructors furthest above that average: the constructor id, its `nationality`, its record count, and the difference from the average (unrounded), largest difference first.
requests.open: How many constructor standings records does each constructor have, and how does that compare with the average per constructor? Show the 10 constructors furthest above the average. Give the constructor id, its nationality, its number of standings records, and the difference from the average, largest first.

readings.A: Only constructors that appear in the standings are counted. The average count per constructor is computed over them.
readings.B: Every constructor is counted, and constructors with no standings records get a count of 0. The average count per constructor is computed over all constructors.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "constructorStandings"."constructorId" AS "e", "constructors"."nationality" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "constructorStandings" AS "constructorStandings" INNER JOIN "constructors" AS "constructors" ON "constructors"."constructorId" = "constructorStandings"."constructorId" GROUP BY "constructorStandings"."constructorId", "constructors"."nationality"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "constructors"."constructorId" AS "e", "constructors"."nationality" AS "g", COUNT("constructorStandings"."constructorStandingsId") AS "m1" FROM "constructors" AS "constructors" LEFT JOIN "constructorStandings" AS "constructorStandings" ON "constructors"."constructorId" = "constructorStandings"."constructorId" GROUP BY "constructors"."constructorId", "constructors"."nationality"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Use the constructor standings records (`constructorStandings`).
Link the records to `constructors` on constructor id. Group by constructor id and constructor nationality.
constructor id
constructor nationality (`constructors.nationality`)
the number of standings records for the constructor
that count minus the average count per constructor, with no rounding
Order by the difference, largest first.
Return the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: Inner join: include only constructors that have at least one standings record. The average is taken over those constructors only.

requests.specific_A: For each film rating, find the average film `length` (ignoring films with no length) and the per-day rental price, defined as the average over the rating's films of each film's `rental_rate` divided by its `rental_duration`. Then take the simple mean of those per-day prices across the ratings, with each rating counting once, and keep only the ratings whose per-day price is above that mean. For those ratings, give one row with the average of their average lengths, the average of their per-day prices, and the average amount by which their per-day price exceeds the cross-rating mean. Don't round anything.
requests.specific_B: For each film rating, find the average film `length` (ignoring films with no length) and the per-day rental price, defined as the rating's average `rental_rate` divided by its average `rental_duration`. Then take the simple mean of those per-day prices across the ratings, with each rating counting once, and keep only the ratings whose per-day price is above that mean. For those ratings, give one row with the average of their average lengths, the average of their per-day prices, and the average amount by which their per-day price exceeds the cross-rating mean. Don't round anything.
requests.open: For each film rating, look at its average film length (ignoring films with no length) and its rental rate per day of rental. Which ratings have a per-day rate above the simple mean of the ratings' per-day rates, with each rating counting once? For just those ratings, give one row with their average length, their average per-day rate, and the average amount by which they exceed that mean. Don't round anything.

readings.A: For each rating, work out each film's rental rate divided by its rental duration, then average those per-film values.
readings.B: For each rating, divide the average rental rate by the average rental duration.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "film"."rating" AS "g", AVG("film"."length") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("film"."rental_rate" AS REAL) / "film"."rental_duration")) AS "m2" FROM "film" AS "film" GROUP BY "film"."rating"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "film"."rating" AS "g", AVG("film"."length") AS "m1", (AVG(CAST("film"."rental_rate" AS REAL)) / AVG("film"."rental_duration")) AS "m2" FROM "film" AS "film" GROUP BY "film"."rating"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every film and group by `film.rating`, one row per rating. For each rating, compute the average `length` (ignoring missing values) and a per-day rental price.

Take the plain mean of the per-day prices across the ratings, with each rating counting once. Keep only the ratings whose per-day price is strictly greater than that mean. Collapse the kept ratings into one result row.
Return the average, over the kept ratings, of their average film length
Return the average, over the kept ratings, of their per-day rental price
Return the average, over the kept ratings, of how much each one's per-day price exceeds the cross-rating mean
Use exactly these three columns in this order, with no rounding

A.requirement: Per-day price of a rating = the average over its films of each film's `rental_rate` / `rental_duration`

B.requirement: Per-day price of a rating = the rating's average `rental_rate` divided by its average `rental_duration`

requests.specific_A: For each patient in `Laboratory` (grouped by `ID`), give the patient ID, their average GOT, their average RBC, and their average GOT minus the mean of all patients' average GOT values. That single overall figure is used for every patient, and if it is missing, return no rows. Ignore missing values in all averages. Show the 10 patients with the largest difference, highest first with missing differences last, unrounded.
requests.specific_B: For each patient in `Laboratory` (grouped by `ID`), give the patient ID, their average GOT, their average RBC, and their average GOT minus the average GOT across all laboratory records. That single overall figure is used for every patient, and if it is missing, return no rows. Ignore missing values in all averages. Show the 10 patients with the largest difference, highest first with missing differences last, unrounded.
requests.open: For each patient in `Laboratory`, show the patient ID, their average GOT, their average RBC, and their average GOT minus the overall average GOT. Use that one overall figure for every patient, and return nothing if it is missing. Ignore missing values. Sort by the difference, highest first with missing differences last, return the top 10, and don't round.

readings.A: Compare each patient's average GOT with the mean of the per-patient averages.
readings.B: Compare each patient's average GOT with the mean GOT taken over all lab records.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Laboratory"."ID" AS "e", AVG("Laboratory"."GOT") AS "m1", AVG("Laboratory"."RBC") AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" GROUP BY "Laboratory"."ID"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Laboratory"."ID" AS "e", AVG("Laboratory"."GOT") AS "m1", AVG("Laboratory"."RBC") AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" GROUP BY "Laboratory"."ID"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("Laboratory"."GOT") AS "v" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

requests.specific_A: For each region (`district`.`A3`): place every client in the district given by their own `client`.`district_id` and count clients per district, considering only districts with at least one client. Give the region, the average of those per-district client counts over the region's districts, and the average over the region's districts of each district's share of clients (its count divided by the total of the counts over all districts, as a fraction); no rounding.
requests.specific_B: For each region (`district`.`A3`): place every client in the branch district (`account`.`district_id`) of each account they own (disposition `type` = 'OWNER'), counting a client once per owned account, and count clients per district, considering only districts with at least one client. Give the region, the average of those per-district client counts over the region's districts, and the average over the region's districts of each district's share of clients (its count divided by the total of the counts over all districts, as a fraction); no rounding.
requests.open: Placing clients in districts by the location of their branch, and counting only districts that have clients: for each region, what is the average number of clients per district, and what is the average share of all clients that a district holds (as a fraction)? Don't round.

readings.A: A client belongs to the district in their own client record (`client.district_id`).
readings.B: A client belongs to the branch district of each account they own: join `disp` (OWNER) to `account` and use `account.district_id`, counting the client once per owned account.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "client"."district_id" AS "e", "district"."A3" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "client" AS "client" INNER JOIN "district" AS "district" ON "district"."district_id" = "client"."district_id" GROUP BY "client"."district_id", "district"."A3"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)) SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s3" AS "s3" GROUP BY "s3"."g"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "account"."district_id" AS "e", "district"."A3" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "client" AS "client" INNER JOIN "disp" AS "disp" ON "disp"."client_id" = "client"."client_id" AND "disp"."type" = 'OWNER' INNER JOIN "account" AS "account" ON "account"."account_id" = "disp"."account_id" INNER JOIN "district" AS "district" ON "district"."district_id" = "account"."district_id" GROUP BY "account"."district_id", "district"."A3"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)) SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s3" AS "s3" GROUP BY "s3"."g"

shared_requirements.requirement: Each client placement is matched (inner join) to the `district` row of the district it is placed in. Only districts with at least one placement exist.
Count placements per district (district id plus its region `A3`). Then group those district rows by region `A3`, giving one row per region.
Region (`district.A3`).
The average of the per-district client counts over the region's districts. No rounding.
The average over the region's districts of each district's share: its count divided by the total of the counts over all districts, as a fraction. No rounding.

A.requirement: Every `client` row is placed in its own `client.district_id`, once per client.

B.requirement: Every client is placed, through `disp` rows with `type` = 'OWNER', in the `account.district_id` of each account they own. A client counts once per owned account, and the shares use the total of these placements.

CREATE TABLE account
(
    account_id  INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    district_id INTEGER default 0 not null,
    frequency   TEXT   not null,
    date        DATE          not null,
    foreign key (district_id) references district (district_id)
);
CREATE TABLE card
(
    card_id INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    disp_id INTEGER           not null,
    type    TEXT    not null,
    issued  DATE          not null,
    foreign key (disp_id) references disp (disp_id)
);
CREATE TABLE client
(
    client_id   INTEGER        not null
        primary key,
    gender      TEXT not null,
    birth_date  DATE       not null,
    district_id INTEGER        not null,
    foreign key (district_id) references district (district_id)
);
CREATE TABLE disp
(
    disp_id    INTEGER        not null
        primary key,
    client_id  INTEGER        not null,
    account_id INTEGER        not null,
    type      TEXT not null,
    foreign key (account_id) references account (account_id),
    foreign key (client_id) references client (client_id)
);
CREATE TABLE district
(
    district_id INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    A2          TEXT   not null,
    A3          TEXT   not null,
    A4          TEXT       not null,
    A5          TEXT           not null,
    A6          TEXT           not null,
    A7          TEXT           not null,
    A8          INTEGER        not null,
    A9          INTEGER           not null,
    A10         REAL not null,
    A11         INTEGER           not null,
    A12         REAL null,
    A13         REAL not null,
    A14         INTEGER           not null,
    A15         INTEGER        null,
    A16         INTEGER          not null
);
CREATE TABLE loan
(
    loan_id    INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    account_id INTEGER           not null,
    date       DATE          not null,
    amount     INTEGER           not null,
    duration   INTEGER           not null,
    payments   REAL not null,
    status     TEXT    not null,
    foreign key (account_id) references account (account_id)
);
CREATE TABLE `order`
(
    order_id   INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    account_id INTEGER           not null,
    bank_to    TEXT    not null,
    account_to INTEGER           not null,
    amount     REAL not null,
    k_symbol   TEXT    not null,
    foreign key (account_id) references account (account_id)
);
CREATE TABLE trans
(
    trans_id   INTEGER default 0    not null
        primary key,
    account_id INTEGER default 0    not null,
    date       DATE             not null,
    type       TEXT       not null,
    operation  TEXT      null,
    amount     INTEGER              not null,
    balance    INTEGER             not null,
    k_symbol   TEXT      null,
    bank       TEXT       null,
    account    INTEGER          null,
    foreign key (account_id) references account (account_id)
);

requests.specific_A: Match manager awards to players on `player_id`, dropping unmatched awards, and group by the player's throwing hand (`throws`), with a missing value as its own group. In each group, count the award rows, so a manager who won three awards adds 3. Turn each count into a share of the total of the counts across all groups. Keep only the hands whose share is above the average share across hands. Return one row with the total of their counts, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that average share. No rounding.
requests.specific_B: Match manager awards to players on `player_id`, dropping unmatched awards, and group by the player's throwing hand (`throws`), with a missing value as its own group. In each group, count the distinct managers (`player_id`) who won awards, so a manager who won three awards adds 1. Turn each count into a share of the total of the counts across all groups. Keep only the hands whose share is above the average share across hands. Return one row with the total of their counts, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that average share. No rounding.
requests.open: Tally manager award winners by throwing hand (`throws`, with missing as its own group; awards matched to players on `player_id`, unmatched ones dropped) and work out each hand's share of the overall tally. For the hands whose share is above the average share, give one row with their combined tally, their average share, and how far above the average share they sit on average. Unrounded.

readings.A: Each throwing-hand group is counted by its manager_award rows.
readings.B: Each throwing-hand group is counted by its distinct managers who won awards.

choice_kind: aggregation level (average of ratios vs ratio of totals)

requests.specific_A: Join each scan to its site by site code, dropping scans that have no matching site, and group the scans by the site's risk evaluation status (`riskeval`), with scans whose site has no recorded risk evaluation status forming a group of their own. Work out each group's GB-per-minute rate as the average, over its scans, of file size (`gbsize`) divided by scan duration (`spanmin`), ignoring scans where that ratio is missing. Next, take the simple average of these group rates, with each group counting once, as a benchmark. Using only the groups whose rate is strictly above that benchmark (none if there is no benchmark), return one row with two values: the average of their rates, and the average amount by which their rates exceed the benchmark. Don't round anything.
requests.specific_B: Join each scan to its site by site code, dropping scans that have no matching site, and group the scans by the site's risk evaluation status (`riskeval`), with scans whose site has no recorded risk evaluation status forming a group of their own. Work out each group's GB-per-minute rate as the group's total file size (`gbsize`) divided by its total scan duration (`spanmin`). Next, take the simple average of these group rates, with each group counting once, as a benchmark. Using only the groups whose rate is strictly above that benchmark (none if there is no benchmark), return one row with two values: the average of their rates, and the average amount by which their rates exceed the benchmark. Don't round anything.
requests.open: Looking only at scans that match a site, what's the GB-per-minute rate of file size (`gbsize`) to scan duration (`spanmin`) for each site risk evaluation status (`riskeval`), treating scans at sites with no recorded status as a group of their own? Use the plain average of those group rates as a benchmark, with each group counting once. For the groups strictly above the benchmark (none if there's no benchmark), give me one row: their average rate and their average margin above the benchmark, unrounded.

readings.A: Each risk group's rate is the mean of the individual scans' size-to-duration ratios.
readings.B: Each risk group's rate is the group's total file size divided by its total scan duration.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "sites"."riskeval" AS "g", AVG((CAST("scans"."gbsize" AS REAL) / "scans"."spanmin")) AS "m1" FROM "scans" AS "scans" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scans"."zoneref" GROUP BY "sites"."riskeval"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "sites"."riskeval" AS "g", (CAST(SUM("scans"."gbsize") AS REAL) / SUM("scans"."spanmin")) AS "m1" FROM "scans" AS "scans" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scans"."zoneref" GROUP BY "sites"."riskeval"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s3" AS "s3"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from `scans` records and inner-join `sites` on `sites.zoneregistry` = `scans.zoneref`. Unmatched scans are dropped.
Group by `sites.riskeval`, giving one GB-per-minute rate (`gbsize` relative to `spanmin`) per status. Scans whose site has a missing `riskeval` form their own group.
The benchmark is the simple average of the group rates, with each group counting once. Keep the groups whose rate is strictly above the benchmark, and only if the benchmark exists.
All kept groups together give a single row.
The average of the kept groups' rates.
The average of (rate − benchmark) over the kept groups. No rounding.

A.requirement: A group's rate is the average of the per-scan values of `gbsize`/`spanmin`, ignoring missing ratios.

B.requirement: A group's rate is SUM(`gbsize`) / SUM(`spanmin`) over the group's scans.

requests.specific_A: For each branch district (`account.district_id`), count its accounts and work out its share of all accounts (its count divided by the total number of accounts). Show the district id, the account count, the share, and how far the share is above the average share across districts (share minus that average). Sort by that difference from highest to lowest and return exactly 10 rows, dropping any other districts tied with the 10th. Don't round anything.
requests.specific_B: For each branch district (`account.district_id`), count its accounts and work out its share of all accounts (its count divided by the total number of accounts). Show the district id, the account count, the share, and how far the share is above the average share across districts (share minus that average). Sort by that difference from highest to lowest and return the top 10, plus any other districts tied with the 10th. Don't round anything.
requests.open: For each branch district (`account.district_id`), count its accounts and work out its share of all accounts (its count divided by the total number of accounts). Show the district id, the account count, the share, and how far the share is above the average share across districts (share minus that average). Which are the top 10 districts by that difference, from highest to lowest? Don't round anything.

readings.A: Cut the sorted list at exactly 10 rows and drop rows tied with the 10th.
readings.B: Cut the sorted list at the 10th row's value and keep every row tied with it.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "account"."district_id" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "account" AS "account" GROUP BY "account"."district_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "account"."district_id" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "account" AS "account" GROUP BY "account"."district_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") >= (SELECT MIN("cut"."d") FROM (SELECT ("s3b"."m2" - "s4b"."v") AS "d" FROM "s3" AS "s3b" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4b" ON NOT ("s4b"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s3b"."m2" - "s4b"."v") DESC LIMIT 10) AS "cut") ORDER BY ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") DESC

shared_requirements.requirement: Use every `account` record, grouped by branch location (`account.district_id`). Each district's account count is the number of records in its group.
Compare each district's share with the single overall value: the total number of accounts (the sum of the district counts). Then compare each share with the average share across all districts.
District id (`account.district_id`).
Number of accounts in the district.
District share: its account count divided by the total number of accounts. Not rounded.
District share minus the average share across all districts. Not rounded.
Sort by output 4 from highest to lowest.
Return the top 10 by output 4.

A.requirement: Return exactly 10 rows. Drop any further districts tied with the 10th.

B.requirement: Keep every district whose output 4 equals the 10th row's value, even if that gives more than 10 rows.

context.schema:
CREATE TABLE account
(
    account_id  INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    district_id INTEGER default 0 not null,
    frequency   TEXT   not null,
    date        DATE          not null,
    foreign key (district_id) references district (district_id)
);
CREATE TABLE card
(
    card_id INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    disp_id INTEGER           not null,
    type    TEXT    not null,
    issued  DATE          not null,
    foreign key (disp_id) references disp (disp_id)
);
CREATE TABLE client
(
    client_id   INTEGER        not null
        primary key,
    gender      TEXT not null,
    birth_date  DATE       not null,
    district_id INTEGER        not null,
    foreign key (district_id) references district (district_id)
);
CREATE TABLE disp
(
    disp_id    INTEGER        not null
        primary key,
    client_id  INTEGER        not null,
    account_id INTEGER        not null,
    type      TEXT not null,
    foreign key (account_id) references account (account_id),
    foreign key (client_id) references client (client_id)
);
CREATE TABLE district
(
    district_id INTEGER default 0 not null

Then, for each event `status`, average those event-level figures. Ignore missing values in every average, and don't round anything.

Then, for each event `status`, average those event-level figures. Return the status, its average remaining, its average overspend rate, and its average remaining divided by the mean of the event-level average remaining values across all events regardless of status, with each event weighted equally. shared_requirements.requirement: Start from budget lines (`budget` records)
Match each budget line to its event on `budget.link_to_event` = `event.event_id`; drop budget lines that have no matching event

Work in two stages: first group by event (`link_to_event`) with its `event.status`, then group those event-level figures by `event.status`; return one row per status with the status as the first column
Average remaining: for each event, the average of `budget.remaining` over its lines; then, for each status, the average of those event averages. Missing values are ignored.

Average overspend rate: for each event, the average over its lines of (`spent` − `amount`) ÷ `amount`; then, for each status, the average of those event averages. Missing values are ignored, and a line with a zero amount gives a missing value.

Fourth column: the status's average remaining (output 2) divided by an overall baseline average remaining. The baseline is computed once and ignores missing values. If the baseline is missing, no rows are returned.
No rounding, no ordering, no limit

A.requirement: Baseline = the simple mean of the per-status average remaining values (output 2), so each status counts equally

B.requirement: Baseline = the mean of the event-level average remaining values across all events of any status, so each event counts equally

requests.specific_A: Using budget lines matched to their event (drop lines with no matching event), work out for each event its average spending rate, `spent` ÷ `amount`, across its lines, counting lines where `spent` is 0 as a rate of 0. Then, for each event `type`, average those event-level rates. Return the type, its average spending rate, and that rate divided by the simple mean of the per-type average rates. Ignore missing values in the averages, and don't round.
requests.specific_B: Using budget lines matched to their event (drop lines with no matching event), work out for each event its average spending rate, `spent` ÷ `amount`, across its lines, leaving out lines where `spent` is 0. Then, for each event `type`, average those event-level rates. Return the type, its average spending rate, and that rate divided by the simple mean of the per-type average rates. Ignore missing values in the averages, and don't round.
requests.open: Using budget lines matched to their event (drop lines with no matching event), work out for each event its average spending rate, `spent` ÷ `amount`, across its lines. Then, for each event `type`, average those event-level rates. Show the type, its average spending rate, and that rate divided by the simple mean of the per-type average rates. Ignore missing values in the averages, and don't round.

readings.A: A budget line with `spent` = 0 is a real zero, so it adds a rate of 0 to the averages.
readings.B: A budget line with `spent` = 0 means nothing has been spent yet, so it is left out of the rate averages.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "budget"."link_to_event" AS "e", "event"."type" AS "g", AVG((CAST("budget"."spent" AS REAL) / "budget"."amount")) AS "m1" FROM "budget" AS "budget" INNER JOIN "event" AS "event" ON "event"."event_id" = "budget"."link_to_event" GROUP BY "budget"."link_to_event", "event"."type"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT AVG("s2"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s2" AS "s2") SELECT "s2"."g" AS "g", "s2"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s2"."m1" AS REAL) / "s3"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s2" AS "s2" INNER JOIN "s3" AS "s3" ON NOT ("s3"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "budget"."link_to_event" AS "e", "event"."type" AS "g", AVG((CAST(NULLIF("budget"."spent", 0) AS REAL) / "budget"."amount")) AS "m1" FROM "budget" AS "budget" INNER JOIN "event" AS "event" ON "event"."event_id" = "budget"."link_to_event" GROUP BY "budget"."link_to_event", "event"."type"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT AVG("s2"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s2" AS "s2") SELECT "s2"."g" AS "g", "s2"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s2"."m1" AS REAL) / "s3"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s2" AS "s2" INNER JOIN "s3" AS "s3" ON NOT ("s3"."v" IS NULL)

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from `budget` lines
Match each budget line to its event on `budget.link_to_event` = `event.event_id`; drop lines with no matching event
Work in two stages: group by event (with its `event.type`), then group the event-level figures by `event.type`; one row per type, with the type as the first column

Average spending rate: for each event, the average over its lines of `spent` ÷ `amount`; then, for each type, the average of those event averages. Missing values are ignored, and a zero amount gives a missing value.
The type's average spending rate divided by the simple mean of the per-type average spending rates. If that mean is missing, no rows are returned. No rounding, ordering or limit.

A.requirement: Lines where `spent` = 0 count as a rate of 0

B.requirement: Lines where `spent` = 0 are left out of the rate averages (treated as missing)

requests.specific_A: Considering only advanced behaviour analyses whose linked transaction record and trader both exist, count for each trader type (`tradekind`) the number of analysis records (a transaction analysed twice counts twice), and that count's share of the total of these counts over all trader types. For the trader types whose count is strictly above the average count across trader types, give in one row the sum of their counts, the average of their shares, and the average amount by which their counts exceed that average count, without rounding.
requests.specific_B: Considering only advanced behaviour analyses whose linked transaction record and trader both exist, count for each trader type (`tradekind`) the number of distinct transactions analysed (a transaction analysed twice counts once), and that count's share of the total of these counts over all trader types. For the trader types whose count is strictly above the average count across trader types, give in one row the sum of their counts, the average of their shares, and the average amount by which their counts exceed that average count, without rounding.
requests.open: Using the advanced behaviour data (only where the trade and its trader can be found), work out for each trader type how many analysed trade records it has and its share of the overall total. Then, for the trader types whose number is strictly above the average across trader types, give in one row their combined number, their average share, and on average how far above that average number they sit. Don't round.

readings.A: Count analysis records per trader type and compute each type's share of the total. For the types above the average count, report the summed count, the average share and the average excess over the average count.
readings.B: Count distinct analysed transactions per trader type and compute each type's share of the total. For the types above the average count, report the summed count, the average share and the average excess over the average count.

sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "trader"."tradekind" AS "g", COUNT(DISTINCT "advancedbehavior"."translink") AS "m1" FROM "advancedbehavior" AS "advancedbehavior" INNER JOIN "transactionrecord" AS "transactionrecord" ON "transactionrecord"."transreg" = "advancedbehavior"."translink" INNER JOIN "trader" AS "trader" ON "trader"."tradereg" = "transactionrecord"."trdref" GROUP BY "trader"."tradekind"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m1" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from `advancedbehavior` records. Inner-join to `transactionrecord` on `transreg` = `translink` and to `trader` on `tradereg` = `trdref`, dropping unmatched rows. Group by trader type (`tradekind`).
Each trader type's share = its count ÷ the sum of the counts over all trader types
Baseline = the unweighted average of the per-trader-type counts. Keep only trader types whose count is strictly greater than this baseline. Return a single row.
Sum of the kept trader types' counts
Average of the kept trader types' shares
Average of (count − baseline) over the kept trader types. No rounding.

A.requirement: Per-trader-type count = the number of joined analysis records. A transaction with two analyses counts twice.

B.requirement: Per-trader-type count = the number of distinct linked transactions (`translink`). A transaction with two analyses counts once.

requests.specific_A: For every account that appears in `trans`, give the account id (`account_id`), the average of its transactions' `amount` exactly as stored (always non-negative, so credits and withdrawals both add positively), its number of transactions, and that number divided by the average number of transactions per account (averaged over all accounts in `trans`). Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest and keep exactly the first 10 rows, breaking any tie at the 10th place arbitrarily; do not round anything.
requests.specific_B: For every account that appears in `trans`, give the account id (`account_id`), the average of its transactions' signed `amount`, taking `amount` as positive when `type` is 'PRIJEM' (credit) and as negative for every other `type` (the withdrawals 'VYDAJ' and 'VYBER'), its number of transactions, and that number divided by the average number of transactions per account (averaged over all accounts in `trans`). Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest and keep exactly the first 10 rows, breaking any tie at the 10th place arbitrarily; do not round anything.
requests.open: For every account in `trans`, show the account id, its average transaction `amount` across its credits and withdrawals, how many transactions it has, and that count divided by the average number of transactions per account over all accounts. Rank by that ratio, highest first, and keep only the first 10 rows (break any tie at the cut arbitrarily); don't round.

readings.A: The average transaction amount is the plain average of the stored, unsigned `amount`.
readings.B: The average transaction amount is the average of a signed amount: positive for credits (PRIJEM) and negative for withdrawals (VYDAJ and VYBER). This gives the average net flow per transaction.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "trans"."account_id" AS "e", AVG("trans"."amount") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "trans" AS "trans" GROUP BY "trans"."account_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "trans"."account_id" AS "e", AVG(CASE WHEN "trans"."type" = 'PRIJEM' THEN "trans"."amount" ELSE -"trans"."amount" END) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "trans" AS "trans" GROUP BY "trans"."account_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every `trans` record; keep all of them (no filter) and group them by `trans.account_id`, giving one row per account.
Account id (`trans.account_id`).
The account's number of transactions, which is the count of its `trans` rows.
Attach to every account row the single overall value: the average of the per-account transaction counts over all accounts. Accounts are kept only when that average is not missing.
The account's transaction count divided by the overall average transaction count per account, as a real-valued ratio.
Order by that ratio, highest first. Missing values go last.
Keep exactly the first 10 rows. A tie at the cut is broken arbitrarily.
The average amount per transaction for the account. Missing values are ignored. No rounding is applied to any output.

A.requirement: Average `amount` as stored (unsigned), so credits and withdrawals both count as positive.

B.requirement: Average of a signed amount: +`amount` when `type` = 'PRIJEM', and −`amount` for every other type ('VYDAJ', and the undocumented 'VYBER').

requests.specific_A: For each order channel (`orders.orderbase`, with a missing channel counted as its own group), looking only at executions that link to an order (`orderexecutions.ordersmark` = `orders.recordvault`), give the channel, the average filled quantity (`fillcount`) across its executions (ignoring missing values), the number of executions, and that number as a fraction of the total number of executions across all channels, unrounded.
requests.specific_B: For each order channel (`orders.orderbase`, with a missing channel counted as its own group), looking only at executions that link to an order (`orderexecutions.ordersmark` = `orders.recordvault`), give the channel, the average filled quantity (`fillcount`) across its executions (ignoring missing values), the number of distinct orders those executions belong to, and that number as a fraction of these order counts summed across all channels, unrounded.
requests.open: Break down executed orders by channel (`orders.orderbase`, with a missing channel as its own group), using only executions that match an order on `ordersmark` = `recordvault`: for each channel, show the average filled quantity (`fillcount`, ignoring missing values), the count, and the channel's share of the total, unrounded.

readings.A: Per channel, count execution rows and give each channel's share of all execution rows.
readings.B: Per channel, count distinct executed orders and give each channel's share of the total of those order counts.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orders"."orderbase" AS "g", AVG("orderexecutions"."fillcount") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "orderexecutions" AS "orderexecutions" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "orderexecutions"."ordersmark" GROUP BY "orders"."orderbase"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orders"."orderbase" AS "g", AVG("orderexecutions"."fillcount") AS "m1", COUNT(DISTINCT "orders"."recordvault") AS "m2" FROM "orderexecutions" AS "orderexecutions" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "orderexecutions"."ordersmark" GROUP BY "orders"."orderbase"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from execution records (`orderexecutions`)
Inner-join to `orders` on `orders.recordvault` = `orderexecutions.ordersmark`; executions with no matching order are dropped
Group by order channel (`orders.orderbase`); a missing channel forms its own group
Order channel (`orders.orderbase`)
Average filled quantity (`orderexecutions.fillcount`) over the channel's matched execution rows, ignoring missing values
Share = the channel's count (output 3) divided by the sum of that count over all channels; no rounding
One row per channel, no particular order, unrounded

A.requirement: Count = number of matched execution rows in the channel; the share is therefore executions over total executions

B.requirement: Count = number of distinct orders (`orders.recordvault`) among the channel's matched executions; the share is therefore orders over the total of these order counts

requests.specific_A: Grouping the examination records by patient `ID`, with records that have no patient ID kept together as one group of their own, compute each group's average ANA titer (`ANA`, missing values ignored). Then take the mean of those group averages, and list the groups whose average ANA is above it. Show the patient ID, the average ANA, and how much it exceeds the overall mean, sorted by that excess from largest to smallest (missing values last), top 10 only.
requests.specific_B: Grouping the examination records by patient `ID`, leaving out records that have no patient ID, compute each group's average ANA titer (`ANA`, missing values ignored). Then take the mean of those group averages, and list the groups whose average ANA is above it. Show the patient ID, the average ANA, and how much it exceeds the overall mean, sorted by that excess from largest to smallest (missing values last), top 10 only.
requests.open: In the Examination table, average the ANA titer (`ANA`) per `ID`, ignoring missing values. Which IDs have an average above the mean of all those per-ID averages? Show the ID, its average ANA, and how far above the mean it is. Return the top 10 by that gap, largest first (missing values last).

readings.A: Examination records with no patient ID form their own group, which counts toward the overall mean and can be listed.
readings.B: Examination records with no patient ID are excluded before grouping and averaging.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Examination"."ID" AS "e", AVG("Examination"."ANA") AS "m1" FROM "Examination" AS "Examination" GROUP BY "Examination"."ID"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v" ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Examination"."ID" AS "e", AVG("Examination"."ANA") AS "m1" FROM "Examination" AS "Examination" WHERE "Examination"."ID" IS NOT NULL GROUP BY "Examination"."ID"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v" ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from `Examination` records. Group by `Examination.ID`. Which records form groups is the choice.
The group's ID (`Examination.ID`).
The group's average `ANA`, ignoring missing values.
Compare each group with the overall mean of the per-group average ANA values, ignoring missing values. Only use that mean when it is not missing.
Keep groups whose average ANA is greater than the overall mean.
The group's average ANA minus the overall mean.
Sort by that difference, largest first. Missing values go last.
Keep the first 10 rows. No rounding.

A.requirement: Records with a missing `ID` stay in as one group of their own. That group counts toward the overall mean and can appear in the output.

B.requirement: Records with a missing `ID` are dropped before grouping.

shared_requirements.requirement: Source records are examination records (`Examination`), counted as rows.

Group the examinations by patient ID (`Examination.ID`); one row per ID with its examination count. Each group's share is its count divided by the total count summed over the groups in play, and that result is joined to every group.
Keep only groups whose share is greater than the average share across groups.
Return the patient ID.
Return the number of examinations for that ID.
Return the share (count ÷ total over groups), unrounded.
Return share minus average share, unrounded.
Sort by share minus average share, descending (missing last).
Keep only the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: Examinations with a NULL patient ID form one group of their own, which counts toward the total and the average share and can appear in the output.

B.requirement: Examinations with a NULL patient ID are excluded before grouping; the total and the average share cover only examinations that have a patient ID.

requests.specific_A: Match each fee record to its order (the order's `recordvault` equals the fee's `orderslink`, compared exactly as text), and leave out fee records with no matching order. Group the matched records by trading pair (`mktnote`), with records lacking a trading pair forming one group, and work out each pair's average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`). For the benchmark, take the mean of those per-pair average net fee rates, with each trading pair counting equally. Keep only the trading pairs whose average net fee rate is strictly above this benchmark (if the benchmark is missing, keep none), and return a single row with: the average of their average net fee rates, and the average amount by which they exceed the benchmark. Skip missing values in every average (an average with nothing to average is missing), and don't round the results.
requests.specific_B: Match each fee record to its order (the order's `recordvault` equals the fee's `orderslink`, compared exactly as text), and leave out fee records with no matching order. Group the matched records by trading pair (`mktnote`), with records lacking a trading pair forming one group, and work out each pair's average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`). For the benchmark, take the average net fee rate over all matched fee records pooled together, with each fee record counting equally. Keep only the trading pairs whose average net fee rate is strictly above this benchmark (if the benchmark is missing, keep none), and return a single row with: the average of their average net fee rates, and the average amount by which they exceed the benchmark. Skip missing values in every average (an average with nothing to average is missing), and don't round the results.
requests.open: Using fee records matched to their orders (the order's `recordvault` equals the fee's `orderslink`, compared exactly as text; unmatched fees dropped), which trading pairs (`mktnote`, with records lacking a pair treated as one group) have an average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`) strictly above the overall average net fee rate? Give me one row for those pairs: the mean of their average net fee rate, and the mean amount by which they exceed the overall average. If the overall average is missing, no pairs count. Skip missing values in the averages (missing if there's nothing to average) and don't round anything.

readings.A: The benchmark is the average of the per-trading-pair average net fee rates, so each pair counts equally.
readings.B: The benchmark is the average net fee rate over all matched fee records pooled together, so each fee record counts equally.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orders"."mktnote" AS "g", AVG(("fees"."feerate" - "fees"."rebrate")) AS "m1" FROM "fees" AS "fees" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "fees"."orderslink" GROUP BY "orders"."mktnote"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orders"."mktnote" AS "g", AVG(("fees"."feerate" - "fees"."rebrate")) AS "m1" FROM "fees" AS "fees" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "fees"."orderslink" GROUP BY "orders"."mktnote"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG(("fees"."feerate" - "fees"."rebrate")) AS "v" FROM "fees" AS "fees" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "fees"."orderslink"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s3" AS "s3"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from fee records and inner-join orders where `orders.recordvault` = `fees.orderslink`, compared exactly as text; fees with no matching order are dropped
Group the matched records by trading pair `orders.mktnote`; records with missing mktnote form one group
Per pair: average of (`feerate` − `rebrate`), missing values ignored, missing if none
Keep only pairs whose average net fee rate is strictly greater than the benchmark; if the benchmark is missing, keep none
All kept pairs collapse into exactly one result row
Average of the kept pairs' average net fee rates (missing ignored; missing if none)
Average of (pair average net fee rate − benchmark) over kept pairs (missing ignored; missing if none)
Column order: output 1 then output 2; no rounding

A.requirement: Benchmark = mean of the per-pair average net fee rates, each pair weighted equally

B.requirement: Benchmark = average net fee rate over all matched fee records pooled, each fee record weighted equally

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orders"."orderbase" AS "g", AVG("fees"."feerate") AS "m1" FROM "fees" AS "fees" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "fees"."orderslink" GROUP BY "orders"."orderbase"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orders"."orderbase" AS "g", AVG("fees"."feerate") AS "m1" FROM "fees" AS "fees" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "fees"."orderslink" GROUP BY "orders"."orderbase"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("fees"."feerate") AS "v" FROM "fees" AS "fees" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "fees"."orderslink"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s3" AS "s3"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from fee records; inner-join to `orders` on `orders.recordvault` = `fees.orderslink`; unmatched fees are dropped
Compute each order channel's (`orders.orderbase`) average fee rate (`fees.feerate`), ignoring missing values
Keep the channels whose average is strictly above the benchmark; excess = channel average minus the benchmark
Return exactly one summary row covering the kept channels
Mean of the kept channels' average fee rates, unrounded
Mean of the kept channels' excess over the benchmark, unrounded

A.requirement: Benchmark = unweighted mean of the per-channel average fee rates

B.requirement: Benchmark = average fee rate over all fee records that link to an order

readings.A: Clients are attributed to the district in their own client record.
readings.B: Clients are attributed, through their dispositions, to the branch district of each account they are linked to.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "client"."district_id" AS "e", "district"."A3" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "client" AS "client" INNER JOIN "district" AS "district" ON "district"."district_id" = "client"."district_id" GROUP BY "client"."district_id", "district"."A3"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g"), "s4" AS (SELECT SUM("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "account"."district_id" AS "e", "district"."A3" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "client" AS "client" INNER JOIN "disp" AS "disp" ON "disp"."client_id" = "client"."client_id" INNER JOIN "account" AS "account" ON "account"."account_id" = "disp"."account_id" INNER JOIN "district" AS "district" ON "district"."district_id" = "account"."district_id" GROUP BY "account"."district_id", "district"."A3"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g"), "s4" AS (SELECT SUM("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Count clients (`client` records), each attributed to a district that has a matching `district` row.
Join to `district` on the district id to get the region `district.A3`. Which district id is used is the choice.
Output the district id.
Output the region (`district.A3`).
Output the count of client records for the district.
Output the district's count divided by the total count of its region.
Output the district's count divided by the overall total count.
Sort by output 5, highest first.
Keep the top 10 rows. No rounding.

A.requirement: Use the client's own district, `client.district_id`. Each client is counted once.

B.requirement: Go from client to `disp` to `account` and use the account's branch district, `account.district_id`. Each client–account link is counted.

CREATE TABLE account
(
    account_id  INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    district_id INTEGER default 0 not null,
    frequency   TEXT   not null,
    date        DATE          not null,
    foreign key (district_id) references district (district_id)
);
CREATE TABLE card
(
    card_id INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    disp_id INTEGER           not null,
    type    TEXT    not null,
    issued  DATE          not null,
    foreign key (disp_id) references disp (disp_id)
);
CREATE TABLE client
(
    client_id   INTEGER        not null
        primary key,
    gender      TEXT not null,
    birth_date  DATE       not null,
    district_id INTEGER        not null,
    foreign key (district_id) references district (district_id)
);
CREATE TABLE disp
(
    disp_id    INTEGER        not null
        primary key,
    client_id  INTEGER        not null,
    account_id INTEGER        not null,
    type      TEXT not null,
    foreign key (account_id) references account (account_id),
    foreign key (client_id) references client (client_id)
);
CREATE TABLE district
(
    district_id INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    A2          TEXT   not null,
    A3          TEXT   not null,
    A4          TEXT       not null,
    A5          TEXT           not null,

    A12         REAL null,
    A13         REAL not null,
    A14         INTEGER           not null,
    A15         INTEGER        null,

);

(
    loan_id    INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    account_id INTEGER           not null,

    amount     INTEGER           not null,
    duration   INTEGER           not null,
    payments   REAL not null,

(
    order_id   INTEGER default 0 not null

requests.specific_A: Link each rental to its inventory copy and that copy's film, dropping rentals with no matching copy or film. For each film `rating`, count the rental transactions, so a film rented many times counts each time. Compute each rating's share as its count divided by the total of these counts across all ratings. Keep only the ratings whose share is above the average share across ratings, with each rating weighted equally. Return a single row with: the total count of those ratings, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that average share. Do not round anything.
requests.specific_B: Link each rental to its inventory copy and that copy's film, dropping rentals with no matching copy or film. For each film `rating`, count the distinct films that were rented, so each film counts once however often it was rented. Compute each rating's share as its count divided by the total of these counts across all ratings. Keep only the ratings whose share is above the average share across ratings, with each rating weighted equally. Return a single row with: the total count of those ratings, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that average share. Do not round anything.
requests.open: Looking at what has actually been rented (each rental traced through its inventory copy to the film, skipping any that don't link up), what share of the rented films does each film `rating` account for, out of the total across all ratings? For the ratings whose share is above the average share across ratings, give one row with: their combined number of rented films, their average share, and how far on average their share sits above that average share. No rounding.

readings.A: Each rating's share is its number of rental transactions as a fraction of all rental transactions.
readings.B: Each rating's share is its number of distinct rented films as a fraction of the total distinct rented films summed over ratings.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "film"."rating" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "rental" AS "rental" INNER JOIN "inventory" AS "inventory" ON "inventory"."inventory_id" = "rental"."inventory_id" INNER JOIN "film" AS "film" ON "film"."film_id" = "inventory"."film_id" GROUP BY "film"."rating"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "film"."rating" AS "g", COUNT(DISTINCT "film"."film_id") AS "m1" FROM "rental" AS "rental" INNER JOIN "inventory" AS "inventory" ON "inventory"."inventory_id" = "rental"."inventory_id" INNER JOIN "film" AS "film" ON "film"."film_id" = "inventory"."film_id" GROUP BY "film"."rating"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from rental records. Inner-join each one to inventory on inventory_id, then to film on film_id. Drop rentals with no matching inventory item or film.
Group by film.rating, giving one count per rating (what is counted is the choice).
A rating's share is its count divided by the sum of the counts over all ratings.
Compute the average share across ratings, with each rating weighted equally. Keep only the ratings whose share is strictly greater than this average.
Return exactly one row that summarises the kept ratings, with three columns in this order: output 1, output 2, output 3. No rounding.
The sum of the kept ratings' counts.
The average share of the kept ratings.
The average of (share minus the average share) over the kept ratings.

A.requirement: A rating's count is the number of rental transactions. A film rented many times counts each time.

B.requirement: A rating's count is the number of distinct films rented (COUNT DISTINCT film_id). Each film counts once.

Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate), AVG(length), AVG(replacement_cost) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '3.0348430493273613', '120.4439461883408', '20.402556053811544'], ['NC-17', '210', '2.970952380952388', '113.22857142857143', '20.137619047618937'], ['R', '195', '2.9387179487179553', '118.66153846153846', '20.23102564102554'], ['PG', '194', '3.051855670103099', '112.00515463917526', '18.959072164948356'], ['G', '178', '2.888876404494388', '111.0505617977528', '20.12483146067407']] scale (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows exactly 5 levels: G, PG, PG-13, R and NC-17. These are the standard MPAA bands, which are ordered by audience restriction, so the column is an ordinal class. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY rating -> [['G', '178'], ['NC-17', '210'], ['PG', '194'], ['PG-13', '223'], ['R', '195']]
category.name: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 16 genres, each shared by many films (about 50-75 each), so the column is a grouping label and does not identify single records. Evidence: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film_category fc JOIN category c ON c.category_id = fc.category_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY films DESC -> [['Sports', '74'], ['Foreign', '73'], ['Family', '69'], ['Documentary', '68'], ['Animation', '66'], ['Action', '64']]
customer.store_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 2 stores with about 300 customers each, so the column is a grouping label shared by many rows. Evidence: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS customers, SUM(active) AS active_customers FROM customer GROUP BY store_id -> [['1', '326', '318'], ['2', '273', '266']]
inventory.store_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 2 store values over 4581 copies, about 2270 per store, so the column is a grouping label. Evidence: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS copies, COUNT(DISTINCT film_id) AS titles FROM inventory GROUP BY store_id -> [['1', '2270', '759'], ['2', '2311', '762']]
country.country: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Many customers share a country (the top countries have dozens of customers each), so country works as a grouping attribute for customers. Evidence: SELECT co.country, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customer cu JOIN address a ON a.address_id = cu.address_id JOIN city ci ON ci.city_id = a.city_id JOIN country co ON co.country_id = ci.country_id GROUP BY co.country ORDER BY customers DESC LIMIT 10 -> [['India', '60'], ['China', '53'], ['United States', '36'], ['Japan', '31'], ['Mexico', '30'], ['Russian Federation', '28']]
film.special_features: desc (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 15 distinct values, all of them combinations of the same 4 feature names (for example 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes'). The column is a set, not a single category. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']] semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows 15 distinct values, all combinations of the same 4 feature names, such as 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes' and 'Trailers,Commentaries'. The column is a set, not a single class, so it should not be offered as a grouping. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']]
film.length: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified rating query already returns AVG(length) between 111.05 (G) and 120.44 (PG-13). The catalogue profile gives 140 distinct values from 46 to 185 minutes. So length is a continuous ratio-scale quantity whose group averages can be read directly. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(length) AS avg_minutes, MIN(length), MAX(length) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '120.4439461883408', '46', '185'], ['NC-17', '210', '113.22857142857143', '46', '184'], ['R', '195', '118.66153846153846', '49', '185'], ['PG', '194', '112.00515463917526', '46', '185'], ['G', '178', '111.0505617977528', '47', '185']]
film.rental_duration: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows 5 values from 3 to 7 days, all well above zero, so the column is a ratio-scale number of days per film. The query shows how many films fall at each value. Evidence: SELECT rental_duration, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate) AS avg_rate FROM film GROUP BY rental_duration ORDER BY rental_duration -> [['3', '203', '2.8323645320197115'], ['4', '203', '2.97029556650247'], ['5', '191', '3.19942408376964'], ['6', '212', '2.895660377358497'], ['7', '191', '3.021413612565451']]

The auditor noted that the difference is always about −17 and the relative gap about −0.85, which fits two different quantities rather than one price seen two ways. Evidence: SELECT MIN(replacement_cost - rental_rate), MAX(replacement_cost - rental_rate), AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) FROM film -> [['5.0', '29.0', '0.16651517608314595']]

Return one row with those states' average count and their average excess over that overall average. No rounding.
