requests.specific_A: For each patient ID in the Laboratory table, compute their average hemoglobin (`HGB`) over their lab records, ignoring missing values. Define the overall average as the mean of these per-patient averages, so every patient counts once no matter how many tests they had. Keep the patients whose average is above that overall average. For each kept patient, list the ID, their average HGB, how far it is above the overall average, and their average minus the mean of the kept patients' averages. Sort by that last value from highest to lowest and show the top 10, unrounded.
requests.specific_B: For each patient ID in the Laboratory table, compute their average hemoglobin (`HGB`) over their lab records, ignoring missing values. Define the overall average as the mean `HGB` over all individual lab records pooled together, so each test counts once and patients with more tests weigh more. Keep the patients whose average is above that overall average. For each kept patient, list the ID, their average HGB, how far it is above the overall average, and their average minus the mean of the kept patients' averages. Sort by that last value from highest to lowest and show the top 10, unrounded.
requests.open: Among patients whose average hemoglobin (`HGB`) across their lab records (ignoring missing values) is above the overall average hemoglobin, list the patient ID, their average HGB, how far it is above the overall average, and their average minus the average of these above-average patients' averages. Show the top 10 by that last value, highest first, unrounded.

readings.A: The overall HGB average is an average of patient averages, so each patient counts once.
readings.B: The overall HGB average is taken over every lab record directly, so patients with more tests weigh more.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Laboratory"."ID" AS "e", AVG("Laboratory"."HGB") AS "m1" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" GROUP BY "Laboratory"."ID"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Laboratory"."ID" AS "e", AVG("Laboratory"."HGB") AS "m1" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" GROUP BY "Laboratory"."ID"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("Laboratory"."HGB") AS "v" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: For each Laboratory.ID, compute the average HGB (missing values ignored). Keep the patients whose average is strictly greater than the overall HGB average.
Compare each kept patient's average with the overall average (the cutoff). Separately, compute the mean of the kept patients' averages and compare each patient against it.
patient ID
the patient's average HGB
the patient's average − the overall average

sort by output 4 descending, with missing values last

requests.specific_A: Match risk/margin records to orders (`ordervault` = `recordvault`) and orders to users (`userlink` = `userstamp`), dropping anything without a match. For each account scope (`users.acctscope`), give the scope, the number of risk/margin records (an order with two risk/margin records counts twice), that number as a fraction of the total across all scopes, and that number divided by the average of those numbers across scopes, unrounded.
requests.specific_B: Match risk/margin records to orders (`ordervault` = `recordvault`) and orders to users (`userlink` = `userstamp`), dropping anything without a match. For each account scope (`users.acctscope`), give the scope, the number of distinct orders (an order with two risk/margin records counts once), that number as a fraction of the total across all scopes, and that number divided by the average of those numbers across scopes, unrounded.
requests.open: Matching risk/margin records to their orders (`ordervault` = `recordvault`) and orders to their users (`userlink` = `userstamp`), and ignoring anything that doesn't match: for each account scope (`users.acctscope`), how many risk/margin-matched orders are there? Show the scope, that count, its share of the total across all scopes, and the count divided by the average count per scope, without rounding.

readings.A: For each account scope, count the risk/margin records that link through orders to users, so an order with several risk/margin records counts once per record. Report the count, its share of the total across scopes, and its ratio to the average count across scopes.
readings.B: For each account scope, count the distinct orders that have risk/margin records and link to users, so each order counts once. Report the count, its share of the total across scopes, and its ratio to the average count across scopes.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "riskandmargin"."ordervault" AS "e", "users"."acctscope" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "riskandmargin" AS "riskandmargin" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "riskandmargin"."ordervault" INNER JOIN "users" AS "users" ON "users"."userstamp" = "orders"."userlink" GROUP BY "riskandmargin"."ordervault", "users"."acctscope"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", SUM("s1"."m1") AS "m1" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT SUM("s2"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s2" AS "s2"), "s4" AS (SELECT "s2"."g" AS "g", "s2"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s2"."m1" AS REAL) / "s3"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s2" AS "s2" INNER JOIN "s3" AS "s3" ON NOT ("s3"."v" IS NULL)), "s5" AS (SELECT AVG("s4"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s4" AS "s4") SELECT "s4"."g" AS "g", "s4"."m1" AS "m1", "s4"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s4"."m1" AS REAL) / "s5"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s4" AS "s4" INNER JOIN "s5" AS "s5" ON NOT ("s5"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "riskandmargin"."ordervault" AS "e", "users"."acctscope" AS "g", COUNT(DISTINCT "riskandmargin"."ordervault") AS "m1" FROM "riskandmargin" AS "riskandmargin" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "riskandmargin"."ordervault" INNER JOIN "users" AS "users" ON "users"."userstamp" = "orders"."userlink" GROUP BY "riskandmargin"."ordervault", "users"."acctscope"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", SUM("s1"."m1") AS "m1" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT SUM("s2"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s2" AS "s2"), "s4" AS (SELECT "s2"."g" AS "g", "s2"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s2"."m1" AS REAL) / "s3"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s2" AS "s2" INNER JOIN "s3" AS "s3" ON NOT ("s3"."v" IS NULL)), "s5" AS (SELECT AVG("s4"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s4" AS "s4") SELECT "s4"."g" AS "g", "s4"."m1" AS "m1", "s4"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s4"."m1" AS REAL) / "s5"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s4" AS "s4" INNER JOIN "s5" AS "s5" ON NOT ("s5"."v" IS NULL)

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from risk/margin records and match each one to orders where `orders.recordvault` = `riskandmargin.ordervault` (exact text match). Drop risk/margin records that have no matching order.
Match each order to users where `users.userstamp` = `orders.userlink` (exact text match). Drop any combined record that has no matching user.
Return one row per account scope (`users.acctscope`). The first column is the account scope.
The second column is a count for each account scope. Choice A or B decides what is counted.
The third column is the scope's count divided by the sum of the counts across all scopes. It is not rounded.
The fourth column is the scope's count divided by the average of the counts across scopes. It is not rounded.
Return exactly these four columns in this order. No row order and no row limit are required.

A.requirement: Count the matched risk/margin records, so an order with two risk/margin records counts twice.

B.requirement: Count distinct orders, so an order with two risk/margin records counts once.

requests.specific_A: For each account with standing orders (`order.account_id`), count its orders. Work out the average number of orders per account, using only accounts that have at least one order. Keep the accounts whose order count is above that average. For each, show the account id, its order count, how far the count is above that average, and how far the count is above the average order count of the kept above-average accounts. Sort by this last difference from largest to smallest and return only the first 10 rows. Don't round anything.
requests.specific_B: For each account with standing orders (`order.account_id`), count its orders. Work out the average number of orders per account, averaging over every account in `account`, with accounts that have no orders counting as zero. Keep the accounts whose order count is above that average. For each, show the account id, its order count, how far the count is above that average, and how far the count is above the average order count of the kept above-average accounts. Sort by this last difference from largest to smallest and return only the first 10 rows. Don't round anything.
requests.open: For each account with standing orders (`order.account_id`), count its orders. Which accounts have more orders than the average number of orders per account? For each, show the account id, its order count, how far the count is above that average, and how far the count is above the average order count of those above-average accounts. Sort by this last difference from largest to smallest and give only the first 10. Don't round anything.

readings.A: The average number of orders per account counts only accounts that have orders.
readings.B: The average number of orders per account counts all accounts, with zero for accounts that have no orders.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "order"."account_id" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "order" AS "order" GROUP BY "order"."account_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "order"."account_id" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "order" AS "order" GROUP BY "order"."account_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT CAST(SUM("s1"."m1") AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT("a"."account_id") FROM "account" AS "a") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Use `order` records grouped by account (`order.account_id`). Each account's order count is the number of its order records.

Compare each account's count with the single average-orders-per-account value. Keep only accounts whose count is strictly greater than that average. Then compare each kept account with the average order count of the kept accounts.
Account id (`order.account_id`).
The account's number of orders.
Order count minus the average orders per account. Not rounded.
Order count minus the average order count of the kept above-average accounts. Not rounded.
Sort by output 4 from largest to smallest.
Return only the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: Average orders per account is taken only over accounts with at least one order.

B.requirement: Average orders per account is taken over every account in `account`, and accounts with no orders count as 0.

context.schema:
CREATE TABLE account
(
    account_id  INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    district_id INTEGER default 0 not null,
    frequency   TEXT   not null,
    date        DATE          not null,
    foreign key (district_id) references district (district_id)
);
CREATE TABLE card
(
    card_id INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    disp_id INTEGER           not null,
    type    TEXT    not null,
    issued  DATE          not null,
    foreign key (disp_id) references disp (disp_id)
);
CREATE TABLE client
(
    client_id   INTEGER        not null
        primary key,
    gender      TEXT not null,
    birth_date  DATE       not null,
    district_id INTEGER        not null,
    foreign key (district_id) references district (district_id)
);
CREATE TABLE disp
(
    disp_id    INTEGER        not null
        primary key,
    client_id  INTEGER        not null,
    account_id INTEGER        not null,
    type      TEXT not null,
    foreign key (account_id) references account (account_id),
    foreign key (client_id) references client (client_id)
);
CREATE TABLE district
(
    district_id INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    A2          TEXT   not null,
    A3          TEXT   not null,
    A4          TEXT       not null,
    A5          TEXT           not null,
    A6          TEXT           not null,
    A7          TEXT           not null,
    A8          INTEGER        not null,
    A9          INTEGER           not null,
    A10         REAL not null,
    A11         INTEGER           not null,
    A12         REAL null,
    A13         REAL not null,
    A14         INTEGER           not null,
    A15         INTEGER        null,
    A16         INTEGER          not null
);
CREATE TABLE loan
(
    loan_id    INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    account_id INTEGER           not null,
    date       DATE          not null,
    amount     INTEGER           not null,
    duration   INTEGER           not null,
    payments   REAL not null,
    status     TEXT    not null,
    foreign key (account_id) references account (account_id)
);
CREATE TABLE `order`
(
    order_id   INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    account_id INTEGER           not null,
    bank_to    TEXT    not null,
    account_to INTEGER           not null,
    amount     REAL not null,
    k_symbol   TEXT    not null,
    foreign key (account_id) references account (account_id)
);
CREATE TABLE trans
(
    trans_id   INTEGER default 0    not null
        primary key,
    account_id INTEGER default 0    not null,
    date       DATE             not null,
    type       TEXT       not null,
    operation  TEXT      null,
    amount     INTEGER              not null,
    balance    INTEGER             not null,
    k_symbol   TEXT      null,
    bank       TEXT       null,
    account    INTEGER          null,
    foreign key (account_id) references account (account_id)
);

requests.specific_A: For each archival status (`archstat`) in the QC data, with a missing status treated as its own group, count the QC records. Work out each status's share as that count divided by the sum of the counts over all statuses. Return only the statuses whose share is above the average share across statuses. Show the status, the count, the share, and how far the share is above the average share, with no rounding.
requests.specific_B: For each archival status (`archstat`) in the QC data, with a missing status treated as its own group, count the distinct projects (`arcref`) that have QC records with that status. Work out each status's share as that count divided by the sum of the counts over all statuses. Return only the statuses whose share is above the average share across statuses. Show the status, the count, the share, and how far the share is above the average share, with no rounding.
requests.open: In the QC data, tally the projects under each archival status (`archstat`), with a missing status treated as its own group. Work out each status's share as its tally divided by the sum of the tallies over all statuses. Return only the statuses whose share is above the average share across statuses. Show the status, the tally, the share, and how far the share is above the average share, with no rounding.

readings.A: For each archival status, count the QC records. Each share is that count divided by the sum of the counts. Return the statuses whose share is above the average share, with the status, count, share and share minus average.
readings.B: For each archival status, count the distinct projects with QC records of that status. Each share is that count divided by the sum of these counts. Return the statuses whose share is above the average share, with the status, count, share and share minus average.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scanqc"."archstat" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "scanqc" AS "scanqc" GROUP BY "scanqc"."archstat"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scanqc"."archstat" AS "g", COUNT(DISTINCT "scanqc"."arcref") AS "m1" FROM "scanqc" AS "scanqc" GROUP BY "scanqc"."archstat"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every row of `scanqc`. Group by archival status (`scanqc.archstat`), with a missing status forming its own group.

Pair each status row with the grand total, which is the sum of the per-status counts across all statuses. Then pair it with the average share across statuses. A status row is dropped only if the total or the average is missing.
Keep only the statuses whose share is strictly greater than the average share across all statuses.
First column: the archival status (`archstat`).
Third column: the share, which is the status's count divided by the sum of the counts over all statuses. Not rounded.
Fourth column: the share minus the average share across all statuses. Not rounded.
Second column: the per-status count. The share and the average are computed from this count. No ordering is specified.

A.requirement: The count is the number of QC records with that status (COUNT(*)).

B.requirement: The count is the number of distinct projects (`arcref`) with QC records of that status (COUNT DISTINCT arcref).

context.documentation:
Equipment.EquipDesign: Full name: 'Equipment Model'. Explanation: Model name or identifier. Data type: VARCHAR(14). Example: 'Model-669'.
Equipment.EquipForm: Full name: 'Equipment Type'. Explanation: Type or category of scanning equipment. Data type: VARCHAR(28). Possible categories: LiDAR, Structured Light, Photogrammetry, Laser.
Equipment.EquipRegistry: Full name: 'Equipment ID'. Explanation: Primary key for equipment. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
Equipment.EquipStatus: Full name: 'Equipment Condition'. Explanation: Overall condition of the equipment. Data type: VARCHAR(16). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor.
Equipment.EquipTune: Full name: 'Calibration Date'. Explanation: Date the equipment was last calibrated. Data type: DATE. Example: '2024-11-01'.
Equipment.PowerLevel: Full name: 'Battery Level (%)'. Explanation: Battery level as an integer percentage. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 62.
Personnel.CrewLabel: Full name: 'Operator Name'. Explanation: Name or label for the operator. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Example: 'Joel Wallace'.
Personnel.CrewRegistry: Full name: 'Operator ID'. Explanation: Primary key for Personnel, representing an operator. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
Personnel.LeadLabel: Full name: 'Supervisor Name'. Explanation: Name of the supervisor. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Example: 'Michael Kaiser'.
Personnel.LeadRegistry: Full name: 'Supervisor ID'. Explanation: Identifies a supervisor. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'SV7658'.
Projects.ArcRegistry: Full name: 'Project ID'. Explanation: Primary key for Projects, a unique project identifier. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
Projects.AuthHalt: Full name: 'Permit Expiry Date'. Explanation: Date on which the permit expires. Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-12-05'.
Projects.AuthPin: Full name: 'Permit Number'. Explanation: Authorization or permit ID. Data type: CHAR(6). Example: 'PMT4719'.
Projects.FundFlux: Full name: 'Funding Source'. Explanation: Source of funds for the project. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Government'.
Projects.VesselTag: Full name: 'Project Name'. Explanation: Label or name for the project. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Example: 'Project Happy'.
ScanConservation.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Associates conservation data with a project. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanConservation.CureRank: Full name: 'Conservation Priority'. Explanation: Priority level for conservation efforts. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Critical, Low, High.
ScanConservation.CureRegistry: Full name: 'Conservation Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for conservation data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 6001.
ScanConservation.HarmAssess: Full name: 'Damage Assessment'. Explanation: Indicates severity of damage. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: None, Moderate, Severe.
ScanConservation.IntervHistory: Full name: 'Intervention History'. Explanation: Past restoration or intervention records. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: None, Major, Minor.
ScanConservation.PriorDocs: Full name: 'Previous Documentation'. Explanation: Level of existing documentation. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: None, Partial, Complete.
ScanConservation.StructState: Full name: 'Structural Stability'. Explanation: Stability level of the structure. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Stable, Moderate, Unstable.
ScanConservation.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Associates conservation data with a site code. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanEnvironment.AirRegistry: Full name: 'Environment Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for environment data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 1001.
ScanEnvironment.AmbicTemp: Full name: 'Ambient Temperature (C)'. Explanation: Air temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 25.3.
ScanEnvironment.EquipRef: Full name: 'Equipment Reference'. Explanation: Identifies which equipment these environment data refer to. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
ScanEnvironment.GeoSignal: Full name: 'GPS Signal Quality'. Explanation: Quality rating for GPS reception. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: None, Poor, Good, Excellent.
ScanEnvironment.HumePct: Full name: 'Relative Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 60.4.
ScanEnvironment.IllumeLux: Full name: 'Light Conditions (lux)'. Explanation: Measured illumination in lux. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 86054.
ScanEnvironment.ImgCount: Full name: 'Number of Images'. Explanation: How many images were taken for photogrammetry. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 248.
ScanEnvironment.LinkStatus: Full name: 'Network Status'. Explanation: Status of network connectivity. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Possible categories: Disconnected, Connected.
ScanEnvironment.PhotoMap: Full name: 'Photogrammetry Overlap'. Explanation: Percentage overlap for photogrammetry images. Data type: CHAR(4). Possible categories: 80%, 60%, 90%.
ScanEnvironment.TrackStatus: Full name: 'RTK Status'. Explanation: Real-Time Kinematic correction state. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Possible categories: None, Fixed.
ScanEnvironment.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Links environment conditions to a specific site code. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanFeatures.ArtiCount: Full name: 'Artifact Count'. Explanation: Number of artifacts recognized. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 71.
ScanFeatures.EquipRef: Full name: 'Equipment Reference'. Explanation: Equipment ID used to detect these features. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
ScanFeatures.HueStudy: Full name: 'Color Analysis'. Explanation: Status of color analysis (done or pending). Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Partial, Completed, Not Required.
ScanFeatures.MatKind: Full name: 'Material Type'. Explanation: Primary composition or material. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Organic, Metal, Mixed, Ceramic, Stone.
ScanFeatures.PatternNote: Full name: 'Pattern Recognition'. Explanation: Notes regarding detected patterns. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Not Required, None, Partial.
ScanFeatures.StructKind: Full name: 'Structure Type'. Explanation: Type of structural element. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Artifact, Complex, Wall, Foundation.
ScanFeatures.TextureStudy: Full name: 'Texture Analysis'. Explanation: Status of texture analysis. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Partial, Completed, Not Required.

ScanFeatures.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Site code tied to these features. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.

ScanMesh.FacetFaces: Full name: 'Mesh Faces'. Explanation: Count of triangular or polygonal faces. Data type: BIGINT. Example: 5997318.

ScanMesh.FacetVerts: Full name: 'Mesh Vertices'. Explanation: Count of mesh vertices. Data type: BIGINT. Example: 7234721.

ScanMesh.TexPix: Full name: 'Texture Size (px)'. Explanation: Texture image dimension in pixels. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 2048.
ScanMesh.UVMapQual: Full name: 'UV Mapping Quality'. Explanation: Quality of the UV mapping process. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Possible categories: Medium, High, Low.
ScanMesh.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Associates mesh data with a site code. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanPointCloud.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Project ID associated with this point cloud. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanPointCloud.CloudDense: Full name: 'Point-Cloud Density Code'. Explanation: A numeric code classifying point density. Data type: INTEGER. Possible categories: 9449, 431, 7553, 1746.
ScanPointCloud.CloudRegistry: Full name: 'Point Cloud Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for point cloud data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 2001.

requests.specific_A: For each order status (`orders.orderflow`), using order executions linked to their order where `orderexecutions.ordersmark` matches `orders.recordvault` (executions with no matching order are left out), show the status, the average filled quantity (`fillcount`) across its executions — ignoring missing values but counting zero fills as zero —, the number of executions, and that number as a fraction of the total number of executions across all statuses. Don't round anything.
requests.specific_B: For each order status (`orders.orderflow`), using order executions linked to their order where `orderexecutions.ordersmark` matches `orders.recordvault` (executions with no matching order are left out), show the status, the average filled quantity (`fillcount`) across its executions — ignoring missing values and treating zero fills as no fill, so they are left out —, the number of executions, and that number as a fraction of the total number of executions across all statuses. Don't round anything.
requests.open: For each order status, looking at order executions matched to their order (`orderexecutions.ordersmark` = `orders.recordvault`; unmatched executions dropped), show the status, the average filled quantity (`fillcount`), the number of executions, and what fraction of all executions that number is. No rounding.

readings.A: Per order status, average the filled quantity over all linked executions with a non-missing fill, counting zero fills as zero.
readings.B: Per order status, average the filled quantity only over linked executions with a non-missing, non-zero fill, treating zero fills as no fill.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orders"."orderflow" AS "g", AVG("orderexecutions"."fillcount") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "orderexecutions" AS "orderexecutions" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "orderexecutions"."ordersmark" GROUP BY "orders"."orderflow"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orders"."orderflow" AS "g", AVG(NULLIF("orderexecutions"."fillcount", 0)) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "orderexecutions" AS "orderexecutions" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "orderexecutions"."ordersmark" GROUP BY "orders"."orderflow"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)

shared_requirements.requirement: Source rows are order executions (`orderexecutions`), one per execution record
Inner-join each execution to `orders` on `orders.recordvault` = `orderexecutions.ordersmark` (text equality); executions without a matching order are dropped; one row per match
Group by order status `orders.orderflow`; one row per status; output the status
Average filled quantity `orderexecutions.fillcount` per status, missing (NULL) values ignored, NULL if no values remain
Number of joined execution rows per status (all rows, including zero or missing fills)
Per-status row count divided by the total of those counts across all statuses (fraction, not percent)
No rounding, no ordering, no limit; output columns in order: status, average fill, count, share

A.requirement: Executions with `fillcount` = 0 are included in the average as zero

B.requirement: Executions with `fillcount` = 0 are treated as no fill and excluded from the average (still counted in output 3)

requests.specific_A: Group the income records by linked member (`income.link_to_member`), and put all income records whose `link_to_member` is missing together as one extra group of their own, which counts like any other group. Sum `amount` in each group. Each group's share is its sum divided by the sum of all the group sums; then take the plain average of the shares across groups. Keep only groups whose share is strictly greater than that average, and return one row with: (1) the total of their summed amounts, (2) the average of their shares, and (3) the average of (share minus average share). Do not round.
requests.specific_B: Group the income records by linked member (`income.link_to_member`), after first dropping every income record whose `link_to_member` is missing, so such income plays no part in anything below. Sum `amount` in each group. Each group's share is its sum divided by the sum of all the group sums; then take the plain average of the shares across groups. Keep only groups whose share is strictly greater than that average, and return one row with: (1) the total of their summed amounts, (2) the average of their shares, and (3) the average of (share minus average share). Do not round.
requests.open: Total up income `amount` by member (`link_to_member`) and work out each total's share of the sum of all the totals. For those whose share is strictly above the average share, give one row with: their combined amount, their average share, and the average amount by which their share is above the average share. No rounding.

readings.A: Group income by linked member, with unlinked income as its own group, then compute shares, the average share, and summarise the above-average groups.
readings.B: Drop unlinked income, group the rest by linked member, then compute shares, the average share, and summarise the above-average groups.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "income"."link_to_member" AS "e", SUM("income"."amount") AS "m1" FROM "income" AS "income" GROUP BY "income"."link_to_member"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "income"."link_to_member" AS "e", SUM("income"."amount") AS "m1" FROM "income" AS "income" WHERE "income"."link_to_member" IS NOT NULL GROUP BY "income"."link_to_member"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from income records; group by `income.link_to_member` and sum `amount` per group (missing amounts ignored)
Each group's share = its sum ÷ the sum of all group sums; then take the plain average of the shares across groups
Keep only groups whose share is strictly greater than the average share, and return a single summary row
Total of the qualifying groups' summed amounts
Average of the qualifying groups' shares
Average of (share − average share) over the qualifying groups; no rounding

A.requirement: Income records with no linked member (NULL `link_to_member`) form one extra group of their own; that group adds to the total, counts toward the average share, and can qualify

B.requirement: Income records with no linked member (NULL `link_to_member`) are dropped before grouping, so they play no part in the total, the average, or the result

requests.specific_A: Joining each transaction to its account (dropping transactions with no matching account), compute for each account statement frequency (`account.frequency`) the average signed transaction amount — `trans.amount` taken as positive when `trans.type` is 'PRIJEM', negative when it is 'VYDAJ', and left out (no value) for every other type, including 'VYBER' — and the average `trans.balance` over all its transactions. Then take the plain mean of those per-frequency average signed amounts, keep only the frequencies whose average signed amount is above that mean, and return a single row with: the average of their average signed amounts, the average of their average balances, and the average of how far their average signed amount exceeds the mean. Don't round.
requests.specific_B: Joining each transaction to its account (dropping transactions with no matching account), compute for each account statement frequency (`account.frequency`) the average signed transaction amount — `trans.amount` taken as positive when `trans.type` is 'PRIJEM', negative when it is 'VYDAJ' or 'VYBER' (treating 'VYBER' as a debit), and left out (no value) for every other type — and the average `trans.balance` over all its transactions. Then take the plain mean of those per-frequency average signed amounts, keep only the frequencies whose average signed amount is above that mean, and return a single row with: the average of their average signed amounts, the average of their average balances, and the average of how far their average signed amount exceeds the mean. Don't round.
requests.open: Linking each transaction to its account (skipping transactions without one), for each account statement frequency work out the average signed transaction amount — credits ('PRIJEM') positive, withdrawals negative, and any transaction that is neither left out — along with the average balance after the transaction. Then take the simple mean of those per-frequency signed averages, keep the frequencies above it, and give me one row: the average of their signed averages, the average of their balance averages, and the average amount by which their signed average exceeds the mean. Don't round.

readings.A: Only PRIJEM (positive) and VYDAJ (negative) give a signed amount; VYBER transactions are left out of the signed-amount average.
readings.B: VYBER transactions are treated as debits, so their amount is negated like VYDAJ and they enter the signed-amount average.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "account"."frequency" AS "g", AVG(CASE WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('PRIJEM') THEN "trans"."amount" WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('VYDAJ') THEN (0 - "trans"."amount") END) AS "m1", AVG("trans"."balance") AS "m2" FROM "trans" AS "trans" INNER JOIN "account" AS "account" ON "account"."account_id" = "trans"."account_id" GROUP BY "account"."frequency"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "account"."frequency" AS "g", AVG(CASE WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('PRIJEM') THEN "trans"."amount" WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('VYDAJ', 'VYBER') THEN (0 - "trans"."amount") END) AS "m1", AVG("trans"."balance") AS "m2" FROM "trans" AS "trans" INNER JOIN "account" AS "account" ON "account"."account_id" = "trans"."account_id" GROUP BY "account"."frequency"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from transactions inner-joined to account on account_id; transactions with no matching account are dropped
Group by account.frequency, one row per frequency

Per frequency: the average signed amount. trans.amount is positive when trans.type = 'PRIJEM' and negative when trans.type = 'VYDAJ'. Types other than PRIJEM, VYDAJ and VYBER have no value. Missing values are ignored.
Per frequency: average of trans.balance over all of its transactions (missing ignored)
Take the plain mean of the per-frequency average signed amounts. Keep only frequencies whose average signed amount is strictly greater than that mean. If the mean is missing, keep none.
Return exactly one row built over the kept frequencies
Column 1: average of the kept frequencies' average signed amounts
Column 2: average of the kept frequencies' average balances
Column 3: average of (frequency's average signed amount minus the mean)
No rounding; columns in this order

A.requirement: Rows with trans.type = 'VYBER' have no signed value and are left out of the average

B.requirement: Rows with trans.type = 'VYBER' count as debits: amount negated, like VYDAJ

requests.specific_A: Using the order executions, find each order's (`ordersmark`) average unfilled quantity (`remaincount`), ignoring missing values; executions with no order reference count together as one order. Take the mean of these per-order averages, counting each order once, and keep the orders whose average is above it, noting how far above it they are. Among those orders, take the mean of their averages, keep only the orders above that mean as well, and note how far above it they are. Return one row with three values, without rounding: the average of the remaining orders' averages, their average excess over the first benchmark, and their average excess over the second.
requests.specific_B: Using the order executions, find each order's (`ordersmark`) average unfilled quantity (`remaincount`), ignoring missing values; executions with no order reference count together as one order. Take the mean unfilled quantity across all individual execution records, and keep the orders whose average is above it, noting how far above it they are. Among those orders, take the mean of their averages, keep only the orders above that mean as well, and note how far above it they are. Return one row with three values, without rounding: the average of the remaining orders' averages, their average excess over the first benchmark, and their average excess over the second.
requests.open: Using the order executions, find each order's (`ordersmark`) average unfilled quantity (`remaincount`), ignoring missing values; executions with no order reference count together as one order. Which orders are above the overall average unfilled quantity, and by how much? Among those orders, keep only the ones that are also above the group's own average, and note how far above it they are. Return one row with three values, without rounding: the average of these orders' averages, their average excess over the overall average, and their average excess over the second average.

readings.A: The first benchmark is the mean of the per-order average unfilled quantities.
readings.B: The first benchmark is the mean unfilled quantity over all execution records.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orderexecutions"."ordersmark" AS "e", AVG("orderexecutions"."remaincount") AS "m1" FROM "orderexecutions" AS "orderexecutions" GROUP BY "orderexecutions"."ordersmark"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m1" > "s4"."v") SELECT AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orderexecutions"."ordersmark" AS "e", AVG("orderexecutions"."remaincount") AS "m1" FROM "orderexecutions" AS "orderexecutions" GROUP BY "orderexecutions"."ordersmark"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("oe"."remaincount") AS "v" FROM "orderexecutions" AS "oe"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m1" > "s4"."v") SELECT AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from `orderexecutions`. Compute each order's average unfilled quantity (`remaincount`), grouped by `ordersmark`; executions without an `ordersmark` form one group of their own, and missing `remaincount` values are ignored. Keep orders whose average is greater than the first overall average and record the excess. Among those kept orders, take the mean of their per-order averages; keep only orders above this second mean and record that excess too
Return a single row that aggregates the orders left after both filters
Return the mean of the remaining orders' per-order averages. Do not round
Return the mean of their excess over the first overall average. Do not round
Return the mean of their excess over the second mean. Do not round

A.requirement: Compute the first overall average as the mean of the per-order averages, counting each order once

B.requirement: Compute the first overall average as the mean `remaincount` over all individual execution records, so each order is weighted by how many rows it has

readings.B: Rank districts by their share of accounts and return every district whose share reaches the 10th-highest share, including all ties at the cut.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "account"."district_id" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "account" AS "account" GROUP BY "account"."district_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "account"."district_id" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "account" AS "account" GROUP BY "account"."district_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" >= (SELECT "t"."m1" FROM "s1" AS "t" ORDER BY "t"."m1" DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 9) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from all `account` records.
Group accounts by branch district (`account.district_id`), count the accounts per district, and divide each count by the total of all district counts to get the district's share.
Output column 1: the district id (`account.district_id`).
Output column 2: the district's account count.
Output column 3: the district's share of all accounts, not rounded.
Order rows by share, highest first.
Restrict to the top 10 districts by share (how ties at 10th place are treated is the choice).

A.requirement: Return exactly 10 rows. If several districts tie at 10th place, keep only enough to reach 10, picked arbitrarily.

B.requirement: Return every district whose share is at least the 10th-highest share, so districts tied at 10th place are all included, even if that gives more than 10 rows.

requests.specific_A: Count the telescopes at each observatory (`observstation` in the telescopes table), and express each observatory's share of all telescopes as a fraction between 0 and 1 (its count ÷ the total across all observatories). Considering only the observatories whose share is above the average share across all observatories, give a single summary row with: the total number of telescopes they have, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share. Don't round.
requests.specific_B: Count the telescopes at each observatory (`observstation` in the telescopes table), and express each observatory's share of all telescopes as a percentage between 0 and 100 (100 × its count ÷ the total across all observatories). Considering only the observatories whose share is above the average share across all observatories, give a single summary row with: the total number of telescopes they have, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share. Don't round.
requests.open: For each observatory (`observstation` in the telescopes table), work out its share of all telescopes. Taking just the observatories whose share is above the average share across all observatories, give a single summary row with: their combined number of telescopes, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share. Don't round.

readings.A: Each observatory's share of all telescopes is a fraction: count ÷ total.
readings.B: Each observatory's share of all telescopes is a percentage: 100 × count ÷ total.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (100.0 * CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every row of the telescopes table and group the rows by `telescopes.observstation`. Each observatory's count is its number of telescope rows.
An observatory's share is its count divided by the total count over all observatories. The total is the sum of the per-observatory counts.
Keep only the observatories whose share is strictly greater than the average share. The average is the plain mean of the per-observatory shares across all observatories.
Combine all kept observatories into a single result row.
The sum of the telescope counts of the kept observatories.
The average share of the kept observatories.
The average of (share − average share over all observatories) across the kept observatories.
Return exactly three columns in the order output 1, output 2, output 3, with no rounding.

A.requirement: The share is a fraction between 0 and 1 (count ÷ total). This also sets the scale of output 3.

B.requirement: The share is a percentage between 0 and 100 (100 × count ÷ total). This also sets the scale of output 3.

ObservationalConditions.ObsDate: Full name: 'Observation Date'. Explanation: Local date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD). Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-08-01'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsDurHrs: Full name: 'Observation Duration (hours)'. Explanation: How long the observation lasted in hours. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '2.50'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsTime: Full name: 'Observation Time'. Explanation: Local time of the observation in HH:MM:SS. Data type: TIME. Example: '13:45:59'.
ObservationalConditions.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-PQR-9876'.
Observatories.AirTempC: Full name: 'Air Temperature (°C)'. Explanation: Ambient temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '18.45'.
Observatories.AtmosTransparency: Full name: 'Atmospheric Transparency'. Explanation: A numeric measure of how transparent the atmosphere is. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.867'.
Observatories.GeomagStatus: Full name: 'Geomagnetic Activity'. Explanation: The level of geomagnetic activity during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Active, Quiet, Storm.
Observatories.HumidityRate: Full name: 'Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Relative humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '62.300'.
Observatories.LunarDistDeg: Full name: 'Moon Distance (Degrees)'. Explanation: Angular distance to the Moon in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '97.52'.
Observatories.LunarStage: Full name: 'Lunar Phase'. Explanation: The current phase of the Moon during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: First Quarter, Full, Last Quarter, New.
Observatories.ObservStation: Full name: 'Observatory Name'. Explanation: This field holds the name or unique identifier for the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
Observatories.PressHpa: Full name: 'Pressure (hPa)'. Explanation: Atmospheric pressure in hectopascals. Data type: DECIMAL(6,1). Example: '1013.2'.
Observatories.SeeingProfile: Full name: 'Seeing Profile'. Explanation: Assessment of sky seeing conditions (atmospheric steadiness). Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
Observatories.SiderealLocal: Full name: 'Local Sidereal Time'. Explanation: Sidereal time at the observatory in HH:MM:SS format. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: '12:34:56'.
Observatories.SolarStatus: Full name: 'Solar Activity'. Explanation: The level of solar activity at the time of observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Moderate.
Observatories.WeathProfile: Full name: 'Weather Profile'. Explanation: A short description of weather conditions during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Clear, Cloudy, Partially Cloudy.
Observatories.WindSpeedMs: Full name: 'Wind Speed (m/s)'. Explanation: Wind speed in meters per second. Data type: NUMERIC(4,2). Example: '3.45'.
ResearchProcess.AnalysisPrio: Full name: 'Analysis Priority'. Explanation: Priority assigned for analyzing this signal. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, Urgent.
ResearchProcess.CollabStat: Full name: 'Collaboration Status'. Explanation: The nature of collaboration on this signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: International, Solo, Team.
ResearchProcess.DiscStat: Full name: 'Disclosure Status'. Explanation: How much information about the signal is shared publicly. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Full, None, Partial.
ResearchProcess.FollowStat: Full name: 'Follow-up Status'. Explanation: Status of any follow-up observations. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Required, Scheduled.
ResearchProcess.FundStat: Full name: 'Funding Status'. Explanation: Funding situation for further study. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Funded, Pending, Unfunded.
ResearchProcess.NotesMemo: Full name: 'Research Notes'. Explanation: Any extra remarks or context by researchers. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Project requires further funding...'
ResearchProcess.PeerRevStat: Full name: 'Peer Review Status'. Explanation: Where this signal stands in peer review. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, In Progress, Pending.
ResearchProcess.PubStat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether findings about the signal have been published. Data type: CHAR(25). Possible categories: Draft, Published, Submitted.

ResearchProcess.SecClass: Full name: 'Security Classification'. Explanation: Visibility and clearance level for the data. Data type: CHAR(35). Possible categories: Classified, Public, Restricted.

requests.specific_A: Group the members by their major id (`link_to_major`), treating members with no major as a group of their own. For each group, show the major id, the number of members, and that number as a fraction of the total members across all groups, including the no-major group. Sort by that fraction from highest to lowest and show only the top 10, without rounding.
requests.specific_B: Group the members by their major id (`link_to_major`), leaving out members who have no major. For each group, show the major id, the number of members, and that number as a fraction of the total members across those major groups only. Sort by that fraction from highest to lowest and show only the top 10, without rounding.
requests.open: Group members by their major (`link_to_major`) and show each major id, how many members it has, and that count's share of the total. List the top 10 by share, highest first, with no rounding.

readings.A: Members without a major form their own group, and they are included in the total used as the denominator.
readings.B: Members without a major are left out of both the groups and the total used as the denominator.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "member"."link_to_major" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "member" AS "member" GROUP BY "member"."link_to_major"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "member"."link_to_major" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "member" AS "member" WHERE "member"."link_to_major" IS NOT NULL GROUP BY "member"."link_to_major"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the member table and group members by their major id (`member.link_to_major`); count the members in each group (count of rows)
Combine each group row with the single overall total of the group counts
Return the major id (`link_to_major`)
Return the number of members in the group
Return the group's count divided by the sum of all group counts, unrounded
Sort by output 3 from highest to lowest
Keep only the first 10 rows

A.requirement: Members with no major (NULL `link_to_major`) form their own group, which counts toward the total and can appear in the output

B.requirement: Members with no major are left out, so they are in neither the groups nor the total

requests.specific_A: For each patient in the Laboratory table, compute their average PIC and their hemoglobin-to-hematocrit ratio, taken as the average of the `HGB`/`HCT` ratios of their individual lab records (ignoring missing values). Keep the patients whose ratio is above the average of all patients' ratios, and give one summary row for them: the average of their average PIC values, the average of their ratios, and the average amount by which their ratios exceed that all-patient average.
requests.specific_B: For each patient in the Laboratory table, compute their average PIC and their hemoglobin-to-hematocrit ratio, taken as their average `HGB` divided by their average `HCT` (ignoring missing values). Keep the patients whose ratio is above the average of all patients' ratios, and give one summary row for them: the average of their average PIC values, the average of their ratios, and the average amount by which their ratios exceed that all-patient average.
requests.open: Looking at each patient's hemoglobin-to-hematocrit (`HGB`/`HCT`) ratio from their lab records (ignoring missing values), take the patients whose ratio is above the average across all patients. Give one summary row for them: the mean of their average PIC, the mean of their ratios, and the mean amount by which their ratios exceed that cross-patient average.

readings.A: Each patient's HGB/HCT ratio is the mean of the ratios computed for each of their lab records.
readings.B: Each patient's HGB/HCT ratio is their mean HGB divided by their mean HCT.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Laboratory"."ID" AS "e", AVG("Laboratory"."PIC") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("Laboratory"."HGB" AS REAL) / "Laboratory"."HCT")) AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" GROUP BY "Laboratory"."ID"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Laboratory"."ID" AS "e", AVG("Laboratory"."PIC") AS "m1", (CAST(AVG("Laboratory"."HGB") AS REAL) / AVG("Laboratory"."HCT")) AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" GROUP BY "Laboratory"."ID"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from all Laboratory records grouped by patient ID; for each patient, compute the average PIC (ignoring missing values) and a hemoglobin-to-hematocrit ratio. Compute the cutoff as the mean of the per-patient ratios, and keep patients whose ratio is strictly greater than it
Collapse the kept patients into a single summary row
Mean of the kept patients' average PIC values
Mean of the kept patients' ratios
Mean of (patient ratio minus the all-patient mean ratio) over the kept patients; values are not rounded

A.requirement: A patient's ratio is the average of the per-record HGB/HCT ratios, ignoring missing values

B.requirement: A patient's ratio is the patient's average HGB divided by the patient's average HCT

requests.specific_A: Match each `player_college` record to `college` on exactly equal `college_id`, and leave out records whose college isn't found. For each college `state` (a blank or missing state is its own group), give the state, its number of matched records, and that number divided by the sum of the matched counts over all states, so the shares add up to 1. Don't round.
requests.specific_B: Match each `player_college` record to `college` on exactly equal `college_id`, and leave out records whose college isn't found. For each college `state` (a blank or missing state is its own group), give the state, its number of matched records, and that number divided by the total number of `player_college` records, counting every record, including those whose college isn't found. Don't round.
requests.open: Counting `player_college` records under the `state` of their college (matching on exactly equal `college_id`; records whose college isn't found don't count toward any state; a blank or missing state is its own group), how many records does each state have, and what share of the player-college records is that? Don't round.

readings.A: Each state's matched count is divided by the sum of the matched counts across all states.
readings.B: Each state's matched count is divided by the total number of `player_college` records, whether or not they match a college.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "college"."state" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "player_college" AS "player_college" INNER JOIN "college" AS "college" ON "college"."college_id" = "player_college"."college_id" GROUP BY "college"."state"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "college"."state" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "player_college" AS "player_college" INNER JOIN "college" AS "college" ON "college"."college_id" = "player_college"."college_id" GROUP BY "college"."state"), "s2" AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS "v" FROM "player_college" AS "player_college") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from `player_college` records.
Inner join to `college` where `college.college_id` = `player_college.college_id`, compared as exact text. For the per-state counts, `player_college` records with no matching college are dropped.
One row per college `state`, with a blank or missing state forming its own group. Return the state.
Number of matched records in that state (count of rows).
The state's count divided by a total, as an unrounded share. No ordering and no limit.

A.requirement: The total is the sum of the per-state matched counts. Unmatched records are excluded, so the shares add up to 1.

B.requirement: The total is the count of all `player_college` records, including those whose `college_id` has no match in `college`.

requests.specific_A: Group the compliance cases by broker reporting status (`brokrepstat`), treating cases with no status as their own group, and find each status's average model confidence (`modelconf`). For the baseline, take the mean of those per-status averages, counting each status once no matter how many cases it has. Which statuses have an average above that baseline? For each, show the status, its average model confidence, its average minus the baseline, and its average divided by the mean of the qualifying statuses' averages. Averages ignore missing values. Return nothing if either reference value is missing. Don't round.
requests.specific_B: Group the compliance cases by broker reporting status (`brokrepstat`), treating cases with no status as their own group, and find each status's average model confidence (`modelconf`). For the baseline, take the average model confidence computed directly over every individual compliance case, so statuses with more cases weigh more. Which statuses have an average above that baseline? For each, show the status, its average model confidence, its average minus the baseline, and its average divided by the mean of the qualifying statuses' averages. Averages ignore missing values. Return nothing if either reference value is missing. Don't round.
requests.open: Which broker reporting statuses (`brokrepstat`) have above-average model confidence (`modelconf`)? Treat cases with no status as their own status. For each one, show the status, its average model confidence, how far above average it is, and its average divided by the mean of the qualifying statuses' averages. Ignore missing values when averaging, return nothing if a reference value is missing, and don't round.

readings.A: A status qualifies if its average model confidence exceeds the mean of all the status-level averages, with each status weighted equally.
readings.B: A status qualifies if its average model confidence exceeds the average model confidence taken over every individual compliance case.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "compliancecase"."brokrepstat" AS "g", AVG("compliancecase"."modelconf") AS "m1" FROM "compliancecase" AS "compliancecase" GROUP BY "compliancecase"."brokrepstat"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "compliancecase"."brokrepstat" AS "g", AVG("compliancecase"."modelconf") AS "m1" FROM "compliancecase" AS "compliancecase" GROUP BY "compliancecase"."brokrepstat"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("compliancecase"."modelconf") AS "v" FROM "compliancecase" AS "compliancecase"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL)

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from all compliance cases (`compliancecase`) and group them by broker reporting status (`brokrepstat`). Cases with no status form their own group. Each group gets the average model confidence (`modelconf`), ignoring missing values.
Compare each status's average with a single baseline value. Return nothing if the baseline is missing. Keep only statuses whose average is strictly greater than the baseline.
Column 1 is the broker reporting status.
Column 2 is that status's average model confidence.
Column 3 is the status's average minus the baseline.
Column 4 is the status's average divided by the unweighted mean of the kept statuses' averages. Return nothing if that mean is missing.
Output columns are in the order status, average, difference, ratio. No rounding and no ordering are specified.

A.requirement: The baseline is the unweighted mean of the per-status averages, with each status counting equally.

B.requirement: The baseline is the average model confidence computed directly over all individual compliance cases, so statuses with more cases weigh more.

requests.specific_A: For each media type (`Track.MediaTypeId`), across all tracks, work out the average track `UnitPrice` and the average of each track's `Bytes` divided by its `Milliseconds` (tracks with no size ignored). Take the simple average of that byte rate across the media types, and keep only the media types whose rate is above it. requests.specific_A: Matching each attendance record to its member by member id (dropping attendance with no matching member), count the attendance records for each member id and `position` combination, and work out each count as a share of the total of all these counts. List the member id, position, attendance count and share, sorted by share from highest to lowest, and return exactly 10 rows. If there is a tie at 10th place, keep only as many of the tied rows as fit, chosen arbitrarily.
requests.specific_B: Matching each attendance record to its member by member id (dropping attendance with no matching member), count the attendance records for each member id and `position` combination, and work out each count as a share of the total of all these counts. List the member id, position, attendance count and share, sorted by share from highest to lowest, and return the top 10 rows, plus any further rows whose share equals that of the 10th row.
requests.open: Which are the top 10 members by share of total event attendance? Match attendance to members by member id, count attendance per member id and position, and show the member id, position, attendance count and share of all attendance, from highest share to lowest.

readings.A: Rank member/position groups by their share of all attendance and return exactly 10 rows, cutting arbitrarily through any tie at 10th place.
readings.B: Rank member/position groups by their share of all attendance and return the top 10 plus every row tied with the 10th row's share.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "attendance"."link_to_member" AS "e", "member"."position" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "attendance" AS "attendance" INNER JOIN "member" AS "member" ON "member"."member_id" = "attendance"."link_to_member" GROUP BY "attendance"."link_to_member", "member"."position"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "attendance"."link_to_member" AS "e", "member"."position" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "attendance" AS "attendance" INNER JOIN "member" AS "member" ON "member"."member_id" = "attendance"."link_to_member" GROUP BY "attendance"."link_to_member", "member"."position"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" >= (SELECT "x"."m1" FROM "s1" AS "x" ORDER BY "x"."m1" DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 9) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from attendance records; each attendance record is one counted unit
Inner-join attendance to member on member.member_id = attendance.link_to_member; attendance rows with no matching member are dropped
Group by attendance.link_to_member and member.position; first output column is the member id (attendance.link_to_member)
Second output column is the member's position (member.position)
Third output column is the number of attendance records in the group
Fourth output column is the group's count divided by the sum of all group counts (share of all attendance), not rounded
Order rows by the share, highest first (missing shares last)
Keep the top 10 rows by share

A.requirement: Return exactly 10 rows. If several rows tie at 10th place, keep only enough of them to reach 10 and pick those arbitrarily

B.requirement: Return the top 10 rows plus every other row whose share equals the 10th row's share

requests.specific_A: For each circuit (`races.circuitId`), give the average `round` of its races, its number of races, and its share of all races (its count divided by the total number of races across all circuits), sorted by share from highest to lowest, and return exactly the first 10 rows, picking arbitrarily among circuits tied at 10th place.
requests.specific_B: For each circuit (`races.circuitId`), give the average `round` of its races, its number of races, and its share of all races (its count divided by the total number of races across all circuits), sorted by share from highest to lowest, and return the top 10 by share, also including any circuits tied with the 10th one.
requests.open: What are the 10 circuits with the largest share of all races? For each, show the circuit Id (`races.circuitId`), the average `round` of its races, its number of races, and its share (its count divided by the total number of races across all circuits), largest share first.

readings.A: Order circuits by their share of all races and return exactly 10, cutting through any tie at 10th place arbitrarily.
readings.B: Order circuits by their share of all races and return every circuit whose share is at least the 10th-highest, including all circuits tied with the 10th one.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "races"."circuitId" AS "e", AVG("races"."round") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "races" AS "races" GROUP BY "races"."circuitId"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "races"."circuitId" AS "e", AVG("races"."round") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "races" AS "races" GROUP BY "races"."circuitId"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" >= (SELECT MIN("t"."m2") FROM (SELECT "s1x"."m2" AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1x" ORDER BY "s1x"."m2" DESC LIMIT 10) AS "t") ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every `races` record and group by circuit Id (`races.circuitId`)
Compute each circuit's share by dividing its race count by the total race count summed over all circuits (the single total is attached to every circuit row)
Return the circuit Id (`races.circuitId`)
Return the average round number (`races.round`) of the circuit's races, ignoring missing values, not rounded
Return the circuit's race count
Return the circuit's share of all races (count ÷ total, not rounded)
Order by share, highest first
Cut off at the top 10 positions by share

A.requirement: Return exactly 10 rows; if circuits tie at 10th place, pick among them arbitrarily

B.requirement: Return every circuit whose race count is at least the 10th-highest count, so circuits tied with the 10th one are also included

requests.specific_A: Match each budget line to its event (`budget.link_to_event` = `event.event_id`, dropping lines with no matching event). Including lines where `spent` is 0, give the following for each event `type`: the average ratio of `spent` to `amount` across its budget lines (ignoring missing values), and how far that average is from the mean of the per-type averages.
requests.specific_B: Match each budget line to its event (`budget.link_to_event` = `event.event_id`, dropping lines with no matching event). Leaving out lines where `spent` is 0, give the following for each event `type`: the average ratio of `spent` to `amount` across its budget lines (ignoring missing values), and how far that average is from the mean of the per-type averages.
requests.open: For each event type (`event.type`), matching budget lines to their events through `budget.link_to_event`, what is the average spent-to-budgeted ratio (`spent` / `amount`) across its budget lines, ignoring missing values? Also show how far each type's average is from the mean of the per-type averages.

readings.A: Budget lines with zero spent are real spending data and are included in the ratio averages.
readings.B: Budget lines with zero spent are treated as not yet recorded and are excluded before averaging.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "event"."type" AS "g", AVG((CAST("budget"."spent" AS REAL) / "budget"."amount")) AS "m1" FROM "budget" AS "budget" INNER JOIN "event" AS "event" ON "event"."event_id" = "budget"."link_to_event" GROUP BY "event"."type"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "event"."type" AS "g", AVG((CAST("budget"."spent" AS REAL) / "budget"."amount")) AS "m1" FROM "budget" AS "budget" INNER JOIN "event" AS "event" ON "event"."event_id" = "budget"."link_to_event" WHERE "budget"."spent" <> 0 GROUP BY "event"."type"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)

shared_requirements.requirement: Use each budget line.
Match each budget line to its event on `event.event_id` = `budget.link_to_event` (an inner join, so lines with no matching event are dropped), then group by `event.type`.
The event type.
The average of `spent` ÷ `amount` over the type's budget lines, ignoring missing values.
That type's average minus the mean of all the per-type averages, where each type counts once.

A.requirement: Keep the budget lines where `spent` = 0; they count as a real ratio of 0.

B.requirement: Leave out the budget lines where `spent` = 0, treating them as 'nothing recorded yet'.
