requests.specific_A: Take every order id that appears in `Invoices` (only orders with at least one invoice; orders without invoices are not included) and count its invoices. Give each such order a share: its invoice count divided by the total invoice count across those orders. Average the shares over those same invoiced orders only. For the orders whose share is strictly above that average, return one unrounded row with: their total number of invoices, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share.
requests.specific_B: Take every order in `Orders`, including orders with no invoice (which get a count of 0), and count its invoices. Give each such order a share: its invoice count divided by the total invoice count across those orders. Average the shares over all of those orders, the zero-invoice ones included. For the orders whose share is strictly above that average, return one unrounded row with: their total number of invoices, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share.
requests.open: For each order, count its invoices and work out its share of all invoices (its count divided by the total). For the orders whose share is strictly above the average share, give one unrounded row with: their total number of invoices, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share.

readings.A: Only orders that have at least one invoice are included.
readings.B: All orders in Orders are included, and orders with no invoice count as 0.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Invoices"."order_id" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "Invoices" AS "Invoices" GROUP BY "Invoices"."order_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Orders"."order_id" AS "e", COUNT("Invoices"."invoice_number") AS "m1" FROM "Orders" AS "Orders" LEFT JOIN "Invoices" AS "Invoices" ON "Invoices"."order_id" = "Orders"."order_id" GROUP BY "Orders"."order_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

requests.specific_A: Join transactions to their accounts and accounts to their districts, dropping anything unmatched. For each account and region (`district.A3`), compute two values: (a) the average transaction amount over credits and withdrawals only (`trans.type` 'PRIJEM' or 'VYDAJ'; other types ignored), with credits counted as positive and withdrawals as negative; and (b) the average balance after transaction (`trans.balance`) over all of the account's transactions. Then, for each region, take the plain average of these per-account values. Return each region with its average of the account amount averages, its average of the account balance averages, and the ratio of the first to the plain mean of that first value across all regions (return nothing if that overall mean is missing). No rounding, any order.
requests.specific_B: Join transactions to their accounts and accounts to their districts, dropping anything unmatched. For each account and region (`district.A3`), compute two values: (a) the average transaction amount over credits and withdrawals only (`trans.type` 'PRIJEM' or 'VYDAJ'; other types ignored), using the stored unsigned `amount` for both; and (b) the average balance after transaction (`trans.balance`) over all of the account's transactions. Then, for each region, take the plain average of these per-account values. Return each region with its average of the account amount averages, its average of the account balance averages, and the ratio of the first to the plain mean of that first value across all regions (return nothing if that overall mean is missing). No rounding, any order.
requests.open: By region (`district.A3`), using only transactions whose account and district exist: for each account, find its average transaction amount over its credit and withdrawal transactions ('PRIJEM' and 'VYDAJ' only, other types ignored), and its average balance after transaction over all of its transactions. Then take the simple average of both figures across the region's accounts. List each region with these two averages, plus the region's amount average divided by the simple mean of all regions' amount averages (no rows if that mean can't be computed). Any order, no rounding.

readings.A: Withdrawal (VYDAJ) amounts are negated before averaging, so the average is a signed net figure.
readings.B: The stored unsigned amount is averaged as-is for both credits and withdrawals.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "trans"."account_id" AS "e", "district"."A3" AS "g", AVG(CASE WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('PRIJEM') THEN "trans"."amount" WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('VYDAJ') THEN (0 - "trans"."amount") END) AS "m1", AVG("trans"."balance") AS "m2" FROM "trans" AS "trans" INNER JOIN "account" AS "account" ON "account"."account_id" = "trans"."account_id" INNER JOIN "district" AS "district" ON "district"."district_id" = "account"."district_id" GROUP BY "trans"."account_id", "district"."A3"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT AVG("s2"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s2" AS "s2") SELECT "s2"."g" AS "g", "s2"."m1" AS "m1", "s2"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s2"."m1" AS REAL) / "s3"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s2" AS "s2" INNER JOIN "s3" AS "s3" ON NOT ("s3"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "trans"."account_id" AS "e", "district"."A3" AS "g", AVG(CASE WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('PRIJEM') THEN "trans"."amount" WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('VYDAJ') THEN "trans"."amount" END) AS "m1", AVG("trans"."balance") AS "m2" FROM "trans" AS "trans" INNER JOIN "account" AS "account" ON "account"."account_id" = "trans"."account_id" INNER JOIN "district" AS "district" ON "district"."district_id" = "account"."district_id" GROUP BY "trans"."account_id", "district"."A3"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT AVG("s2"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s2" AS "s2") SELECT "s2"."g" AS "g", "s2"."m1" AS "m1", "s2"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s2"."m1" AS REAL) / "s3"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s2" AS "s2" INNER JOIN "s3" AS "s3" ON NOT ("s3"."v" IS NULL)

player id (`batting_postseason.player_id`)

the player's average postseason doubles (`double`) per record; missing values ignored
relative doubles index = the player's average doubles ÷ the overall average of all per-player averages (an unweighted mean over player groups); computed only when that overall average is not missing

requests.specific_A: Using transactions joined to their account (drop transactions with no matching account), group by account number (`trans.account_id`) and statement issuance frequency (`account.frequency`). For each group, compute the average transaction amount where credits (`trans.type` = 'PRIJEM') count as positive `amount`, withdrawals ('VYDAJ') count as negative `amount`, and transactions of any other type are left out. Then, for each frequency, take the plain average of these per-account averages. Return the account number, the frequency, the account's average, and the ratio of the account's average to its frequency's average. Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest, with missing ratios last, and keep the top 10 rows. Don't round anything.
requests.specific_B: Using transactions joined to their account (drop transactions with no matching account), group by account number (`trans.account_id`) and statement issuance frequency (`account.frequency`). For each group, compute the plain average of the stored `amount` over all of the group's transactions, regardless of type. Then, for each frequency, take the plain average of these per-account averages. Return the account number, the frequency, the account's average, and the ratio of the account's average to its frequency's average. Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest, with missing ratios last, and keep the top 10 rows. Don't round anything.
requests.open: For transactions that belong to an existing account, find each account's average transaction amount, grouped by account number and statement issuance frequency (`account.frequency`). Then compare each account with the others of the same frequency: divide its average by the plain mean of the per-account averages for that frequency. Show the account number, the frequency, the account's average and that ratio. Give the top 10 by ratio (highest first, any missing ratio last), unrounded.

readings.A: Each account's average counts credits as positive and withdrawals as negative. Transactions of other types are ignored.
readings.B: Each account's average is the plain mean of the stored unsigned trans.amount over all of its transactions.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "trans"."account_id" AS "e", "account"."frequency" AS "g", AVG(CASE WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('PRIJEM') THEN "trans"."amount" WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('VYDAJ') THEN (0 - "trans"."amount") END) AS "m1" FROM "trans" AS "trans" INNER JOIN "account" AS "account" ON "account"."account_id" = "trans"."account_id" GROUP BY "trans"."account_id", "account"."frequency"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g" ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "trans"."account_id" AS "e", "account"."frequency" AS "g", AVG("trans"."amount") AS "m1" FROM "trans" AS "trans" INNER JOIN "account" AS "account" ON "account"."account_id" = "trans"."account_id" GROUP BY "trans"."account_id", "account"."frequency"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g" ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

Inner-join each transaction to its account on `account.account_id` = `trans.account_id`. Drop transactions with no matching account.
Group by `trans.account_id` and `account.frequency`. Output the account number (`trans.account_id`).
Output the statement issuance frequency (`account.frequency`).
Output the per-account average amount, defined by the choice. Values are not rounded.
For each frequency, take the plain (unweighted) mean of the per-account averages. Output the account's average divided by its frequency's mean. Values are not rounded.
Sort by the ratio, highest first. Missing ratios go last.
Keep only the first 10 rows.

B.requirement: Average the stored unsigned `amount` over all of the account's transactions, whatever their type.

Ignore missing values. Then take the simple average of that area-to-volume figure across all funding sources. List only the funding sources whose figure is above that average. Show the funding source, the average Y-vs-X difference, the area-to-volume figure, and how far the figure is above the cross-source average, with no rounding.
requests.open: Using the spatial records (`scanspatial`) whose `arcref` matches a project's `arcregistry` and dropping any that don't match, look at each funding source (`projects.fundflux`). For each one, give the average relative difference between `boxy` and `boxx`, computed per record as (`boxy` − `boxx`) ÷ `boxx`, and give its area-to-volume ratio (`aream2` to `volm3`). Ignore missing values. Which funding sources have a ratio above the simple average of that ratio across all funding sources? Show the funding source, the average Y-vs-X difference, the ratio, and how far the ratio is above that average, with no rounding.

readings.A: A funding source's area-to-volume figure is the mean of each spatial record's area ÷ volume.
readings.B: A funding source's area-to-volume figure is its summed area divided by its summed volume.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "projects"."fundflux" AS "g", AVG((CAST(("scanspatial"."boxy" - "scanspatial"."boxx") AS REAL) / "scanspatial"."boxx")) AS "m1", AVG((CAST("scanspatial"."aream2" AS REAL) / "scanspatial"."volm3")) AS "m2" FROM "scanspatial" AS "scanspatial" INNER JOIN "projects" AS "projects" ON "projects"."arcregistry" = "scanspatial"."arcref" GROUP BY "projects"."fundflux"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "projects"."fundflux" AS "g", AVG((CAST(("scanspatial"."boxy" - "scanspatial"."boxx") AS REAL) / "scanspatial"."boxx")) AS "m1", (CAST(SUM("scanspatial"."aream2") AS REAL) / SUM("scanspatial"."volm3")) AS "m2" FROM "scanspatial" AS "scanspatial" INNER JOIN "projects" AS "projects" ON "projects"."arcregistry" = "scanspatial"."arcref" GROUP BY "projects"."fundflux"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the spatial records (`scanspatial`).

Match each spatial record to its project where `projects.arcregistry` = `scanspatial.arcref`. This is an inner join, so spatial records with no matching project are dropped. Group the matched records by funding source (`projects.fundflux`).
First column: the funding source (`projects.fundflux`).
Second column: the average over the funding source's records of each record's (`boxy` − `boxx`) ÷ `boxx`. Missing values are ignored.
Take the plain (unweighted) average of the funding sources' area-to-volume figures across all funding sources. Keep only the funding sources whose figure is strictly greater than that average.
Fourth column: the funding source's area-to-volume figure minus the cross-source average. No rounding, and no ordering is required.

A.requirement: Third column: the area-to-volume figure, computed as the average over the funding source's records of each record's `aream2` ÷ `volm3`. Missing values are ignored.

B.requirement: Third column: the area-to-volume figure, computed as the funding source's total `aream2` divided by its total `volm3`. Missing values are ignored.

Equipment.EquipDesign: Full name: 'Equipment Model'. Explanation: Model name or identifier. Data type: VARCHAR(14). Example: 'Model-669'.

requests.specific_A: Match attendance entries to their events (drop entries with no matching event). For each event `status`, show the status, the total number of attendance entries for events with that status (a member who attended three such events adds three), and that number divided by the sum of these per-status numbers over all statuses. Do not round.
requests.specific_B: Match attendance entries to their events (drop entries with no matching event). For each event `status`, show the status, the number of different members who attended at least one event with that status (a member who attended three such events adds one), and that number divided by the sum of these per-status numbers over all statuses. Do not round.
requests.open: Taking attendance entries that match an event (others left out), how many attendees does each event `status` have, and what share of the total across all statuses is that? Show the status, its number of attendees, and the share, without rounding.

readings.A: A status's attendance is the total number of member-event attendance entries for events with that status.
readings.B: A status's attendance is the number of different members who attended any event with that status.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "attendance"."link_to_event" AS "e", "event"."status" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "attendance" AS "attendance" INNER JOIN "event" AS "event" ON "event"."event_id" = "attendance"."link_to_event" GROUP BY "attendance"."link_to_event", "event"."status"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", SUM("s1"."m1") AS "m1" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT SUM("s2"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s2" AS "s2") SELECT "s2"."g" AS "g", "s2"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s2"."m1" AS REAL) / "s3"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s2" AS "s2" INNER JOIN "s3" AS "s3" ON NOT ("s3"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT MIN("attendance"."link_to_event") AS "e", "event"."status" AS "g", COUNT(DISTINCT "attendance"."link_to_member") AS "m1" FROM "attendance" AS "attendance" INNER JOIN "event" AS "event" ON "event"."event_id" = "attendance"."link_to_event" GROUP BY "event"."status"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", SUM("s1"."m1") AS "m1" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT SUM("s2"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s2" AS "s2") SELECT "s2"."g" AS "g", "s2"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s2"."m1" AS REAL) / "s3"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s2" AS "s2" INNER JOIN "s3" AS "s3" ON NOT ("s3"."v" IS NULL)

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from attendance entries (`attendance` records).
Match each attendance entry to its event where `event.event_id` = `attendance.link_to_event` (an inner join, so unmatched entries are dropped). Group by event `status`, giving one row per status.
Column 1: the event status.
Column 2: the attendance figure for that status. How attendance is counted is the choice.
Column 3: the status's attendance figure divided by the sum of the attendance figures over all statuses. No rounding, no ordering and no limit apply to any column.

A.requirement: Count attendance entries, one per member-event pair. A member who attended three events with that status counts three times.

B.requirement: Count distinct members who attended at least one event with that status. A member who attended three events with that status counts once, but can still count again under another status.

context.schema:
CREATE TABLE event
(
    event_id   TEXT
        constraint event_pk
            primary key,
    event_name TEXT,
    event_date TEXT,
    type       TEXT,
    notes      TEXT,
    location   TEXT,
    status     TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE major
(
    major_id   TEXT
        constraint major_pk
            primary key,
    major_name TEXT,
    department TEXT,
    college    TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE zip_code
(
    zip_code    INTEGER
        constraint zip_code_pk
            primary key,
    type        TEXT,
    city        TEXT,
    county      TEXT,
    state       TEXT,
    short_state TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "attendance"
(
    link_to_event  TEXT,
    link_to_member TEXT,
    primary key (link_to_event, link_to_member),
    foreign key (link_to_event) references event(event_id),
    foreign key (link_to_member) references member(member_id)
);
CREATE TABLE "budget"
(
    budget_id     TEXT
            primary key,
    category      TEXT,
    spent         REAL,
    remaining     REAL,
    amount        INTEGER,
    event_status  TEXT,
    link_to_event TEXT,
    foreign key (link_to_event) references event(event_id)
);
CREATE TABLE "expense"
(
    expense_id          TEXT
            primary key,
    expense_description TEXT,
    expense_date        TEXT,
    cost                REAL,
    approved            TEXT,
    link_to_member      TEXT,
    link_to_budget      TEXT,
    foreign key (link_to_budget) references budget(budget_id),
    foreign key (link_to_member) references member(member_id)
);
CREATE TABLE "income"
(
    income_id      TEXT
        constraint income_pk
            primary key,
    date_received  TEXT,
    amount         INTEGER,
    source         TEXT,
    notes          TEXT,
    link_to_member TEXT,
    foreign key (link_to_member) references member(member_id)
);
CREATE TABLE "member"
(
    member_id     TEXT
        constraint member_pk
            primary key,
    first_name    TEXT,
    last_name     TEXT,
    email         TEXT,
    position      TEXT,
    t_shirt_size  TEXT,
    phone         TEXT,
    zip           INTEGER,
    link_to_major TEXT,
    foreign key (link_to_major) references major(major_id),
    foreign key (zip) references zip_code(zip_code)
);

requests.specific_A: Match each conservation record to its site by site code, and drop records with no matching site. Under each site health and safety status (`healtheval`), with a missing status as its own group, count every conservation record, so a site with several records counts once per record. Work out each status's share of the sum of those counts. Then take only the statuses whose share is above the average share across all statuses, and return one summary row with the average count, the average share, and the average amount by which the share exceeds the average share. Don't round.
requests.specific_B: Match each conservation record to its site by site code, and drop records with no matching site. Under each site health and safety status (`healtheval`), with a missing status as its own group, count the number of different sites (distinct `zoneref`) that have at least one conservation record, so a site with several records counts only once. Work out each status's share of the sum of those counts. Then take only the statuses whose share is above the average share across all statuses, and return one summary row with the average count, the average share, and the average amount by which the share exceeds the average share. Don't round.
requests.open: Match the conservation records to their sites by site code, and drop any with no matching site. How much does each site health and safety status (`healtheval`) account for in the conservation data? Treat a missing status as its own group, and give a count and that count's share of the sum. Then take only the statuses with an above-average share, and return one summary row with the average count, the average share, and the average amount by which the share exceeds the average share. Don't round.

readings.A: Each status's count is the number of conservation records.
readings.B: Each status's count is the number of distinct sites that have conservation records.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "sites"."healtheval" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "scanconservation" AS "scanconservation" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scanconservation"."zoneref" GROUP BY "sites"."healtheval"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "sites"."healtheval" AS "g", COUNT(DISTINCT "scanconservation"."zoneref") AS "m1" FROM "scanconservation" AS "scanconservation" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scanconservation"."zoneref" GROUP BY "sites"."healtheval"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the conservation records (`scanconservation`). Match each one to its site where `sites.zoneregistry` equals `zoneref`, and drop records with no matching site. Group by the site's health and safety status (`healtheval`), with a missing status forming its own group. Each status's share is its count divided by the sum of the counts across all statuses. Keep only the statuses whose share is strictly greater than the average share across all statuses.
Return a single row of averages taken over the kept statuses.
The average share.
The average excess of the share over the average share. Do not round any output.

A.requirement: The average count, where a status's count is the number of matched conservation records, so a site with several records counts several times.

B.requirement: The average count, where a status's count is the number of distinct sites (`zoneref`) that have at least one conservation record.

requests.specific_A: For each order id in `Order_Items`, compute the order's average `product_quantity` (ignoring missing values). Then compute a baseline by averaging those per-order averages, so each order counts once no matter how many items it has (ignoring missing ones). Return rows only if this baseline exists. List the order id, the order's average quantity, and the order's average minus the baseline. Sort by that difference from largest to smallest, with missing differences last, and keep the top 10.
requests.specific_B: For each order id in `Order_Items`, compute the order's average `product_quantity` (ignoring missing values). Then compute a baseline by averaging `product_quantity` directly over all individual order-item rows, so each item counts once and orders with more items weigh more (ignoring missing values). Return rows only if this baseline exists. List the order id, the order's average quantity, and the order's average minus the baseline. Sort by that difference from largest to smallest, with missing differences last, and keep the top 10.
requests.open: For each order in `Order_Items`, how does its average `product_quantity` (ignoring missing values) compare with the overall average quantity? Show the order id, the order's average quantity, and the order's average minus the overall average, with results only if the overall average exists. Sort by the difference from largest to smallest, with missing differences last, and keep the top 10.

readings.A: The baseline is the average of the per-order average quantities.
readings.B: The baseline is the average quantity over all individual order items.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Order_Items"."order_id" AS "e", AVG("Order_Items"."product_quantity") AS "m1" FROM "Order_Items" AS "Order_Items" GROUP BY "Order_Items"."order_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Order_Items"."order_id" AS "e", AVG("Order_Items"."product_quantity") AS "m1" FROM "Order_Items" AS "Order_Items" GROUP BY "Order_Items"."order_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("Order_Items"."product_quantity") AS "v" FROM "Order_Items" AS "Order_Items") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every Order_Items record, group by order_id, and compute each order's average product_quantity (missing values ignored)
Pair every order row with the single baseline average, and return rows only when the baseline exists
order id
the order's average quantity
sort by output 3 descending, missing values last
keep the first 10 rows

A.requirement: order average minus the baseline, where the baseline is the mean of the per-order averages (each order weighted equally)

B.requirement: order average minus the baseline, where the baseline is the mean product_quantity over all order-item rows (each item weighted equally)

requests.specific_A: Match each telescope to its observatory on `observstation`, and drop telescopes without a matching observatory. For each moon phase (`observatories.lunarstage`; a missing phase is its own group), return four columns. First, the phase. Second, the average bandwidth usage (`telescopes.bandusagepct`), computed by averaging per observatory station first and then averaging those station averages (missing values ignored). Third, the number of telescopes in that phase. Fourth, that count as a fraction of the total number of telescopes across all phases. Don't round.
requests.specific_B: Match each telescope to its observatory on `observstation`, and drop telescopes without a matching observatory. For each moon phase (`observatories.lunarstage`; a missing phase is its own group), return four columns. First, the phase. Second, the average bandwidth usage (`telescopes.bandusagepct`), computed by averaging per observatory station first and then averaging those station averages (missing values ignored). Third, the number of observatory stations in that phase. Fourth, that count as a fraction of the total number of observatory stations across all phases. Don't round.
requests.open: Match each telescope to its observatory on `observstation`, and drop telescopes without a match. For each moon phase (`observatories.lunarstage`; a missing phase is its own group), show four things. First, the phase. Second, the average bandwidth usage (`telescopes.bandusagepct`), averaging per station first and then across stations (missing values ignored). Third, how many there are with that phase. Fourth, what share of the overall total that is. Don't round.

readings.A: For each moon phase, count the telescopes, and give each phase's share of the total number of telescopes.
readings.B: For each moon phase, count the observatory stations, and give each phase's share of the total number of stations.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", "observatories"."lunarstage" AS "g", AVG("telescopes"."bandusagepct") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" INNER JOIN "observatories" AS "observatories" ON "observatories"."observstation" = "telescopes"."observstation" GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation", "observatories"."lunarstage"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", SUM("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT SUM("s2"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s2" AS "s2") SELECT "s2"."g" AS "g", "s2"."m1" AS "m1", "s2"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s2"."m2" AS REAL) / "s3"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s2" AS "s2" INNER JOIN "s3" AS "s3" ON NOT ("s3"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", "observatories"."lunarstage" AS "g", AVG("telescopes"."bandusagepct") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" INNER JOIN "observatories" AS "observatories" ON "observatories"."observstation" = "telescopes"."observstation" GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation", "observatories"."lunarstage"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT SUM("s2"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s2" AS "s2") SELECT "s2"."g" AS "g", "s2"."m1" AS "m1", "s2"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s2"."m2" AS REAL) / "s3"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s2" AS "s2" INNER JOIN "s3" AS "s3" ON NOT ("s3"."v" IS NULL)

shared_requirements.requirement: Match each telescope to its observatory where `telescopes.observstation` equals `observatories.observstation` (exact text match). Drop telescopes that have no matching observatory.
Group by moon phase (`observatories.lunarstage`), with a missing phase forming its own group. Return one row per phase.
Column 1: the moon phase.
Column 2: the average bandwidth usage (`telescopes.bandusagepct`). First average it per observatory station within the phase (missing values ignored), then average those station averages.
Column 4: column 3 divided by the total of column 3 across all phases. No rounding.

A.requirement: Column 3: the number of telescopes in the phase (joined rows).
The share uses telescope counts, divided by the total number of telescopes.

B.requirement: Column 3: the number of observatory stations in the phase.
The share uses station counts, divided by the total number of stations.

context.documentation:
ObservationalConditions.ObsDate: Full name: 'Observation Date'. Explanation: Local date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD). Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-08-01'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsDurHrs: Full name: 'Observation Duration (hours)'. Explanation: How long the observation lasted in hours. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '2.50'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsTime: Full name: 'Observation Time'. Explanation: Local time of the observation in HH:MM:SS. Data type: TIME. Example: '13:45:59'.
ObservationalConditions.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-PQR-9876'.
Observatories.AirTempC: Full name: 'Air Temperature (°C)'. Explanation: Ambient temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '18.45'.
Observatories.AtmosTransparency: Full name: 'Atmospheric Transparency'. Explanation: A numeric measure of how transparent the atmosphere is. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.867'.
Observatories.GeomagStatus: Full name: 'Geomagnetic Activity'. Explanation: The level of geomagnetic activity during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Active, Quiet, Storm.
Observatories.HumidityRate: Full name: 'Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Relative humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '62.300'.
Observatories.LunarDistDeg: Full name: 'Moon Distance (Degrees)'. Explanation: Angular distance to the Moon in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '97.52'.
Observatories.LunarStage: Full name: 'Lunar Phase'. Explanation: The current phase of the Moon during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: First Quarter, Full, Last Quarter, New.
Observatories.ObservStation: Full name: 'Observatory Name'. Explanation: This field holds the name or unique identifier for the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
Observatories.PressHpa: Full name: 'Pressure (hPa)'. Explanation: Atmospheric pressure in hectopascals. Data type: DECIMAL(6,1). Example: '1013.2'.
Observatories.SeeingProfile: Full name: 'Seeing Profile'. Explanation: Assessment of sky seeing conditions (atmospheric steadiness). Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
Observatories.SiderealLocal: Full name: 'Local Sidereal Time'. Explanation: Sidereal time at the observatory in HH:MM:SS format. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: '12:34:56'.
Observatories.SolarStatus: Full name: 'Solar Activity'. Explanation: The level of solar activity at the time of observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Moderate.
Observatories.WeathProfile: Full name: 'Weather Profile'. Explanation: A short description of weather conditions during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Clear, Cloudy, Partially Cloudy.
Observatories.WindSpeedMs: Full name: 'Wind Speed (m/s)'. Explanation: Wind speed in meters per second. Data type: NUMERIC(4,2). Example: '3.45'.
ResearchProcess.AnalysisPrio: Full name: 'Analysis Priority'. Explanation: Priority assigned for analyzing this signal. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, Urgent.
ResearchProcess.CollabStat: Full name: 'Collaboration Status'. Explanation: The nature of collaboration on this signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: International, Solo, Team.
ResearchProcess.DiscStat: Full name: 'Disclosure Status'. Explanation: How much information about the signal is shared publicly. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Full, None, Partial.
ResearchProcess.FollowStat: Full name: 'Follow-up Status'. Explanation: Status of any follow-up observations. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Required, Scheduled.
ResearchProcess.FundStat: Full name: 'Funding Status'. Explanation: Funding situation for further study. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Funded, Pending, Unfunded.
ResearchProcess.NotesMemo: Full name: 'Research Notes'. Explanation: Any extra remarks or context by researchers. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Project requires further funding...'
ResearchProcess.PeerRevStat: Full name: 'Peer Review Status'. Explanation: Where this signal stands in peer review. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, In Progress, Pending.
ResearchProcess.PubStat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether findings about the signal have been published. Data type: CHAR(25). Possible categories: Draft, Published, Submitted.
ResearchProcess.ResPrio: Full name: 'Research Priority'. Explanation: How urgently this signal needs scientific attention. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium.
ResearchProcess.SecClass: Full name: 'Security Classification'. Explanation: Visibility and clearance level for the data. Data type: CHAR(35). Possible categories: Classified, Public, Restricted.
ResearchProcess.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-MNO-7890'.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.CultSig: Full name: 'Cultural Significance'. Explanation: The level of cultural impact or interest. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: High, Low, None.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.EncryptEvid: Full name: 'Encryption Evidence'. Explanation: Whether there is indication the signal is encrypted. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: None, Possible, Strong.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.GravLens: Full name: 'Gravitational Lensing'. Explanation: Whether the signal is affected by gravitational lensing. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: None, Strong, Weak.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.InterMedEffects: Full name: 'Interstellar Medium Effects'. Explanation: Impact of interstellar medium on the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.LangStruct: Full name: 'Language Structure'. Explanation: Presence of linguistic or structured patterns. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Complex, None, Simple.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.MsgContent: Full name: 'Message Content'. Explanation: Indicates whether an actual message was detected. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Identified, None, Possible.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.QuantEffects: Full name: 'Quantum Effects'. Explanation: Quantum-level phenomena observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(85). Possible categories: None, Observed, Significant.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SciImpact: Full name: 'Scientific Impact'. Explanation: Significance of the signal to scientific research. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Major, Minor, Moderate.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-ABC-1234'.
SignalClassification.ClassConf: Full name: 'Classification Confidence (%)'. Explanation: How confident we are in the assigned signal class. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '92.50'.
SignalClassification.ComplexIdx: Full name: 'Complexity Index'. Explanation: Numeric measure of the signal’s complexity. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '5.678'.
SignalClassification.EntropyVal: Full name: 'Entropy'. Explanation: Entropy measurement of the signal. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.45'.
SignalClassification.InfoDense: Full name: 'Information Density'. Explanation: Estimated information per unit time/frequency. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.345'.
SignalClassification.PeriodSec: Full name: 'Period (s)'. Explanation: Duration of each cycle if periodic. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '12.345'.
SignalClassification.RepeatCount: Full name: 'Repetition Count'. Explanation: Number of times the signal has repeated. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '3'.
SignalClassification.SigClassType: Full name: 'Classification Type'. Explanation: High-level category for the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Artificial, Candidate, Natural, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SigPattern: Full name: 'Signal Pattern'. Explanation: Pattern observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: Periodic, Random, Structured, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-DEF-5678'.
SignalDecoding.AnalysisDp: Full name: 'Analysis Depth'. Explanation: How thoroughly the signal was analyzed. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Comprehensive, Detailed, Preliminary.
SignalDecoding.CompResources: Full name: 'Computational Resources'. Explanation: Level of computing power used. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Extreme, High, Low, Medium.
SignalDecoding.CompressRatio: Full name: 'Compression Ratio'. Explanation: Factor by which the raw signal data was compressed. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.500'.
SignalDecoding.ConfirmStat: Full name: 'Confirmation Status'. Explanation: Whether the decoding results have been confirmed. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Confirmed, Pending, Rejected.
SignalDecoding.DecodeConf: Full name: 'Decoding Confidence (%)'. Explanation: Confidence level that the decoding is correct. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '88.75'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeIters: Full name: 'Decoding Iterations'. Explanation: Number of algorithmic passes attempted. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '7'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeMethod: Full name: 'Decoding Method'. Explanation: Method used to decode the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: FFT, Neural Network, Quantum, Wavelet.
SignalDecoding.DecodeStat: Full name: 'Decoding Status'. Explanation: Status of the decoding process. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Failed, In Progress.
SignalDecoding.EncodeType: Full name: 'Encoding Type'. Explanation: The type of signal encoding used (e.g., Binary). Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Binary, Complex, Tertiary, Unknown.
SignalDecoding.ErrCorrLvl: Full name: 'Error Correction Level'. Explanation: Degree of error correction applied. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, None.
SignalDecoding.ProcTimeHrs: Full name: 'Processing Time (hours)'. Explanation: Total hours spent decoding. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.50'.
SignalDecoding.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal entry. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-GHI-9012'.
SignalDecoding.VerifLvl: Full name: 'Verification Level'. Explanation: Extent to which decoding has been verified. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Partially, Unverified, Verified.
SignalDynamics.AmpStab: Full name: 'Amplitude Stability'. Explanation: Consistency of signal amplitude. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Unstable'.
SignalDynamics.FreqStab: Full name: 'Frequency Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal’s frequency is. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighlyStable'.
SignalDynamics.ModStab: Full name: 'Modulation Stability'. Explanation: Consistency in the signal’s modulation scheme. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'Consistent'.
SignalDynamics.PhaseStab: Full name: 'Phase Stability'. Explanation: Any variation in signal phase. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'VaryingPhase'.
SignalDynamics.SigCoherence: Full name: 'Signal Coherence'. Explanation: How coherent the signal remains over its duration. Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighCoherence'.
SignalDynamics.SigDisp: Full name: 'Signal Dispersion'. Explanation: The degree to which the signal is dispersed (time/frequency smearing). Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'SignificantDisp'.
SignalDynamics.SigEvolve: Full name: 'Signal Evolution'. Explanation: Indicates if the signal changes/evolves during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Dynamic, Static, Unknown.
SignalDynamics.SigIntegrity: Full name: 'Signal Integrity'. Explanation: Rating of how intact or uncorrupted the signal is. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighIntegrity'.
SignalDynamics.SigRecurr: Full name: 'Signal Recurrence'. Explanation: Whether the signal recurs over time. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: None, Regular, Sporadic.
SignalDynamics.SigScint: Full name: 'Signal Scintillation'. Explanation: Fluctuation in signal amplitude due to propagation effects. Data type: VARCHAR(45). If no fixed categories, example: 'MildScintillation'.
SignalDynamics.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-JKL-3456'.
SignalDynamics.SpatStab: Full name: 'Spatial Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal is spatially (e.g., consistent direction). Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Moderate'.
SignalDynamics.TempStab: Full name: 'Temporal Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal remains over time. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Stable'.

SignalProbabilities.ArtSrcProb: Full name: 'Artificial Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from an artificial source. Data type: NUMERIC(3,1). Example: '3.4'.
SignalProbabilities.BioSigProb: Full name: 'Biosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal indicates a biological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '45.21'.
SignalProbabilities.CorrScore: Full name: 'Correlation Score'. Explanation: How well the signal aligns with expected patterns. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.9950'.
SignalProbabilities.FalsePosProb: Full name: 'False Positive Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is falsely detected. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.0135'.
SignalProbabilities.NatSrcProb: Full name: 'Natural Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from a natural source. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '98.761'.
SignalProbabilities.SigUnique: Full name: 'Signal Uniqueness'. Explanation: A measure of how unique the signal is compared to others. Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '99.1234'.
SignalProbabilities.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-XYZ-9876'.
SignalProbabilities.SimIndex: Full name: 'Similarity Index'. Explanation: Compares the signal to known references. Data type: NUMERIC(5,4). Example: '0.8222'.
SignalProbabilities.TechSigProb: Full name: 'Technosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is of artificial technological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.6789'.

requests.specific_A: Joining each order to its account and that account's branch district, for each account with orders give the account id, the region of its branch (`A3`), its number of orders, and that number minus the average number of orders per account (averaged over all accounts that have orders). Sort by that difference from largest to smallest and return exactly 10 rows, picking arbitrarily among accounts tied at 10th place; no rounding.
requests.specific_B: Joining each order to its account and that account's branch district, for each account with orders give the account id, the region of its branch (`A3`), its number of orders, and that number minus the average number of orders per account (averaged over all accounts that have orders). Sort by that difference from largest to smallest and return the top 10 plus every account tied with the 10th-place value; no rounding.
requests.open: Using each order's account and that account's branch district: which accounts rank in the top 10 for how far their number of orders is above the average number of orders per account (averaged over accounts that have orders)? For each one, show the account id, the region of its branch, its order count and that difference (order count minus the average), largest difference first, unrounded.

readings.A: Return exactly 10 accounts. Any tie at 10th place is broken arbitrarily.
readings.B: Return every account whose difference is at least the 10th-place value, so all accounts tied at 10th place are included.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "order"."account_id" AS "e", "district"."A3" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "order" AS "order" INNER JOIN "account" AS "account" ON "account"."account_id" = "order"."account_id" INNER JOIN "district" AS "district" ON "district"."district_id" = "account"."district_id" GROUP BY "order"."account_id", "district"."A3"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "order"."account_id" AS "e", "district"."A3" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "order" AS "order" INNER JOIN "account" AS "account" ON "account"."account_id" = "order"."account_id" INNER JOIN "district" AS "district" ON "district"."district_id" = "account"."district_id" GROUP BY "order"."account_id", "district"."A3"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" >= (SELECT "t"."m1" FROM "s1" AS "t" ORDER BY "t"."m1" DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 9) ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every `order` record.

Inner-join each order to its `account` (by `account_id`), then to that account's branch `district` (by `account.district_id`). Group by `order.account_id` and `district.A3`, giving one row per account with orders.
Account id (`order.account_id`).
The region of the account's branch (`district.A3`).
The account's number of orders.
The account's order count minus the average order count per account. The average is taken over all accounts that have orders. No rounding.
Order by that difference, largest first.
Cut the ranking at 10th place.

A.requirement: Return exactly 10 rows, picking arbitrarily among accounts tied at 10th place.

B.requirement: Return the top 10 plus every account whose value ties with the 10th-place value.

context.schema:
CREATE TABLE account
(
    account_id  INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    district_id INTEGER default 0 not null,
    frequency   TEXT   not null,
    date        DATE          not null,
    foreign key (district_id) references district (district_id)
);
CREATE TABLE card
(
    card_id INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    disp_id INTEGER           not null,
    type    TEXT    not null,
    issued  DATE          not null,
    foreign key (disp_id) references disp (disp_id)
);
CREATE TABLE client
(
    client_id   INTEGER        not null
        primary key,
    gender      TEXT not null,
    birth_date  DATE       not null,
    district_id INTEGER        not null,
    foreign key (district_id) references district (district_id)
);

(
    disp_id    INTEGER        not null

    client_id  INTEGER        not null,
    account_id INTEGER        not null,
    type      TEXT not null,
    foreign key (account_id) references account (account_id),
    foreign key (client_id) references client (client_id)

(

requests.specific_A: Compute each film `rating`'s average `length`, ignoring missing lengths. As the baseline, take the average of these per-rating averages, with each rating counting equally. Keep the ratings whose average length is above that baseline. Among those ratings, take the mean of their average lengths and keep only the ratings that are above that mean too. Return one row with: the mean of the remaining ratings' average lengths, the mean amount by which they exceed the baseline, and the mean amount by which they exceed the kept ratings' mean. Do not round anything.
requests.specific_B: Compute each film `rating`'s average `length`, ignoring missing lengths. As the baseline, take the average length over all films, with each film counting equally. Keep the ratings whose average length is above that baseline. Among those ratings, take the mean of their average lengths and keep only the ratings that are above that mean too. Return one row with: the mean of the remaining ratings' average lengths, the mean amount by which they exceed the baseline, and the mean amount by which they exceed the kept ratings' mean. Do not round anything.
requests.open: Which film ratings have an average `length` (ignoring missing lengths) that is longer than average? Of those ratings, keep only the ones that also run longer than the mean of their own average lengths. Give one row with: the mean of the remaining ratings' average lengths, how far on average they sit above that first average, and how far on average they sit above the mean of the ratings that passed the first cut. No rounding.

readings.A: Each rating's average length is compared with the unweighted mean of the per-rating averages.
readings.B: Each rating's average length is compared with the mean length over all individual films.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "film"."rating" AS "g", AVG("film"."length") AS "m1" FROM "film" AS "film" GROUP BY "film"."rating"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m1" > "s4"."v") SELECT AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from all film records. Compute the average of film.length per rating, ignoring missing lengths.
Compute a single baseline average length (how it is computed is the choice). Keep only the ratings whose average length is strictly greater than the baseline.
Among the kept ratings, compute the mean of their average lengths, with each rating weighted equally. Keep only the ratings whose average length is strictly greater than this mean.
The mean of the remaining ratings' average lengths.
The mean of (rating average minus baseline) over the remaining ratings.
The mean of (rating average minus the kept ratings' mean) over the remaining ratings. Return a single row with these three columns in this order, with no rounding.

A.requirement: The baseline is the average of the per-rating average lengths, with each rating counting once.

B.requirement: The baseline is the average length over all films, with each film counting once.

film.rating: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns exactly 5 rating levels, each covering roughly 180-225 films, so every group is well populated and rating works as a grouping class. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate), AVG(length), AVG(replacement_cost) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '3.0348430493273613', '120.4439461883408', '20.402556053811544'], ['NC-17', '210', '2.970952380952388', '113.22857142857143', '20.137619047618937'], ['R', '195', '2.9387179487179553', '118.66153846153846', '20.23102564102554'], ['PG', '194', '3.051855670103099', '112.00515463917526', '18.959072164948356'], ['G', '178', '2.888876404494388', '111.0505617977528', '20.12483146067407']] scale (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows exactly 5 levels: G, PG, PG-13, R and NC-17. These are the standard MPAA bands, which are ordered by audience restriction, so the column is an ordinal class. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY rating -> [['G', '178'], ['NC-17', '210'], ['PG', '194'], ['PG-13', '223'], ['R', '195']]
category.name: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 16 genres, each shared by many films (about 50-75 each), so the column is a grouping label and does not identify single records. Evidence: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film_category fc JOIN category c ON c.category_id = fc.category_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY films DESC -> [['Sports', '74'], ['Foreign', '73'], ['Family', '69'], ['Documentary', '68'], ['Animation', '66'], ['Action', '64']]
customer.store_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 2 stores with about 300 customers each, so the column is a grouping label shared by many rows. Evidence: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS customers, SUM(active) AS active_customers FROM customer GROUP BY store_id -> [['1', '326', '318'], ['2', '273', '266']]
inventory.store_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 2 store values over 4581 copies, about 2270 per store, so the column is a grouping label. Evidence: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS copies, COUNT(DISTINCT film_id) AS titles FROM inventory GROUP BY store_id -> [['1', '2270', '759'], ['2', '2311', '762']]
country.country: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Many customers share a country (the top countries have dozens of customers each), so country works as a grouping attribute for customers. Evidence: SELECT co.country, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customer cu JOIN address a ON a.address_id = cu.address_id JOIN city ci ON ci.city_id = a.city_id JOIN country co ON co.country_id = ci.country_id GROUP BY co.country ORDER BY customers DESC LIMIT 10 -> [['India', '60'], ['China', '53'], ['United States', '36'], ['Japan', '31'], ['Mexico', '30'], ['Russian Federation', '28']]
film.special_features: desc (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 15 distinct values, all of them combinations of the same 4 feature names (for example 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes'). The column is a set, not a single category. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']] semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows 15 distinct values, all combinations of the same 4 feature names, such as 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes' and 'Trailers,Commentaries'. The column is a set, not a single class, so it should not be offered as a grouping. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']]
film.length: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified rating query already returns AVG(length) between 111.05 (G) and 120.44 (PG-13). The catalogue profile gives 140 distinct values from 46 to 185 minutes. So length is a continuous ratio-scale quantity whose group averages can be read directly. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(length) AS avg_minutes, MIN(length), MAX(length) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '120.4439461883408', '46', '185'], ['NC-17', '210', '113.22857142857143', '46', '184'], ['R', '195', '118.66153846153846', '49', '185'], ['PG', '194', '112.00515463917526', '46', '185'], ['G', '178', '111.0505617977528', '47', '185']]
film.rental_duration: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows 5 values from 3 to 7 days, all well above zero, so the column is a ratio-scale number of days per film. The query shows how many films fall at each value. Evidence: SELECT rental_duration, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate) AS avg_rate FROM film GROUP BY rental_duration ORDER BY rental_duration -> [['3', '203', '2.8323645320197115'], ['4', '203', '2.97029556650247'], ['5', '191', '3.19942408376964'], ['6', '212', '2.895660377358497'], ['7', '191', '3.021413612565451']]
film.rental_rate: desc (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows rental_rate takes only 0.99, 2.99 and 4.99, while replacement_cost runs from 9.99 to 29.99. The query shows how large and uniform the gap is. The auditor noted that the difference is always about −17 and the relative gap about −0.85, which fits two different quantities rather than one price seen two ways. Evidence: SELECT MIN(replacement_cost - rental_rate), MAX(replacement_cost - rental_rate), AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) FROM film -> [['5.0', '29.0', '0.16651517608314595']]
film.replacement_cost: quantity (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The column holds a per-copy value that becomes meaningful when summed over physical copies in inventory, for example as stock value. That is the reading of an asset value, not of a price charged per rental. Evidence: SELECT f.rating, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copies, SUM(f.replacement_cost) AS stock_value FROM inventory i JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating -> [['G', '791', '16185.089999999853'], ['NC-17', '944', '19128.56000000009'], ['PG', '924', '17755.759999999962'], ['PG-13', '1018', '21052.82000000024'], ['R', '904', '18498.960000000006']]

Each value is therefore shared by thousands of rows, which makes it a grouping label rather than a record identifier. Evidence: SELECT staff_id, COUNT(*) AS payments, SUM(amount) AS revenue, AVG(amount) FROM payment GROUP BY staff_id -> [['1', '8057', '33489.470000005174', '4.156568201564499'], ['2', '7992', '33927.04000000482', '4.245125125125728']]
rental.staff_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows only 2 distinct values across 16,044 rentals, so each staff value covers thousands of rentals and works as a grouping class. Evidence: SELECT staff_id, COUNT(*) AS rentals, SUM(CASE WHEN return_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unreturned FROM rental GROUP BY staff_id -> [['1', '8040', '85'], ['2', '8004', '98']]

requests.specific_A: For each manager in `manager_award` who matches a `player` record on `player_id`, count their award rows by manager and the player's `death_country`. Managers with a NULL death country drop out. Keep managers whose death country is an empty string, and treat that blank as a death-country group of its own. Then show each manager's award count as a share of the total awards for all managers with the same death country. List manager id, death country, award count and share, sorted by share from highest to lowest (missing last). Show the top 10, unrounded.
requests.specific_B: For each manager in `manager_award` who matches a `player` record on `player_id`, count their award rows by manager and the player's `death_country`. Managers with a NULL death country drop out. Also leave out managers whose death country is an empty string, so blank death countries form no group at all. Then show each manager's award count as a share of the total awards for all managers with the same death country. List manager id, death country, award count and share, sorted by share from highest to lowest (missing last). Show the top 10, unrounded.
requests.open: For managers in `manager_award` who match a `player` record on `player_id`, count each manager's awards by their `death_country` (NULL death countries drop out), and show what share of all the awards for managers with that same death country each one accounts for. Give manager id, death country, award count and share, top 10 by share (highest first, missing last), unrounded.

readings.A: A blank death_country is treated as one ordinary group, and shares are computed within it.
readings.B: Managers with a blank death_country are excluded before counting and computing shares.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "manager_award"."player_id" AS "e", "player"."death_country" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "manager_award" AS "manager_award" INNER JOIN "player" AS "player" ON "player"."player_id" = "manager_award"."player_id" GROUP BY "manager_award"."player_id", "player"."death_country"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g" ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "manager_award"."player_id" AS "e", "player"."death_country" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "manager_award" AS "manager_award" INNER JOIN "player" AS "player" ON "player"."player_id" = "manager_award"."player_id" WHERE "player"."death_country" <> '' GROUP BY "manager_award"."player_id", "player"."death_country"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g" ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Source records are `manager_award` rows. Count the award rows per manager (`player_id`) and death country.
Inner join to `player` on `player_id`, dropping unmatched awards. Managers whose death country is NULL drop out because they cannot match a country total.
Output the manager id (`manager_award.player_id`).
Output the death country (`player.death_country`).
Output the manager's award count.
Output the share: the manager's award count divided by the total awards of all managers with the same death country. No rounding.
Sort by share descending, with missing values last.
Keep the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: An empty-string death country is kept and treated as a group of its own.

B.requirement: Managers whose death country is an empty string are left out entirely.

requests.specific_A: For each media type (grouped by name, using only tracks linked to a media type), compute its byte rate as the average of each track's `Bytes` divided by that track's `Milliseconds` (tracks with no size ignored), and count its tracks. Take the simple average of these rates across all media types, and keep only the media types whose rate is above it. Across those media types, return one row giving the average of their rates, the average of their track counts, and the average amount by which their rate exceeds the overall average, without rounding.
requests.specific_B: For each media type (grouped by name, using only tracks linked to a media type), compute its byte rate as the media type's total `Bytes` divided by its total `Milliseconds`, and count its tracks. Take the simple average of these rates across all media types, and keep only the media types whose rate is above it. Across those media types, return one row giving the average of their rates, the average of their track counts, and the average amount by which their rate exceeds the overall average, without rounding.
requests.open: Consider only the media types (by name, counting only tracks that have a media type) whose bytes-per-millisecond rate is above the simple average of that rate across all media types. In one unrounded row, what are their average rate, their average number of tracks, and their average margin above that overall average?

readings.A: Per media type, rate = the mean of its tracks' Bytes/Milliseconds ratios; among media types above the unweighted mean rate, report the average rate, average track count, and average excess.
readings.B: Per media type, rate = its total Bytes / its total Milliseconds; among media types above the unweighted mean rate, report the average rate, average track count, and average excess.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "MediaType"."Name" AS "g", AVG((CAST("Track"."Bytes" AS REAL) / "Track"."Milliseconds")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "Track" AS "Track" INNER JOIN "MediaType" AS "MediaType" ON "MediaType"."MediaTypeId" = "Track"."MediaTypeId" GROUP BY "MediaType"."Name"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "MediaType"."Name" AS "g", (CAST(SUM("Track"."Bytes") AS REAL) / SUM("Track"."Milliseconds")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "Track" AS "Track" INNER JOIN "MediaType" AS "MediaType" ON "MediaType"."MediaTypeId" = "Track"."MediaTypeId" GROUP BY "MediaType"."Name"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"

Group employees by ReportsTo; each group's share = its count ÷ sum of all group counts; the average share is taken across the groups
ReportsTo value
Number of employees in the group
Share = count ÷ total of the group counts, unrounded
Share minus the average share across groups, unrounded
Order by output 4 descending
Keep the first 10 rows

A.requirement: Employees with a missing ReportsTo are kept and form their own group, which shows as a row with a blank ReportsTo and counts in the total and the average

B.requirement: Employees with a missing ReportsTo are excluded before grouping, so they count in neither the total, the average, nor the output rows

requests.specific_A: Match each transaction record to its trader (`trdref` = `tradereg`, exact text match) and drop records with no matching trader. Then, for each trader type (`tradekind`), count the transaction records. Count every record, so a trader with five records adds five. Traders with no type form their own group. Which trader types have a count strictly above the plain average of the per-type counts? For each one, show the trader type, its count, that count divided by the total of all the per-type counts, and the count minus the average. Don't round anything, and return nothing if the average is missing.
requests.specific_B: Match each transaction record to its trader (`trdref` = `tradereg`, exact text match) and drop records with no matching trader. Then, for each trader type (`tradekind`), count the distinct traders (`trdref`) who have at least one matched transaction record. Count each trader once, however many records they have. Traders with no type form their own group. Which trader types have a count strictly above the plain average of the per-type counts? For each one, show the trader type, its count, that count divided by the total of all the per-type counts, and the count minus the average. Don't round anything, and return nothing if the average is missing.
requests.open: Using the transaction records matched to their traders (`trdref` = `tradereg`, exact text match, dropping records with no matching trader), how big is each trader type (`tradekind`) in this data? Traders with no type form their own group. Which trader types have a count strictly above the plain average of the per-type counts? For each one, show the trader type, its count, that count divided by the total of all the per-type counts, and the count minus the average. Don't round anything, and return nothing if the average is missing.

readings.A: Each trader type's size is the number of transaction records belonging to traders of that type.
readings.B: Each trader type's size is the number of different traders of that type who have transaction records.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "trader"."tradekind" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "transactionrecord" AS "transactionrecord" INNER JOIN "trader" AS "trader" ON "trader"."tradereg" = "transactionrecord"."trdref" GROUP BY "trader"."tradekind"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m1" > "s4"."v"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "trader"."tradekind" AS "g", COUNT(DISTINCT "transactionrecord"."trdref") AS "m1" FROM "transactionrecord" AS "transactionrecord" INNER JOIN "trader" AS "trader" ON "trader"."tradereg" = "transactionrecord"."trdref" GROUP BY "trader"."tradekind"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m1" > "s4"."v"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from transaction records (`transactionrecord`).
Inner join each transaction record to the trader whose `tradereg` equals its `trdref`, comparing exact text. Records with no matching trader are dropped.
Group by trader type (`trader.tradekind`). Traders with no type form their own group. Return the trader type.
The group's count divided by the total of the counts across all trader-type groups, unrounded.
Keep only the trader types whose count is strictly greater than the plain (unweighted) average of the per-type counts. Return no rows if that average is missing.
The count minus the average of the per-type counts, unrounded.
Output columns in this order: type, count, share, excess over average. No ordering and no rounding.

A.requirement: The count is the number of joined transaction records in the group. Every record counts, so one trader with many records adds many.

B.requirement: The count is the number of distinct traders (distinct `trdref`) in the group that have at least one matching transaction record.

requests.specific_A: Match each conservation record (`scanconservation`) to its site where `sites.zoneregistry` equals `scanconservation.zoneref`, and drop records with no matching site. For each combination of site reference (`zoneref`) and insurance status (`insurstat`), with a missing status kept as its own value, show the site reference, the insurance status, the number of conservation records, and that number as a fraction of all matched conservation records, unrounded. Sort by that fraction from highest to lowest (missing last) and return exactly 10 rows, breaking any ties at 10th place arbitrarily.
requests.specific_B: Match each conservation record (`scanconservation`) to its site where `sites.zoneregistry` equals `scanconservation.zoneref`, and drop records with no matching site. For each combination of site reference (`zoneref`) and insurance status (`insurstat`), with a missing status kept as its own value, show the site reference, the insurance status, the number of conservation records, and that number as a fraction of all matched conservation records, unrounded. Sort by that fraction from highest to lowest (missing last) and return every row whose fraction is at least the 10th-highest, keeping all rows tied at 10th place.
requests.open: Matching conservation records (`scanconservation`) to their sites on `zoneref` = `sites.zoneregistry` and dropping any without a site, which are the top 10 site reference and insurance status (`insurstat`) combinations by share of conservation records? Treat a missing status as its own value. Show the site reference, the insurance status, the record count, and the count as a fraction of all matched conservation records (unrounded), sorted by that fraction from highest to lowest with missing values last.

readings.A: List the 10 site/insurance-status groups with the largest share of conservation records. Return exactly 10, breaking ties at the cutoff arbitrarily.
readings.B: List the site/insurance-status groups with the largest share of conservation records. Return all rows whose share reaches the 10th-highest value, including every row tied at the cutoff.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scanconservation"."zoneref" AS "e", "sites"."insurstat" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "scanconservation" AS "scanconservation" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scanconservation"."zoneref" GROUP BY "scanconservation"."zoneref", "sites"."insurstat"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scanconservation"."zoneref" AS "e", "sites"."insurstat" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "scanconservation" AS "scanconservation" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scanconservation"."zoneref" GROUP BY "scanconservation"."zoneref", "sites"."insurstat"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") >= (SELECT MIN("t"."r") FROM (SELECT CAST("x"."m1" AS REAL) / "y"."v" AS "r" FROM "s1" AS "x" CROSS JOIN "s2" AS "y" ORDER BY "r" DESC LIMIT 10) AS "t") ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from conservation records (`scanconservation`).
Inner join each conservation record to its site where `sites.zoneregistry` = `scanconservation.zoneref` (exact text match). Records with no matching site are dropped.
Group by site reference (`scanconservation.zoneref`) and insurance status (`sites.insurstat`). Return the site reference.
Return the insurance status. A missing status is kept as its own value.
Return the number of conservation records in the group.
Return that count divided by the total number of matched conservation records. Not rounded.
Sort by the share, highest first. Missing values go last.
Keep the top 10 by share.

A.requirement: Return exactly 10 rows. Rows that tie at 10th place are cut arbitrarily.

B.requirement: Return every row whose share is at least the 10th-highest share, so all rows tied at the cut are kept.
