context.documentation:
Equipment.EquipDesign: Full name: 'Equipment Model'. Explanation: Model name or identifier. Data type: VARCHAR(14). Example: 'Model-669'.
Equipment.EquipForm: Full name: 'Equipment Type'. Explanation: Type or category of scanning equipment. Data type: VARCHAR(28). Possible categories: LiDAR, Structured Light, Photogrammetry, Laser.
Equipment.EquipRegistry: Full name: 'Equipment ID'. Explanation: Primary key for equipment. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
Equipment.EquipStatus: Full name: 'Equipment Condition'. Explanation: Overall condition of the equipment. Data type: VARCHAR(16). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor.
Equipment.EquipTune: Full name: 'Calibration Date'. Explanation: Date the equipment was last calibrated. Data type: DATE. Example: '2024-11-01'.
Equipment.PowerLevel: Full name: 'Battery Level (%)'. Explanation: Battery level as an integer percentage. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 62.
Personnel.CrewLabel: Full name: 'Operator Name'. Explanation: Name or label for the operator. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Example: 'Joel Wallace'.
Personnel.CrewRegistry: Full name: 'Operator ID'. Explanation: Primary key for Personnel, representing an operator. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
Personnel.LeadLabel: Full name: 'Supervisor Name'. Explanation: Name of the supervisor. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Example: 'Michael Kaiser'.
Personnel.LeadRegistry: Full name: 'Supervisor ID'. Explanation: Identifies a supervisor. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'SV7658'.
Projects.ArcRegistry: Full name: 'Project ID'. Explanation: Primary key for Projects, a unique project identifier. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
Projects.AuthHalt: Full name: 'Permit Expiry Date'. Explanation: Date on which the permit expires. Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-12-05'.
Projects.AuthPin: Full name: 'Permit Number'. Explanation: Authorization or permit ID. Data type: CHAR(6). Example: 'PMT4719'.
Projects.FundFlux: Full name: 'Funding Source'. Explanation: Source of funds for the project. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Government'.
Projects.VesselTag: Full name: 'Project Name'. Explanation: Label or name for the project. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Example: 'Project Happy'.
ScanConservation.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Associates conservation data with a project. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanConservation.CureRank: Full name: 'Conservation Priority'. Explanation: Priority level for conservation efforts. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Critical, Low, High.
ScanConservation.CureRegistry: Full name: 'Conservation Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for conservation data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 6001.
ScanConservation.HarmAssess: Full name: 'Damage Assessment'. Explanation: Indicates severity of damage. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: None, Moderate, Severe.
ScanConservation.IntervHistory: Full name: 'Intervention History'. Explanation: Past restoration or intervention records. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: None, Major, Minor.
ScanConservation.PriorDocs: Full name: 'Previous Documentation'. Explanation: Level of existing documentation. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: None, Partial, Complete.
ScanConservation.StructState: Full name: 'Structural Stability'. Explanation: Stability level of the structure. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Stable, Moderate, Unstable.
ScanConservation.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Associates conservation data with a site code. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanEnvironment.AirRegistry: Full name: 'Environment Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for environment data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 1001.
ScanEnvironment.AmbicTemp: Full name: 'Ambient Temperature (C)'. Explanation: Air temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 25.3.
ScanEnvironment.EquipRef: Full name: 'Equipment Reference'. Explanation: Identifies which equipment these environment data refer to. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
ScanEnvironment.GeoSignal: Full name: 'GPS Signal Quality'. Explanation: Quality rating for GPS reception. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: None, Poor, Good, Excellent.
ScanEnvironment.HumePct: Full name: 'Relative Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 60.4.
ScanEnvironment.IllumeLux: Full name: 'Light Conditions (lux)'. Explanation: Measured illumination in lux. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 86054.

requests.specific_A: For each telescope (`telescref`) in the signals table, compute its average modulation index (`modindex`), ignoring missing values. Take the overall average to be the mean of these per-telescope averages, so each telescope counts once. Keep only the telescopes whose average is above that overall average. For each one, show the telescope reference, its average modulation index, how far it is above the overall average (its average minus the overall average), and its average divided by the mean of the averages of just these above-average telescopes. Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest and return the top 10, without rounding.
requests.specific_B: For each telescope (`telescref`) in the signals table, compute its average modulation index (`modindex`), ignoring missing values. Take the overall average to be the mean of these per-telescope averages, so each telescope counts once. Keep only the telescopes whose average is above that overall average. For each one, show the telescope reference, its average modulation index, how far it is above the overall average (its average minus the overall average), and its average divided by the overall average. Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest and return the top 10, without rounding.
requests.open: For each telescope (`telescref`) in the signals table, compute its average modulation index (`modindex`), ignoring missing values. Then list the telescopes whose average is above the overall average, taking the overall average as the mean of the per-telescope averages. For each one, show the telescope reference, its average modulation index, how much it exceeds the overall average, and its average as a ratio to the group average. Return the top 10 by that ratio, highest first, without rounding.

readings.A: The ratio column divides each kept telescope's average modulation index by the mean of the averages of only the above-average telescopes.
readings.B: The ratio column divides each kept telescope's average modulation index by the overall average, which is the mean of the per-telescope averages across all telescopes.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "signals"."telescref" AS "e", AVG("signals"."modindex") AS "m1" FROM "signals" AS "signals" GROUP BY "signals"."telescref"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "signals"."telescref" AS "e", AVG("signals"."modindex") AS "m1" FROM "signals" AS "signals" GROUP BY "signals"."telescref"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every signals record and group by telescope reference (`telescref`). For each telescope, compute the average modulation index (`modindex`), ignoring missing values; a telescope with no values has a missing average.

Compute the overall average as the mean of the per-telescope averages, so each telescope counts once. Pair each telescope with it, and keep only telescopes whose average is strictly greater than this overall average.
First column: telescope reference (`telescref`).
Second column: the telescope's average modulation index.
Third column: the telescope's average minus the overall average (mean of per-telescope averages).
Fourth column: the telescope's average divided by a reference average (which one is the choice). No rounding on any column.
Sort by the fourth column (the ratio), highest first, with missing values last.
Keep only the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: The divisor is the mean of the average modulation index taken over only the kept, above-average telescopes.

B.requirement: The divisor is the overall average: the mean of the per-telescope averages across all telescopes, the same value used for the filter and the difference.

  "veriflvl" text(30),
  "confirmstat" text(30),
  CONSTRAINT "signaldecoding_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalref"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_decoding_signal" FOREIGN KEY ("signalref") REFERENCES "signals" ("signalregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "signaldynamics" (
  "signalref" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "sigintegrity" text(30),
  "sigrecurr" text(25),
  "sigevolve" text(25),
  "tempstab" text(20),
  "spatstab" text(20),
  "freqstab" text(35),
  "phasestab" text(35),
  "ampstab" text(20),
  "modstab" text(30),
  "sigcoherence" text(25),
  "sigdisp" text(25),
  "sigscint" text(45),
  CONSTRAINT "signaldynamics_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalref"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_dynamics_signal" FOREIGN KEY ("signalref") REFERENCES "signals" ("signalregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "signalprobabilities" (
  "signalref" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "falseposprob" real(5,4),
  "sigunique" real(7,4),
  "simindex" real(5,4),
  "corrscore" real(5,4),
  "anomscore" integer(53),
  "techsigprob" real(5,4),
  "biosigprob" real(6,2),
  "natsrcprob" real(7,3),
  "artsrcprob" real(3,1),
  CONSTRAINT "signalprobabilities_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalref"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_probabilities_signal" FOREIGN KEY ("signalref") REFERENCES "signals" ("signalregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "signals" (
  "signalregistry" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "timemark" text(6),
  "telescref" text(20) NOT NULL,
  "detectinstr" text(50),
  "signalclass" text(50),
  "sigstrdb" real(7,2),
  "freqmhz" real(9,3),
  "bwhz" real(10,3),
  "centerfreqmhz" real(8,3),
  "freqdrifthzs" real(9,3),
  "doppshifthz" integer(53),
  "sigdursec" real(6,2),
  "pulsepersec" real(6,3),
  "pulsewidms" real(6,3),
  "modtype" text(30),
  "modindex" real(6,4),
  "carrierfreqmhz" real(9,3),
  "phaseshiftdeg" real(6,2),
  "polarmode" text(30),
  "polarangledeg" real(5,1),
  "snrratio" real(6,2),
  "noisefloordbm" integer(53),
  "interflvl" text(30),
  "rfistat" text(30),
  "atmointerf" text(30),
  CONSTRAINT "signals_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_signals_telescopesref" FOREIGN KEY ("telescref") REFERENCES "telescopes" ("telescregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "sourceproperties" (
  "signalref" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "sourceradeg" real(7,4),
  "sourcedecdeg" real(7,4),
  "sourcedistly" real(10,2),
  "gallong" real(6,2),
  "gallat" real(6,2),
  "celestobj" text(75),
  "objtype" text(50),
  "objmag" real(5,2),
  "objtempk" integer(32),
  "objmasssol" real(6,3),
  "objagegyr" real(6,3),
  "objmetal" real(5,3),
  "objpropmotion" real(7,2),
  "objradvel" real(7,2),
  CONSTRAINT "sourceproperties_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalref"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_source_signal" FOREIGN KEY ("signalref") REFERENCES "signals" ("signalregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "telescopes" (
  "telescregistry" text(20) NOT NULL,
  "observstation" text(60) NOT NULL,
  "equipstatus" text(35),
  "calibrstatus" text(50),
  "pointaccarc" real(6,2),
  "trackaccarc" real(6,2),
  "focusquality" text(25),
  "detecttempk" real(7,2),
  "coolsysstatus" text(35),
  "powerstatus" text(30),
  "datastorstatus" text(35),
  "netstatus" text(40),
  "bandusagepct" real(5,2),
  "procqueuestatus" text(40),
  CONSTRAINT "telescopes_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("telescregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_telescopes_observatoriesref" FOREIGN KEY ("observstation") REFERENCES "observatories" ("observstation")
);
context.documentation:
ObservationalConditions.ObsDate: Full name: 'Observation Date'. Explanation: Local date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD). Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-08-01'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsDurHrs: Full name: 'Observation Duration (hours)'. Explanation: How long the observation lasted in hours. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '2.50'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsTime: Full name: 'Observation Time'. Explanation: Local time of the observation in HH:MM:SS. Data type: TIME. Example: '13:45:59'.
ObservationalConditions.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-PQR-9876'.
Observatories.AirTempC: Full name: 'Air Temperature (°C)'. Explanation: Ambient temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '18.45'.
Observatories.AtmosTransparency: Full name: 'Atmospheric Transparency'. Explanation: A numeric measure of how transparent the atmosphere is. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.867'.
Observatories.GeomagStatus: Full name: 'Geomagnetic Activity'. Explanation: The level of geomagnetic activity during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Active, Quiet, Storm.
Observatories.HumidityRate: Full name: 'Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Relative humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '62.300'.
Observatories.LunarDistDeg: Full name: 'Moon Distance (Degrees)'. Explanation: Angular distance to the Moon in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '97.52'.
Observatories.LunarStage: Full name: 'Lunar Phase'. Explanation: The current phase of the Moon during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: First Quarter, Full, Last Quarter, New.
Observatories.ObservStation: Full name: 'Observatory Name'. Explanation: This field holds the name or unique identifier for the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
Observatories.PressHpa: Full name: 'Pressure (hPa)'. Explanation: Atmospheric pressure in hectopascals. Data type: DECIMAL(6,1). Example: '1013.2'.
Observatories.SeeingProfile: Full name: 'Seeing Profile'. Explanation: Assessment of sky seeing conditions (atmospheric steadiness). Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
Observatories.SiderealLocal: Full name: 'Local Sidereal Time'. Explanation: Sidereal time at the observatory in HH:MM:SS format. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: '12:34:56'.
Observatories.SolarStatus: Full name: 'Solar Activity'. Explanation: The level of solar activity at the time of observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Moderate.
Observatories.WeathProfile: Full name: 'Weather Profile'. Explanation: A short description of weather conditions during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Clear, Cloudy, Partially Cloudy.
Observatories.WindSpeedMs: Full name: 'Wind Speed (m/s)'. Explanation: Wind speed in meters per second. Data type: NUMERIC(4,2). Example: '3.45'.
ResearchProcess.AnalysisPrio: Full name: 'Analysis Priority'. Explanation: Priority assigned for analyzing this signal. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, Urgent.
ResearchProcess.CollabStat: Full name: 'Collaboration Status'. Explanation: The nature of collaboration on this signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: International, Solo, Team.
ResearchProcess.DiscStat: Full name: 'Disclosure Status'. Explanation: How much information about the signal is shared publicly. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Full, None, Partial.
ResearchProcess.FollowStat: Full name: 'Follow-up Status'. Explanation: Status of any follow-up observations. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Required, Scheduled.
ResearchProcess.FundStat: Full name: 'Funding Status'. Explanation: Funding situation for further study. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Funded, Pending, Unfunded.
ResearchProcess.NotesMemo: Full name: 'Research Notes'. Explanation: Any extra remarks or context by researchers. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Project requires further funding...'
ResearchProcess.PeerRevStat: Full name: 'Peer Review Status'. Explanation: Where this signal stands in peer review. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, In Progress, Pending.
ResearchProcess.PubStat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether findings about the signal have been published. Data type: CHAR(25). Possible categories: Draft, Published, Submitted.
ResearchProcess.ResPrio: Full name: 'Research Priority'. Explanation: How urgently this signal needs scientific attention. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium.
ResearchProcess.SecClass: Full name: 'Security Classification'. Explanation: Visibility and clearance level for the data. Data type: CHAR(35). Possible categories: Classified, Public, Restricted.
ResearchProcess.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-MNO-7890'.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.CultSig: Full name: 'Cultural Significance'. Explanation: The level of cultural impact or interest. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: High, Low, None.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.EncryptEvid: Full name: 'Encryption Evidence'. Explanation: Whether there is indication the signal is encrypted. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: None, Possible, Strong.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.GravLens: Full name: 'Gravitational Lensing'. Explanation: Whether the signal is affected by gravitational lensing. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: None, Strong, Weak.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.InterMedEffects: Full name: 'Interstellar Medium Effects'. Explanation: Impact of interstellar medium on the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.LangStruct: Full name: 'Language Structure'. Explanation: Presence of linguistic or structured patterns. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Complex, None, Simple.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.MsgContent: Full name: 'Message Content'. Explanation: Indicates whether an actual message was detected. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Identified, None, Possible.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.QuantEffects: Full name: 'Quantum Effects'. Explanation: Quantum-level phenomena observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(85). Possible categories: None, Observed, Significant.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SciImpact: Full name: 'Scientific Impact'. Explanation: Significance of the signal to scientific research. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Major, Minor, Moderate.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-ABC-1234'.
SignalClassification.ClassConf: Full name: 'Classification Confidence (%)'. Explanation: How confident we are in the assigned signal class. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '92.50'.
SignalClassification.ComplexIdx: Full name: 'Complexity Index'. Explanation: Numeric measure of the signal’s complexity. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '5.678'.
SignalClassification.EntropyVal: Full name: 'Entropy'. Explanation: Entropy measurement of the signal. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.45'.
SignalClassification.InfoDense: Full name: 'Information Density'. Explanation: Estimated information per unit time/frequency. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.345'.
SignalClassification.PeriodSec: Full name: 'Period (s)'. Explanation: Duration of each cycle if periodic. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '12.345'.
SignalClassification.RepeatCount: Full name: 'Repetition Count'. Explanation: Number of times the signal has repeated. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '3'.
SignalClassification.SigClassType: Full name: 'Classification Type'. Explanation: High-level category for the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Artificial, Candidate, Natural, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SigPattern: Full name: 'Signal Pattern'. Explanation: Pattern observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: Periodic, Random, Structured, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-DEF-5678'.
SignalDecoding.AnalysisDp: Full name: 'Analysis Depth'. Explanation: How thoroughly the signal was analyzed. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Comprehensive, Detailed, Preliminary.
SignalDecoding.CompResources: Full name: 'Computational Resources'. Explanation: Level of computing power used. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Extreme, High, Low, Medium.
SignalDecoding.CompressRatio: Full name: 'Compression Ratio'. Explanation: Factor by which the raw signal data was compressed. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.500'.
SignalDecoding.ConfirmStat: Full name: 'Confirmation Status'. Explanation: Whether the decoding results have been confirmed. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Confirmed, Pending, Rejected.
SignalDecoding.DecodeConf: Full name: 'Decoding Confidence (%)'. Explanation: Confidence level that the decoding is correct. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '88.75'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeIters: Full name: 'Decoding Iterations'. Explanation: Number of algorithmic passes attempted. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '7'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeMethod: Full name: 'Decoding Method'. Explanation: Method used to decode the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: FFT, Neural Network, Quantum, Wavelet.
SignalDecoding.DecodeStat: Full name: 'Decoding Status'. Explanation: Status of the decoding process. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Failed, In Progress.
SignalDecoding.EncodeType: Full name: 'Encoding Type'. Explanation: The type of signal encoding used (e.g., Binary). Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Binary, Complex, Tertiary, Unknown.
SignalDecoding.ErrCorrLvl: Full name: 'Error Correction Level'. Explanation: Degree of error correction applied. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, None.
SignalDecoding.ProcTimeHrs: Full name: 'Processing Time (hours)'. Explanation: Total hours spent decoding. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.50'.
SignalDecoding.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal entry. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-GHI-9012'.
SignalDecoding.VerifLvl: Full name: 'Verification Level'. Explanation: Extent to which decoding has been verified. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Partially, Unverified, Verified.
SignalDynamics.AmpStab: Full name: 'Amplitude Stability'. Explanation: Consistency of signal amplitude. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Unstable'.
SignalDynamics.FreqStab: Full name: 'Frequency Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal’s frequency is. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighlyStable'.
SignalDynamics.ModStab: Full name: 'Modulation Stability'. Explanation: Consistency in the signal’s modulation scheme. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'Consistent'.
SignalDynamics.PhaseStab: Full name: 'Phase Stability'. Explanation: Any variation in signal phase. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'VaryingPhase'.
SignalDynamics.SigCoherence: Full name: 'Signal Coherence'. Explanation: How coherent the signal remains over its duration. Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighCoherence'.
SignalDynamics.SigDisp: Full name: 'Signal Dispersion'. Explanation: The degree to which the signal is dispersed (time/frequency smearing). Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'SignificantDisp'.
SignalDynamics.SigEvolve: Full name: 'Signal Evolution'. Explanation: Indicates if the signal changes/evolves during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Dynamic, Static, Unknown.
SignalDynamics.SigIntegrity: Full name: 'Signal Integrity'. Explanation: Rating of how intact or uncorrupted the signal is. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighIntegrity'.
SignalDynamics.SigRecurr: Full name: 'Signal Recurrence'. Explanation: Whether the signal recurs over time. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: None, Regular, Sporadic.
SignalDynamics.SigScint: Full name: 'Signal Scintillation'. Explanation: Fluctuation in signal amplitude due to propagation effects. Data type: VARCHAR(45). If no fixed categories, example: 'MildScintillation'.
SignalDynamics.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-JKL-3456'.
SignalDynamics.SpatStab: Full name: 'Spatial Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal is spatially (e.g., consistent direction). Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Moderate'.
SignalDynamics.TempStab: Full name: 'Temporal Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal remains over time. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Stable'.
SignalProbabilities.AnomScore: Full name: 'Anomaly Score'. Explanation: How unusual or unexpected the signal is. Data type: FLOAT. Example: '1.23'.
SignalProbabilities.ArtSrcProb: Full name: 'Artificial Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from an artificial source. Data type: NUMERIC(3,1). Example: '3.4'.
SignalProbabilities.BioSigProb: Full name: 'Biosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal indicates a biological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '45.21'.
SignalProbabilities.CorrScore: Full name: 'Correlation Score'. Explanation: How well the signal aligns with expected patterns. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.9950'.
SignalProbabilities.FalsePosProb: Full name: 'False Positive Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is falsely detected. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.0135'.
SignalProbabilities.NatSrcProb: Full name: 'Natural Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from a natural source. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '98.761'.
SignalProbabilities.SigUnique: Full name: 'Signal Uniqueness'. Explanation: A measure of how unique the signal is compared to others. Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '99.1234'.
SignalProbabilities.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-XYZ-9876'.
SignalProbabilities.SimIndex: Full name: 'Similarity Index'. Explanation: Compares the signal to known references. Data type: NUMERIC(5,4). Example: '0.8222'.
SignalProbabilities.TechSigProb: Full name: 'Technosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is of artificial technological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.6789'.
Signals.AtmoInterf: Full name: 'Atmospheric Interference'. Explanation: Impact of atmospheric conditions on signal. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
Signals.BwHz: Full name: 'Bandwidth (Hz)'. Explanation: Signal’s bandwidth in Hertz. Data type: DECIMAL(10,3). Example: '500000.000'.
Signals.CarrierFreqMhz: Full name: 'Carrier Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Frequency of the carrier wave in MHz. Data type: DECIMAL(9,3). Example: '1000.000'.
Signals.CenterFreqMhz: Full name: 'Center Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Center frequency of the detected signal in MHz. Data type: NUMERIC(8,3). Example: '1420.500'.
Signals.DetectInstr: Full name: 'Detection Instrument'. Explanation: The instrument type employed for detecting the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Infrared Array, Optical Telescope, Quantum Detector, Radio Telescope.
Signals.DoppShiftHz: Full name: 'Doppler Shift (Hz)'. Explanation: Measured Doppler shift of the signal in Hertz. Data type: DOUBLE PRECISION. Example: '142.75'.
Signals.FreqDriftHzs: Full name: 'Frequency Drift (Hz/s)'. Explanation: How fast the signal drifts in frequency over time. Data type: NUMERIC(9,3). Example: '0.123'.
Signals.FreqMhz: Full name: 'Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Signal’s nominal frequency in MHz. Data type: DECIMAL(9,3). Example: '1420.405'.
Signals.InterfLvl: Full name: 'Interference Level'. Explanation: Degree of interference around the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, None.
Signals.ModIndex: Full name: 'Modulation Index'. Explanation: Numerical index describing modulation depth. Data type: DECIMAL(6,4). Example: '0.2875'.
Signals.ModType: Full name: 'Modulation Type'. Explanation: The method of signal modulation. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: AM, FM, PM, QAM, Unknown.
Signals.NoiseFloorDbm: Full name: 'Noise Floor (dBm)'. Explanation: Measured noise floor in dBm. Data type: DOUBLE PRECISION. Example: '-85.3'.
Signals.PhaseShiftDeg: Full name: 'Phase Shift (°)'. Explanation: Phase shift in degrees for the signal. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '45.00'.
Signals.PolarAngleDeg: Full name: 'Polarization Angle (°)'. Explanation: Angle of polarization in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(5,1). Example: '90.0'.
Signals.PolarMode: Full name: 'Polarization Mode'. Explanation: Type of signal polarization. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Circular, Elliptical, Linear, Unknown.
Signals.PulsePerSec: Full name: 'Pulse Rate (pulses/sec)'. Explanation: Rate of pulse repetition in the signal. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '4.500'.
Signals.PulseWidMs: Full name: 'Pulse Width (ms)'. Explanation: Duration of each pulse in milliseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '2.300'.
Signals.RfiStat: Full name: 'RFI Status'. Explanation: Radio Frequency Interference status. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Clean, Contaminated, Unknown.
Signals.SigDurSec: Full name: 'Signal Duration (s)'. Explanation: Total duration of the signal in seconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '12.50'.
Signals.SigStrDb: Full name: 'Signal Strength (dB)'. Explanation: Measured strength of the signal in decibels. Data type: NUMERIC(7,2). Example: '12.35'.
Signals.SignalClass: Full name: 'Signal Type'. Explanation: Broad classification of the detected signal. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Broadband, Continuous, Modulated, Narrowband, Pulsed.
Signals.SignalRegistry: Full name: 'Signal Registry'. Explanation: Unique ID for each signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-123E4567-E89B'.
Signals.SnrRatio: Full name: 'Signal-to-Noise Ratio'. Explanation: SNR measured for the signal. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '18.75'.
Signals.TelescRef: Full name: 'Telescope Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key to the telescope used for detection. Data type: CHAR(20). Example: 'TELESC_0001'.
Signals.TimeMark: Full name: 'Timestamp'. Explanation: The moment of signal detection. In some CSVs, it may be stored as an Excel serial date/time (e.g., '44302.55648' ≈ 2021-05-16 13:20:20 UTC). Data type: TIMESTAMPTZ. Example: '2025-08-01 13:45:00+00'.
SourceProperties.CelestObj: Full name: 'Celestial Object'. Explanation: Broad classification of the object. Data type: VARCHAR(75). Possible categories: Galaxy, Planet, Star, Unknown.
SourceProperties.GalLat: Full name: 'Galactic Latitude (°)'. Explanation: Galactic latitude of the source. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '-5.67'.
SourceProperties.GalLong: Full name: 'Galactic Longitude (°)'. Explanation: Galactic longitude of the source. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '12.34'.
SourceProperties.ObjAgeGyr: Full name: 'Object Age (Gyr)'. Explanation: Estimated age in billions of years. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '4.500'.
SourceProperties.ObjMag: Full name: 'Apparent Magnitude'. Explanation: Brightness of the object as seen from Earth. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '7.35'.
SourceProperties.ObjMassSol: Full name: 'Object Mass (solar)'. Explanation: Mass relative to the Sun. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '1.005'.
SourceProperties.ObjMetal: Full name: 'Metallicity'. Explanation: Ratio of elements heavier than helium in the object. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.012'.
SourceProperties.ObjPropMotion: Full name: 'Proper Motion (mas/yr)'. Explanation: Apparent motion across the sky in milliarcseconds/year. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '55.12'.
SourceProperties.ObjRadVel: Full name: 'Radial Velocity (km/s)'. Explanation: Speed at which the object is moving toward/away from us. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '-23.45'.
SourceProperties.ObjTempK: Full name: 'Object Temperature (K)'. Explanation: Approximate surface temperature in Kelvin. Data type: INTEGER. Example: '5800'.
SourceProperties.ObjType: Full name: 'Object Subtype'. Explanation: More specific object type. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Dwarf, Giant, Main Sequence, Unknown.
SourceProperties.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-STU-5432'.
SourceProperties.SourceDecDeg: Full name: 'Declination (°)'. Explanation: Declination of the source in degrees (-90 to +90). Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '-20.4567'.
SourceProperties.SourceDistLy: Full name: 'Distance (ly)'. Explanation: Approximate distance to the source in light-years. Data type: NUMERIC(10,2). Example: '26000.45'.
SourceProperties.SourceRaDeg: Full name: 'Right Ascension (°)'. Explanation: RA of the source in degrees (0 to 360). Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '123.4567'.
Telescopes.BandUsagePct: Full name: 'Bandwidth Usage (%)'. Explanation: Network bandwidth usage as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '73.25'.
Telescopes.CalibrStatus: Full name: 'Calibration Status'. Explanation: Status of telescope’s calibration. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Current, Due, Overdue.
Telescopes.CoolSysStatus: Full name: 'Cooling System Status'. Explanation: Status of the telescope’s cooling system. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Critical, Normal, Warning.
Telescopes.DataStorStatus: Full name: 'Data Storage Status'. Explanation: Capacity and status of local data storage. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Available, Critical, Low.
Telescopes.DetectTempK: Full name: 'Detector Temperature (K)'. Explanation: Temperature of the telescope’s primary detector in Kelvin. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '123.45'.
Telescopes.EquipStatus: Full name: 'Equipment Status'. Explanation: Operational state of the telescope. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Degraded, Maintenance, Operational.
Telescopes.FocusQuality: Full name: 'Focus Quality'. Explanation: Quality of the telescope’s focusing system. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
Telescopes.NetStatus: Full name: 'Network Status'. Explanation: Status of the network connection for telescope data transfer. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Connected, Disconnected, Limited.
Telescopes.ObservStation: Full name: 'Observatory Name Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key linking to the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
Telescopes.PointAccArc: Full name: 'Pointing Accuracy (arcsec)'. Explanation: How precise the telescope can point, in arcseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '0.45'.
Telescopes.PowerStatus: Full name: 'Power Supply Status'. Explanation: Indicates which power source or level is in use. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Backup, Critical, Main.
Telescopes.ProcQueueStatus: Full name: 'Processing Queue Status'. Explanation: Indicates how full the processing queue is. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Empty, Full, Normal.
Telescopes.TelescRegistry: Full name: 'Telescope Registry'. Explanation: A unique identifier for the telescope. Data type: CHAR(20). Example: 'TELESC_0001'.
Telescopes.TrackAccArc: Full name: 'Tracking Accuracy (arcsec)'. Explanation: How accurately the telescope can track a target, in arcseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '1.20'.
observationalconditions.obsdate: Local date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD)
observationalconditions.obsdurhrs: How long the observation lasted in hours

requests.specific_A: Link each sentiment snapshot to its transaction record (`transref` = `transreg`) and to that record's trader (`trdref` = `tradereg`), dropping snapshots without both matches. For each combination of transaction reference (`transref`) and trader type (`tradekind`), compute the average option volume ratio (`optvolrt`). Take as the baseline the plain average of these per-combination averages, with each combination counting equally. Each combination's deviation is its average minus the baseline (no rows if the baseline is missing). Within each trader type, average those deviations. Keep only the combinations whose deviation is above their trader type's average deviation, and give each one an excess: its deviation minus the type's average deviation. Combinations with no trader type get a deviation too but are dropped at this comparison. Finally, for each trader type, report the type, the average of the kept combinations' average option volume ratios, the average of their deviations, and the average of their excess. Averages ignore missing values. No rounding.
requests.specific_B: Link each sentiment snapshot to its transaction record (`transref` = `transreg`) and to that record's trader (`trdref` = `tradereg`), dropping snapshots without both matches. For each combination of transaction reference (`transref`) and trader type (`tradekind`), compute the average option volume ratio (`optvolrt`). Take as the baseline the plain average of `optvolrt` over all sentiment snapshots, including those without a matching transaction or trader. Each combination's deviation is its average minus the baseline (no rows if the baseline is missing). Within each trader type, average those deviations. Keep only the combinations whose deviation is above their trader type's average deviation, and give each one an excess: its deviation minus the type's average deviation. Combinations with no trader type get a deviation too but are dropped at this comparison. Finally, for each trader type, report the type, the average of the kept combinations' average option volume ratios, the average of their deviations, and the average of their excess. Averages ignore missing values. No rounding.
requests.open: Link each sentiment snapshot to its transaction record (`transref` = `transreg`) and that record's trader (`trdref` = `tradereg`), keeping only full matches, and compute the average option volume ratio (`optvolrt`) for each transaction reference and trader type (`tradekind`) pair. Measure each pair's deviation from the overall average option volume ratio (no rows if that's missing). Then, within each trader type, keep only the pairs whose deviation beats the type's average deviation, and note by how much (pairs with no trader type drop out at this step). For each trader type, what are the average option volume ratio, the average deviation and the average excess of those pairs? Averages ignore missing values. Don't round.

readings.A: The overall average option volume ratio is the average of the transaction-reference and trader-type combination averages.
readings.B: The overall average option volume ratio is the plain average of the option volume ratio across every sentiment snapshot.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "sentimentandfundamentals"."transref" AS "e", "trader"."tradekind" AS "g", AVG("sentimentandfundamentals"."optvolrt") AS "m1" FROM "sentimentandfundamentals" AS "sentimentandfundamentals" INNER JOIN "transactionrecord" AS "transactionrecord" ON "transactionrecord"."transreg" = "sentimentandfundamentals"."transref" INNER JOIN "trader" AS "trader" ON "trader"."tradereg" = "transactionrecord"."trdref" GROUP BY "sentimentandfundamentals"."transref", "trader"."tradekind"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3" GROUP BY "s3"."g"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON "s3"."g" = "s4"."g" WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT "s5"."g" AS "g", AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5" GROUP BY "s5"."g"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "sentimentandfundamentals"."transref" AS "e", "trader"."tradekind" AS "g", AVG("sentimentandfundamentals"."optvolrt") AS "m1" FROM "sentimentandfundamentals" AS "sentimentandfundamentals" INNER JOIN "transactionrecord" AS "transactionrecord" ON "transactionrecord"."transreg" = "sentimentandfundamentals"."transref" INNER JOIN "trader" AS "trader" ON "trader"."tradereg" = "transactionrecord"."trdref" GROUP BY "sentimentandfundamentals"."transref", "trader"."tradekind"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("sentimentandfundamentals"."optvolrt") AS "v" FROM "sentimentandfundamentals" AS "sentimentandfundamentals"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3" GROUP BY "s3"."g"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON "s3"."g" = "s4"."g" WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT "s5"."g" AS "g", AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5" GROUP BY "s5"."g"

shared_requirements.requirement: Link each sentiment snapshot to its transaction record (`transref` = `transreg`), then link that record to its trader (`trdref` = `tradereg`). Use inner joins and drop snapshots without both matches.
Group by transaction reference (`transref`) and trader type (`tradekind`). For each combination, compute the average option volume ratio (`optvolrt`), ignoring missing values.
Each combination's deviation is its average minus one overall baseline value. If the baseline is missing, return no rows.

Within each trader type, average the deviations. Keep only combinations whose deviation is strictly greater than their type's average deviation. For each kept combination, the excess is its deviation minus the type's average deviation. Combinations with no trader type get a deviation but are dropped at this comparison.
Final rows have one row per trader type. First column: the trader type.
Second column: the average of the kept combinations' average option volume ratios.
Third column: the average of the kept combinations' deviations.
Fourth column: the average of the kept combinations' excess.
Averages ignore missing values. No rounding, ordering or limit.

A.requirement: The baseline is the plain average of the per-combination average option volume ratios, with each combination weighted equally.

B.requirement: The baseline is the plain average of `optvolrt` over all sentiment snapshots, including snapshots without a matching transaction or trader.

choice_kind: average of ratios vs ratio of totals

requests.specific_A: Match each scan in `scans` to its site in `sites` on site code (`zoneref` = `zoneregistry`), leaving out scans whose site code isn't found. Group by the site's health and safety status (`healtheval`). For each status, compute the total of `scancount` and a GB-per-minute rate obtained by first dividing each scan's own `gbsize` by its own `spanmin` and then taking the mean of those per-scan ratios. Missing values are ignored in sums and averages. Compute the average of that rate across all statuses and keep only the statuses whose rate is strictly above it (none if that average is missing). List the status, the total scan count, the rate, and the rate minus that average. No rounding.
requests.specific_B: Match each scan in `scans` to its site in `sites` on site code (`zoneref` = `zoneregistry`), leaving out scans whose site code isn't found. Group by the site's health and safety status (`healtheval`). For each status, compute the total of `scancount` and a GB-per-minute rate obtained by adding up all the status's `gbsize` and dividing that by the sum of all its `spanmin` (a ratio of totals, not an average of per-scan ratios). Missing values are ignored in sums and averages. Compute the average of that rate across all statuses and keep only the statuses whose rate is strictly above it (none if that average is missing). List the status, the total scan count, the rate, and the rate minus that average. No rounding.
requests.open: For scans matched to their site (skip any whose site code isn't in `sites`), break things down by the site's health and safety status (`healtheval`). For each status, show the total number of scans (`scancount`) and the GB per minute of scanning, based on `gbsize` and `spanmin`, ignoring missing values. Only include statuses whose GB per minute is strictly above the average of that figure across statuses (none if that average is missing). Show the status, the total scans, the GB per minute, and how much it exceeds that average. No rounding.

readings.A: Compute GB per minute for each scan, then average those ratios within each health/safety status.
readings.B: Divide each status's total gbsize by its total spanmin.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "sites"."healtheval" AS "g", SUM("scans"."scancount") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("scans"."gbsize" AS REAL) / "scans"."spanmin")) AS "m2" FROM "scans" AS "scans" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scans"."zoneref" GROUP BY "sites"."healtheval"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "sites"."healtheval" AS "g", SUM("scans"."scancount") AS "m1", (CAST(SUM("scans"."gbsize") AS REAL) / SUM("scans"."spanmin")) AS "m2" FROM "scans" AS "scans" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scans"."zoneref" GROUP BY "sites"."healtheval"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from `scans` and inner-join to `sites` on `sites.zoneregistry` = `scans.zoneref`. Drop unmatched scans. Group by `sites.healtheval`.
The health and safety status (`healtheval`).
Sum of `scancount` in the group, ignoring missing values.
Average of the per-status rate across all statuses. If that average is missing, no rows are returned.
Keep only statuses whose rate is strictly greater than that average.
Rate − the average rate.
No rounding. No ordering or limit.

A.requirement: Rate = the average of the per-scan ratios `gbsize` ÷ `spanmin`, ignoring missing ratios.

B.requirement: Rate = SUM(`gbsize`) ÷ SUM(`spanmin`) over the group.

requests.specific_A: Looking only at films that have at least one copy in inventory (films with no copies are left out completely, including from every average), count each film's inventory copies. For each film, show its id, its rating, its number of copies, its copy count minus the average copy count per film for films of the same rating, and its copy count minus the overall average copy count per film (averaged over the individual films, not over the rating averages; averages ignore missing values). Sort by the difference from the overall average, largest first, and keep the top 10 (ties broken arbitrarily). Do not round.
requests.specific_B: Looking at every film in the catalogue (a film with no copies in inventory counts as having 0 copies, and that 0 is included in every average), count each film's inventory copies. For each film, show its id, its rating, its number of copies, its copy count minus the average copy count per film for films of the same rating, and its copy count minus the overall average copy count per film (averaged over the individual films, not over the rating averages; averages ignore missing values). Sort by the difference from the overall average, largest first, and keep the top 10 (ties broken arbitrarily). Do not round.
requests.open: Which 10 films have the most inventory copies compared with the average number of copies per film? For each, show the film id, its rating, its number of copies, how far that is from the average copies per film for its rating, and how far it is from the overall average copies per film (averaged over films, not over the rating averages; averages ignore missing values). Sort by the overall difference, largest first. Ties can go in any order, and nothing is rounded.

readings.A: Average copies per film (per rating and overall) are computed only over films that have at least one copy in inventory. Films with no copies are excluded.
readings.B: Average copies per film (per rating and overall) are computed over every film in the catalogue. Films with no copies in inventory count as having 0 copies.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "inventory"."film_id" AS "e", "film"."rating" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "inventory" AS "inventory" INNER JOIN "film" AS "film" ON "film"."film_id" = "inventory"."film_id" GROUP BY "inventory"."film_id", "film"."rating"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "film"."film_id" AS "e", "film"."rating" AS "g", COUNT("inventory"."inventory_id") AS "m1" FROM "film" AS "film" LEFT JOIN "inventory" AS "inventory" ON "film"."film_id" = "inventory"."film_id" GROUP BY "film"."film_id", "film"."rating"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: One row per film, holding that film's number of physical copies in `inventory`
Inventory copies are matched to films on `film_id`. The film's `rating` comes from `film`
Film id
Film rating
Number of inventory copies of the film
The film's copy count minus the average copy count per film among films with the same rating. This is the average of per-film counts in that rating, with missing values ignored

requests.specific_A: For each product (`product_id` on the order items), count the order-item lines. Give each product a share: its count divided by the sum over all products. Then take the plain average of those shares across products. For the products whose share is strictly above that average, return a single unrounded row with: their combined count, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the overall average share.
requests.specific_B: For each product (`product_id` on the order items), add up the units ordered (`product_quantity`, read as a whole number, ignoring missing values). Give each product a share: its units divided by the sum over all products. Then take the plain average of those shares across products. For the products whose share is strictly above that average, return a single unrounded row with: their combined units, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the overall average share.
requests.open: Looking at the order items, work out each product's (`product_id`) share of total order volume and the plain average of those shares across products. For the products whose share is strictly above that average, give me one unrounded row: their combined order volume, their average share, and how far, on average, their share sits above the average share.

readings.A: A product's figure is how many order lines it appears on.
readings.B: A product's figure is the total units ordered across its order lines.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Order_Items"."product_id" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "Order_Items" AS "Order_Items" GROUP BY "Order_Items"."product_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Order_Items"."product_id" AS "e", SUM(CAST("Order_Items"."product_quantity" AS INTEGER)) AS "m1" FROM "Order_Items" AS "Order_Items" GROUP BY "Order_Items"."product_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from advanced behaviour records (`advancedbehavior`).

Inner join each behaviour record to the transaction where `transreg` = `translink`, then to the trader where `tradereg` = `trdref`. All comparisons are exact text, and anything without a match is dropped.
Group by trader type (`tradekind`). A missing type forms its own group. Return the type.
The share: the group's count divided by the total of the counts across all groups, unrounded.
Keep only the types whose share is strictly greater than the plain average of the per-type shares. Return no rows if that average is missing.
The share minus the average share, unrounded.
Output columns in this order: type, count, share, excess share. No ordering and no rounding.

A.requirement: The count is the number of joined behaviour records. Several behaviour records on the same transaction each count.

B.requirement: The count is the number of distinct transactions (`transreg`) reached through behaviour records. Each transaction counts once.

requests.specific_A: Group the fee records by order (`orderslink`); fee records with no order form one group of their own. For each order, work out the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`). For the benchmark, take the mean of those per-order average net fee rates, with each order counting once. For the orders whose average net fee rate is above this benchmark, return a single row with: the average of their average total rebates, the average of their average net fee rates, and the average amount by which their average net fee rate exceeds the benchmark. Skip missing values in every average, and don't round the results.
requests.specific_B: Group the fee records by order (`orderslink`); fee records with no order form one group of their own. For each order, work out the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`). For the benchmark, take the average net fee rate over all fee records directly, so an order counts once for each fee record it has. For the orders whose average net fee rate is above this benchmark, return a single row with: the average of their average total rebates, the average of their average net fee rates, and the average amount by which their average net fee rate exceeds the benchmark. Skip missing values in every average, and don't round the results.
requests.open: Looking at fees per order (`orderslink`, with fee records that have no order treated as one group), which orders have an average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`) above the overall average net fee rate? For those orders, give me one row: the mean of their average total rebate (`rebtotal`), the mean of their average net fee rate, and the mean amount by which they exceed the overall average net fee rate. Skip missing values in the averages and don't round anything.

readings.A: The benchmark is the average of the per-order average net fee rates, with each order weighted equally.
readings.B: The benchmark is the average net fee rate over all individual fee records, so orders with more fee records weigh more.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "fees"."orderslink" AS "e", AVG("fees"."rebtotal") AS "m1", AVG(("fees"."feerate" - "fees"."rebrate")) AS "m2" FROM "fees" AS "fees" GROUP BY "fees"."orderslink"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "fees"."orderslink" AS "e", AVG("fees"."rebtotal") AS "m1", AVG(("fees"."feerate" - "fees"."rebrate")) AS "m2" FROM "fees" AS "fees" GROUP BY "fees"."orderslink"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG(("fees"."feerate" - "fees"."rebrate")) AS "v" FROM "fees" AS "fees"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from all `fees` records and group them by order link (`fees.orderslink`). Fee records with no order link form one group of their own.
For each order group, compute the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`). Averages skip missing values and are missing if the group has no values.
Compare each order's average net fee rate with an overall benchmark net fee rate. Keep only orders strictly above the benchmark. If the benchmark is missing, keep no orders.
Collapse the kept orders into a single row. Each output is an average over the kept orders that skips missing values. No rounding.
The average of the kept orders' average total rebate.
The average of the kept orders' average net fee rate.
The average of (the order's average net fee rate minus the benchmark) over the kept orders.

A.requirement: The benchmark is the mean of the per-order average net fee rates. Each order counts once.

B.requirement: The benchmark is the mean of (`feerate` - `rebrate`) taken directly over all fee records. An order counts once per fee record it has.

requests.specific_A: Considering only payments that link to a rental record, credit each payment to the staff member who handled that rental (`rental.staff_id`). For each such staff member, return the staff ID, the total payment `amount`, and that total as a fraction of the combined total across all staff members. Do not round anything.
requests.specific_B: Considering only payments that link to a rental record, credit each payment to the staff member who processed the payment (`payment.staff_id`). For each such staff member, return the staff ID, the total payment `amount`, and that total as a fraction of the combined total across all staff members. Do not round anything.
requests.open: For payments that link to a rental, how much payment revenue does each staff member bring in? Show the staff ID, their total payment `amount`, and that total as a fraction of the combined total across all staff. No rounding.

readings.A: Each payment is credited to the staff member recorded on the rental it pays for.
readings.B: Each payment is credited to the staff member recorded on the payment itself as having processed it.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "rental"."staff_id" AS "g", SUM("payment"."amount") AS "m1" FROM "payment" AS "payment" INNER JOIN "rental" AS "rental" ON "rental"."rental_id" = "payment"."rental_id" GROUP BY "rental"."staff_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "payment"."staff_id" AS "g", SUM("payment"."amount") AS "m1" FROM "payment" AS "payment" INNER JOIN "rental" AS "rental" ON "rental"."rental_id" = "payment"."rental_id" GROUP BY "payment"."staff_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from payment records.
Inner-join payment to rental on payment.rental_id = rental.rental_id. Drop payments with no matching rental.
Group by a staff id (which one is the choice). Return one row per staff member.
The staff ID.
The sum of payment.amount for that staff member.
That sum divided by the total of the sums over all staff members. Columns appear in this order, with no rounding and no ordering required.

A.requirement: Credit each payment to rental.staff_id, the staff member who handled the linked rental.

B.requirement: Credit each payment to payment.staff_id, the staff member who processed the payment.

VERIFIED ON THE DATA (these override the descriptions above):
film.rating: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns exactly 5 rating levels, each covering roughly 180-225 films, so every group is well populated and rating works as a grouping class. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate), AVG(length), AVG(replacement_cost) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '3.0348430493273613', '120.4439461883408', '20.402556053811544'], ['NC-17', '210', '2.970952380952388', '113.22857142857143', '20.137619047618937'], ['R', '195', '2.9387179487179553', '118.66153846153846', '20.23102564102554'], ['PG', '194', '3.051855670103099', '112.00515463917526', '18.959072164948356'], ['G', '178', '2.888876404494388', '111.0505617977528', '20.12483146067407']] scale (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows exactly 5 levels: G, PG, PG-13, R and NC-17. These are the standard MPAA bands, which are ordered by audience restriction, so the column is an ordinal class. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY rating -> [['G', '178'], ['NC-17', '210'], ['PG', '194'], ['PG-13', '223'], ['R', '195']]
category.name: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 16 genres, each shared by many films (about 50-75 each), so the column is a grouping label and does not identify single records. Evidence: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film_category fc JOIN category c ON c.category_id = fc.category_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY films DESC -> [['Sports', '74'], ['Foreign', '73'], ['Family', '69'], ['Documentary', '68'], ['Animation', '66'], ['Action', '64']]
customer.store_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 2 stores with about 300 customers each, so the column is a grouping label shared by many rows. Evidence: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS customers, SUM(active) AS active_customers FROM customer GROUP BY store_id -> [['1', '326', '318'], ['2', '273', '266']]
inventory.store_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 2 store values over 4581 copies, about 2270 per store, so the column is a grouping label. Evidence: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS copies, COUNT(DISTINCT film_id) AS titles FROM inventory GROUP BY store_id -> [['1', '2270', '759'], ['2', '2311', '762']]
country.country: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Many customers share a country (the top countries have dozens of customers each), so country works as a grouping attribute for customers. Evidence: SELECT co.country, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customer cu JOIN address a ON a.address_id = cu.address_id JOIN city ci ON ci.city_id = a.city_id JOIN country co ON co.country_id = ci.country_id GROUP BY co.country ORDER BY customers DESC LIMIT 10 -> [['India', '60'], ['China', '53'], ['United States', '36'], ['Japan', '31'], ['Mexico', '30'], ['Russian Federation', '28']]
film.special_features: desc (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 15 distinct values, all of them combinations of the same 4 feature names (for example 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes'). The column is a set, not a single category. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']] semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows 15 distinct values, all combinations of the same 4 feature names, such as 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes' and 'Trailers,Commentaries'. The column is a set, not a single class, so it should not be offered as a grouping. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']]
film.length: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified rating query already returns AVG(length) between 111.05 (G) and 120.44 (PG-13). The catalogue profile gives 140 distinct values from 46 to 185 minutes. So length is a continuous ratio-scale quantity whose group averages can be read directly. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(length) AS avg_minutes, MIN(length), MAX(length) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '120.4439461883408', '46', '185'], ['NC-17', '210', '113.22857142857143', '46', '184'], ['R', '195', '118.66153846153846', '49', '185'], ['PG', '194', '112.00515463917526', '46', '185'], ['G', '178', '111.0505617977528', '47', '185']]
film.rental_duration: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows 5 values from 3 to 7 days, all well above zero, so the column is a ratio-scale number of days per film. The query shows how many films fall at each value. Evidence: SELECT rental_duration, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate) AS avg_rate FROM film GROUP BY rental_duration ORDER BY rental_duration -> [['3', '203', '2.8323645320197115'], ['4', '203', '2.97029556650247'], ['5', '191', '3.19942408376964'], ['6', '212', '2.895660377358497'], ['7', '191', '3.021413612565451']]
film.rental_rate: desc (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows rental_rate takes only 0.99, 2.99 and 4.99, while replacement_cost runs from 9.99 to 29.99. The query shows how large and uniform the gap is. The auditor noted that the difference is always about −17 and the relative gap about −0.85, which fits two different quantities rather than one price seen two ways. Evidence: SELECT MIN(replacement_cost - rental_rate), MAX(replacement_cost - rental_rate), AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) FROM film -> [['5.0', '29.0', '0.16651517608314595']]
film.replacement_cost: quantity (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The column holds a per-copy value that becomes meaningful when summed over physical copies in inventory, for example as stock value. That is the reading of an asset value, not of a price charged per rental. Evidence: SELECT f.rating, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copies, SUM(f.replacement_cost) AS stock_value FROM inventory i JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating -> [['G', '791', '16185.089999999853'], ['NC-17', '944', '19128.56000000009'], ['PG', '924', '17755.759999999962'], ['PG-13', '1018', '21052.82000000024'], ['R', '904', '18498.960000000006']]
payment.staff_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows only 2 distinct values (1 and 2) across 16,049 payments. Each value is therefore shared by thousands of rows, which makes it a grouping label rather than a record identifier. Evidence: SELECT staff_id, COUNT(*) AS payments, SUM(amount) AS revenue, AVG(amount) FROM payment GROUP BY staff_id -> [['1', '8057', '33489.470000005174', '4.156568201564499'], ['2', '7992', '33927.04000000482', '4.245125125125728']]
rental.staff_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows only 2 distinct values across 16,044 rentals, so each staff value covers thousands of rentals and works as a grouping class. Evidence: SELECT staff_id, COUNT(*) AS rentals, SUM(CASE WHEN return_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unreturned FROM rental GROUP BY staff_id -> [['1', '8040', '85'], ['2', '8004', '98']]

requests.specific_A: For each project (`arcref`) in the QC data, count its QC records. Work out its share as that count divided by the total over all projects. Compute the deviation as the share minus the average share across projects. List the project, the count, the share and the deviation, with no rounding, sorted by deviation from highest to lowest (missing last). Return exactly the first 10 rows, cutting through any tie at the 10th place.
requests.specific_B: For each project (`arcref`) in the QC data, count its QC records. Work out its share as that count divided by the total over all projects. Compute the deviation as the share minus the average share across projects. List the project, the count, the share and the deviation, with no rounding, sorted by deviation from highest to lowest (missing last). Return every project whose deviation is at least the 10th-highest deviation, including all projects tied with the 10th.
requests.open: For each project (`arcref`) in the QC data, count its QC records. Work out its share as that count divided by the total over all projects. Compute the deviation as the share minus the average share across projects. Show the top 10 projects by deviation, highest first (missing last), with the project, the count, the share and the deviation, and no rounding.

readings.A: Rank projects by how far their share of QC records is above the average share, and return exactly 10 rows, cutting through any tie at the cutoff.
readings.B: Rank projects by how far their share of QC records is above the average share, and return every project whose deviation is at least the 10th-highest, including ties.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scanqc"."arcref" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "scanqc" AS "scanqc" GROUP BY "scanqc"."arcref"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scanqc"."arcref" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "scanqc" AS "scanqc" GROUP BY "scanqc"."arcref"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") >= (SELECT MIN("t"."d") FROM (SELECT ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "d" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10) AS "t") ORDER BY ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") DESC

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every row of `scanqc`. Group by project reference (`scanqc.arcref`) and count the QC records in each project.

Pair each project row with the total, which is the sum of the counts over all projects. Then pair it with the average share across projects. A project row is dropped only if the total or the average is missing.
First column: the project reference (`arcref`).
Second column: the number of QC records for the project.
Third column: the share, which is the project's count divided by the total count over all projects. Not rounded.
Fourth column: the deviation, which is the share minus the average share across projects. Not rounded.
Order by deviation, highest first, with missing values last.
The cutoff is set at the 10th-highest deviation.

A.requirement: Return exactly 10 rows. If projects tie at the cutoff, cut through the tie group arbitrarily.

B.requirement: Return every project whose deviation is at least the 10th-highest deviation. This includes all projects tied with the 10th.

context.documentation:
Equipment.EquipDesign: Full name: 'Equipment Model'. Explanation: Model name or identifier. Data type: VARCHAR(14). Example: 'Model-669'.
Equipment.EquipForm: Full name: 'Equipment Type'. Explanation: Type or category of scanning equipment. Data type: VARCHAR(28). Possible categories: LiDAR, Structured Light, Photogrammetry, Laser.
Equipment.EquipRegistry: Full name: 'Equipment ID'. Explanation: Primary key for equipment. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
Equipment.EquipStatus: Full name: 'Equipment Condition'. Explanation: Overall condition of the equipment. Data type: VARCHAR(16). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor.
Equipment.EquipTune: Full name: 'Calibration Date'. Explanation: Date the equipment was last calibrated. Data type: DATE. Example: '2024-11-01'.
Equipment.PowerLevel: Full name: 'Battery Level (%)'. Explanation: Battery level as an integer percentage. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 62.
Personnel.CrewLabel: Full name: 'Operator Name'. Explanation: Name or label for the operator. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Example: 'Joel Wallace'.
Personnel.CrewRegistry: Full name: 'Operator ID'. Explanation: Primary key for Personnel, representing an operator. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
Personnel.LeadLabel: Full name: 'Supervisor Name'. Explanation: Name of the supervisor. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Example: 'Michael Kaiser'.
Personnel.LeadRegistry: Full name: 'Supervisor ID'. Explanation: Identifies a supervisor. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'SV7658'.
Projects.ArcRegistry: Full name: 'Project ID'. Explanation: Primary key for Projects, a unique project identifier. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
Projects.AuthHalt: Full name: 'Permit Expiry Date'. Explanation: Date on which the permit expires. Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-12-05'.
Projects.AuthPin: Full name: 'Permit Number'. Explanation: Authorization or permit ID. Data type: CHAR(6). Example: 'PMT4719'.
Projects.FundFlux: Full name: 'Funding Source'. Explanation: Source of funds for the project. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Government'.
Projects.VesselTag: Full name: 'Project Name'. Explanation: Label or name for the project. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Example: 'Project Happy'.
ScanConservation.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Associates conservation data with a project. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanConservation.CureRank: Full name: 'Conservation Priority'. Explanation: Priority level for conservation efforts. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Critical, Low, High.

ScanConservation.HarmAssess: Full name: 'Damage Assessment'. Explanation: Indicates severity of damage. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: None, Moderate, Severe.
ScanConservation.IntervHistory: Full name: 'Intervention History'. Explanation: Past restoration or intervention records. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: None, Major, Minor.
ScanConservation.PriorDocs: Full name: 'Previous Documentation'. Explanation: Level of existing documentation. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: None, Partial, Complete.
ScanConservation.StructState: Full name: 'Structural Stability'. Explanation: Stability level of the structure. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Stable, Moderate, Unstable.
ScanConservation.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Associates conservation data with a site code. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanEnvironment.AirRegistry: Full name: 'Environment Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for environment data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 1001.
ScanEnvironment.AmbicTemp: Full name: 'Ambient Temperature (C)'. Explanation: Air temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 25.3.
ScanEnvironment.EquipRef: Full name: 'Equipment Reference'. Explanation: Identifies which equipment these environment data refer to. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
ScanEnvironment.GeoSignal: Full name: 'GPS Signal Quality'. Explanation: Quality rating for GPS reception. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: None, Poor, Good, Excellent.
ScanEnvironment.HumePct: Full name: 'Relative Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 60.4.
ScanEnvironment.IllumeLux: Full name: 'Light Conditions (lux)'. Explanation: Measured illumination in lux. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 86054.

ScanMesh.TexDist: Full name: 'Texture Resolution Setting'. Explanation: Preset texture resolution. Data type: VARCHAR(5). Possible categories: 2K, 1K, 4K.
