requests.specific_A: Link each signal to its telescope and that telescope's observatory, dropping signals that don't match. For each telescope and weather profile (`weathprofile`), work out the average modulation index and the average phase shift. Keep the telescope/weather groups whose average modulation index is above the mean of those group averages, with each group counting equally. Then for each weather profile, return the weather profile, the average of the kept groups' average modulation index, the average of their average phase shift, and the average amount by which their modulation index is above that baseline. Don't round anything.
requests.specific_B: Link each signal to its telescope and that telescope's observatory, dropping signals that don't match. For each telescope and weather profile (`weathprofile`), work out the average modulation index and the average phase shift. Keep the telescope/weather groups whose average modulation index is above the average modulation index across all linked signals, with each signal counting equally. Then for each weather profile, return the weather profile, the average of the kept groups' average modulation index, the average of their average phase shift, and the average amount by which their modulation index is above that baseline. Don't round anything.
requests.open: Linking signals to their telescopes and observatories (signals that don't match are dropped), find the average modulation index and average phase shift for each telescope and weather profile (`weathprofile`). Keep the telescope/weather groups whose modulation index is above the overall average modulation index. Then, per weather profile, show the average modulation index and average phase shift of those groups, and how far above the overall average they are on average. Don't round anything.

readings.A: The baseline is the average of the group-level averages, with every telescope/weather group counting equally.
readings.B: The baseline is the average modulation index over all linked signals, with every signal counting equally.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "signals"."telescref" AS "e", "observatories"."weathprofile" AS "g", AVG("signals"."modindex") AS "m1", AVG("signals"."phaseshiftdeg") AS "m2" FROM "signals" AS "signals" INNER JOIN "telescopes" AS "telescopes" ON "telescopes"."telescregistry" = "signals"."telescref" INNER JOIN "observatories" AS "observatories" ON "observatories"."observstation" = "telescopes"."observstation" GROUP BY "signals"."telescref", "observatories"."weathprofile"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" GROUP BY "s3"."g"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "signals"."telescref" AS "e", "observatories"."weathprofile" AS "g", AVG("signals"."modindex") AS "m1", AVG("signals"."phaseshiftdeg") AS "m2" FROM "signals" AS "signals" INNER JOIN "telescopes" AS "telescopes" ON "telescopes"."telescregistry" = "signals"."telescref" INNER JOIN "observatories" AS "observatories" ON "observatories"."observstation" = "telescopes"."observstation" GROUP BY "signals"."telescref", "observatories"."weathprofile"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("signals"."modindex") AS "v" FROM "signals" AS "signals" INNER JOIN "telescopes" AS "telescopes" ON "telescopes"."telescregistry" = "signals"."telescref" INNER JOIN "observatories" AS "observatories" ON "observatories"."observstation" = "telescopes"."observstation"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" GROUP BY "s3"."g"

shared_requirements.requirement: Link each signal to its telescope (`signals.telescref` = `telescopes.telescregistry`) and that telescope to its observatory (`observstation`), using inner joins so signals without a match are dropped

Group by telescope reference and observatory weather profile (`weathprofile`); compute the average modulation index (`modindex`) and average phase shift (`phaseshiftdeg`) per group, ignoring missing values
Keep only telescope/weather groups whose average modulation index is strictly greater than the baseline, and compute how far above the baseline each one is
Group the kept telescope/weather groups by weather profile, one result row per weather profile
Weather profile
Average of the kept groups' average modulation index
Average of the kept groups' average phase shift
Average amount by which the kept groups' average modulation index exceeds the baseline; no rounding of any output

A.requirement: Baseline = the mean of the per-telescope/weather-group average modulation indexes, with every group counting equally

B.requirement: Baseline = the average modulation index over all linked signals, with every signal counting equally

context.schema:
CREATE TABLE "observationalconditions" (
  "signalref" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "obstime" text(6),
  "obsdate" text,
  "obsdurhrs" real(5,2),
  CONSTRAINT "observationalconditions_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalref"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_observcond_signalsref" FOREIGN KEY ("signalref") REFERENCES "signals" ("signalregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "observatories" (
  "observstation" text(60) NOT NULL,
  "weathprofile" text(40),
  "seeingprofile" text(50),
  "atmostransparency" real(5,3),
  "lunarstage" text(25),
  "lunardistdeg" real(7,2),
  "solarstatus" text(35),
  "geomagstatus" text(35),
  "sidereallocal" text(8),
  "airtempc" real(5,2),
  "humidityrate" real(6,3),
  "windspeedms" real(4,2),
  "presshpa" real(6,1),
  CONSTRAINT "observatories_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("observstation")
);
CREATE TABLE "researchprocess" (
  "signalref" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "analysisprio" text,
  "followstat" text(25),
  "peerrevstat" text(25),
  "pubstat" text(25),
  "resprio" text(30),
  "fundstat" text(30),
  "collabstat" text(35),
  "secclass" text(35),
  "discstat" text(40),
  "notesmemo" text,
  CONSTRAINT "researchprocess_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalref"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_researchprocess_signalsref" FOREIGN KEY ("signalref") REFERENCES "signals" ("signalregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "signaladvancedphenomena" (
  "signalref" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "intermedeffects" text(40),
  "gravlens" text(50),
  "quanteffects" text(85),
  "encryptevid" text(40),
  "langstruct" text,
  "msgcontent" text,
  "cultsig" text(60),
  "sciimpact" text(50),
  CONSTRAINT "signaladvancedphenomena_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalref"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_advanced_signal" FOREIGN KEY ("signalref") REFERENCES "signals" ("signalregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "signalclassification" (
  "signalref" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "sigclasstype" text(40),
  "sigpattern" text(60),
  "repeatcount" integer(16),
  "periodsec" real(12,3),
  "complexidx" real(6,3),
  "entropyval" real(6,2),
  "infodense" real(6,3),
  "classconf" real(5,2),
  CONSTRAINT "signalclassification_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalref"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_classification_signal" FOREIGN KEY ("signalref") REFERENCES "signals" ("signalregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "signaldecoding" (
  "signalref" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "encodetype" text(40),
  "compressratio" real(6,3),
  "errcorrlvl" text(35),
  "decodeconf" real(5,2),
  "decodemethod" text(35),
  "decodestat" text(25),
  "decodeiters" integer(16),
  "proctimehrs" real(6,2),
  "compresources" text(50),
  "analysisdp" text(25),
  "veriflvl" text(30),
  "confirmstat" text(30),
  CONSTRAINT "signaldecoding_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalref"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_decoding_signal" FOREIGN KEY ("signalref") REFERENCES "signals" ("signalregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "signaldynamics" (
  "signalref" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "sigintegrity" text(30),
  "sigrecurr" text(25),
  "sigevolve" text(25),
  "tempstab" text(20),
  "spatstab" text(20),
  "freqstab" text(35),
  "phasestab" text(35),
  "ampstab" text(20),
  "modstab" text(30),
  "sigcoherence" text(25),
  "sigdisp" text(25),
  "sigscint" text(45),
  CONSTRAINT "signaldynamics_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalref"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_dynamics_signal" FOREIGN KEY ("signalref") REFERENCES "signals" ("signalregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "signalprobabilities" (
  "signalref" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "falseposprob" real(5,4),
  "sigunique" real(7,4),
  "simindex" real(5,4),
  "corrscore" real(5,4),
  "anomscore" integer(53),
  "techsigprob" real(5,4),
  "biosigprob" real(6,2),
  "natsrcprob" real(7,3),
  "artsrcprob" real(3,1),
  CONSTRAINT "signalprobabilities_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalref"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_probabilities_signal" FOREIGN KEY ("signalref") REFERENCES "signals" ("signalregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "signals" (
  "signalregistry" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "timemark" text(6),
  "telescref" text(20) NOT NULL,
  "detectinstr" text(50),
  "signalclass" text(50),
  "sigstrdb" real(7,2),
  "freqmhz" real(9,3),
  "bwhz" real(10,3),
  "centerfreqmhz" real(8,3),
  "freqdrifthzs" real(9,3),
  "doppshifthz" integer(53),
  "sigdursec" real(6,2),
  "pulsepersec" real(6,3),
  "pulsewidms" real(6,3),
  "modtype" text(30),
  "modindex" real(6,4),
  "carrierfreqmhz" real(9,3),
  "phaseshiftdeg" real(6,2),
  "polarmode" text(30),
  "polarangledeg" real(5,1),
  "snrratio" real(6,2),
  "noisefloordbm" integer(53),
  "interflvl" text(30),
  "rfistat" text(30),
  "atmointerf" text(30),
  CONSTRAINT "signals_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_signals_telescopesref" FOREIGN KEY ("telescref") REFERENCES "telescopes" ("telescregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "sourceproperties" (
  "signalref" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "sourceradeg" real(7,4),
  "sourcedecdeg" real(7,4),
  "sourcedistly" real(10,2),
  "gallong" real(6,2),
  "gallat" real(6,2),
  "celestobj" text(75),
  "objtype" text(50),
  "objmag" real(5,2),
  "objtempk" integer(32),
  "objmasssol" real(6,3),
  "objagegyr" real(6,3),
  "objmetal" real(5,3),
  "objpropmotion" real(7,2),
  "objradvel" real(7,2),
  CONSTRAINT "sourceproperties_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalref"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_source_signal" FOREIGN KEY ("signalref") REFERENCES "signals" ("signalregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "telescopes" (
  "telescregistry" text(20) NOT NULL,
  "observstation" text(60) NOT NULL,
  "equipstatus" text(35),
  "calibrstatus" text(50),
  "pointaccarc" real(6,2),
  "trackaccarc" real(6,2),
  "focusquality" text(25),
  "detecttempk" real(7,2),
  "coolsysstatus" text(35),
  "powerstatus" text(30),
  "datastorstatus" text(35),
  "netstatus" text(40),
  "bandusagepct" real(5,2),
  "procqueuestatus" text(40),
  CONSTRAINT "telescopes_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("telescregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_telescopes_observatoriesref" FOREIGN KEY ("observstation") REFERENCES "observatories" ("observstation")
);
context.documentation:
ObservationalConditions.ObsDate: Full name: 'Observation Date'. Explanation: Local date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD). Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-08-01'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsDurHrs: Full name: 'Observation Duration (hours)'. Explanation: How long the observation lasted in hours. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '2.50'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsTime: Full name: 'Observation Time'. Explanation: Local time of the observation in HH:MM:SS. Data type: TIME. Example: '13:45:59'.
ObservationalConditions.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-PQR-9876'.
Observatories.AirTempC: Full name: 'Air Temperature (°C)'. Explanation: Ambient temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '18.45'.
Observatories.AtmosTransparency: Full name: 'Atmospheric Transparency'. Explanation: A numeric measure of how transparent the atmosphere is. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.867'.
Observatories.GeomagStatus: Full name: 'Geomagnetic Activity'. Explanation: The level of geomagnetic activity during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Active, Quiet, Storm.
Observatories.HumidityRate: Full name: 'Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Relative humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '62.300'.
Observatories.LunarDistDeg: Full name: 'Moon Distance (Degrees)'. Explanation: Angular distance to the Moon in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '97.52'.
Observatories.LunarStage: Full name: 'Lunar Phase'. Explanation: The current phase of the Moon during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: First Quarter, Full, Last Quarter, New.
Observatories.ObservStation: Full name: 'Observatory Name'. Explanation: This field holds the name or unique identifier for the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
Observatories.PressHpa: Full name: 'Pressure (hPa)'. Explanation: Atmospheric pressure in hectopascals. Data type: DECIMAL(6,1). Example: '1013.2'.
Observatories.SeeingProfile: Full name: 'Seeing Profile'. Explanation: Assessment of sky seeing conditions (atmospheric steadiness). Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
Observatories.SiderealLocal: Full name: 'Local Sidereal Time'. Explanation: Sidereal time at the observatory in HH:MM:SS format. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: '12:34:56'.
Observatories.SolarStatus: Full name: 'Solar Activity'. Explanation: The level of solar activity at the time of observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Moderate.
Observatories.WeathProfile: Full name: 'Weather Profile'. Explanation: A short description of weather conditions during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Clear, Cloudy, Partially Cloudy.
Observatories.WindSpeedMs: Full name: 'Wind Speed (m/s)'. Explanation: Wind speed in meters per second. Data type: NUMERIC(4,2). Example: '3.45'.
ResearchProcess.AnalysisPrio: Full name: 'Analysis Priority'. Explanation: Priority assigned for analyzing this signal. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, Urgent.
ResearchProcess.CollabStat: Full name: 'Collaboration Status'. Explanation: The nature of collaboration on this signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: International, Solo, Team.
ResearchProcess.DiscStat: Full name: 'Disclosure Status'. Explanation: How much information about the signal is shared publicly. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Full, None, Partial.
ResearchProcess.FollowStat: Full name: 'Follow-up Status'. Explanation: Status of any follow-up observations. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Required, Scheduled.
ResearchProcess.FundStat: Full name: 'Funding Status'. Explanation: Funding situation for further study. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Funded, Pending, Unfunded.
ResearchProcess.NotesMemo: Full name: 'Research Notes'. Explanation: Any extra remarks or context by researchers. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Project requires further funding...'
ResearchProcess.PeerRevStat: Full name: 'Peer Review Status'. Explanation: Where this signal stands in peer review. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, In Progress, Pending.
ResearchProcess.PubStat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether findings about the signal have been published. Data type: CHAR(25). Possible categories: Draft, Published, Submitted.
ResearchProcess.ResPrio: Full name: 'Research Priority'. Explanation: How urgently this signal needs scientific attention. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium.
ResearchProcess.SecClass: Full name: 'Security Classification'. Explanation: Visibility and clearance level for the data. Data type: CHAR(35). Possible categories: Classified, Public, Restricted.
ResearchProcess.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-MNO-7890'.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.CultSig: Full name: 'Cultural Significance'. Explanation: The level of cultural impact or interest. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: High, Low, None.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.EncryptEvid: Full name: 'Encryption Evidence'. Explanation: Whether there is indication the signal is encrypted. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: None, Possible, Strong.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.GravLens: Full name: 'Gravitational Lensing'. Explanation: Whether the signal is affected by gravitational lensing. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: None, Strong, Weak.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.InterMedEffects: Full name: 'Interstellar Medium Effects'. Explanation: Impact of interstellar medium on the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.LangStruct: Full name: 'Language Structure'. Explanation: Presence of linguistic or structured patterns. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Complex, None, Simple.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.MsgContent: Full name: 'Message Content'. Explanation: Indicates whether an actual message was detected. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Identified, None, Possible.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.QuantEffects: Full name: 'Quantum Effects'. Explanation: Quantum-level phenomena observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(85). Possible categories: None, Observed, Significant.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SciImpact: Full name: 'Scientific Impact'. Explanation: Significance of the signal to scientific research. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Major, Minor, Moderate.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-ABC-1234'.
SignalClassification.ClassConf: Full name: 'Classification Confidence (%)'. Explanation: How confident we are in the assigned signal class. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '92.50'.
SignalClassification.ComplexIdx: Full name: 'Complexity Index'. Explanation: Numeric measure of the signal’s complexity. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '5.678'.
SignalClassification.EntropyVal: Full name: 'Entropy'. Explanation: Entropy measurement of the signal. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.45'.
SignalClassification.InfoDense: Full name: 'Information Density'. Explanation: Estimated information per unit time/frequency. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.345'.
SignalClassification.PeriodSec: Full name: 'Period (s)'. Explanation: Duration of each cycle if periodic. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '12.345'.
SignalClassification.RepeatCount: Full name: 'Repetition Count'. Explanation: Number of times the signal has repeated. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '3'.
SignalClassification.SigClassType: Full name: 'Classification Type'. Explanation: High-level category for the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Artificial, Candidate, Natural, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SigPattern: Full name: 'Signal Pattern'. Explanation: Pattern observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: Periodic, Random, Structured, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-DEF-5678'.
SignalDecoding.AnalysisDp: Full name: 'Analysis Depth'. Explanation: How thoroughly the signal was analyzed. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Comprehensive, Detailed, Preliminary.
SignalDecoding.CompResources: Full name: 'Computational Resources'. Explanation: Level of computing power used. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Extreme, High, Low, Medium.
SignalDecoding.CompressRatio: Full name: 'Compression Ratio'. Explanation: Factor by which the raw signal data was compressed. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.500'.
SignalDecoding.ConfirmStat: Full name: 'Confirmation Status'. Explanation: Whether the decoding results have been confirmed. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Confirmed, Pending, Rejected.
SignalDecoding.DecodeConf: Full name: 'Decoding Confidence (%)'. Explanation: Confidence level that the decoding is correct. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '88.75'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeIters: Full name: 'Decoding Iterations'. Explanation: Number of algorithmic passes attempted. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '7'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeMethod: Full name: 'Decoding Method'. Explanation: Method used to decode the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: FFT, Neural Network, Quantum, Wavelet.
SignalDecoding.DecodeStat: Full name: 'Decoding Status'. Explanation: Status of the decoding process. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Failed, In Progress.
SignalDecoding.EncodeType: Full name: 'Encoding Type'. Explanation: The type of signal encoding used (e.g., Binary). Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Binary, Complex, Tertiary, Unknown.
SignalDecoding.ErrCorrLvl: Full name: 'Error Correction Level'. Explanation: Degree of error correction applied. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, None.
SignalDecoding.ProcTimeHrs: Full name: 'Processing Time (hours)'. Explanation: Total hours spent decoding. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.50'.
SignalDecoding.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal entry. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-GHI-9012'.
SignalDecoding.VerifLvl: Full name: 'Verification Level'. Explanation: Extent to which decoding has been verified. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Partially, Unverified, Verified.
SignalDynamics.AmpStab: Full name: 'Amplitude Stability'. Explanation: Consistency of signal amplitude. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Unstable'.
SignalDynamics.FreqStab: Full name: 'Frequency Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal’s frequency is. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighlyStable'.
SignalDynamics.ModStab: Full name: 'Modulation Stability'. Explanation: Consistency in the signal’s modulation scheme. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'Consistent'.
SignalDynamics.PhaseStab: Full name: 'Phase Stability'. Explanation: Any variation in signal phase. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'VaryingPhase'.
SignalDynamics.SigCoherence: Full name: 'Signal Coherence'. Explanation: How coherent the signal remains over its duration. Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighCoherence'.
SignalDynamics.SigDisp: Full name: 'Signal Dispersion'. Explanation: The degree to which the signal is dispersed (time/frequency smearing). Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'SignificantDisp'.
SignalDynamics.SigEvolve: Full name: 'Signal Evolution'. Explanation: Indicates if the signal changes/evolves during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Dynamic, Static, Unknown.
SignalDynamics.SigIntegrity: Full name: 'Signal Integrity'. Explanation: Rating of how intact or uncorrupted the signal is. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighIntegrity'.
SignalDynamics.SigRecurr: Full name: 'Signal Recurrence'. Explanation: Whether the signal recurs over time. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: None, Regular, Sporadic.
SignalDynamics.SigScint: Full name: 'Signal Scintillation'. Explanation: Fluctuation in signal amplitude due to propagation effects. Data type: VARCHAR(45). If no fixed categories, example: 'MildScintillation'.
SignalDynamics.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-JKL-3456'.
SignalDynamics.SpatStab: Full name: 'Spatial Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal is spatially (e.g., consistent direction). Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Moderate'.
SignalDynamics.TempStab: Full name: 'Temporal Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal remains over time. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Stable'.
SignalProbabilities.AnomScore: Full name: 'Anomaly Score'. Explanation: How unusual or unexpected the signal is. Data type: FLOAT. Example: '1.23'.
SignalProbabilities.ArtSrcProb: Full name: 'Artificial Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from an artificial source. Data type: NUMERIC(3,1). Example: '3.4'.
SignalProbabilities.BioSigProb: Full name: 'Biosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal indicates a biological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '45.21'.
SignalProbabilities.CorrScore: Full name: 'Correlation Score'. Explanation: How well the signal aligns with expected patterns. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.9950'.
SignalProbabilities.FalsePosProb: Full name: 'False Positive Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is falsely detected. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.0135'.
SignalProbabilities.NatSrcProb: Full name: 'Natural Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from a natural source. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '98.761'.
SignalProbabilities.SigUnique: Full name: 'Signal Uniqueness'. Explanation: A measure of how unique the signal is compared to others. Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '99.1234'.
SignalProbabilities.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-XYZ-9876'.
SignalProbabilities.SimIndex: Full name: 'Similarity Index'. Explanation: Compares the signal to known references. Data type: NUMERIC(5,4). Example: '0.8222'.
SignalProbabilities.TechSigProb: Full name: 'Technosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is of artificial technological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.6789'.
Signals.AtmoInterf: Full name: 'Atmospheric Interference'. Explanation: Impact of atmospheric conditions on signal. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
Signals.BwHz: Full name: 'Bandwidth (Hz)'. Explanation: Signal’s bandwidth in Hertz. Data type: DECIMAL(10,3). Example: '500000.000'.
Signals.CarrierFreqMhz: Full name: 'Carrier Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Frequency of the carrier wave in MHz. Data type: DECIMAL(9,3). Example: '1000.000'.
Signals.CenterFreqMhz: Full name: 'Center Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Center frequency of the detected signal in MHz. Data type: NUMERIC(8,3). Example: '1420.500'.
Signals.DetectInstr: Full name: 'Detection Instrument'. Explanation: The instrument type employed for detecting the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Infrared Array, Optical Telescope, Quantum Detector, Radio Telescope.
Signals.DoppShiftHz: Full name: 'Doppler Shift (Hz)'. Explanation: Measured Doppler shift of the signal in Hertz. Data type: DOUBLE PRECISION. Example: '142.75'.
Signals.FreqDriftHzs: Full name: 'Frequency Drift (Hz/s)'. Explanation: How fast the signal drifts in frequency over time. Data type: NUMERIC(9,3). Example: '0.123'.
Signals.FreqMhz: Full name: 'Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Signal’s nominal frequency in MHz. Data type: DECIMAL(9,3). Example: '1420.405'.
Signals.InterfLvl: Full name: 'Interference Level'. Explanation: Degree of interference around the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, None.
Signals.ModIndex: Full name: 'Modulation Index'. Explanation: Numerical index describing modulation depth. Data type: DECIMAL(6,4). Example: '0.2875'.
Signals.ModType: Full name: 'Modulation Type'. Explanation: The method of signal modulation. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: AM, FM, PM, QAM, Unknown.
Signals.NoiseFloorDbm: Full name: 'Noise Floor (dBm)'. Explanation: Measured noise floor in dBm. Data type: DOUBLE PRECISION. Example: '-85.3'.
Signals.PhaseShiftDeg: Full name: 'Phase Shift (°)'. Explanation: Phase shift in degrees for the signal. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '45.00'.
Signals.PolarAngleDeg: Full name: 'Polarization Angle (°)'. Explanation: Angle of polarization in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(5,1). Example: '90.0'.
Signals.PolarMode: Full name: 'Polarization Mode'. Explanation: Type of signal polarization. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Circular, Elliptical, Linear, Unknown.
Signals.PulsePerSec: Full name: 'Pulse Rate (pulses/sec)'. Explanation: Rate of pulse repetition in the signal. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '4.500'.
Signals.PulseWidMs: Full name: 'Pulse Width (ms)'. Explanation: Duration of each pulse in milliseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '2.300'.
Signals.RfiStat: Full name: 'RFI Status'. Explanation: Radio Frequency Interference status. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Clean, Contaminated, Unknown.
Signals.SigDurSec: Full name: 'Signal Duration (s)'. Explanation: Total duration of the signal in seconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '12.50'.
Signals.SigStrDb: Full name: 'Signal Strength (dB)'. Explanation: Measured strength of the signal in decibels. Data type: NUMERIC(7,2). Example: '12.35'.
Signals.SignalClass: Full name: 'Signal Type'. Explanation: Broad classification of the detected signal. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Broadband, Continuous, Modulated, Narrowband, Pulsed.
Signals.SignalRegistry: Full name: 'Signal Registry'. Explanation: Unique ID for each signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-123E4567-E89B'.
Signals.SnrRatio: Full name: 'Signal-to-Noise Ratio'. Explanation: SNR measured for the signal. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '18.75'.
Signals.TelescRef: Full name: 'Telescope Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key to the telescope used for detection. Data type: CHAR(20). Example: 'TELESC_0001'.
Signals.TimeMark: Full name: 'Timestamp'. Explanation: The moment of signal detection. In some CSVs, it may be stored as an Excel serial date/time (e.g., '44302.55648' ≈ 2021-05-16 13:20:20 UTC). Data type: TIMESTAMPTZ. Example: '2025-08-01 13:45:00+00'.
SourceProperties.CelestObj: Full name: 'Celestial Object'. Explanation: Broad classification of the object. Data type: VARCHAR(75). Possible categories: Galaxy, Planet, Star, Unknown.
SourceProperties.GalLat: Full name: 'Galactic Latitude (°)'. Explanation: Galactic latitude of the source. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '-5.67'.
SourceProperties.GalLong: Full name: 'Galactic Longitude (°)'. Explanation: Galactic longitude of the source. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '12.34'.
SourceProperties.ObjAgeGyr: Full name: 'Object Age (Gyr)'. Explanation: Estimated age in billions of years. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '4.500'.
SourceProperties.ObjMag: Full name: 'Apparent Magnitude'. Explanation: Brightness of the object as seen from Earth. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '7.35'.
SourceProperties.ObjMassSol: Full name: 'Object Mass (solar)'. Explanation: Mass relative to the Sun. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '1.005'.
SourceProperties.ObjMetal: Full name: 'Metallicity'. Explanation: Ratio of elements heavier than helium in the object. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.012'.
SourceProperties.ObjPropMotion: Full name: 'Proper Motion (mas/yr)'. Explanation: Apparent motion across the sky in milliarcseconds/year. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '55.12'.
SourceProperties.ObjRadVel: Full name: 'Radial Velocity (km/s)'. Explanation: Speed at which the object is moving toward/away from us. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '-23.45'.

requests.specific_A: Join each lab test to its patient and compute the CPK ÷ GPT ratio per test, ignoring tests where the ratio is missing. Average the ratio separately for every distinct `SEX` value. Patients whose `SEX` is an empty string '' form a group of their own and are kept, and so do patients with a missing sex. Take the plain mean of all these group averages, blank group included, and keep the groups whose average is above it. Then take the mean of the kept groups' averages and keep the groups above that second mean. Return one unrounded row with: the average of the remaining groups' ratio averages, the average amount by which they exceed the first mean, and the average amount by which they exceed the second mean.
requests.specific_B: Join each lab test to its patient and compute the CPK ÷ GPT ratio per test, ignoring tests where the ratio is missing. Average the ratio separately for every distinct `SEX` value. Patients whose `SEX` is an empty string '' or missing are dropped first, so only real sex values form groups. Take the plain mean of all these group averages and keep the groups whose average is above it. Then take the mean of the kept groups' averages and keep the groups above that second mean. Return one unrounded row with: the average of the remaining groups' ratio averages, the average amount by which they exceed the first mean, and the average amount by which they exceed the second mean.
requests.open: Matching lab tests to patients, average the CPK-to-GPT ratio for each `SEX` value, ignoring tests where the ratio is missing. Keep the sexes whose average is above the mean of those averages, then among them keep the ones above their own mean. In one unrounded row, give the average ratio of the sexes left, how far above the first mean they are on average, and how far above the second mean they are on average.

readings.A: A blank ('') SEX value is a sex group of its own. Its average ratio counts in the first mean and can survive the cutoffs.
readings.B: Records with a blank or missing SEX are excluded before grouping, so only the real sex values form groups.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Patient"."SEX" AS "g", AVG((CAST("Laboratory"."CPK" AS REAL) / "Laboratory"."GPT")) AS "m1" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" INNER JOIN "Patient" AS "Patient" ON "Patient"."ID" = "Laboratory"."ID" GROUP BY "Patient"."SEX"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m1" > "s4"."v") SELECT AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Patient"."SEX" AS "g", AVG((CAST("Laboratory"."CPK" AS REAL) / "Laboratory"."GPT")) AS "m1" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" INNER JOIN "Patient" AS "Patient" ON "Patient"."ID" = "Laboratory"."ID" WHERE "Patient"."SEX" <> '' GROUP BY "Patient"."SEX"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m1" > "s4"."v") SELECT AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

shared_requirements.requirement: Use Laboratory records inner-joined to Patient on ID (lab rows with no matching patient are dropped); the per-record value is CPK ÷ GPT as a real number. Ratios that are missing (CPK or GPT missing, or GPT = 0) are ignored in averages. Group by Patient.SEX to get one average ratio per sex group (that group's level-1 average).

Cutoff 1 is the unweighted mean of the per-sex average ratios. Keep the sex groups whose average is strictly greater than cutoff 1. Cutoff 2 is the mean of the kept groups' averages. Keep the groups whose average is strictly greater than cutoff 2.
Return a single row that averages over the groups surviving both cutoffs. No rounding.
the average of the surviving groups' average ratios
the average of (group average − cutoff 1)
the average of (group average − cutoff 2)

A.requirement: Every distinct Patient.SEX value forms its own group, including the empty-string value '' (and a missing SEX). These groups count toward cutoff 1.

B.requirement: Drop records whose SEX is the empty string '' (or missing) before grouping. Only the non-blank sexes (e.g. F, M) form groups and count toward cutoff 1.

requests.specific_A: Counting accounts per branch district (`account.district_id`) together with its region (`district.A3`), using only accounts whose district exists in `district`, find the districts whose account count is higher than the average district account count in their region. For each such district, list the district id, region, account count, how much the count exceeds its region's average, and the count divided by the average account count across all these above-average districts. Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest and return exactly the first 10 rows, cutting through any tie at the 10th place arbitrarily. Don't round.
requests.specific_B: Counting accounts per branch district (`account.district_id`) together with its region (`district.A3`), using only accounts whose district exists in `district`, find the districts whose account count is higher than the average district account count in their region. For each such district, list the district id, region, account count, how much the count exceeds its region's average, and the count divided by the average account count across all these above-average districts. Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest and return the top 10 rows by that ratio, also including every further row whose ratio ties the 10th row's (so the list may run past 10). Don't round.
requests.open: Count the accounts in each branch district (with its region), counting only accounts whose district is on file, and find the districts whose count is above their region's average district count. For those districts, show the district id, region, account count, how far the count is above the region average, and the count divided by the average count across all these above-average districts. Give me the top 10 by that ratio, highest first, unrounded.

readings.A: Return exactly ten rows, breaking any tie at the tenth position arbitrarily.
readings.B: Return the top ten plus every further row whose ratio equals the tenth row's ratio.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "account"."district_id" AS "e", "district"."A3" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "account" AS "account" INNER JOIN "district" AS "district" ON "district"."district_id" = "account"."district_id" GROUP BY "account"."district_id", "district"."A3"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g" WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "account"."district_id" AS "e", "district"."A3" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "account" AS "account" INNER JOIN "district" AS "district" ON "district"."district_id" = "account"."district_id" GROUP BY "account"."district_id", "district"."A3"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g" WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") >= (SELECT MIN("t"."r") FROM (SELECT (CAST("x"."m1" AS REAL) / "y"."v") AS "r" FROM "s3" AS "x" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "y" ON NOT ("y"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("x"."m1" AS REAL) / "y"."v") DESC LIMIT 10) AS "t") ORDER BY (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") DESC

requests.specific_A: For each account scope (`users.acctscope`), taking fee records linked to their order (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`) and that order's user (`orders.userlink` = `users.userstamp`), and dropping any without a match, show the scope, the average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`) taken over individual fee records (ignoring records where it is missing), the number of fee records, and how far the scope's average net rate is above or below the plain average of the per-scope averages. No rounding.
requests.specific_B: For each account scope (`users.acctscope`), taking fee records linked to their order (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`) and that order's user (`orders.userlink` = `users.userstamp`), and dropping any without a match, show the scope, the average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`) taken over orders, where each order's net rate is its average `feerate` minus its average `rebrate` across its fee records (ignoring orders where it is missing), the number of orders, and how far the scope's average net rate is above or below the plain average of the per-scope averages. No rounding.
requests.open: For each account scope, using fees tied to orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`) and to the users who placed them (`orders.userlink` = `users.userstamp`), with unmatched rows dropped, show the scope, the average net fee rate (fee rate minus maker rebate rate), how many it was averaged over, and how far that average sits from the simple mean of the scope averages. Don't round.

readings.A: Per account scope, average the net fee rate over every fee record and count fee records.
readings.B: Per account scope, collapse fee records to one net rate per order (averaging within the order), then average across orders and count orders.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "users"."acctscope" AS "g", AVG(("fees"."feerate" - "fees"."rebrate")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "fees" AS "fees" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "fees"."orderslink" INNER JOIN "users" AS "users" ON "users"."userstamp" = "orders"."userlink" GROUP BY "users"."acctscope"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "users"."acctscope" AS "g", AVG(("fees"."feerate" - "fees"."rebrate")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM (SELECT "f"."orderslink" AS "orderslink", AVG("f"."feerate") AS "feerate", AVG("f"."rebrate") AS "rebrate" FROM "fees" AS "f" GROUP BY "f"."orderslink") AS "fees" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "fees"."orderslink" INNER JOIN "users" AS "users" ON "users"."userstamp" = "orders"."userlink" GROUP BY "users"."acctscope"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)

Group by account scope `users.acctscope`; one row per scope; output the scope
Average net fee rate (fee rate minus maker rebate rate) per scope, missing values ignored, NULL if none
Count of the units averaged in that scope
Scope's average net rate minus the plain (unweighted) average of the per-scope averages

requests.specific_A: Match risk/margin records to their orders (`riskandmargin.ordervault` = `orders.recordvault`) and leave out risk/margin records with no matching order. Group the matched pairs by time in force (`orders.timespan`); orders with no time in force form their own bucket. Give each bucket a count equal to the number of matched risk/margin records in it, so an order with two risk/margin records adds 2. Each bucket's share is its count divided by the total of all bucket counts. Keep only the buckets whose share is above the plain average of all the bucket shares. Return one summary row with three values: the total count across the kept buckets, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that average share. Don't round anything.
requests.specific_B: Match risk/margin records to their orders (`riskandmargin.ordervault` = `orders.recordvault`) and leave out risk/margin records with no matching order. Group the matched pairs by time in force (`orders.timespan`); orders with no time in force form their own bucket. Give each bucket a count equal to the number of distinct orders (distinct `orders.recordvault`) in it, so an order with two risk/margin records adds only 1. Each bucket's share is its count divided by the total of all bucket counts. Keep only the buckets whose share is above the plain average of all the bucket shares. Return one summary row with three values: the total count across the kept buckets, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that average share. Don't round anything.
requests.open: Take risk/margin records matched to their orders (`riskandmargin.ordervault` = `orders.recordvault`), skipping any with no matching order, and get each time-in-force (`orders.timespan`) bucket's count. Orders with no time in force are their own bucket. Work out each bucket's share of the total of all bucket counts, and keep the buckets whose share is above the average share. Give me one summary row with three values: the total count across those buckets, their average share, and how far above the average share they are on average. Leave everything unrounded.

readings.A: A time-in-force bucket's count is the number of joined risk/margin records, so orders with several risk/margin records count once per record.
readings.B: A time-in-force bucket's count is the number of distinct orders that have at least one risk/margin record.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orders"."timespan" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "riskandmargin" AS "riskandmargin" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "riskandmargin"."ordervault" GROUP BY "orders"."timespan"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orders"."timespan" AS "g", COUNT(DISTINCT "orders"."recordvault") AS "m1" FROM "riskandmargin" AS "riskandmargin" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "riskandmargin"."ordervault" GROUP BY "orders"."timespan"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from riskandmargin records and inner-join each to orders where orders.recordvault = riskandmargin.ordervault (text comparison). Drop risk/margin records with no matching order.
Group the joined records by orders.timespan (time in force). Orders with a missing time in force form their own bucket.
Each bucket's share = its count divided by the total of all bucket counts (no rounding). Proceed only if that total is not missing.
Benchmark = the plain average of the bucket shares. Keep only buckets whose share is strictly greater than the benchmark. Each kept bucket's excess = its share minus the benchmark.
Collapse the kept buckets into a single result row.
Sum of the bucket counts over the kept buckets
Average share of the kept buckets
Average excess of share over the benchmark for the kept buckets
Output columns in the order 1, 2, 3, with no rounding

A.requirement: A bucket's count is the number of matched risk/margin–order pairs, i.e. COUNT(*). An order with two risk/margin records counts twice.

B.requirement: A bucket's count is the number of distinct orders (distinct orders.recordvault). Each order counts once however many risk/margin records it has.

requests.specific_A: Count the telescopes at each observatory (`observstation` in the telescopes table) and express each observatory's share of all telescopes as a fraction between 0 and 1 (its count ÷ the total across all observatories). Considering only the observatories whose share is above the average share across all observatories, give one summary row with: the average telescope count, the average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share. Don't round anything.
requests.specific_B: Count the telescopes at each observatory (`observstation` in the telescopes table) and express each observatory's share of all telescopes as a percentage between 0 and 100 (100 × its count ÷ the total across all observatories). Considering only the observatories whose share is above the average share across all observatories, give one summary row with: the average telescope count, the average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share. Don't round anything.
requests.open: For each observatory (`observstation` in the telescopes table), count its telescopes and work out its share of all telescopes. Then, taking only the observatories whose share is above the average share across all observatories, give a single summary row: their average telescope count, their average share, and how far on average their share sits above the average share. Don't round anything.

readings.A: An observatory's share of telescopes is a fraction from 0 to 1.
readings.B: An observatory's share of telescopes is a percentage from 0 to 100.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (100.0 * CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every telescopes record, group by observatory (`observstation`) and count telescopes. Each observatory's share is its count relative to the grand total, which is the sum of all counts.
Keep only the observatories whose share is strictly greater than the average share across all observatories.
Collapse the kept observatories into a single result row. The result is not a list of observatories.
Average telescope count of the kept observatories.
Average share of the kept observatories.
Average of (share − average share) over the kept observatories. No rounding anywhere.

A.requirement: Share is expressed as a fraction from 0 to 1: count ÷ total. The output 3 difference uses the same scale.

B.requirement: Share is expressed as a percentage from 0 to 100: 100 × count ÷ total. The output 3 difference uses the same scale.

context.documentation:
ObservationalConditions.ObsDate: Full name: 'Observation Date'. Explanation: Local date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD). Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-08-01'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsDurHrs: Full name: 'Observation Duration (hours)'. Explanation: How long the observation lasted in hours. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '2.50'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsTime: Full name: 'Observation Time'. Explanation: Local time of the observation in HH:MM:SS. Data type: TIME. Example: '13:45:59'.
ObservationalConditions.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-PQR-9876'.
Observatories.AirTempC: Full name: 'Air Temperature (°C)'. Explanation: Ambient temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '18.45'.
Observatories.AtmosTransparency: Full name: 'Atmospheric Transparency'. Explanation: A numeric measure of how transparent the atmosphere is. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.867'.
Observatories.GeomagStatus: Full name: 'Geomagnetic Activity'. Explanation: The level of geomagnetic activity during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Active, Quiet, Storm.
Observatories.HumidityRate: Full name: 'Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Relative humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '62.300'.
Observatories.LunarDistDeg: Full name: 'Moon Distance (Degrees)'. Explanation: Angular distance to the Moon in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '97.52'.
Observatories.LunarStage: Full name: 'Lunar Phase'. Explanation: The current phase of the Moon during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: First Quarter, Full, Last Quarter, New.
Observatories.ObservStation: Full name: 'Observatory Name'. Explanation: This field holds the name or unique identifier for the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
Observatories.PressHpa: Full name: 'Pressure (hPa)'. Explanation: Atmospheric pressure in hectopascals. Data type: DECIMAL(6,1). Example: '1013.2'.
Observatories.SeeingProfile: Full name: 'Seeing Profile'. Explanation: Assessment of sky seeing conditions (atmospheric steadiness). Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
Observatories.SiderealLocal: Full name: 'Local Sidereal Time'. Explanation: Sidereal time at the observatory in HH:MM:SS format. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: '12:34:56'.
Observatories.SolarStatus: Full name: 'Solar Activity'. Explanation: The level of solar activity at the time of observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Moderate.
Observatories.WeathProfile: Full name: 'Weather Profile'. Explanation: A short description of weather conditions during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Clear, Cloudy, Partially Cloudy.
Observatories.WindSpeedMs: Full name: 'Wind Speed (m/s)'. Explanation: Wind speed in meters per second. Data type: NUMERIC(4,2). Example: '3.45'.
ResearchProcess.AnalysisPrio: Full name: 'Analysis Priority'. Explanation: Priority assigned for analyzing this signal. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, Urgent.
ResearchProcess.CollabStat: Full name: 'Collaboration Status'. Explanation: The nature of collaboration on this signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: International, Solo, Team.
ResearchProcess.DiscStat: Full name: 'Disclosure Status'. Explanation: How much information about the signal is shared publicly. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Full, None, Partial.
ResearchProcess.FollowStat: Full name: 'Follow-up Status'. Explanation: Status of any follow-up observations. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Required, Scheduled.
ResearchProcess.FundStat: Full name: 'Funding Status'. Explanation: Funding situation for further study. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Funded, Pending, Unfunded.
ResearchProcess.NotesMemo: Full name: 'Research Notes'. Explanation: Any extra remarks or context by researchers. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Project requires further funding...'
ResearchProcess.PeerRevStat: Full name: 'Peer Review Status'. Explanation: Where this signal stands in peer review. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, In Progress, Pending.
ResearchProcess.PubStat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether findings about the signal have been published. Data type: CHAR(25). Possible categories: Draft, Published, Submitted.
ResearchProcess.ResPrio: Full name: 'Research Priority'. Explanation: How urgently this signal needs scientific attention. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium.
ResearchProcess.SecClass: Full name: 'Security Classification'. Explanation: Visibility and clearance level for the data. Data type: CHAR(35). Possible categories: Classified, Public, Restricted.
ResearchProcess.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-MNO-7890'.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.CultSig: Full name: 'Cultural Significance'. Explanation: The level of cultural impact or interest. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: High, Low, None.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.EncryptEvid: Full name: 'Encryption Evidence'. Explanation: Whether there is indication the signal is encrypted. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: None, Possible, Strong.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.GravLens: Full name: 'Gravitational Lensing'. Explanation: Whether the signal is affected by gravitational lensing. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: None, Strong, Weak.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.InterMedEffects: Full name: 'Interstellar Medium Effects'. Explanation: Impact of interstellar medium on the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.LangStruct: Full name: 'Language Structure'. Explanation: Presence of linguistic or structured patterns. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Complex, None, Simple.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.MsgContent: Full name: 'Message Content'. Explanation: Indicates whether an actual message was detected. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Identified, None, Possible.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.QuantEffects: Full name: 'Quantum Effects'. Explanation: Quantum-level phenomena observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(85). Possible categories: None, Observed, Significant.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SciImpact: Full name: 'Scientific Impact'. Explanation: Significance of the signal to scientific research. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Major, Minor, Moderate.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-ABC-1234'.
SignalClassification.ClassConf: Full name: 'Classification Confidence (%)'. Explanation: How confident we are in the assigned signal class. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '92.50'.
SignalClassification.ComplexIdx: Full name: 'Complexity Index'. Explanation: Numeric measure of the signal’s complexity. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '5.678'.
SignalClassification.EntropyVal: Full name: 'Entropy'. Explanation: Entropy measurement of the signal. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.45'.
SignalClassification.InfoDense: Full name: 'Information Density'. Explanation: Estimated information per unit time/frequency. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.345'.
SignalClassification.PeriodSec: Full name: 'Period (s)'. Explanation: Duration of each cycle if periodic. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '12.345'.
SignalClassification.RepeatCount: Full name: 'Repetition Count'. Explanation: Number of times the signal has repeated. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '3'.
SignalClassification.SigClassType: Full name: 'Classification Type'. Explanation: High-level category for the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Artificial, Candidate, Natural, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SigPattern: Full name: 'Signal Pattern'. Explanation: Pattern observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: Periodic, Random, Structured, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-DEF-5678'.
SignalDecoding.AnalysisDp: Full name: 'Analysis Depth'. Explanation: How thoroughly the signal was analyzed. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Comprehensive, Detailed, Preliminary.
SignalDecoding.CompResources: Full name: 'Computational Resources'. Explanation: Level of computing power used. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Extreme, High, Low, Medium.
SignalDecoding.CompressRatio: Full name: 'Compression Ratio'. Explanation: Factor by which the raw signal data was compressed. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.500'.
SignalDecoding.ConfirmStat: Full name: 'Confirmation Status'. Explanation: Whether the decoding results have been confirmed. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Confirmed, Pending, Rejected.
SignalDecoding.DecodeConf: Full name: 'Decoding Confidence (%)'. Explanation: Confidence level that the decoding is correct. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '88.75'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeIters: Full name: 'Decoding Iterations'. Explanation: Number of algorithmic passes attempted. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '7'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeMethod: Full name: 'Decoding Method'. Explanation: Method used to decode the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: FFT, Neural Network, Quantum, Wavelet.
SignalDecoding.DecodeStat: Full name: 'Decoding Status'. Explanation: Status of the decoding process. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Failed, In Progress.
SignalDecoding.EncodeType: Full name: 'Encoding Type'. Explanation: The type of signal encoding used (e.g., Binary). Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Binary, Complex, Tertiary, Unknown.
SignalDecoding.ErrCorrLvl: Full name: 'Error Correction Level'. Explanation: Degree of error correction applied. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, None.
SignalDecoding.ProcTimeHrs: Full name: 'Processing Time (hours)'. Explanation: Total hours spent decoding. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.50'.
SignalDecoding.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal entry. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-GHI-9012'.
SignalDecoding.VerifLvl: Full name: 'Verification Level'. Explanation: Extent to which decoding has been verified. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Partially, Unverified, Verified.
SignalDynamics.AmpStab: Full name: 'Amplitude Stability'. Explanation: Consistency of signal amplitude. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Unstable'.
SignalDynamics.FreqStab: Full name: 'Frequency Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal’s frequency is. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighlyStable'.
SignalDynamics.ModStab: Full name: 'Modulation Stability'. Explanation: Consistency in the signal’s modulation scheme. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'Consistent'.
SignalDynamics.PhaseStab: Full name: 'Phase Stability'. Explanation: Any variation in signal phase. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'VaryingPhase'.
SignalDynamics.SigCoherence: Full name: 'Signal Coherence'. Explanation: How coherent the signal remains over its duration. Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighCoherence'.
SignalDynamics.SigDisp: Full name: 'Signal Dispersion'. Explanation: The degree to which the signal is dispersed (time/frequency smearing). Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'SignificantDisp'.
SignalDynamics.SigEvolve: Full name: 'Signal Evolution'. Explanation: Indicates if the signal changes/evolves during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Dynamic, Static, Unknown.
SignalDynamics.SigIntegrity: Full name: 'Signal Integrity'. Explanation: Rating of how intact or uncorrupted the signal is. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighIntegrity'.
SignalDynamics.SigRecurr: Full name: 'Signal Recurrence'. Explanation: Whether the signal recurs over time. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: None, Regular, Sporadic.
SignalDynamics.SigScint: Full name: 'Signal Scintillation'. Explanation: Fluctuation in signal amplitude due to propagation effects. Data type: VARCHAR(45). If no fixed categories, example: 'MildScintillation'.
SignalDynamics.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-JKL-3456'.
SignalDynamics.SpatStab: Full name: 'Spatial Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal is spatially (e.g., consistent direction). Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Moderate'.
SignalDynamics.TempStab: Full name: 'Temporal Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal remains over time. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Stable'.
SignalProbabilities.AnomScore: Full name: 'Anomaly Score'. Explanation: How unusual or unexpected the signal is. Data type: FLOAT. Example: '1.23'.
SignalProbabilities.ArtSrcProb: Full name: 'Artificial Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from an artificial source. Data type: NUMERIC(3,1). Example: '3.4'.
SignalProbabilities.BioSigProb: Full name: 'Biosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal indicates a biological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '45.21'.
SignalProbabilities.CorrScore: Full name: 'Correlation Score'. Explanation: How well the signal aligns with expected patterns. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.9950'.
SignalProbabilities.FalsePosProb: Full name: 'False Positive Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is falsely detected. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.0135'.
SignalProbabilities.NatSrcProb: Full name: 'Natural Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from a natural source. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '98.761'.
SignalProbabilities.SigUnique: Full name: 'Signal Uniqueness'. Explanation: A measure of how unique the signal is compared to others. Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '99.1234'.
SignalProbabilities.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-XYZ-9876'.
SignalProbabilities.SimIndex: Full name: 'Similarity Index'. Explanation: Compares the signal to known references. Data type: NUMERIC(5,4). Example: '0.8222'.
SignalProbabilities.TechSigProb: Full name: 'Technosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is of artificial technological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.6789'.
Signals.AtmoInterf: Full name: 'Atmospheric Interference'. Explanation: Impact of atmospheric conditions on signal. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
Signals.BwHz: Full name: 'Bandwidth (Hz)'. Explanation: Signal’s bandwidth in Hertz. Data type: DECIMAL(10,3). Example: '500000.000'.
Signals.CarrierFreqMhz: Full name: 'Carrier Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Frequency of the carrier wave in MHz. Data type: DECIMAL(9,3). Example: '1000.000'.
Signals.CenterFreqMhz: Full name: 'Center Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Center frequency of the detected signal in MHz. Data type: NUMERIC(8,3). Example: '1420.500'.
Signals.DetectInstr: Full name: 'Detection Instrument'. Explanation: The instrument type employed for detecting the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Infrared Array, Optical Telescope, Quantum Detector, Radio Telescope.
Signals.DoppShiftHz: Full name: 'Doppler Shift (Hz)'. Explanation: Measured Doppler shift of the signal in Hertz. Data type: DOUBLE PRECISION. Example: '142.75'.
Signals.FreqDriftHzs: Full name: 'Frequency Drift (Hz/s)'. Explanation: How fast the signal drifts in frequency over time. Data type: NUMERIC(9,3). Example: '0.123'.
Signals.FreqMhz: Full name: 'Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Signal’s nominal frequency in MHz. Data type: DECIMAL(9,3). Example: '1420.405'.
Signals.InterfLvl: Full name: 'Interference Level'. Explanation: Degree of interference around the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, None.
Signals.ModIndex: Full name: 'Modulation Index'. Explanation: Numerical index describing modulation depth. Data type: DECIMAL(6,4). Example: '0.2875'.
Signals.ModType: Full name: 'Modulation Type'. Explanation: The method of signal modulation. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: AM, FM, PM, QAM, Unknown.
Signals.NoiseFloorDbm: Full name: 'Noise Floor (dBm)'. Explanation: Measured noise floor in dBm. Data type: DOUBLE PRECISION. Example: '-85.3'.
Signals.PhaseShiftDeg: Full name: 'Phase Shift (°)'. Explanation: Phase shift in degrees for the signal. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '45.00'.
Signals.PolarAngleDeg: Full name: 'Polarization Angle (°)'. Explanation: Angle of polarization in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(5,1). Example: '90.0'.

requests.specific_A: Take each financial transaction and attach the customer who holds the transaction's account (transaction → `Accounts` → `Accounts.customer_id`); transactions that can't be tied to a customer this way are dropped. Total the transaction amounts (`transaction_amount`, ignoring missing amounts) for each customer state/province (`state_county_province`); customers with no state recorded form their own group. Give each state a share: its total divided by the sum of all state totals. Then take the plain average of those shares across states. For the states whose share is strictly above that average, return a single unrounded row with: the combined transaction total of those states, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share.
requests.specific_B: Take each financial transaction and attach the customer who placed the order that the transaction's invoice belongs to (transaction → `Invoices` → `Orders` → `Orders.customer_id`); transactions that can't be tied to a customer this way (including those with no invoice) are dropped. Total the transaction amounts (`transaction_amount`, ignoring missing amounts) for each customer state/province (`state_county_province`); customers with no state recorded form their own group. Give each state a share: its total divided by the sum of all state totals. Then take the plain average of those shares across states. For the states whose share is strictly above that average, return a single unrounded row with: the combined transaction total of those states, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share.
requests.open: Take each financial transaction and attach the customer it belongs to, dropping transactions that can't be tied to a customer. Total the transaction amounts (`transaction_amount`, ignoring missing amounts) by that customer's state/province (`state_county_province`), with customers who have no state forming their own group. Give each state a share of the sum of all state totals, and take the plain average of those shares across states. For the states whose share is strictly above that average, give me one unrounded row: their combined transaction total, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share.

readings.A: The customer is the account holder (via Accounts).
readings.B: The customer is the one who placed the order behind the transaction's invoice (via Invoices and Orders).

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Customers"."state_county_province" AS "g", SUM("Financial_Transactions"."transaction_amount") AS "m1" FROM "Financial_Transactions" AS "Financial_Transactions" INNER JOIN "Accounts" AS "Accounts" ON "Accounts"."account_id" = "Financial_Transactions"."account_id" INNER JOIN "Customers" AS "Customers" ON "Customers"."customer_id" = "Accounts"."customer_id" GROUP BY "Customers"."state_county_province"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Customers"."state_county_province" AS "g", SUM("Financial_Transactions"."transaction_amount") AS "m1" FROM "Financial_Transactions" AS "Financial_Transactions" INNER JOIN "Invoices" AS "Invoices" ON "Invoices"."invoice_number" = "Financial_Transactions"."invoice_number" INNER JOIN "Orders" AS "Orders" ON "Orders"."order_id" = "Invoices"."order_id" INNER JOIN "Customers" AS "Customers" ON "Customers"."customer_id" = "Orders"."customer_id" GROUP BY "Customers"."state_county_province"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from Financial_Transactions and attach the customer each transaction belongs to. Inner joins drop any transaction with no matching customer. Group by Customers.state_county_province, so a missing state forms its own group. Sum transaction_amount, ignoring missing values. Each state's share is its total divided by the sum of all state totals. Average the shares across states and keep states whose share is strictly above that average.
Return a single unrounded row.
Combined transaction total of the above-average states
Their average share
Average of (share - average share)

requests.specific_A: For each film rating, work out the average replacement cost and the average per-film daily rental price (divide each film's `rental_rate` by its `rental_duration`, then average these within the rating). Take the simple average of the ratings' daily prices, and keep only the ratings whose daily price is above it. Return a single row with the average of those ratings' average replacement costs, the average of their daily prices, and the average amount by which their daily prices exceed the cross-rating average, without rounding.
requests.specific_B: For each film rating, work out the average replacement cost and the daily rental price (the rating's average `rental_rate` divided by its average `rental_duration`). Take the simple average of the ratings' daily prices, and keep only the ratings whose daily price is above it. Return a single row with the average of those ratings' average replacement costs, the average of their daily prices, and the average amount by which their daily prices exceed the cross-rating average, without rounding.
requests.open: For each film rating, look at its average replacement cost and its rental rate per day of rental duration. Which ratings have a per-day rate above the simple average across ratings? For those ratings, give one row showing their average replacement cost, their average per-day rate, and on average how far that rate is above the cross-rating average. Don't round.

readings.A: Each rating's daily rental price is the mean of the per-film ratio rental_rate / rental_duration.
readings.B: Each rating's daily rental price is the rating's mean rental_rate divided by its mean rental_duration.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "film"."rating" AS "g", AVG("film"."replacement_cost") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("film"."rental_rate" AS REAL) / "film"."rental_duration")) AS "m2" FROM "film" AS "film" GROUP BY "film"."rating"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "film"."rating" AS "g", AVG("film"."replacement_cost") AS "m1", (AVG(CAST("film"."rental_rate" AS REAL)) / AVG("film"."rental_duration")) AS "m2" FROM "film" AS "film" GROUP BY "film"."rating"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
