film.rating: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns exactly 5 rating levels, each covering roughly 180-225 films, so every group is well populated and rating works as a grouping class. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate), AVG(length), AVG(replacement_cost) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '3.0348430493273613', '120.4439461883408', '20.402556053811544'], ['NC-17', '210', '2.970952380952388', '113.22857142857143', '20.137619047618937'], ['R', '195', '2.9387179487179553', '118.66153846153846', '20.23102564102554'], ['PG', '194', '3.051855670103099', '112.00515463917526', '18.959072164948356'], ['G', '178', '2.888876404494388', '111.0505617977528', '20.12483146067407']] scale (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows exactly 5 levels: G, PG, PG-13, R and NC-17. These are the standard MPAA bands, which are ordered by audience restriction, so the column is an ordinal class. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY rating -> [['G', '178'], ['NC-17', '210'], ['PG', '194'], ['PG-13', '223'], ['R', '195']]
category.name: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 16 genres, each shared by many films (about 50-75 each), so the column is a grouping label and does not identify single records. Evidence: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film_category fc JOIN category c ON c.category_id = fc.category_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY films DESC -> [['Sports', '74'], ['Foreign', '73'], ['Family', '69'], ['Documentary', '68'], ['Animation', '66'], ['Action', '64']]
customer.store_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 2 stores with about 300 customers each, so the column is a grouping label shared by many rows. Evidence: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS customers, SUM(active) AS active_customers FROM customer GROUP BY store_id -> [['1', '326', '318'], ['2', '273', '266']]
inventory.store_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 2 store values over 4581 copies, about 2270 per store, so the column is a grouping label. Evidence: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS copies, COUNT(DISTINCT film_id) AS titles FROM inventory GROUP BY store_id -> [['1', '2270', '759'], ['2', '2311', '762']]
country.country: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Many customers share a country (the top countries have dozens of customers each), so country works as a grouping attribute for customers. Evidence: SELECT co.country, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customer cu JOIN address a ON a.address_id = cu.address_id JOIN city ci ON ci.city_id = a.city_id JOIN country co ON co.country_id = ci.country_id GROUP BY co.country ORDER BY customers DESC LIMIT 10 -> [['India', '60'], ['China', '53'], ['United States', '36'], ['Japan', '31'], ['Mexico', '30'], ['Russian Federation', '28']]
film.special_features: desc (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 15 distinct values, all of them combinations of the same 4 feature names (for example 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes'). The column is a set, not a single category. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']] semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows 15 distinct values, all combinations of the same 4 feature names, such as 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes' and 'Trailers,Commentaries'. The column is a set, not a single class, so it should not be offered as a grouping. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']]
film.length: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified rating query already returns AVG(length) between 111.05 (G) and 120.44 (PG-13). The catalogue profile gives 140 distinct values from 46 to 185 minutes. So length is a continuous ratio-scale quantity whose group averages can be read directly. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(length) AS avg_minutes, MIN(length), MAX(length) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '120.4439461883408', '46', '185'], ['NC-17', '210', '113.22857142857143', '46', '184'], ['R', '195', '118.66153846153846', '49', '185'], ['PG', '194', '112.00515463917526', '46', '185'], ['G', '178', '111.0505617977528', '47', '185']]
film.rental_duration: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows 5 values from 3 to 7 days, all well above zero, so the column is a ratio-scale number of days per film. The query shows how many films fall at each value. Evidence: SELECT rental_duration, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate) AS avg_rate FROM film GROUP BY rental_duration ORDER BY rental_duration -> [['3', '203', '2.8323645320197115'], ['4', '203', '2.97029556650247'], ['5', '191', '3.19942408376964'], ['6', '212', '2.895660377358497'], ['7', '191', '3.021413612565451']]
film.rental_rate: desc (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows rental_rate takes only 0.99, 2.99 and 4.99, while replacement_cost runs from 9.99 to 29.99. The query shows how large and uniform the gap is. The auditor noted that the difference is always about −17 and the relative gap about −0.85, which fits two different quantities rather than one price seen two ways. Evidence: SELECT MIN(replacement_cost - rental_rate), MAX(replacement_cost - rental_rate), AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) FROM film -> [['5.0', '29.0', '0.16651517608314595']]
film.replacement_cost: quantity (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The column holds a per-copy value that becomes meaningful when summed over physical copies in inventory, for example as stock value. That is the reading of an asset value, not of a price charged per rental. Evidence: SELECT f.rating, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copies, SUM(f.replacement_cost) AS stock_value FROM inventory i JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating -> [['G', '791', '16185.089999999853'], ['NC-17', '944', '19128.56000000009'], ['PG', '924', '17755.759999999962'], ['PG-13', '1018', '21052.82000000024'], ['R', '904', '18498.960000000006']]
payment.staff_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows only 2 distinct values (1 and 2) across 16,049 payments. Each value is therefore shared by thousands of rows, which makes it a grouping label rather than a record identifier. Evidence: SELECT staff_id, COUNT(*) AS payments, SUM(amount) AS revenue, AVG(amount) FROM payment GROUP BY staff_id -> [['1', '8057', '33489.470000005174', '4.156568201564499'], ['2', '7992', '33927.04000000482', '4.245125125125728']]
rental.staff_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows only 2 distinct values across 16,044 rentals, so each staff value covers thousands of rentals and works as a grouping class. Evidence: SELECT staff_id, COUNT(*) AS rentals, SUM(CASE WHEN return_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unreturned FROM rental GROUP BY staff_id -> [['1', '8040', '85'], ['2', '8004', '98']]

requests.specific_A: For each time-in-force value (`orders.timespan`), looking at risk/margin records matched to their order (`riskandmargin.ordervault` = `orders.recordvault`; unmatched records dropped), show the time in force, the number of risk/margin records (an order with several records counts once per record), that number's share of the total across all time-in-force values, and how much the share differs from the average share across the time-in-force values. Don't round.
requests.specific_B: For each time-in-force value (`orders.timespan`), looking at risk/margin records matched to their order (`riskandmargin.ordervault` = `orders.recordvault`; unmatched records dropped), show the time in force, the number of distinct orders with risk/margin records (an order with several records counts once), that number's share of the total across all time-in-force values, and how much the share differs from the average share across the time-in-force values. Don't round.
requests.open: For each time in force, using risk/margin records matched to their orders (`riskandmargin.ordervault` = `orders.recordvault`; unmatched dropped), show the time in force, its risk/margin count, that count's share of the overall total, and how far the share is from the average share across time-in-force values. No rounding.

readings.A: Per time in force, count every matched risk/margin record and take its share of the overall record total.
readings.B: Per time in force, count each distinct order with risk/margin data once and take its share of the overall order total.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "riskandmargin"."ordervault" AS "e", "orders"."timespan" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "riskandmargin" AS "riskandmargin" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "riskandmargin"."ordervault" GROUP BY "riskandmargin"."ordervault", "orders"."timespan"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", SUM("s1"."m1") AS "m1" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT SUM("s2"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s2" AS "s2"), "s4" AS (SELECT "s2"."g" AS "g", "s2"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s2"."m1" AS REAL) / "s3"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s2" AS "s2" INNER JOIN "s3" AS "s3" ON NOT ("s3"."v" IS NULL)), "s5" AS (SELECT AVG("s4"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s4" AS "s4") SELECT "s4"."g" AS "g", "s4"."m1" AS "m1", "s4"."m2" AS "m2", ("s4"."m2" - "s5"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s4" AS "s4" INNER JOIN "s5" AS "s5" ON NOT ("s5"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "riskandmargin"."ordervault" AS "e", "orders"."timespan" AS "g", COUNT(DISTINCT "orders"."recordvault") AS "m1" FROM "riskandmargin" AS "riskandmargin" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "riskandmargin"."ordervault" GROUP BY "riskandmargin"."ordervault", "orders"."timespan"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", SUM("s1"."m1") AS "m1" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT SUM("s2"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s2" AS "s2"), "s4" AS (SELECT "s2"."g" AS "g", "s2"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s2"."m1" AS REAL) / "s3"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s2" AS "s2" INNER JOIN "s3" AS "s3" ON NOT ("s3"."v" IS NULL)), "s5" AS (SELECT AVG("s4"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s4" AS "s4") SELECT "s4"."g" AS "g", "s4"."m1" AS "m1", "s4"."m2" AS "m2", ("s4"."m2" - "s5"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s4" AS "s4" INNER JOIN "s5" AS "s5" ON NOT ("s5"."v" IS NULL)

shared_requirements.requirement: Source rows are risk/margin records (`riskandmargin`)
Inner-join to `orders` on `riskandmargin.ordervault` = `orders.recordvault` (text equality); unmatched records dropped
Group by time in force `orders.timespan`; one row per value; output it
A count per time-in-force value
That count divided by the sum of the counts across all time-in-force values (fraction)
Share minus the plain average of the shares across time-in-force values
No rounding, no ordering, no limit; columns: time in force, count, share, difference

A.requirement: Count every joined risk/margin record; an order with several records counts once per record

B.requirement: Count distinct orders (`orders.recordvault`); an order with several risk/margin records counts once

requests.specific_A: Looking only at accounts that have placed at least one order (`order`), and leaving out accounts with no orders entirely, find each account's number of orders and its share of all orders (its order count divided by the total number of orders). Average the shares over these accounts and take the accounts whose share is above that average. In a single row, give the total number of orders of those accounts, their average share, and on average how far their share is above the average share. Do not round.
requests.specific_B: Looking at every account in `account`, including accounts with no orders (`order`), which count as 0 orders and a share of 0, find each account's number of orders and its share of all orders (its order count divided by the total number of orders). Average the shares over these accounts and take the accounts whose share is above that average. In a single row, give the total number of orders of those accounts, their average share, and on average how far their share is above the average share. Do not round.
requests.open: For each account, work out its share of all orders: its order count divided by the total number of orders (`order`). For the accounts whose share is above the average share, give one row with the total number of orders they have, their average share, and on average how far above the average share they are. Do not round.

readings.A: Shares and their average cover only accounts that placed at least one order.
readings.B: Shares and their average cover all accounts, with zero-order accounts given share 0.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "order"."account_id" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "order" AS "order" GROUP BY "order"."account_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "account"."account_id" AS "e", COUNT("order"."order_id") AS "m1" FROM "account" AS "account" LEFT JOIN "order" AS "order" ON "order"."account_id" = "account"."account_id" GROUP BY "account"."account_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

Average the shares over the accounts considered. Keep accounts whose share is strictly above that average and summarise them in one row. Do not round.

Ignore missing values in every average and do not round.

Then, for each product type description, average those three values over its products, and finally return one row with the average, across all product types, of each of the three per-type averages (average quantity, average order-item count, average share). Ignore missing values in every average and do not round.

requests.specific_A: For each event (`budget.link_to_event`), give the average `spent` and the average `remaining` across its budget lines. Also give how much its average remaining exceeds the mean of all the per-event average remaining values (each event counted once), as average remaining minus that mean. Ignore missing values in the averages. Sort by that difference, highest first, with missing values last, and show the top 10. Don't round.
requests.specific_B: For each event (`budget.link_to_event`), give the average `spent` and the average `remaining` across its budget lines. Also give how much its average remaining exceeds the mean of `remaining` over all budget lines (each line counted once), as average remaining minus that mean. Ignore missing values in the averages. Sort by that difference, highest first, with missing values last, and show the top 10. Don't round.
requests.open: For each event (`budget.link_to_event`), show the average `spent` and the average `remaining` across its budget lines. Also show how far its average remaining is above the overall average remaining (its average minus the overall average). Ignore missing values in the averages. List the 10 events with the largest difference, highest first, with missing values last. Don't round.

readings.A: Each event's average remaining is compared with the mean of the per-event average remaining values, so every event carries equal weight.
readings.B: Each event's average remaining is compared with the mean of `remaining` over every budget line, so every budget line carries equal weight.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "budget"."link_to_event" AS "e", AVG("budget"."spent") AS "m1", AVG("budget"."remaining") AS "m2" FROM "budget" AS "budget" GROUP BY "budget"."link_to_event"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "budget"."link_to_event" AS "e", AVG("budget"."spent") AS "m1", AVG("budget"."remaining") AS "m2" FROM "budget" AS "budget" GROUP BY "budget"."link_to_event"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("budget"."remaining") AS "v" FROM "budget" AS "budget") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from all `budget` lines, with no join to `event`
Attach a single overall average remaining value to every event row. If that value is missing, no rows are returned.
One row per `budget.link_to_event` value; the first column is that event link
The average `spent` over the event's budget lines, ignoring missing values
The average `remaining` over the event's budget lines, ignoring missing values
The event's average remaining minus the overall average remaining (the overall average ignores missing values); no rounding
Sort by that difference, highest first, with missing values last
Keep the top 10 rows

A.requirement: Overall average = the mean of the per-event average remaining values (each event counts equally)

B.requirement: Overall average = the mean of `remaining` over all budget lines (each budget line counts equally)

requests.specific_A: Using only processing records whose site code (`scanprocessing.zoneref`) matches a site in `sites`, group by that site code and the site's insurance status (`sites.insurstat`). For each group, show the site code, the insurance status, the average remaining storage (`remaingb`), the average of CPU usage minus GPU usage (`proccpu` − `procgpu`, kept signed so it can be negative), and the ratio of the group's average remaining storage to the mean of all groups' average remaining storage values (ignoring missing ones; return no rows if that mean is missing). Ignore missing values in all averages and don't round anything. Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest with missing ratios last, and return only the top 10 rows.
requests.specific_B: Using only processing records whose site code (`scanprocessing.zoneref`) matches a site in `sites`, group by that site code and the site's insurance status (`sites.insurstat`). For each group, show the site code, the insurance status, the average remaining storage (`remaingb`), the average absolute difference between CPU usage and GPU usage (|`proccpu` − `procgpu`|, regardless of which is larger), and the ratio of the group's average remaining storage to the mean of all groups' average remaining storage values (ignoring missing ones; return no rows if that mean is missing). Ignore missing values in all averages and don't round anything. Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest with missing ratios last, and return only the top 10 rows.
requests.open: Using only processing records whose site code (`scanprocessing.zoneref`) matches a site in `sites`, group by that site code and the site's insurance status (`sites.insurstat`). For each group, show the site code, the insurance status, the average remaining storage (`remaingb`), the average CPU–GPU usage gap (`proccpu`, `procgpu`), and the ratio of the group's average remaining storage to the mean of all groups' average remaining storage values (ignoring missing ones; return no rows if that mean is missing). Ignore missing values in all averages and don't round anything. Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest with missing ratios last, and return only the top 10 rows.

readings.A: The usage gap is CPU minus GPU, keeping the sign.
readings.B: The usage gap is the size of the difference, whichever of CPU or GPU is larger.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scanprocessing"."zoneref" AS "e", "sites"."insurstat" AS "g", AVG("scanprocessing"."remaingb") AS "m1", AVG(("scanprocessing"."proccpu" - "scanprocessing"."procgpu")) AS "m2" FROM "scanprocessing" AS "scanprocessing" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scanprocessing"."zoneref" GROUP BY "scanprocessing"."zoneref", "sites"."insurstat"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scanprocessing"."zoneref" AS "e", "sites"."insurstat" AS "g", AVG("scanprocessing"."remaingb") AS "m1", AVG(ABS("scanprocessing"."proccpu" - "scanprocessing"."procgpu")) AS "m2" FROM "scanprocessing" AS "scanprocessing" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scanprocessing"."zoneref" GROUP BY "scanprocessing"."zoneref", "sites"."insurstat"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

ScanConservation.HarmAssess: Full name: 'Damage Assessment'. Explanation: Indicates severity of damage. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: None, Moderate, Severe.

ScanConservation.StructState: Full name: 'Structural Stability'. Explanation: Stability level of the structure. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Stable, Moderate, Unstable.
ScanConservation.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Associates conservation data with a site code. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanEnvironment.AirRegistry: Full name: 'Environment Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for environment data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 1001.
ScanEnvironment.AmbicTemp: Full name: 'Ambient Temperature (C)'. Explanation: Air temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 25.3.
ScanEnvironment.EquipRef: Full name: 'Equipment Reference'. Explanation: Identifies which equipment these environment data refer to. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
ScanEnvironment.GeoSignal: Full name: 'GPS Signal Quality'. Explanation: Quality rating for GPS reception. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: None, Poor, Good, Excellent.
ScanEnvironment.HumePct: Full name: 'Relative Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 60.4.
ScanEnvironment.IllumeLux: Full name: 'Light Conditions (lux)'. Explanation: Measured illumination in lux. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 86054.
ScanEnvironment.ImgCount: Full name: 'Number of Images'. Explanation: How many images were taken for photogrammetry. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 248.
ScanEnvironment.LinkStatus: Full name: 'Network Status'. Explanation: Status of network connectivity. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Possible categories: Disconnected, Connected.
ScanEnvironment.PhotoMap: Full name: 'Photogrammetry Overlap'. Explanation: Percentage overlap for photogrammetry images. Data type: CHAR(4). Possible categories: 80%, 60%, 90%.
ScanEnvironment.TrackStatus: Full name: 'RTK Status'. Explanation: Real-Time Kinematic correction state. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Possible categories: None, Fixed.
ScanEnvironment.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Links environment conditions to a specific site code. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanFeatures.ArtiCount: Full name: 'Artifact Count'. Explanation: Number of artifacts recognized. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 71.
ScanFeatures.EquipRef: Full name: 'Equipment Reference'. Explanation: Equipment ID used to detect these features. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
ScanFeatures.HueStudy: Full name: 'Color Analysis'. Explanation: Status of color analysis (done or pending). Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Partial, Completed, Not Required.
ScanFeatures.MatKind: Full name: 'Material Type'. Explanation: Primary composition or material. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Organic, Metal, Mixed, Ceramic, Stone.
ScanFeatures.PatternNote: Full name: 'Pattern Recognition'. Explanation: Notes regarding detected patterns. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Not Required, None, Partial.
ScanFeatures.StructKind: Full name: 'Structure Type'. Explanation: Type of structural element. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Artifact, Complex, Wall, Foundation.
ScanFeatures.TextureStudy: Full name: 'Texture Analysis'. Explanation: Status of texture analysis. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Partial, Completed, Not Required.
ScanFeatures.TraitCount: Full name: 'Number of Detected Features'. Explanation: How many features were identified. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 516.
ScanFeatures.TraitExtract: Full name: 'Feature Extraction Method'. Explanation: Method used to extract features (manual or automated). Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Manual, Semi-automatic, Automatic.
ScanFeatures.TraitRegistry: Full name: 'Feature Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for feature data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 5001.
ScanFeatures.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Site code tied to these features. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanMesh.EquipRef: Full name: 'Equipment Reference'. Explanation: Identifies which equipment was used to generate the mesh. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
ScanMesh.FacetFaces: Full name: 'Mesh Faces'. Explanation: Count of triangular or polygonal faces. Data type: BIGINT. Example: 5997318.
ScanMesh.FacetRegistry: Full name: 'Mesh Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for mesh data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 3001.
ScanMesh.FacetResMm: Full name: 'Mesh Resolution (mm)'. Explanation: Mesh vertex spacing in mm. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 3.2.
ScanMesh.FacetVerts: Full name: 'Mesh Vertices'. Explanation: Count of mesh vertices. Data type: BIGINT. Example: 7234721.
ScanMesh.GeomDeltaMm: Full name: 'Geometric Accuracy (mm)'. Explanation: Estimated geometric deviation in millimeters. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: 2.74.
ScanMesh.TexDist: Full name: 'Texture Resolution Setting'. Explanation: Preset texture resolution. Data type: VARCHAR(5). Possible categories: 2K, 1K, 4K.
ScanMesh.TexPix: Full name: 'Texture Size (px)'. Explanation: Texture image dimension in pixels. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 2048.
ScanMesh.UVMapQual: Full name: 'UV Mapping Quality'. Explanation: Quality of the UV mapping process. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Possible categories: Medium, High, Low.
ScanMesh.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Associates mesh data with a site code. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanPointCloud.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Project ID associated with this point cloud. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanPointCloud.CloudDense: Full name: 'Point-Cloud Density Code'. Explanation: A numeric code classifying point density. Data type: INTEGER. Possible categories: 9449, 431, 7553, 1746.
ScanPointCloud.CloudRegistry: Full name: 'Point Cloud Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for point cloud data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 2001.
ScanPointCloud.CoverPct: Full name: 'Coverage (%)'. Explanation: Surface coverage percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(4,1). Example: 91.2.
ScanPointCloud.CrewRef: Full name: 'Operator Reference'. Explanation: Which operator is linked to this point cloud. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
ScanPointCloud.LapPct: Full name: 'Overlap (%)'. Explanation: Overlap percentage among multiple scans. Data type: NUMERIC(4,1). Example: 31.3.
ScanPointCloud.NoiseDb: Full name: 'Noise Level (dB)'. Explanation: Measured noise in decibels. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: 1.318.
ScanPointCloud.PointDense: Full name: 'Point Density (points/m²)'. Explanation: Density of points per square meter. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 42812.
ScanPointCloud.RefPct: Full name: 'Surface Reflectivity (%)'. Explanation: Reflectivity percentage of scanned surfaces. Data type: NUMERIC(4,1). Example: 65.4.
ScanPointCloud.ScanResolMm: Full name: 'Scan Resolution (mm)'. Explanation: Resolution of points in millimeters. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 2.4.
ScanPointCloud.TotalPts: Full name: 'Total Points'. Explanation: Overall number of points in the cloud. Data type: BIGINT. Example: 46562436.
ScanProcessing.CamCal: Full name: 'Camera Calibration Status'. Explanation: Whether camera calibration is completed or pending. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Required'.
ScanProcessing.ColorTune: Full name: 'Color Balance Status'. Explanation: Indicates color adjustment requirement. Data type: CHAR(10). Possible categories: Required, Adjusted.
ScanProcessing.CoordFrame: Full name: 'Coordinate System'. Explanation: Defines spatial reference frame. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Possible categories: Local, WGS84, Custom.
ScanProcessing.DataLevel: Full name: 'Data Access Level'. Explanation: Access restrictions or sharing level. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Confidential, Public, Restricted.
ScanProcessing.ElevRef: Full name: 'Elevation Reference'. Explanation: Reference for altitude or elevation. Data type: VARCHAR(16). Possible categories: Arbitrary, Sea Level, Local.
ScanProcessing.EquipRef: Full name: 'Equipment Reference'. Explanation: Equipment ID used for processing. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
ScanProcessing.FlowHrs: Full name: 'Processing Time (hours)'. Explanation: Time spent on processing. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 21.9.
ScanProcessing.FlowRegistry: Full name: 'Processing Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for processing workflow. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 8001.
ScanProcessing.FlowSoft: Full name: 'Processing Software'. Explanation: Name of the software used. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: RealityCapture, CloudCompare, Agisoft.
ScanProcessing.FlowStage: Full name: 'Processing Stage'. Explanation: Current stage of the processing workflow. Data type: VARCHAR(18). Possible categories: Aligned, Meshed, Final.
ScanProcessing.FmtVer: Full name: 'Export Format Version'. Explanation: Version tag for exported files. Data type: CHAR(3). Possible categories: 2.3, 2.7, 4.0, 1.1.
ScanProcessing.LensDist: Full name: 'Lens Distortion Status'. Explanation: Whether lens distortion is corrected or unknown. Data type: VARCHAR(14). Possible categories: Corrected, Unknown.
ScanProcessing.MemUsageGb: Full name: 'Memory Usage (GB)'. Explanation: RAM usage during processing. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: 70.3.
ScanProcessing.MetaBench: Full name: 'Metadata Standard'. Explanation: Which metadata framework is applied. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Possible categories: Dublin Core, CIDOC CRM, Custom.
ScanProcessing.ProcCPU: Full name: 'CPU Usage (%)'. Explanation: CPU usage as an integer percentage. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 81.
ScanProcessing.ProcGPU: Full name: 'GPU Usage (%)'. Explanation: GPU usage as an integer percentage. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 56.
ScanProcessing.RemainGb: Full name: 'Remaining Storage (GB)'. Explanation: Remaining disk or cloud space. Data type: NUMERIC(7,2). Example: 983.5.
ScanProcessing.SafeBak: Full name: 'Backup Status'. Explanation: Indicates progress of data backup. Data type: CHAR(8). Possible categories: In Progress, Completed, Pending.
ScanProcessing.StashLoc: Full name: 'Storage Location'. Explanation: Where processed data is stored. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Possible categories: Local, Network, Cloud.
ScanProcessing.StationLink: Full name: 'Total Station Integration'. Explanation: Indicates if total station integration is used. Data type: CHAR(6). Example: 'Yes'.
ScanProcessing.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Site code for which processing applies. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanQC.AccuCheck: Full name: 'Accuracy Assessment'. Explanation: Indicates if accuracy check was done. Data type: VARCHAR(22). Possible categories: Pending, Completed, Not Required.
ScanQC.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Points to a project for QC. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanQC.ArchStat: Full name: 'Archival Status'. Explanation: Indicates if data is archived. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Possible categories: Verified, Pending.
ScanQC.CopyStat: Full name: 'Copyright Status'. Explanation: Copyright or licensing restriction. Data type: CHAR(10). Possible categories: Reserved, Restricted, Open Access.
ScanQC.CrewRef: Full name: 'Operator Reference'. Explanation: Identifies the operator associated with QC. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
ScanQC.CtrlState: Full name: 'Quality Control Status'. Explanation: State of QC checks. Data type: CHAR(10). Possible categories: Failed, Pending.
ScanQC.PubStat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether data is published, drafted, etc. Data type: VARCHAR(24). Possible categories: Draft, Submitted.
ScanQC.QualRegistry: Full name: 'QC Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for quality control records. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 9001.
ScanQC.RefMention: Full name: 'Data Citation'. Explanation: Reference or citation code for the data. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: Citation-8447, Citation-6197, Citation-8090, Citation-2238.
ScanQC.Remark: Full name: 'Additional Notes'. Explanation: Any free-text remarks or comments. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Sell shoulder understand serious degree particular game.'
ScanQC.ValiMeth: Full name: 'Validation Method'. Explanation: How the data was validated (automated or manual). Data type: VARCHAR(18). Possible categories: Automated, Visual.
ScanQC.ValiState: Full name: 'Validation Status'. Explanation: Final status of validation. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Rejected, Approved.
ScanRegistration.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Project ID linked to registration data. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanRegistration.CrewRef: Full name: 'Operator Reference'. Explanation: Operator ID who performed registration. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
ScanRegistration.CtrlPts: Full name: 'Control Points'. Explanation: Numeric codes for control points. Data type: VARCHAR(6). Possible categories: 73, 99, 6, 84.
ScanRegistration.ErrScale: Full name: 'Error Metrics'. Explanation: Type of error measurement. Data type: VARCHAR(20). Possible categories: Cloud-to-Mesh, Cloud-to-Cloud, RMSE.
ScanRegistration.ErrValMm: Full name: 'Error Value (mm)'. Explanation: Measured error in millimeters. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: 6.962.
ScanRegistration.LogAccuMm: Full name: 'Registration Accuracy (mm)'. Explanation: Accuracy of the registration in mm. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: 0.84.
ScanRegistration.LogMethod: Full name: 'Registration Method'. Explanation: Method for aligning scans. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Target-based, Hybrid, Automatic.
ScanRegistration.LogRegistry: Full name: 'Registration Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for registration logs. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 7001.
ScanRegistration.RefMark: Full name: 'Reference Markers'. Explanation: Numeric codes for registration targets. Data type: VARCHAR(6). Possible categories: 40, 31, 25, 21.
ScanRegistration.TransForm: Full name: 'Transformation Matrix'. Explanation: Identifier for the transform matrix used. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Matrix-47, Matrix-113, Matrix-543.
ScanSpatial.AngleAz: Full name: 'Orientation (degrees)'. Explanation: Azimuth or rotation angle around vertical axis. Data type: REAL. Example: 342.4.
ScanSpatial.AngleTilt: Full name: 'Tilt Angle (degrees)'. Explanation: Inclination angle from horizontal. Data type: DOUBLE PRECISION. Example: 23.9.
ScanSpatial.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Project ID linking spatial data. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanSpatial.AreaM2: Full name: 'Surface Area (m²)'. Explanation: Calculated area in square meters. Data type: NUMERIC(8,3). Example: 78.01.
ScanSpatial.BoxX: Full name: 'Bounding Box X (m)'. Explanation: Size of bounding box along X-axis, in meters. Data type: NUMERIC(8,2). Example: 40.12.
ScanSpatial.BoxY: Full name: 'Bounding Box Y (m)'. Explanation: Size of bounding box along Y-axis, in meters. Data type: NUMERIC(8,3). Example: 1.06.
ScanSpatial.BoxZ: Full name: 'Bounding Box Z (m)'. Explanation: Size of bounding box along Z-axis, in meters. Data type: NUMERIC(9,2). Example: 16.41.
ScanSpatial.CrewRef: Full name: 'Operator Reference'. Explanation: Operator ID for these spatial records. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
ScanSpatial.DomainRegistry: Full name: 'Spatial Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for spatial data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 4001.
ScanSpatial.GroundSpan: Full name: 'Ground Sampling Distance (mm)'. Explanation: Effective resolution on the ground, in mm. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: 4.13.
ScanSpatial.VolM3: Full name: 'Volume (m³)'. Explanation: Computed volume in cubic meters. Data type: NUMERIC(9,4). Example: 76.7.
Scans.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Links a scan to a specific project. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
Scans.ChronoTag: Full name: 'Scan Timestamp'. Explanation: Timestamp representing the scan date/time. Data type: TIMESTAMP. If stored as a numeric like 44302.55648, it may be an Excel serial date/time (days since 1900-01-00). Example: 44302.55648.
Scans.ClimTune: Full name: 'Weather Conditions'. Explanation: Indicates the weather during scanning. Data type: VARCHAR(22). Possible categories: Windy, Rainy, Cloudy, Clear.
Scans.CrewRef: Full name: 'Operator Reference'. Explanation: Records which operator performed the scan. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
Scans.FmtFile: Full name: 'File Format'. Explanation: Format in which scan data is saved. Data type: CHAR(4). Possible categories: PTS, PLY, OBJ, LAS, E57.
Scans.GBSize: Full name: 'File Size (GB)'. Explanation: Size of the scan file in gigabytes. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 24.71.
Scans.HueCatch: Full name: 'Color Capture'. Explanation: Mode of color recording. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Possible categories: RGB, Grayscale, None.
Scans.PressRatio: Full name: 'Compression Ratio'. Explanation: Compression level applied to scan data. Data type: NUMERIC(4,2). Example: 3.22.
Scans.QuestRegistry: Full name: 'Scan ID'. Explanation: Primary key identifying a particular scan. Data type: VARCHAR(16). Example: 'ASD409481'.
Scans.ScanCount: Full name: 'Number of Scans'. Explanation: Numeric count of scans in a set. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 5.
Scans.SpanMin: Full name: 'Scan Duration (min)'. Explanation: Duration of the scanning process, in minutes. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 63.
Scans.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Associates the scan with a site code. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
Sites.DepthC: Full name: 'Depth (cm)'. Explanation: Depth measurement in centimeters. Data type: NUMERIC(7,1). Example: 329.9.
Sites.DigUnit: Full name: 'Excavation Unit'. Explanation: Designation of a specific trench or unit. Data type: VARCHAR(8). Example: 'Unit-C9'.
Sites.EntryStat: Full name: 'Site Access Status'. Explanation: Access restrictions or availability of the site. Data type: VARCHAR(8). Possible categories: Closed, Restricted, Open.
Sites.EnvHaz: Full name: 'Environmental Risk'. Explanation: Rating of environmental hazards. Data type: CHAR(6). Possible categories: Low, Medium, High.
Sites.GeoX: Full name: 'Latitude'. Explanation: Geographic latitude in decimal degrees. Data type: NUMERIC(8,5). Example: -9.60213.
Sites.GeoY: Full name: 'Longitude'. Explanation: Geographic longitude in decimal degrees. Data type: NUMERIC(8,5). Example: -2.75641.
Sites.GridTrace: Full name: 'Grid Reference'. Explanation: Grid or coordinate notation for the site location. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'S29-E8'.
Sites.GuardHint: Full name: 'Weather Protection'. Explanation: Indicates if the site is protected from weather. Data type: CHAR(5). Possible categories: None, Temporary.
Sites.GuessDate: Full name: 'Estimated Date'. Explanation: Approximate or labeled date (BCE/CE). Data type: VARCHAR(20). Possible categories: -2929 BCE, 1335 BCE, -4985 BCE, -3387 BCE.
Sites.HealthEval: Full name: 'Health and Safety Status'. Explanation: Indicates health/safety approvals. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Possible categories: Approved, Review, Pending.
Sites.HeightM: Full name: 'Altitude (m)'. Explanation: Elevation above sea level, in meters. Data type: NUMERIC(7,1). Example: 4391.4.
Sites.InsurStat: Full name: 'Insurance Status'. Explanation: Whether the site is insured, pending, or expired. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Expired, Pending.
Sites.PhaseFactor: Full name: 'Cultural/Historical Period'. Explanation: Indicates the archaeological or historical phase. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Iron Age, Medieval, Classical, Bronze Age.
Sites.PresStat: Full name: 'Preservation Status'. Explanation: Condition of preservation at the site. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Excellent, Fair, Critical, Good, Poor.
Sites.RiskEval: Full name: 'Risk Assessment Status'. Explanation: Status of risk evaluation for the site. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Required, Completed, Pending.
Sites.SafeRank: Full name: 'Security Level'. Explanation: Level of security or safety at the site. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Minimal, High, Standard.
Sites.TypeSite: Full name: 'Site Type'. Explanation: Classification of the site. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Burial, Industrial, Military, Settlement, Religious.
Sites.ZoneLabel: Full name: 'Site Name'. Explanation: Descriptive name or label for the site. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Site-North Alexanderville'.
Sites.ZoneRegistry: Full name: 'Site Code'. Explanation: Primary key for a site. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.

requests.specific_A: For each event that has budget lines (matched by event id), average the ratio (`spent` − `amount`) / `amount` over its budget lines. Within each event `location`, rank the events by this average from highest to lowest (events with no average last). Tied events share a rank and the next rank is skipped. Show the event id, location, average ratio and rank for events ranked 3 or better. Events with no recorded location are grouped together as one location and ranked among themselves.
requests.specific_B: For each event that has budget lines (matched by event id), average the ratio (`spent` − `amount`) / `amount` over its budget lines. Within each event `location`, rank the events by this average from highest to lowest (events with no average last). Tied events share a rank and the next rank is skipped. Show the event id, location, average ratio and rank for events ranked 3 or better. Leave out events with no recorded location.
requests.open: For each location, what are the top 3 events by average budget overspend ratio, (`spent` − `amount`) / `amount` averaged over each event's budget lines? Rank events within each location from highest to lowest ratio, with events lacking a ratio last. Tied events share a rank and the next rank is skipped. Show the event id, location, average ratio and rank.

readings.A: Events with a missing location are ranked among themselves as one location group and can appear in the result.
readings.B: Events with a missing location are left out of the ranking and the result.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "budget"."link_to_event" AS "e", "event"."location" AS "g", AVG((CAST(("budget"."spent" - "budget"."amount") AS REAL) / "budget"."amount")) AS "m1" FROM "budget" AS "budget" INNER JOIN "event" AS "event" ON "event"."event_id" = "budget"."link_to_event" GROUP BY "budget"."link_to_event", "event"."location"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY "s1"."g" ORDER BY "s1"."m1" DESC) AS "r" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s2"."e" AS "e", "s2"."g" AS "g", "s2"."m1" AS "m1", "s2"."r" AS "r" FROM "s2" AS "s2" WHERE "s2"."r" <= 3
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "budget"."link_to_event" AS "e", "event"."location" AS "g", AVG((CAST(("budget"."spent" - "budget"."amount") AS REAL) / "budget"."amount")) AS "m1" FROM "budget" AS "budget" INNER JOIN "event" AS "event" ON "event"."event_id" = "budget"."link_to_event" WHERE "event"."location" IS NOT NULL GROUP BY "budget"."link_to_event", "event"."location"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY "s1"."g" ORDER BY "s1"."m1" DESC) AS "r" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s2"."e" AS "e", "s2"."g" AS "g", "s2"."m1" AS "m1", "s2"."r" AS "r" FROM "s2" AS "s2" WHERE "s2"."r" <= 3

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from budget records; inner-join to event on event.event_id = budget.link_to_event (budget rows with no matching event are dropped); group by budget.link_to_event and event.location; for each group, compute the average of (spent − amount) / amount, ignoring missing values
Within each location, rank the events by that average, highest first, missing last; tied events share a rank and the next rank is skipped (RANK)
Keep only rows whose rank is 3 or better
Event id (budget.link_to_event)
Event location
The average overspend ratio, not rounded
The rank within the location

A.requirement: Events with no location (NULL) are kept and ranked together as their own location group

B.requirement: Events with no location (NULL) are excluded before ranking

requests.specific_A: Group the fee records by fee currency (`feecoin`), with records lacking a currency forming one group. For each currency, work out the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average relative rebate-to-fee gap, (`rebrate` minus `feerate`) divided by `feerate`, which is missing when the fee rate is 0. In both averages, count a zero rebate as a real value. For the benchmark, take the mean of the per-currency average total rebates, with each currency counting equally. Keep only the currencies whose average total rebate is strictly above this benchmark (if the benchmark is missing, keep none), and return a single row with: the average of their average total rebates, the average of their average relative rebate-to-fee gaps, and the average amount by which their average total rebate exceeds the benchmark. Skip missing values in every average (an average with nothing to average is missing), and don't round the results.
requests.specific_B: Group the fee records by fee currency (`feecoin`), with records lacking a currency forming one group. For each currency, work out the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average relative rebate-to-fee gap, (`rebrate` minus `feerate`) divided by `feerate`, which is missing when the fee rate is 0. In both averages, treat a zero rebate as not applicable and leave it out: a `rebtotal` of 0 is skipped in the rebate average, and a record with `rebrate` of 0 is skipped in the gap average. For the benchmark, take the mean of the per-currency average total rebates, with each currency counting equally. Keep only the currencies whose average total rebate is strictly above this benchmark (if the benchmark is missing, keep none), and return a single row with: the average of their average total rebates, the average of their average relative rebate-to-fee gaps, and the average amount by which their average total rebate exceeds the benchmark. Skip missing values in every average (an average with nothing to average is missing), and don't round the results.
requests.open: By fee currency (`feecoin`, with records lacking a currency treated as one group), which currencies have an average maker rebate (`rebtotal`) strictly above the average of the currencies' average maker rebates, each currency counting equally? For those currencies, give me one row: the mean of their average maker rebate, the mean of their average relative gap between maker rebate rate and fee rate ((`rebrate` minus `feerate`) divided by `feerate`, missing when the fee rate is 0), and the mean amount by which their average maker rebate exceeds that cross-currency benchmark. If the benchmark is missing, no currencies count. Skip missing values in the averages (missing if there's nothing to average) and don't round anything.

readings.A: Zero rebates are real values and are included in the per-currency rebate and gap averages.
readings.B: Zero rebates mean no rebate applies (taker fills) and are left out of the per-currency rebate and gap averages.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "fees"."feecoin" AS "g", AVG("fees"."rebtotal") AS "m1", AVG((CAST(("fees"."rebrate" - "fees"."feerate") AS REAL) / "fees"."feerate")) AS "m2" FROM "fees" AS "fees" GROUP BY "fees"."feecoin"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "fees"."feecoin" AS "g", AVG(NULLIF("fees"."rebtotal", 0)) AS "m1", AVG((CAST((NULLIF("fees"."rebrate", 0) - "fees"."feerate") AS REAL) / "fees"."feerate")) AS "m2" FROM "fees" AS "fees" GROUP BY "fees"."feecoin"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from all fee records, grouped by fee currency `feecoin`; records with missing feecoin form one group
Per currency: average of `rebtotal` and average of (`rebrate` − `feerate`) ÷ `feerate` (missing when feerate is 0); missing values ignored, missing if none
Benchmark = mean of the per-currency average rebtotal values, each currency counting equally
Keep only currencies whose average rebtotal is strictly greater than the benchmark; if the benchmark is missing, keep none
All kept currencies collapse into exactly one result row
Average of kept currencies' average rebtotal
Average of kept currencies' average relative rebate-to-fee gap
Average of (currency average rebtotal − benchmark) over kept currencies; columns in order 1,2,3; missing ignored; no rounding

A.requirement: Zero rebates (rebtotal = 0, rebrate = 0) are counted as real values in both per-currency averages

B.requirement: Zero rebates are treated as not applicable: rebtotal 0 is skipped in the rebate average and rows with rebrate 0 are skipped in the gap average

requests.specific_A: For each event status in the budget table (`budget.event_status`), what is the average of the amount budgeted minus the amount spent (`amount` − `spent`), ignoring rows where that difference is missing? How far is each status's average from the baseline you get by simply averaging those per-status averages, with each status counting equally? Return the status, its average, and its average minus that baseline, all unrounded. Return nothing if the baseline is missing.
requests.specific_B: For each event status in the budget table (`budget.event_status`), what is the average of the amount budgeted minus the amount spent (`amount` − `spent`), ignoring rows where that difference is missing? How far is each status's average from the baseline you get by averaging `amount` − `spent` across all budget rows together, with each budget row counting equally? Return the status, its average, and its average minus that baseline, all unrounded. Return nothing if the baseline is missing.
requests.open: For each event status in the budget table, what's the average amount left over (amount budgeted minus amount spent, ignoring missing values), and how does it compare with the overall average? Show the status, its average, and its difference from the overall average, unrounded, and return nothing if there is no overall average to compare against.

readings.A: Compare each status's average leftover (amount − spent) with the unweighted mean of the per-status averages.
readings.B: Compare each status's average leftover (amount − spent) with the average leftover over all budget rows taken together.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "budget"."event_status" AS "g", AVG(("budget"."amount" - "budget"."spent")) AS "m1" FROM "budget" AS "budget" GROUP BY "budget"."event_status"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "budget"."event_status" AS "g", AVG(("budget"."amount" - "budget"."spent")) AS "m1" FROM "budget" AS "budget" GROUP BY "budget"."event_status"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG(("budget"."amount" - "budget"."spent")) AS "v" FROM "budget" AS "budget") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every `budget` row (no filter). Group the rows by `budget.event_status`, so each status, including a missing status, gives one row.
Return the event status (`budget.event_status`) as the first column.
The second column is, per status, the average of `amount` − `spent` over its budget rows. Rows where the difference is missing are ignored. The value is missing if a status has no such rows.
Attach a single overall baseline value to every status row. If the baseline is missing, no rows are returned.
The third column is the status's average minus the overall baseline.
No rounding, no ordering and no row limit. The columns come in the order status, average, difference.

A.requirement: The baseline is the plain average of the per-status averages from column 2, with each status counted once (missing averages ignored).

B.requirement: The baseline is the average of `amount` − `spent` over all budget rows together (missing values ignored), so each budget row carries equal weight.

requests.specific_A: For each transaction in `sentimentandfundamentals` (`transref`), take the average analyst coverage count (`anlycount`, ignoring missing values). Keep only the transactions whose average is above the overall average of those per-transaction averages. For each one, show `transref`, its average, how far it is above that overall average, and how far it is above the average among just the kept transactions. Sort by that last difference, highest first (missing last), and return exactly 10 rows, cutting any ties at 10th place arbitrarily. Don't round.
requests.specific_B: For each transaction in `sentimentandfundamentals` (`transref`), take the average analyst coverage count (`anlycount`, ignoring missing values). Keep only the transactions whose average is above the overall average of those per-transaction averages. For each one, show `transref`, its average, how far it is above that overall average, and how far it is above the average among just the kept transactions. Sort by that last difference, highest first (missing last), and return the top 10 rows plus every other row tied with the 10th. Don't round.
requests.open: For each transaction in `sentimentandfundamentals` (`transref`), take the average analyst coverage count (`anlycount`, ignoring missing values). Keep only the transactions whose average is above the overall average of those per-transaction averages. For each one, show `transref`, its average, how far it is above that overall average, and how far it is above the average among just the kept transactions. Give me the top 10 by that last difference, highest first (missing last). Don't round.

readings.A: Return exactly ten rows. Ties at the cut are broken arbitrarily.
readings.B: Return the top ten plus every row tied with the tenth.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "sentimentandfundamentals"."transref" AS "e", AVG("sentimentandfundamentals"."anlycount") AS "m1" FROM "sentimentandfundamentals" AS "sentimentandfundamentals" GROUP BY "sentimentandfundamentals"."transref"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "sentimentandfundamentals"."transref" AS "e", AVG("sentimentandfundamentals"."anlycount") AS "m1" FROM "sentimentandfundamentals" AS "sentimentandfundamentals" GROUP BY "sentimentandfundamentals"."transref"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") >= (SELECT ("x"."m1" - "y"."v") AS "t" FROM "s3" AS "x" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "y" ON NOT ("y"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("x"."m1" - "y"."v") DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 9) ORDER BY ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") DESC

Compare each transaction's average with the overall average of those per-transaction averages. Keep only transactions whose average is strictly greater.
`transref`.

Top 10 by that ordering.

requests.specific_A: For each circuit city (`circuits.location`), count the qualifying records (one per driver per race) at races held there, and work out the city's share as that count divided by the total across all cities. List the cities whose share is above the average share across cities, showing the city, the count, the share, and how far the share is above the average share, all unrounded.
requests.specific_B: For each circuit city (`circuits.location`), count the distinct races held there that have qualifying data, and work out the city's share as that count divided by the total across all cities. List the cities whose share is above the average share across cities, showing the city, the count, the share, and how far the share is above the average share, all unrounded.
requests.open: Which circuit cities have an above-average share of qualifying? For each, show the city, its qualifying count, that count as a share of the total across all cities, and how far its share is above the average city share (all unrounded).

readings.A: Each city's count is its number of driver qualifying entries, and its share is its share of all qualifying entries.
readings.B: Each city's count is its number of distinct races with qualifying data (qualifying sessions), and its share is its share of all such sessions.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "circuits"."location" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "qualifying" AS "qualifying" INNER JOIN "races" AS "races" ON "races"."raceId" = "qualifying"."raceId" INNER JOIN "circuits" AS "circuits" ON "circuits"."circuitId" = "races"."circuitId" GROUP BY "circuits"."location"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "circuits"."location" AS "g", COUNT(DISTINCT "qualifying"."raceId") AS "m1" FROM "qualifying" AS "qualifying" INNER JOIN "races" AS "races" ON "races"."raceId" = "qualifying"."raceId" INNER JOIN "circuits" AS "circuits" ON "circuits"."circuitId" = "races"."circuitId" GROUP BY "circuits"."location"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from `qualifying` records, inner-joined to `races` on raceId and to `circuits` on circuitId, grouped by circuit city (`circuits.location`); only cities with qualifying data appear
Each city's share is its count divided by the sum of the counts across all cities
Keep only the cities whose share is greater than the average share across cities
Return the city (`circuits.location`)
Return the city's count
Return the city's share, unrounded
Return the share minus the average share, unrounded; no ordering is specified

A.requirement: The count is every qualifying record, one per driver per race (COUNT(*))

B.requirement: The count is the number of distinct races with qualifying data (COUNT(DISTINCT raceId))

requests.specific_A: Linking lab records to patients by `ID` (dropping unmatched lab records), first average each patient's (`ID`, `SEX`) `ALB` and their per-test ratio of `UN` to `T-BIL`. Then, for each sex (treating every `SEX` value, including blank or missing, as its own group), average those patient-level figures. Which sexes have an average `ALB` above the mean of the sex-level `ALB` averages? Show the sex, its average `ALB`, its average `UN`/`T-BIL` ratio, and how far its `ALB` average is above that mean. Averages ignore missing values (including ratios that can't be computed); don't round.
requests.specific_B: Linking lab records to patients by `ID` (dropping unmatched lab records), first average each patient's (`ID`, `SEX`) `ALB` and their per-test ratio of `UN` to `T-BIL`. Then, for each sex (leaving out patients whose `SEX` is blank or missing), average those patient-level figures. Which sexes have an average `ALB` above the mean of the sex-level `ALB` averages? Show the sex, its average `ALB`, its average `UN`/`T-BIL` ratio, and how far its `ALB` average is above that mean. Averages ignore missing values (including ratios that can't be computed); don't round.
requests.open: Linking lab records to patients by `ID` (dropping unmatched lab records), first average each patient's (`ID`, `SEX`) `ALB` and their per-test ratio of `UN` to `T-BIL`. Then average those patient-level figures for each sex. Which sexes have an average `ALB` above the mean of the sex-level `ALB` averages? Show the sex, its average `ALB`, its average `UN`/`T-BIL` ratio, and how far its `ALB` average is above that mean. Averages ignore missing values (including ratios that can't be computed); don't round.

readings.A: A blank sex is a group of its own and contributes to the mean of the sex-level ALB averages.
readings.B: A blank sex means unknown, so those patients are dropped before grouping and before the mean is computed.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Laboratory"."ID" AS "e", "Patient"."SEX" AS "g", AVG("Laboratory"."ALB") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("Laboratory"."UN" AS REAL) / "Laboratory"."T-BIL")) AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" INNER JOIN "Patient" AS "Patient" ON "Patient"."ID" = "Laboratory"."ID" GROUP BY "Laboratory"."ID", "Patient"."SEX"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT AVG("s2"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s2" AS "s2") SELECT "s2"."g" AS "g", "s2"."m1" AS "m1", "s2"."m2" AS "m2", ("s2"."m1" - "s3"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s2" AS "s2" INNER JOIN "s3" AS "s3" ON NOT ("s3"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s2"."m1" > "s3"."v"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Laboratory"."ID" AS "e", "Patient"."SEX" AS "g", AVG("Laboratory"."ALB") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("Laboratory"."UN" AS REAL) / "Laboratory"."T-BIL")) AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" INNER JOIN "Patient" AS "Patient" ON "Patient"."ID" = "Laboratory"."ID" WHERE "Patient"."SEX" <> '' GROUP BY "Laboratory"."ID", "Patient"."SEX"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT AVG("s2"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s2" AS "s2") SELECT "s2"."g" AS "g", "s2"."m1" AS "m1", "s2"."m2" AS "m2", ("s2"."m1" - "s3"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s2" AS "s2" INNER JOIN "s3" AS "s3" ON NOT ("s3"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s2"."m1" > "s3"."v"

shared_requirements.requirement: Use Laboratory records.
Link each lab record to its Patient by ID with an inner join. Drop unmatched lab records. Take SEX from Patient.
First, for each patient (ID, SEX), take the average ALB. Then, for each sex, average those patient-level values.
First, for each patient, take the average of the per-test ratio UN ÷ T-BIL (ratios that can't be computed count as missing and are ignored). Then, for each sex, average those patient-level values.
The overall mean is the mean of the sex-level ALB averages. Keep only sexes whose average ALB is strictly above it. Output (4) is how far the sex's average ALB is above that mean. No rounding.
The sex value.

A.requirement: Keep every SEX value, including blank (and missing), as its own group. These groups count toward the overall mean.

B.requirement: Exclude patients whose SEX is blank or missing before any grouping.

requests.specific_A: Match each telescope to its observatory on `observstation`, and drop unmatched telescopes. For each moon phase (`observatories.lunarstage`; a missing phase is its own group), compute two things: the average bandwidth usage (`telescopes.bandusagepct`) over its telescopes, ignoring missing values, and the number of telescopes. Keep the phases whose average is above the mean of all the phase averages. Return one row with three values: the average of the kept phases' bandwidth averages, the total number of telescopes across the kept phases, and the average amount by which the kept phases exceed that mean. Don't round.
requests.specific_B: Match each telescope to its observatory on `observstation`, and drop unmatched telescopes. For each moon phase (`observatories.lunarstage`; a missing phase is its own group), compute two things: the average bandwidth usage (`telescopes.bandusagepct`) over its telescopes, ignoring missing values, and the number of distinct observatory stations. Keep the phases whose average is above the mean of all the phase averages. Return one row with three values: the average of the kept phases' bandwidth averages, the total of those distinct-station counts across the kept phases, and the average amount by which the kept phases exceed that mean. Don't round.
requests.open: Match each telescope to its observatory on `observstation`, and drop unmatched telescopes. For each moon phase (`observatories.lunarstage`; a missing phase is its own group), find the average bandwidth usage (`telescopes.bandusagepct`), ignoring missing values, and how many are in that phase. Keep the phases whose average is above the mean of all the phase averages. Give one row with three values: the average of those phases' bandwidth averages, the total count across them, and the average amount by which they exceed the mean. Don't round.

readings.A: Each phase's count is its number of telescopes, and column 2 sums these counts over the above-average phases.
readings.B: Each phase's count is its number of distinct observatory stations, and column 2 sums these counts over the above-average phases.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "observatories"."lunarstage" AS "g", AVG("telescopes"."bandusagepct") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" INNER JOIN "observatories" AS "observatories" ON "observatories"."observstation" = "telescopes"."observstation" GROUP BY "observatories"."lunarstage"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", SUM("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "observatories"."lunarstage" AS "g", AVG("telescopes"."bandusagepct") AS "m1", COUNT(DISTINCT "telescopes"."observstation") AS "m2" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" INNER JOIN "observatories" AS "observatories" ON "observatories"."observstation" = "telescopes"."observstation" GROUP BY "observatories"."lunarstage"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", SUM("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"

shared_requirements.requirement: Match each telescope to its observatory where `telescopes.observstation` equals `observatories.observstation` (exact text match). Drop unmatched telescopes. Group by moon phase (`observatories.lunarstage`), with a missing phase forming its own group.

For each phase, compute the average bandwidth usage (`telescopes.bandusagepct`) over its telescope records, ignoring missing values. Keep the phases whose average is strictly greater than the mean of all the phase averages, and record each kept phase's excess over that mean.
Return a single row over the kept phases.
Column 1: the average of the kept phases' bandwidth averages.
Column 3: the average excess of the kept phases over the mean. No rounding.

A.requirement: Column 2: the total number of telescope records across the kept phases.

B.requirement: Column 2: the sum, across the kept phases, of each phase's number of distinct observatory stations.

context.documentation:
ObservationalConditions.ObsDate: Full name: 'Observation Date'. Explanation: Local date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD). Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-08-01'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsDurHrs: Full name: 'Observation Duration (hours)'. Explanation: How long the observation lasted in hours. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '2.50'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsTime: Full name: 'Observation Time'. Explanation: Local time of the observation in HH:MM:SS. Data type: TIME. Example: '13:45:59'.
ObservationalConditions.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-PQR-9876'.
Observatories.AirTempC: Full name: 'Air Temperature (°C)'. Explanation: Ambient temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '18.45'.
Observatories.AtmosTransparency: Full name: 'Atmospheric Transparency'. Explanation: A numeric measure of how transparent the atmosphere is. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.867'.
Observatories.GeomagStatus: Full name: 'Geomagnetic Activity'. Explanation: The level of geomagnetic activity during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Active, Quiet, Storm.
Observatories.HumidityRate: Full name: 'Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Relative humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '62.300'.
Observatories.LunarDistDeg: Full name: 'Moon Distance (Degrees)'. Explanation: Angular distance to the Moon in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '97.52'.
Observatories.LunarStage: Full name: 'Lunar Phase'. Explanation: The current phase of the Moon during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: First Quarter, Full, Last Quarter, New.

ResearchProcess.PubStat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether findings about the signal have been published. Data type: CHAR(25). Possible categories: Draft, Published, Submitted.
ResearchProcess.ResPrio: Full name: 'Research Priority'. Explanation: How urgently this signal needs scientific attention. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium.
ResearchProcess.SecClass: Full name: 'Security Classification'. Explanation: Visibility and clearance level for the data. Data type: CHAR(35). Possible categories: Classified, Public, Restricted.
ResearchProcess.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-MNO-7890'.

SignalAdvancedPhenomena.GravLens: Full name: 'Gravitational Lensing'. Explanation: Whether the signal is affected by gravitational lensing. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: None, Strong, Weak.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.InterMedEffects: Full name: 'Interstellar Medium Effects'. Explanation: Impact of interstellar medium on the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.LangStruct: Full name: 'Language Structure'. Explanation: Presence of linguistic or structured patterns. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Complex, None, Simple.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.MsgContent: Full name: 'Message Content'. Explanation: Indicates whether an actual message was detected. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Identified, None, Possible.

SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SciImpact: Full name: 'Scientific Impact'. Explanation: Significance of the signal to scientific research. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Major, Minor, Moderate.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-ABC-1234'.
