requests.specific_A: For each order reference (`orderexecutions.ordersmark`, with executions lacking a reference counted together as one group), count its execution records and compute its share: that count divided by the total number of execution records. Then compute the average share across order references. List the order reference, execution count, share, and share minus the average share, without rounding, sorted by that difference from largest to smallest (missing values last). Return exactly the first 10 rows; if rows tie at the 10th place, include only as many of them as needed to reach 10, chosen arbitrarily.
requests.specific_B: For each order reference (`orderexecutions.ordersmark`, with executions lacking a reference counted together as one group), count its execution records and compute its share: that count divided by the total number of execution records. Then compute the average share across order references. List the order reference, execution count, share, and share minus the average share, without rounding, sorted by that difference from largest to smallest (missing values last). Rank the rows by that difference, with tied rows sharing a rank and later ranks skipping accordingly, and return every row ranked 10th or better, so all rows tied at the 10th place are included even if that gives more than 10 rows.
requests.open: For each order reference (`orderexecutions.ordersmark`, with executions lacking a reference counted together as one group), count its execution records and compute its share of all execution records. What are the top 10 order references by how far their share is above the average share across order references? Show the order reference, execution count, share and share minus the average share, without rounding, from largest difference to smallest (missing values last).

readings.A: Return exactly 10 rows; any rows tied with the 10th are dropped arbitrarily.
readings.B: Return every row whose rank is within the top 10, including all rows tied at the 10th place.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orderexecutions"."ordersmark" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "orderexecutions" AS "orderexecutions" GROUP BY "orderexecutions"."ordersmark"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orderexecutions"."ordersmark" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "orderexecutions" AS "orderexecutions" GROUP BY "orderexecutions"."ordersmark"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "r"."e" AS "e", "r"."m1" AS "m1", "r"."m2" AS "m2", "r"."m3" AS "m3" FROM (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3", RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") DESC) AS "rk" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL)) AS "r" WHERE "r"."rk" <= 10 ORDER BY "r"."m3" DESC

Share = group count ÷ total number of execution records (sum of the counts); rows dropped if the total is missing
Benchmark = average share across groups; difference = share − average share (rows dropped if average missing)
Order reference `ordersmark`
Execution count
Share
Share minus average share; no rounding
Sort by the difference descending, missing values last
Cut at the top 10 by the difference

B.requirement: Rank by difference with ties sharing a rank (gaps after ties); return every row ranked 10th or better, including all rows tied at the cut

requests.specific_A: Total up each customer's invoice `Total`s, and compute each customer's share of overall revenue (their total divided by the sum over all customers). Find the average share across customers, and keep the customers whose share is above it. Return one row with: the average total spent by those customers, their average share, and the average difference between their share and the average share (share minus average share). Don't round.
requests.specific_B: Total up each customer's invoice `Total`s, and compute each customer's share of overall revenue (their total divided by the sum over all customers). Find the average share across customers, and keep the customers whose share is above it. Return one row with: the average total spent by those customers, their average share, and the average relative difference between their share and the average share ((share minus average share) divided by average share). Don't round.
requests.open: Total up each customer's invoice totals and work out each customer's share of overall revenue (their total over the sum across all customers). Keep the customers whose share is above the average share. Give one row with: the average amount those customers spent, their average share, and on average how much their share beats the average share. No rounding.

readings.A: A customer's excess is their share minus the average share.
readings.B: A customer's excess is their share minus the average share, divided by the average share.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Invoice"."CustomerId" AS "e", SUM("Invoice"."Total") AS "m1" FROM "Invoice" AS "Invoice" GROUP BY "Invoice"."CustomerId"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Invoice"."CustomerId" AS "e", SUM("Invoice"."Total") AS "m1" FROM "Invoice" AS "Invoice" GROUP BY "Invoice"."CustomerId"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", (("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") / "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

requests.specific_A: Using the feature records (`scanfeatures`) and ignoring missing detected-feature counts (`traitcount`), add up the counts for each site code so that every site gets one combined total. Work out each site's share of the overall feature total, and keep only those whose share is above the average share across sites. For the 10 with the largest margin above that average, list the site code, its feature count, its share, and how far its share exceeds the average share, from the largest margin down. Don't round.
requests.specific_B: Using the feature records (`scanfeatures`) and ignoring missing detected-feature counts (`traitcount`), take each record's count on its own, without combining records of the same site code, so a site can appear more than once. Work out each record's share of the overall feature total, and keep only those whose share is above the average share across records. For the 10 with the largest margin above that average, list the site code, its feature count, its share, and how far its share exceeds the average share, from the largest margin down. Don't round.
requests.open: Using the feature records (`scanfeatures`) and ignoring missing detected-feature counts (`traitcount`), which site codes' feature counts make up an above-average share of the overall feature total? For the top 10 by margin above the average share, show the site code, the feature count, the share, and how far the share exceeds the average share, largest margin first. Don't round.

readings.A: Sum detected features per site, then compare each site's share with the average site share.
readings.B: Treat each feature record separately, and compare its share with the average record share.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scanfeatures"."zoneref" AS "e", SUM("scanfeatures"."traitcount") AS "m1" FROM "scanfeatures" AS "scanfeatures" GROUP BY "scanfeatures"."zoneref"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v" ORDER BY ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the feature records (`scanfeatures`). Ignore missing `traitcount` values in all sums and averages.
Each unit's share is its detected-feature count divided by the overall total of `traitcount` across all records.
Keep only the units whose share is strictly greater than the average share across all units.
Site code (`zoneref`).
The share.
The share minus the average share.
Sort by that excess, largest first, with missing values last.
Keep the first 10 rows. Do not round any output.

A.requirement: The unit is the site: its detected-feature count is the sum of `traitcount` over all of that site's records, and the average share is taken across sites.

B.requirement: The unit is each individual feature record: its count is that record's own `traitcount`, the average share is taken across records, and a site can appear more than once.

requests.specific_A: For each observatory (`observstation` in the telescopes table), count its telescopes and compute its share of all telescopes as a fraction (its count divided by the total number of telescopes across all observatories). Then subtract the average share across observatories from each observatory's share. List the observatory, its telescope count, its share, and that difference, sorted by the difference from highest to lowest. Return exactly 10 rows and no more: if several observatories are tied on the difference at 10th place, just pick any of them to fill the remaining spots.
requests.specific_B: For each observatory (`observstation` in the telescopes table), count its telescopes and compute its share of all telescopes as a fraction (its count divided by the total number of telescopes across all observatories). Then subtract the average share across observatories from each observatory's share. List the observatory, its telescope count, its share, and that difference, sorted by the difference from highest to lowest. Return the top 10, and if several observatories are tied on the difference at 10th place, include all of them, even if the list then runs past 10 rows.
requests.open: For each observatory (`observstation` in the telescopes table), count its telescopes and work out its share of all telescopes as a fraction (its count divided by the total across all observatories). How far is each observatory's share above or below the average share? Show the observatory, its telescope count, its share and that difference for the top 10 observatories by the difference, highest first.

readings.A: Return exactly 10 observatories. Ties at the 10th place are broken arbitrarily.
readings.B: Return the top 10 observatories plus every observatory tied with the 10th place on the difference.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "r"."e" AS "e", "r"."m1" AS "m1", "r"."m2" AS "m2", "r"."m3" AS "m3" FROM (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3", RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") DESC) AS "rk" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL)) AS "r" WHERE "r"."rk" <= 10 ORDER BY "r"."m3" DESC

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every telescopes record, group by observatory (`observstation`) and count the records in each group.
Attach the grand total of telescopes, which is the sum of all the group counts, to every observatory.
Observatory (`observstation`).
The observatory's telescope count.
Share as a fraction: count ÷ total. No rounding.
Share minus the average share across all observatories. No rounding.
Sort by that difference, highest first.
Cut off at the top 10.

A.requirement: Return exactly 10 rows. If observatories are tied at the cut, pick any of them to fill the remaining spots.

B.requirement: Keep every observatory ranked in the top 10 using rank with ties, so everything tied with the 10th place is included and the result can exceed 10 rows.

context.schema:
CREATE TABLE "observationalconditions" (
  "signalref" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "obstime" text(6),
  "obsdate" text,
  "obsdurhrs" real(5,2),
  CONSTRAINT "observationalconditions_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalref"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_observcond_signalsref" FOREIGN KEY ("signalref") REFERENCES "signals" ("signalregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "observatories" (
  "observstation" text(60) NOT NULL,
  "weathprofile" text(40),
  "seeingprofile" text(50),
  "atmostransparency" real(5,3),
  "lunarstage" text(25),
  "lunardistdeg" real(7,2),

  "signalref" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "analysisprio" text,
  "followstat" text(25),

);

  "signalref" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "intermedeffects" text(40),

  "signalref" text(36) NOT NULL,

context.documentation:
ObservationalConditions.ObsDate: Full name: 'Observation Date'. Explanation: Local date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD). Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-08-01'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsDurHrs: Full name: 'Observation Duration (hours)'. Explanation: How long the observation lasted in hours. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '2.50'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsTime: Full name: 'Observation Time'. Explanation: Local time of the observation in HH:MM:SS. Data type: TIME. Example: '13:45:59'.
ObservationalConditions.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-PQR-9876'.
Observatories.AirTempC: Full name: 'Air Temperature (°C)'. Explanation: Ambient temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '18.45'.
Observatories.AtmosTransparency: Full name: 'Atmospheric Transparency'. Explanation: A numeric measure of how transparent the atmosphere is. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.867'.
Observatories.GeomagStatus: Full name: 'Geomagnetic Activity'. Explanation: The level of geomagnetic activity during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Active, Quiet, Storm.
Observatories.HumidityRate: Full name: 'Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Relative humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '62.300'.
Observatories.LunarDistDeg: Full name: 'Moon Distance (Degrees)'. Explanation: Angular distance to the Moon in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '97.52'.
Observatories.LunarStage: Full name: 'Lunar Phase'. Explanation: The current phase of the Moon during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: First Quarter, Full, Last Quarter, New.
Observatories.ObservStation: Full name: 'Observatory Name'. Explanation: This field holds the name or unique identifier for the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
Observatories.PressHpa: Full name: 'Pressure (hPa)'. Explanation: Atmospheric pressure in hectopascals. Data type: DECIMAL(6,1). Example: '1013.2'.
Observatories.SeeingProfile: Full name: 'Seeing Profile'. Explanation: Assessment of sky seeing conditions (atmospheric steadiness). Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
Observatories.SiderealLocal: Full name: 'Local Sidereal Time'. Explanation: Sidereal time at the observatory in HH:MM:SS format. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: '12:34:56'.
Observatories.SolarStatus: Full name: 'Solar Activity'. Explanation: The level of solar activity at the time of observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Moderate.
Observatories.WeathProfile: Full name: 'Weather Profile'. Explanation: A short description of weather conditions during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Clear, Cloudy, Partially Cloudy.
Observatories.WindSpeedMs: Full name: 'Wind Speed (m/s)'. Explanation: Wind speed in meters per second. Data type: NUMERIC(4,2). Example: '3.45'.
ResearchProcess.AnalysisPrio: Full name: 'Analysis Priority'. Explanation: Priority assigned for analyzing this signal. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, Urgent.
ResearchProcess.CollabStat: Full name: 'Collaboration Status'. Explanation: The nature of collaboration on this signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: International, Solo, Team.
ResearchProcess.DiscStat: Full name: 'Disclosure Status'. Explanation: How much information about the signal is shared publicly. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Full, None, Partial.
ResearchProcess.FollowStat: Full name: 'Follow-up Status'. Explanation: Status of any follow-up observations. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Required, Scheduled.
ResearchProcess.FundStat: Full name: 'Funding Status'. Explanation: Funding situation for further study. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Funded, Pending, Unfunded.
ResearchProcess.NotesMemo: Full name: 'Research Notes'. Explanation: Any extra remarks or context by researchers. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Project requires further funding...'
ResearchProcess.PeerRevStat: Full name: 'Peer Review Status'. Explanation: Where this signal stands in peer review. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, In Progress, Pending.
ResearchProcess.PubStat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether findings about the signal have been published. Data type: CHAR(25). Possible categories: Draft, Published, Submitted.
ResearchProcess.ResPrio: Full name: 'Research Priority'. Explanation: How urgently this signal needs scientific attention. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium.
ResearchProcess.SecClass: Full name: 'Security Classification'. Explanation: Visibility and clearance level for the data. Data type: CHAR(35). Possible categories: Classified, Public, Restricted.
ResearchProcess.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-MNO-7890'.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.CultSig: Full name: 'Cultural Significance'. Explanation: The level of cultural impact or interest. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: High, Low, None.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.EncryptEvid: Full name: 'Encryption Evidence'. Explanation: Whether there is indication the signal is encrypted. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: None, Possible, Strong.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.GravLens: Full name: 'Gravitational Lensing'. Explanation: Whether the signal is affected by gravitational lensing. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: None, Strong, Weak.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.InterMedEffects: Full name: 'Interstellar Medium Effects'. Explanation: Impact of interstellar medium on the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.LangStruct: Full name: 'Language Structure'. Explanation: Presence of linguistic or structured patterns. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Complex, None, Simple.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.MsgContent: Full name: 'Message Content'. Explanation: Indicates whether an actual message was detected. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Identified, None, Possible.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.QuantEffects: Full name: 'Quantum Effects'. Explanation: Quantum-level phenomena observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(85). Possible categories: None, Observed, Significant.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SciImpact: Full name: 'Scientific Impact'. Explanation: Significance of the signal to scientific research. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Major, Minor, Moderate.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-ABC-1234'.
SignalClassification.ClassConf: Full name: 'Classification Confidence (%)'. Explanation: How confident we are in the assigned signal class. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '92.50'.
SignalClassification.ComplexIdx: Full name: 'Complexity Index'. Explanation: Numeric measure of the signal’s complexity. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '5.678'.
SignalClassification.EntropyVal: Full name: 'Entropy'. Explanation: Entropy measurement of the signal. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.45'.
SignalClassification.InfoDense: Full name: 'Information Density'. Explanation: Estimated information per unit time/frequency. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.345'.
SignalClassification.PeriodSec: Full name: 'Period (s)'. Explanation: Duration of each cycle if periodic. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '12.345'.
SignalClassification.RepeatCount: Full name: 'Repetition Count'. Explanation: Number of times the signal has repeated. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '3'.
SignalClassification.SigClassType: Full name: 'Classification Type'. Explanation: High-level category for the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Artificial, Candidate, Natural, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SigPattern: Full name: 'Signal Pattern'. Explanation: Pattern observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: Periodic, Random, Structured, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-DEF-5678'.
SignalDecoding.AnalysisDp: Full name: 'Analysis Depth'. Explanation: How thoroughly the signal was analyzed. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Comprehensive, Detailed, Preliminary.
SignalDecoding.CompResources: Full name: 'Computational Resources'. Explanation: Level of computing power used. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Extreme, High, Low, Medium.
SignalDecoding.CompressRatio: Full name: 'Compression Ratio'. Explanation: Factor by which the raw signal data was compressed. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.500'.
SignalDecoding.ConfirmStat: Full name: 'Confirmation Status'. Explanation: Whether the decoding results have been confirmed. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Confirmed, Pending, Rejected.
SignalDecoding.DecodeConf: Full name: 'Decoding Confidence (%)'. Explanation: Confidence level that the decoding is correct. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '88.75'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeIters: Full name: 'Decoding Iterations'. Explanation: Number of algorithmic passes attempted. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '7'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeMethod: Full name: 'Decoding Method'. Explanation: Method used to decode the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: FFT, Neural Network, Quantum, Wavelet.
SignalDecoding.DecodeStat: Full name: 'Decoding Status'. Explanation: Status of the decoding process. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Failed, In Progress.
SignalDecoding.EncodeType: Full name: 'Encoding Type'. Explanation: The type of signal encoding used (e.g., Binary). Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Binary, Complex, Tertiary, Unknown.
SignalDecoding.ErrCorrLvl: Full name: 'Error Correction Level'. Explanation: Degree of error correction applied. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, None.
SignalDecoding.ProcTimeHrs: Full name: 'Processing Time (hours)'. Explanation: Total hours spent decoding. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.50'.
SignalDecoding.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal entry. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-GHI-9012'.
SignalDecoding.VerifLvl: Full name: 'Verification Level'. Explanation: Extent to which decoding has been verified. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Partially, Unverified, Verified.
SignalDynamics.AmpStab: Full name: 'Amplitude Stability'. Explanation: Consistency of signal amplitude. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Unstable'.
SignalDynamics.FreqStab: Full name: 'Frequency Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal’s frequency is. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighlyStable'.
SignalDynamics.ModStab: Full name: 'Modulation Stability'. Explanation: Consistency in the signal’s modulation scheme. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'Consistent'.
SignalDynamics.PhaseStab: Full name: 'Phase Stability'. Explanation: Any variation in signal phase. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'VaryingPhase'.
SignalDynamics.SigCoherence: Full name: 'Signal Coherence'. Explanation: How coherent the signal remains over its duration. Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighCoherence'.
SignalDynamics.SigDisp: Full name: 'Signal Dispersion'. Explanation: The degree to which the signal is dispersed (time/frequency smearing). Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'SignificantDisp'.
SignalDynamics.SigEvolve: Full name: 'Signal Evolution'. Explanation: Indicates if the signal changes/evolves during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Dynamic, Static, Unknown.
SignalDynamics.SigIntegrity: Full name: 'Signal Integrity'. Explanation: Rating of how intact or uncorrupted the signal is. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighIntegrity'.
SignalDynamics.SigRecurr: Full name: 'Signal Recurrence'. Explanation: Whether the signal recurs over time. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: None, Regular, Sporadic.
SignalDynamics.SigScint: Full name: 'Signal Scintillation'. Explanation: Fluctuation in signal amplitude due to propagation effects. Data type: VARCHAR(45). If no fixed categories, example: 'MildScintillation'.
SignalDynamics.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-JKL-3456'.
SignalDynamics.SpatStab: Full name: 'Spatial Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal is spatially (e.g., consistent direction). Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Moderate'.
SignalDynamics.TempStab: Full name: 'Temporal Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal remains over time. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Stable'.
SignalProbabilities.AnomScore: Full name: 'Anomaly Score'. Explanation: How unusual or unexpected the signal is. Data type: FLOAT. Example: '1.23'.
SignalProbabilities.ArtSrcProb: Full name: 'Artificial Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from an artificial source. Data type: NUMERIC(3,1). Example: '3.4'.
SignalProbabilities.BioSigProb: Full name: 'Biosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal indicates a biological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '45.21'.
SignalProbabilities.CorrScore: Full name: 'Correlation Score'. Explanation: How well the signal aligns with expected patterns. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.9950'.
SignalProbabilities.FalsePosProb: Full name: 'False Positive Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is falsely detected. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.0135'.
SignalProbabilities.NatSrcProb: Full name: 'Natural Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from a natural source. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '98.761'.
SignalProbabilities.SigUnique: Full name: 'Signal Uniqueness'. Explanation: A measure of how unique the signal is compared to others. Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '99.1234'.
SignalProbabilities.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-XYZ-9876'.
SignalProbabilities.SimIndex: Full name: 'Similarity Index'. Explanation: Compares the signal to known references. Data type: NUMERIC(5,4). Example: '0.8222'.
SignalProbabilities.TechSigProb: Full name: 'Technosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is of artificial technological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.6789'.
Signals.AtmoInterf: Full name: 'Atmospheric Interference'. Explanation: Impact of atmospheric conditions on signal. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
Signals.BwHz: Full name: 'Bandwidth (Hz)'. Explanation: Signal’s bandwidth in Hertz. Data type: DECIMAL(10,3). Example: '500000.000'.
Signals.CarrierFreqMhz: Full name: 'Carrier Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Frequency of the carrier wave in MHz. Data type: DECIMAL(9,3). Example: '1000.000'.
Signals.CenterFreqMhz: Full name: 'Center Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Center frequency of the detected signal in MHz. Data type: NUMERIC(8,3). Example: '1420.500'.
Signals.DetectInstr: Full name: 'Detection Instrument'. Explanation: The instrument type employed for detecting the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Infrared Array, Optical Telescope, Quantum Detector, Radio Telescope.
Signals.DoppShiftHz: Full name: 'Doppler Shift (Hz)'. Explanation: Measured Doppler shift of the signal in Hertz. Data type: DOUBLE PRECISION. Example: '142.75'.
Signals.FreqDriftHzs: Full name: 'Frequency Drift (Hz/s)'. Explanation: How fast the signal drifts in frequency over time. Data type: NUMERIC(9,3). Example: '0.123'.
Signals.FreqMhz: Full name: 'Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Signal’s nominal frequency in MHz. Data type: DECIMAL(9,3). Example: '1420.405'.
Signals.InterfLvl: Full name: 'Interference Level'. Explanation: Degree of interference around the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, None.
Signals.ModIndex: Full name: 'Modulation Index'. Explanation: Numerical index describing modulation depth. Data type: DECIMAL(6,4). Example: '0.2875'.
Signals.ModType: Full name: 'Modulation Type'. Explanation: The method of signal modulation. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: AM, FM, PM, QAM, Unknown.
Signals.NoiseFloorDbm: Full name: 'Noise Floor (dBm)'. Explanation: Measured noise floor in dBm. Data type: DOUBLE PRECISION. Example: '-85.3'.
Signals.PhaseShiftDeg: Full name: 'Phase Shift (°)'. Explanation: Phase shift in degrees for the signal. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '45.00'.
Signals.PolarAngleDeg: Full name: 'Polarization Angle (°)'. Explanation: Angle of polarization in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(5,1). Example: '90.0'.
Signals.PolarMode: Full name: 'Polarization Mode'. Explanation: Type of signal polarization. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Circular, Elliptical, Linear, Unknown.
Signals.PulsePerSec: Full name: 'Pulse Rate (pulses/sec)'. Explanation: Rate of pulse repetition in the signal. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '4.500'.
Signals.PulseWidMs: Full name: 'Pulse Width (ms)'. Explanation: Duration of each pulse in milliseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '2.300'.
Signals.RfiStat: Full name: 'RFI Status'. Explanation: Radio Frequency Interference status. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Clean, Contaminated, Unknown.
Signals.SigDurSec: Full name: 'Signal Duration (s)'. Explanation: Total duration of the signal in seconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '12.50'.
Signals.SigStrDb: Full name: 'Signal Strength (dB)'. Explanation: Measured strength of the signal in decibels. Data type: NUMERIC(7,2). Example: '12.35'.
Signals.SignalClass: Full name: 'Signal Type'. Explanation: Broad classification of the detected signal. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Broadband, Continuous, Modulated, Narrowband, Pulsed.
Signals.SignalRegistry: Full name: 'Signal Registry'. Explanation: Unique ID for each signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-123E4567-E89B'.
Signals.SnrRatio: Full name: 'Signal-to-Noise Ratio'. Explanation: SNR measured for the signal. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '18.75'.
Signals.TelescRef: Full name: 'Telescope Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key to the telescope used for detection. Data type: CHAR(20). Example: 'TELESC_0001'.
Signals.TimeMark: Full name: 'Timestamp'. Explanation: The moment of signal detection. In some CSVs, it may be stored as an Excel serial date/time (e.g., '44302.55648' ≈ 2021-05-16 13:20:20 UTC). Data type: TIMESTAMPTZ. Example: '2025-08-01 13:45:00+00'.
SourceProperties.CelestObj: Full name: 'Celestial Object'. Explanation: Broad classification of the object. Data type: VARCHAR(75). Possible categories: Galaxy, Planet, Star, Unknown.
SourceProperties.GalLat: Full name: 'Galactic Latitude (°)'. Explanation: Galactic latitude of the source. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '-5.67'.
SourceProperties.GalLong: Full name: 'Galactic Longitude (°)'. Explanation: Galactic longitude of the source. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '12.34'.
SourceProperties.ObjAgeGyr: Full name: 'Object Age (Gyr)'. Explanation: Estimated age in billions of years. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '4.500'.
SourceProperties.ObjMag: Full name: 'Apparent Magnitude'. Explanation: Brightness of the object as seen from Earth. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '7.35'.
SourceProperties.ObjMassSol: Full name: 'Object Mass (solar)'. Explanation: Mass relative to the Sun. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '1.005'.
SourceProperties.ObjMetal: Full name: 'Metallicity'. Explanation: Ratio of elements heavier than helium in the object. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.012'.
SourceProperties.ObjPropMotion: Full name: 'Proper Motion (mas/yr)'. Explanation: Apparent motion across the sky in milliarcseconds/year. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '55.12'.
SourceProperties.ObjRadVel: Full name: 'Radial Velocity (km/s)'. Explanation: Speed at which the object is moving toward/away from us. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '-23.45'.
SourceProperties.ObjTempK: Full name: 'Object Temperature (K)'. Explanation: Approximate surface temperature in Kelvin. Data type: INTEGER. Example: '5800'.
SourceProperties.ObjType: Full name: 'Object Subtype'. Explanation: More specific object type. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Dwarf, Giant, Main Sequence, Unknown.
SourceProperties.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-STU-5432'.
SourceProperties.SourceDecDeg: Full name: 'Declination (°)'. Explanation: Declination of the source in degrees (-90 to +90). Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '-20.4567'.
SourceProperties.SourceDistLy: Full name: 'Distance (ly)'. Explanation: Approximate distance to the source in light-years. Data type: NUMERIC(10,2). Example: '26000.45'.
SourceProperties.SourceRaDeg: Full name: 'Right Ascension (°)'. Explanation: RA of the source in degrees (0 to 360). Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '123.4567'.
Telescopes.BandUsagePct: Full name: 'Bandwidth Usage (%)'. Explanation: Network bandwidth usage as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '73.25'.
Telescopes.CalibrStatus: Full name: 'Calibration Status'. Explanation: Status of telescope’s calibration. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Current, Due, Overdue.
Telescopes.CoolSysStatus: Full name: 'Cooling System Status'. Explanation: Status of the telescope’s cooling system. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Critical, Normal, Warning.
Telescopes.DataStorStatus: Full name: 'Data Storage Status'. Explanation: Capacity and status of local data storage. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Available, Critical, Low.
Telescopes.DetectTempK: Full name: 'Detector Temperature (K)'. Explanation: Temperature of the telescope’s primary detector in Kelvin. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '123.45'.
Telescopes.EquipStatus: Full name: 'Equipment Status'. Explanation: Operational state of the telescope. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Degraded, Maintenance, Operational.
Telescopes.FocusQuality: Full name: 'Focus Quality'. Explanation: Quality of the telescope’s focusing system. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
Telescopes.NetStatus: Full name: 'Network Status'. Explanation: Status of the network connection for telescope data transfer. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Connected, Disconnected, Limited.
Telescopes.ObservStation: Full name: 'Observatory Name Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key linking to the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
Telescopes.PointAccArc: Full name: 'Pointing Accuracy (arcsec)'. Explanation: How precise the telescope can point, in arcseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '0.45'.
Telescopes.PowerStatus: Full name: 'Power Supply Status'. Explanation: Indicates which power source or level is in use. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Backup, Critical, Main.
Telescopes.ProcQueueStatus: Full name: 'Processing Queue Status'. Explanation: Indicates how full the processing queue is. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Empty, Full, Normal.
Telescopes.TelescRegistry: Full name: 'Telescope Registry'. Explanation: A unique identifier for the telescope. Data type: CHAR(20). Example: 'TELESC_0001'.
Telescopes.TrackAccArc: Full name: 'Tracking Accuracy (arcsec)'. Explanation: How accurately the telescope can track a target, in arcseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '1.20'.

requests.specific_A: Count each race's constructor result entries (`constructorResults` records, linked to the race and its circuit) and total their points, ignoring missing points. Group by race id and circuit country. Among the races whose entry count is above the average entry count across all races, list exactly 10 rows, cutting arbitrarily if races tie at 10th place. Show the race id, the circuit `country`, the total points, the entry count, and how far the entry count is above the average (unrounded). Sort from the largest difference to the smallest.
requests.specific_B: Count each race's constructor result entries (`constructorResults` records, linked to the race and its circuit) and total their points, ignoring missing points. Group by race id and circuit country. Among the races whose entry count is above the average entry count across all races, list every race whose entry count is at least the 10th-highest entry count, so races tied at the cutoff are all included. Show the race id, the circuit `country`, the total points, the entry count, and how far the entry count is above the average (unrounded). Sort from the largest difference to the smallest.
requests.open: Which are the top 10 races by how far their number of constructor result entries exceeds the average number of entries per race? Look only at races above that average. For each one, give the race id, the circuit's country, the total constructor points scored in that race (ignoring missing points), the number of entries, and the difference from the average. List them from the biggest difference down.

readings.A: Take the above-average races ranked by how far their entry count exceeds the average, and return exactly the first 10 rows. When races tie at 10th place, the cut falls inside the tied group.
readings.B: Take the above-average races ranked by how far their entry count exceeds the average, and return every race whose entry count reaches the 10th-highest entry count. All races tied at the cutoff are included.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "constructorResults"."raceId" AS "e", "circuits"."country" AS "g", SUM("constructorResults"."points") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "constructorResults" AS "constructorResults" INNER JOIN "races" AS "races" ON "races"."raceId" = "constructorResults"."raceId" INNER JOIN "circuits" AS "circuits" ON "circuits"."circuitId" = "races"."circuitId" GROUP BY "constructorResults"."raceId", "circuits"."country"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v" ORDER BY ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "constructorResults"."raceId" AS "e", "circuits"."country" AS "g", SUM("constructorResults"."points") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "constructorResults" AS "constructorResults" INNER JOIN "races" AS "races" ON "races"."raceId" = "constructorResults"."raceId" INNER JOIN "circuits" AS "circuits" ON "circuits"."circuitId" = "races"."circuitId" GROUP BY "constructorResults"."raceId", "circuits"."country"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v" AND "s1"."m2" >= (SELECT MIN("t"."m2") FROM (SELECT "s1x"."m2" AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1x" ORDER BY "s1x"."m2" DESC LIMIT 10) AS "t") ORDER BY ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") DESC

shared_requirements.requirement: Use the constructor result records (`constructorResults`). Each record is one constructor's entry in one race.

Link each record to its race (`races.raceId` = `constructorResults.raceId`), then link the race to its circuit (`circuits.circuitId` = `races.circuitId`). Both are inner joins, so records without a match are dropped. Group the records by race id and circuit country.
Keep only the races whose entry count (records in the group) is greater than the average entry count, taken over all race/country groups.
race id (`constructorResults.raceId`)
circuit country (`circuits.country`)
total constructor points in the race: the sum of `constructorResults.points`, ignoring missing values
the number of constructor result records for the race (entry count)
the entry count minus the average entry count, with no rounding
Order by the difference from the average, largest first.
Show the top 10 races by this difference.

A.requirement: Return exactly 10 rows, even if races are tied on entry count at 10th place.

B.requirement: Do not cut at a fixed row count. Return every above-average race whose entry count is at least the 10th-highest entry count, so all races tied at the cutoff are included.

context.schema:
CREATE TABLE "circuits" (
"circuitId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "circuitRef" TEXT,
  "name" TEXT,
  "location" TEXT,
  "country" TEXT,
  "lat" REAL,
  "lng" REAL,
  "alt" TEXT,
  "url" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "races" (
"raceId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "year" INTEGER,
  "round" INTEGER,
  "circuitId" INTEGER,
  "name" TEXT,
  "date" TEXT,
  "time" TEXT,
  "url" TEXT,
  FOREIGN KEY ("circuitId") REFERENCES "circuits"("circuitId")
);
CREATE TABLE "drivers" (
"driverId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "driverRef" TEXT,
  "number" TEXT,
  "code" TEXT,
  "forename" TEXT,
  "surname" TEXT,
  "dob" TEXT,
  "nationality" TEXT,
  "url" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "status" (
"statusId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "status" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "seasons" (
"year" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "url" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "constructors" (
	"constructorId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "constructorRef" TEXT,
  "name" TEXT,
  "nationality" TEXT,
  "url" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "constructorStandings" (
	"constructorStandingsId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "raceId" INTEGER,
  "constructorId" INTEGER,
  "points" REAL,
  "position" INTEGER,
  "positionText" TEXT,
  "wins" INTEGER,
  FOREIGN KEY("constructorId") REFERENCES "constructors"("constructorId"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId")
);
CREATE TABLE "results" (
"resultId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "raceId" INTEGER,
  "driverId" INTEGER,
  "constructorId" INTEGER,
  "number" INTEGER,
  "grid" INTEGER,
  "position" TEXT,
  "positionText" TEXT,
  "positionOrder" INTEGER,
  "points" REAL,
  "laps" TEXT,
  "time" TEXT,
  "milliseconds" TEXT,
  "fastestLap" TEXT,
  "rank" TEXT,
  "fastestLapTime" TEXT,
  "fastestLapSpeed" TEXT,
  "statusId" INTEGER,
  FOREIGN KEY("constructorId") REFERENCES "constructors"("constructorId"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("driverId") REFERENCES "drivers"("driverId")
);
CREATE TABLE "driverStandings" (
"driverStandingsId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "raceId" INTEGER,
  "driverId" INTEGER,
  "points" REAL,
  "position" INTEGER,
  "positionText" TEXT,
  "wins" INTEGER,
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("driverId") REFERENCES "drivers"("driverId")
);
CREATE TABLE "constructorResults" (
"constructorResultsId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "raceId" INTEGER,
  "constructorId" INTEGER,
  "points" REAL,
  "status" TEXT,
  FOREIGN KEY("constructorId") REFERENCES "constructors"("constructorId"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId")
);
CREATE TABLE "qualifying" (
"qualifyId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "raceId" INTEGER,
  "driverId" INTEGER,
  "constructorId" INTEGER,
  "number" INTEGER,
  "position" INTEGER,
  "q1" TEXT,
  "q2" TEXT,
  "q3" TEXT,
  FOREIGN KEY("constructorId") REFERENCES "constructors"("constructorId"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("driverId") REFERENCES "drivers"("driverId")
);
CREATE TABLE "pitStops" (
"raceId" INTEGER,
  "driverId" INTEGER,
  "stop" INTEGER,
  "lap" INTEGER,
  "time" TEXT,
  "duration" TEXT,
  "milliseconds" INTEGER,
  PRIMARY KEY ("raceId", "driverId", "stop"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("driverId") REFERENCES "drivers"("driverId")
);
CREATE TABLE "lapTimes" (
"raceId" INTEGER,
  "driverId" INTEGER,
  "lap" INTEGER,
  "position" INTEGER,
  "time" TEXT,
  "milliseconds" INTEGER,
  PRIMARY KEY("raceId", "driverId", "lap"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("driverId") REFERENCES "drivers"("driverId")
);

requests.specific_A: Group the budget lines by `category`. For each category, find the average relative overspend, (`spent` − `amount`) ÷ `amount` (ignoring missing values), and the number of budget lines. Lines with a `spent` of 0 count as real values in the relative overspend, giving −1. Keep the categories whose line count is above the average line count per category. Then give one summary row: the average of those categories' average relative overspend, the average of their line counts, and the average amount by which their line counts exceed the per-category average line count.
requests.specific_B: Group the budget lines by `category`. For each category, find the average relative overspend, (`spent` − `amount`) ÷ `amount` (ignoring missing values), and the number of budget lines. Lines with a `spent` of 0 are treated as not yet spent and left out of the relative overspend, though they still count as lines. Keep the categories whose line count is above the average line count per category. Then give one summary row: the average of those categories' average relative overspend, the average of their line counts, and the average amount by which their line counts exceed the per-category average line count.
requests.open: For the budget categories (`budget.category`) that have more budget lines than the average category, give me one summary row with three values: their average relative overspend ((`spent` − `amount`) / `amount` per line, averaged within each category and then across categories, ignoring missing values), their average number of budget lines, and on average how many more lines they have than the per-category average.

readings.A: A spent value of 0 is a real zero, so those lines get a relative overspend of −1 and are included in the averages.
readings.B: A spent value of 0 means nothing has been spent yet, so those lines are left out of the relative overspend averages but still counted as lines.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "budget"."category" AS "g", AVG((CAST(("budget"."spent" - "budget"."amount") AS REAL) / "budget"."amount")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "budget" AS "budget" GROUP BY "budget"."category"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "budget"."category" AS "g", AVG((CAST((NULLIF("budget"."spent", 0) - "budget"."amount") AS REAL) / "budget"."amount")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "budget" AS "budget" GROUP BY "budget"."category"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"

requests.specific_A: For each customer in the orders table, show the customer id, how many orders they placed, and their share of all orders (their count divided by the total number of orders). Sort by share from highest to lowest, with missing values last, and return exactly 10 rows. If several customers are tied at the 10th place, pick any of them to fill the remaining spots. Don't round anything.
requests.specific_B: For each customer in the orders table, show the customer id, how many orders they placed, and their share of all orders (their count divided by the total number of orders). Sort by share from highest to lowest, with missing values last, and return the top 10, including every customer tied with the 10th place share even if that gives more than 10 rows. Don't round anything.
requests.open: Which are the top 10 customers by share of all orders? For each, show the customer id, how many orders they placed, and their share (their order count divided by the total number of orders), sorted from highest to lowest share with missing values last. Don't round anything.

readings.A: Cut the list at exactly 10 rows. Which of the tied customers make the cut is arbitrary.
readings.B: Keep everyone whose share reaches the 10th-highest value, so customers tied at the boundary all appear.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Orders"."customer_id" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "Orders" AS "Orders" GROUP BY "Orders"."customer_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Orders"."customer_id" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "Orders" AS "Orders" GROUP BY "Orders"."customer_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") >= (SELECT MIN("t"."x") FROM (SELECT (CAST("q1"."m1" AS REAL) / "q2"."v") AS "x" FROM "s1" AS "q1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "q2" ON NOT ("q2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY "x" DESC LIMIT 10) AS "t") ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC

Keep the teams whose average wins is above the mean of all teams' average wins. Return the team id, the average wins, the average (games − losses) ÷ losses, and how far the average wins is above that mean. Sort by that gap from highest to lowest (missing last), keep the top 10, and don't round.
requests.specific_B: In `manager_half`, for each team (`team_id`), compute its average wins per season (total wins divided by the number of distinct seasons) and its average of (games managed − losses) ÷ losses, ignoring missing values. Keep the teams whose average wins is above the mean of all teams' average wins. Return the team id, the average wins, the average (games − losses) ÷ losses, and how far the average wins is above that mean. Sort by that gap from highest to lowest (missing last), keep the top 10, and don't round.

readings.A: A team's average wins is the average of the wins in its individual manager-half rows.
readings.B: A team's average wins is its wins per season: total wins divided by the number of seasons it appears in.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "manager_half"."team_id" AS "e", AVG("manager_half"."w") AS "m1", AVG((CAST(("manager_half"."g" - "manager_half"."l") AS REAL) / "manager_half"."l")) AS "m2" FROM "manager_half" AS "manager_half" GROUP BY "manager_half"."team_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v" ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "manager_half"."team_id" AS "e", CAST(SUM("manager_half"."w") AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT "manager_half"."year") AS "m1", AVG((CAST(("manager_half"."g" - "manager_half"."l") AS REAL) / "manager_half"."l")) AS "m2" FROM "manager_half" AS "manager_half" GROUP BY "manager_half"."team_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v" ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

requests.specific_A: Link each attendance record to the attending member and to the city of the member's zip code (`member.zip` = `zip_code.zip_code`). For each city, count the attendance records, so each member counts once for every event attended. Then work out each city's share as its count divided by the sum of all cities' counts. Look only at the cities whose share is above the average share across all cities, and give in one row the average count, the average share, and the average amount by which the share is above that overall average.
requests.specific_B: Link each attendance record to the attending member and to the city of the member's zip code (`member.zip` = `zip_code.zip_code`). For each city, count the distinct members who attended at least one event, so each member counts once no matter how many events they attended. Then work out each city's share as its count divided by the sum of all cities' counts. Look only at the cities whose share is above the average share across all cities, and give in one row the average count, the average share, and the average amount by which the share is above that overall average.
requests.open: Using event attendance and the city of each attending member's zip code (`member.zip` = `zip_code.zip_code`), find the number of event attendees from each city and each city's share of the total across all cities. For the cities whose share is above the average city share, give in one row the average number of attendees, the average share, and the average amount by which the share is above that average.

readings.A: The per-city count is the number of attendance records (one per member per event).
readings.B: The per-city count is the number of distinct members who attended at least one event.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "zip_code"."city" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "attendance" AS "attendance" INNER JOIN "member" AS "member" ON "member"."member_id" = "attendance"."link_to_member" INNER JOIN "zip_code" AS "zip_code" ON "zip_code"."zip_code" = "member"."zip" GROUP BY "zip_code"."city"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "zip_code"."city" AS "g", COUNT(DISTINCT "member"."member_id") AS "m1" FROM "attendance" AS "attendance" INNER JOIN "member" AS "member" ON "member"."member_id" = "attendance"."link_to_member" INNER JOIN "zip_code" AS "zip_code" ON "zip_code"."zip_code" = "member"."zip" GROUP BY "zip_code"."city"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

Find the overall mean of these per-patient values and each one's deviation from that overall mean. Then, within each sex (exact text match, so a blank sex is its own group and a missing sex matches nothing), average those deviations. Keep only the per-patient values whose deviation is above their sex's average deviation, and show the top 10 by how far above it they are, largest first (missing last): patient `ID`, `SEX`, the `aCL IgM` value, its deviation from the overall mean, and how far that deviation exceeds the sex's average deviation. All averages ignore missing values; don't round.
requests.specific_B: Linking each examination to its patient by `ID` (dropping examinations with no matching patient), work per examination: take each examination's own `aCL IgM` value along with its patient's `ID` and `SEX`. Find the overall mean of these per-examination values and each one's deviation from that overall mean. Then, within each sex (exact text match, so a blank sex is its own group and a missing sex matches nothing), average those deviations. Keep only the per-examination values whose deviation is above their sex's average deviation, and show the top 10 by how far above it they are, largest first (missing last): patient `ID`, `SEX`, the `aCL IgM` value, its deviation from the overall mean, and how far that deviation exceeds the sex's average deviation. All averages ignore missing values; don't round.
requests.open: Linking examinations to patients by `ID` (dropping examinations with no matching patient), how far is patients' `aCL IgM` above or below the overall mean? Within each sex (exact text match, so a blank sex is its own group and a missing sex matches nothing), what is the average of those deviations? Show the top 10 entries whose deviation is above their sex's average deviation, ranked by how far above it they are, largest first (missing last): patient `ID`, `SEX`, `aCL IgM`, its deviation from the overall mean, and how far that deviation exceeds the sex's average deviation. All averages ignore missing values; don't round.

requests.specific_A: Using spatial records (`scanspatial`) matched to a project (`projects.arcregistry` = `scanspatial.arcref`), for each funding source (`projects.fundflux`, treating a missing source as its own group) compute the average ratio of bounding box Y (`boxy`) to bounding box Z (`boxz`), ignoring missing values, and the number of spatial records. Keep the funding sources whose number of spatial records is above the average of that number across all funding sources. Return one row with: the average of the kept sources' ratios; the total of their spatial record counts; and the average amount by which their counts exceed the cross-source average. No rounding.
requests.specific_B: Using spatial records (`scanspatial`) matched to a project (`projects.arcregistry` = `scanspatial.arcref`), for each funding source (`projects.fundflux`, treating a missing source as its own group) compute the average ratio of bounding box Y (`boxy`) to bounding box Z (`boxz`), ignoring missing values, and the number of distinct projects. Keep the funding sources whose number of distinct projects is above the average of that number across all funding sources. Return one row with: the average of the kept sources' ratios; the total of their distinct project counts; and the average amount by which their counts exceed the cross-source average. No rounding.
requests.open: Looking at spatial scan data (`scanspatial`) linked to projects (`projects.arcregistry` = `scanspatial.arcref`), which funding sources (`projects.fundflux`, treating a missing source as its own group) are bigger than average? For each funding source, work out the average ratio of bounding box Y (`boxy`) to bounding box Z (`boxz`), ignoring missing values, and how big it is. For the sources above the average size across funding sources, give one row with the average of their ratios, their combined size, and how far on average they exceed the average size. No rounding.

readings.A: The size of each funding source is measured by how many spatial records it has.
readings.B: The size of each funding source is measured by how many distinct projects it has spatial data for.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "projects"."fundflux" AS "g", AVG((CAST("scanspatial"."boxy" AS REAL) / "scanspatial"."boxz")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "scanspatial" AS "scanspatial" INNER JOIN "projects" AS "projects" ON "projects"."arcregistry" = "scanspatial"."arcref" GROUP BY "projects"."fundflux"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", SUM("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "projects"."fundflux" AS "g", AVG((CAST("scanspatial"."boxy" AS REAL) / "scanspatial"."boxz")) AS "m1", COUNT(DISTINCT "scanspatial"."arcref") AS "m2" FROM "scanspatial" AS "scanspatial" INNER JOIN "projects" AS "projects" ON "projects"."arcregistry" = "scanspatial"."arcref" GROUP BY "projects"."fundflux"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", SUM("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"

shared_requirements.requirement: Use `scanspatial` records joined to `projects` where `projects.arcregistry` = `scanspatial.arcref` (inner join; unmatched records are dropped).
Group by funding source (`projects.fundflux`). A missing funding source forms its own group.
Per funding source, compute the average of `boxy` ÷ `boxz` (ignoring missing values) and a size count.
Keep the funding sources whose count is strictly above the plain mean of that count across all funding sources.
All kept funding sources form one group that gives one row. There is no rounding.
The average of the kept sources' ratios.
The sum of the kept sources' counts.
The average of (count − cross-source mean count) over the kept sources.

A.requirement: The per-source count is the number of spatial records (`scanspatial` rows).

B.requirement: The per-source count is the number of distinct projects (`scanspatial.arcref`).

Equipment.EquipDesign: Full name: 'Equipment Model'. Explanation: Model name or identifier. Data type: VARCHAR(14). Example: 'Model-669'.

choice_kind: sentinel value / missing group kept or dropped

requests.specific_A: For every player in `appearances` who matches a `player` record, including those whose death country (`player.death_country`) is blank, total `g_1b` − `g_cf` across their appearance rows, skipping rows where either value is missing. Keep each player's total together with their death country. Keep the players whose total is above the average total. Give a single row with two values: the sum of their totals, and the average amount by which their totals exceed that average. Don't round anything.
requests.specific_B: For every player in `appearances` who matches a `player` record, but only those with a recorded, non-blank death country (`player.death_country`), total `g_1b` − `g_cf` across their appearance rows, skipping rows where either value is missing. Keep each player's total together with their death country. Keep the players whose total is above the average total. Give a single row with two values: the sum of their totals, and the average amount by which their totals exceed that average. Don't round anything.
requests.open: For each player in `appearances` matched to `player`, together with the country they died in (`player.death_country`), total games at first base minus games in center field (`g_1b` − `g_cf`) across their appearance rows, skipping rows where either value is missing. Keep the players whose total is above the average total. Give a single row with two values: the sum of their totals, and the average amount by which they exceed that average. Don't round anything.

readings.A: All matched players count, including those with a blank death country (for example, living players).
readings.B: Players with a blank death country are treated as having no death country and are excluded.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "appearances"."player_id" AS "e", "player"."death_country" AS "g", SUM(("appearances"."g_1b" - "appearances"."g_cf")) AS "m1" FROM "appearances" AS "appearances" INNER JOIN "player" AS "player" ON "player"."player_id" = "appearances"."player_id" GROUP BY "appearances"."player_id", "player"."death_country"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT SUM("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "appearances"."player_id" AS "e", "player"."death_country" AS "g", SUM(("appearances"."g_1b" - "appearances"."g_cf")) AS "m1" FROM "appearances" AS "appearances" INNER JOIN "player" AS "player" ON "player"."player_id" = "appearances"."player_id" WHERE "player"."death_country" <> '' GROUP BY "appearances"."player_id", "player"."death_country"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT SUM("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s3" AS "s3"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from `appearances` joined to `player` on equal `player_id` (exact text match); unmatched rows are dropped
One total per player (`appearances.player_id` with `player.death_country`): the sum over their appearance rows of `g_1b` − `g_cf`, ignoring rows where the difference is missing
Average the player totals; keep the players whose total is strictly greater than that average
Collapse the kept players into a single row; no ordering or limit
Sum of the kept players' totals
Average of (total − average total) over the kept players; no rounding

A.requirement: Players whose death country is blank (empty string) are kept as a normal group

B.requirement: Only players with a recorded, non-blank death country are kept; those with a blank or missing death country are dropped

requests.specific_A: Group the sentiment and fundamentals snapshots by announcement timing (`eventannotm`), treating a missing timing as its own group, and compute each group's average institutional ownership (`instownpct`), ignoring missing values. Take as the baseline the simple average of these group averages, each timing group counting equally. For the groups whose average is strictly above that baseline, give in one row the mean of their averages and the mean amount by which they exceed the baseline, without rounding.
requests.specific_B: Group the sentiment and fundamentals snapshots by announcement timing (`eventannotm`), treating a missing timing as its own group, and compute each group's average institutional ownership (`instownpct`), ignoring missing values. Take as the baseline the average institutional ownership across all individual snapshots, ignoring missing values, so larger groups weigh more. For the groups whose average is strictly above that baseline, give in one row the mean of their averages and the mean amount by which they exceed the baseline, without rounding.
requests.open: Looking at announcement timing (`eventannotm`, with a missing timing as its own group), which timings have an average institutional ownership strictly above average? Ignoring missing ownership values, give in one row the mean of those timings' average ownership and how far above average they are on average, without rounding.

readings.A: Compare each timing group's average institutional ownership with the simple mean of the group averages. For the groups above it, report the mean of their averages and their mean excess.
readings.B: Compare each timing group's average institutional ownership with the overall per-snapshot average. For the groups above it, report the mean of their averages and their mean excess.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "sentimentandfundamentals"."eventannotm" AS "g", AVG("sentimentandfundamentals"."instownpct") AS "m1" FROM "sentimentandfundamentals" AS "sentimentandfundamentals" GROUP BY "sentimentandfundamentals"."eventannotm"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "sentimentandfundamentals"."eventannotm" AS "g", AVG("sentimentandfundamentals"."instownpct") AS "m1" FROM "sentimentandfundamentals" AS "sentimentandfundamentals" GROUP BY "sentimentandfundamentals"."eventannotm"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("sf"."instownpct") AS "v" FROM "sentimentandfundamentals" AS "sf"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s3" AS "s3"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from all `sentimentandfundamentals` records and group them by announcement timing (`eventannotm`). A missing timing forms its own group.
Each group's value = its average institutional ownership (`instownpct`), ignoring missing values
Keep the groups whose average is strictly greater than the baseline and return a single row
Average of the kept groups' averages
Average of (group average − baseline) over the kept groups. No rounding.

A.requirement: Baseline = the unweighted mean of the per-timing-group averages, so each group counts equally

B.requirement: Baseline = the average `instownpct` over all individual snapshots (missing values ignored), so larger groups weigh more

requests.specific_A: For each store (`customer.store_id`), how many customers does it have, counting every customer record whether active or inactive? Show the store id, that count, the store's share of the combined count across all stores (count divided by the total, as an unrounded fraction), and its count relative to the average count per store (count divided by that average, unrounded).
requests.specific_B: For each store (`customer.store_id`), how many customers does it have, counting only active customers (`active` = 1)? Show the store id, that count, the store's share of the combined count across all stores (count divided by the total, as an unrounded fraction), and its count relative to the average count per store (count divided by that average, unrounded).
requests.open: How many customers does each store have? For each store, show its store id, its customer count, its share of all customers across the stores (as an unrounded fraction), and its count as a multiple of the average store's count (count divided by the average, unrounded).

readings.A: Each store's count includes all of its customer records, whether active or inactive.
readings.B: Each store's count includes only customers flagged as active.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "customer"."store_id" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "customer" AS "customer" GROUP BY "customer"."store_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "customer"."store_id" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "customer" AS "customer" WHERE "customer"."active" = 1 GROUP BY "customer"."store_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s3"."m1" AS REAL) / "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL)

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from customer records and group them by store (`customer.store_id`), one row per store

Compare each store's count with store-level totals: the sum of the counts across all stores (used for the share) and the plain average of the per-store counts (used for the ratio). Both are single values attached to every store row.
Return the store identifier (`store_id`)
Return the store's customer count
Return the store's share: its count divided by the sum of all stores' counts, not rounded
Return the store's count divided by the average per-store count, as a ratio and not rounded
Use exactly these four columns in this order: store id, count, share, ratio to average. No rounding and no ordering is required.

A.requirement: Count every customer record, both active and inactive

B.requirement: Count only active customers (`active` = 1)

 FOREIGN KEY (actor_id) REFERENCES actor (actor_id),
