film.rating: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns exactly 5 rating levels, each covering roughly 180-225 films, so every group is well populated and rating works as a grouping class. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate), AVG(length), AVG(replacement_cost) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '3.0348430493273613', '120.4439461883408', '20.402556053811544'], ['NC-17', '210', '2.970952380952388', '113.22857142857143', '20.137619047618937'], ['R', '195', '2.9387179487179553', '118.66153846153846', '20.23102564102554'], ['PG', '194', '3.051855670103099', '112.00515463917526', '18.959072164948356'], ['G', '178', '2.888876404494388', '111.0505617977528', '20.12483146067407']] scale (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows exactly 5 levels: G, PG, PG-13, R and NC-17. These are the standard MPAA bands, which are ordered by audience restriction, so the column is an ordinal class. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY rating -> [['G', '178'], ['NC-17', '210'], ['PG', '194'], ['PG-13', '223'], ['R', '195']]
category.name: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 16 genres, each shared by many films (about 50-75 each), so the column is a grouping label and does not identify single records. Evidence: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film_category fc JOIN category c ON c.category_id = fc.category_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY films DESC -> [['Sports', '74'], ['Foreign', '73'], ['Family', '69'], ['Documentary', '68'], ['Animation', '66'], ['Action', '64']]
customer.store_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 2 stores with about 300 customers each, so the column is a grouping label shared by many rows. Evidence: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS customers, SUM(active) AS active_customers FROM customer GROUP BY store_id -> [['1', '326', '318'], ['2', '273', '266']]
inventory.store_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 2 store values over 4581 copies, about 2270 per store, so the column is a grouping label. Evidence: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS copies, COUNT(DISTINCT film_id) AS titles FROM inventory GROUP BY store_id -> [['1', '2270', '759'], ['2', '2311', '762']]
country.country: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Many customers share a country (the top countries have dozens of customers each), so country works as a grouping attribute for customers. Evidence: SELECT co.country, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customer cu JOIN address a ON a.address_id = cu.address_id JOIN city ci ON ci.city_id = a.city_id JOIN country co ON co.country_id = ci.country_id GROUP BY co.country ORDER BY customers DESC LIMIT 10 -> [['India', '60'], ['China', '53'], ['United States', '36'], ['Japan', '31'], ['Mexico', '30'], ['Russian Federation', '28']]
film.special_features: desc (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 15 distinct values, all of them combinations of the same 4 feature names (for example 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes'). The column is a set, not a single category. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']] semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows 15 distinct values, all combinations of the same 4 feature names, such as 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes' and 'Trailers,Commentaries'. The column is a set, not a single class, so it should not be offered as a grouping. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']]
film.length: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified rating query already returns AVG(length) between 111.05 (G) and 120.44 (PG-13). The catalogue profile gives 140 distinct values from 46 to 185 minutes. So length is a continuous ratio-scale quantity whose group averages can be read directly. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(length) AS avg_minutes, MIN(length), MAX(length) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '120.4439461883408', '46', '185'], ['NC-17', '210', '113.22857142857143', '46', '184'], ['R', '195', '118.66153846153846', '49', '185'], ['PG', '194', '112.00515463917526', '46', '185'], ['G', '178', '111.0505617977528', '47', '185']]
film.rental_duration: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows 5 values from 3 to 7 days, all well above zero, so the column is a ratio-scale number of days per film. The query shows how many films fall at each value. Evidence: SELECT rental_duration, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate) AS avg_rate FROM film GROUP BY rental_duration ORDER BY rental_duration -> [['3', '203', '2.8323645320197115'], ['4', '203', '2.97029556650247'], ['5', '191', '3.19942408376964'], ['6', '212', '2.895660377358497'], ['7', '191', '3.021413612565451']]
film.rental_rate: desc (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows rental_rate takes only 0.99, 2.99 and 4.99, while replacement_cost runs from 9.99 to 29.99. The query shows how large and uniform the gap is. The auditor noted that the difference is always about −17 and the relative gap about −0.85, which fits two different quantities rather than one price seen two ways. Evidence: SELECT MIN(replacement_cost - rental_rate), MAX(replacement_cost - rental_rate), AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) FROM film -> [['5.0', '29.0', '0.16651517608314595']]
film.replacement_cost: quantity (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The column holds a per-copy value that becomes meaningful when summed over physical copies in inventory, for example as stock value. That is the reading of an asset value, not of a price charged per rental. Evidence: SELECT f.rating, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copies, SUM(f.replacement_cost) AS stock_value FROM inventory i JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating -> [['G', '791', '16185.089999999853'], ['NC-17', '944', '19128.56000000009'], ['PG', '924', '17755.759999999962'], ['PG-13', '1018', '21052.82000000024'], ['R', '904', '18498.960000000006']]
payment.staff_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows only 2 distinct values (1 and 2) across 16,049 payments. Each value is therefore shared by thousands of rows, which makes it a grouping label rather than a record identifier. Evidence: SELECT staff_id, COUNT(*) AS payments, SUM(amount) AS revenue, AVG(amount) FROM payment GROUP BY staff_id -> [['1', '8057', '33489.470000005174', '4.156568201564499'], ['2', '7992', '33927.04000000482', '4.245125125125728']]
rental.staff_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows only 2 distinct values across 16,044 rentals, so each staff value covers thousands of rentals and works as a grouping class. Evidence: SELECT staff_id, COUNT(*) AS rentals, SUM(CASE WHEN return_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unreturned FROM rental GROUP BY staff_id -> [['1', '8040', '85'], ['2', '8004', '98']]

requests.specific_A: For each observatory station (`observstation`), compute the average bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`) of its telescopes, ignoring missing values. Compute the overall average as the mean of these station averages, so each station counts once. Keep only the stations whose average is above this overall average. Show the station, its average bandwidth usage, and how far it is above the overall average (station average minus overall average). Sort by that difference from largest to smallest and return the top 10, without rounding.
requests.specific_B: For each observatory station (`observstation`), compute the average bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`) of its telescopes, ignoring missing values. Compute the overall average across all individual telescopes, so stations with more telescopes weigh more. Keep only the stations whose average is above this overall average. Show the station, its average bandwidth usage, and how far it is above the overall average (station average minus overall average). Sort by that difference from largest to smallest and return the top 10, without rounding.
requests.open: Which observatory stations (`observstation`) have an average telescope bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`) above the overall average bandwidth usage? Ignore missing values. For each one, show the station, its average bandwidth usage, and how much it exceeds the overall average. Return the top 10 by that margin, largest first, without rounding.

readings.A: Each station's average bandwidth usage is compared against the mean of the station averages, with every station weighted equally.
readings.B: Each station's average bandwidth usage is compared against the mean bandwidth usage over all individual telescopes.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", AVG("telescopes"."bandusagepct") AS "m1" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v" ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", AVG("telescopes"."bandusagepct") AS "m1" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("telescopes"."bandusagepct") AS "v" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v" ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every telescopes record and group by observatory station (`observstation`). For each station, compute the average bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`), ignoring missing values.
Pair each station with a single overall average bandwidth usage value; the definition of that value is the choice.
Keep only stations whose average is strictly greater than the overall average.
First column: the station (`observstation`).
Second column: the station's average bandwidth usage.
Third column: the station's average minus the overall average. No rounding.
Sort by that difference, largest first, with missing values last.
Keep only the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: The overall average is the mean of the per-station averages, so each station counts once.

B.requirement: The overall average is the mean of `bandusagepct` across all telescope records, so stations with more telescopes weigh more.

  "objmasssol" real(6,3),
  "objagegyr" real(6,3),
  "objmetal" real(5,3),
  "objpropmotion" real(7,2),
  "objradvel" real(7,2),
  CONSTRAINT "sourceproperties_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalref"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_source_signal" FOREIGN KEY ("signalref") REFERENCES "signals" ("signalregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "telescopes" (
  "telescregistry" text(20) NOT NULL,
  "observstation" text(60) NOT NULL,
  "equipstatus" text(35),
  "calibrstatus" text(50),
  "pointaccarc" real(6,2),
  "trackaccarc" real(6,2),
  "focusquality" text(25),
  "detecttempk" real(7,2),
  "coolsysstatus" text(35),
  "powerstatus" text(30),
  "datastorstatus" text(35),
  "netstatus" text(40),
  "bandusagepct" real(5,2),
  "procqueuestatus" text(40),
  CONSTRAINT "telescopes_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("telescregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_telescopes_observatoriesref" FOREIGN KEY ("observstation") REFERENCES "observatories" ("observstation")
);

Observatories.WeathProfile: Full name: 'Weather Profile'. Explanation: A short description of weather conditions during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Clear, Cloudy, Partially Cloudy.

ResearchProcess.CollabStat: Full name: 'Collaboration Status'. Explanation: The nature of collaboration on this signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: International, Solo, Team.
ResearchProcess.DiscStat: Full name: 'Disclosure Status'. Explanation: How much information about the signal is shared publicly. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Full, None, Partial.
ResearchProcess.FollowStat: Full name: 'Follow-up Status'. Explanation: Status of any follow-up observations. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Required, Scheduled.
ResearchProcess.FundStat: Full name: 'Funding Status'. Explanation: Funding situation for further study. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Funded, Pending, Unfunded.
ResearchProcess.NotesMemo: Full name: 'Research Notes'. Explanation: Any extra remarks or context by researchers. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Project requires further funding...'
ResearchProcess.PeerRevStat: Full name: 'Peer Review Status'. Explanation: Where this signal stands in peer review. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, In Progress, Pending.
ResearchProcess.PubStat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether findings about the signal have been published. Data type: CHAR(25). Possible categories: Draft, Published, Submitted.
ResearchProcess.ResPrio: Full name: 'Research Priority'. Explanation: How urgently this signal needs scientific attention. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium.
ResearchProcess.SecClass: Full name: 'Security Classification'. Explanation: Visibility and clearance level for the data. Data type: CHAR(35). Possible categories: Classified, Public, Restricted.
ResearchProcess.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-MNO-7890'.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.CultSig: Full name: 'Cultural Significance'. Explanation: The level of cultural impact or interest. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: High, Low, None.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.EncryptEvid: Full name: 'Encryption Evidence'. Explanation: Whether there is indication the signal is encrypted. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: None, Possible, Strong.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.GravLens: Full name: 'Gravitational Lensing'. Explanation: Whether the signal is affected by gravitational lensing. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: None, Strong, Weak.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.InterMedEffects: Full name: 'Interstellar Medium Effects'. Explanation: Impact of interstellar medium on the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.LangStruct: Full name: 'Language Structure'. Explanation: Presence of linguistic or structured patterns. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Complex, None, Simple.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.MsgContent: Full name: 'Message Content'. Explanation: Indicates whether an actual message was detected. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Identified, None, Possible.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.QuantEffects: Full name: 'Quantum Effects'. Explanation: Quantum-level phenomena observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(85). Possible categories: None, Observed, Significant.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SciImpact: Full name: 'Scientific Impact'. Explanation: Significance of the signal to scientific research. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Major, Minor, Moderate.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-ABC-1234'.
SignalClassification.ClassConf: Full name: 'Classification Confidence (%)'. Explanation: How confident we are in the assigned signal class. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '92.50'.
SignalClassification.ComplexIdx: Full name: 'Complexity Index'. Explanation: Numeric measure of the signal’s complexity. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '5.678'.
SignalClassification.EntropyVal: Full name: 'Entropy'. Explanation: Entropy measurement of the signal. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.45'.
SignalClassification.InfoDense: Full name: 'Information Density'. Explanation: Estimated information per unit time/frequency. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.345'.
SignalClassification.PeriodSec: Full name: 'Period (s)'. Explanation: Duration of each cycle if periodic. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '12.345'.
SignalClassification.RepeatCount: Full name: 'Repetition Count'. Explanation: Number of times the signal has repeated. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '3'.
SignalClassification.SigClassType: Full name: 'Classification Type'. Explanation: High-level category for the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Artificial, Candidate, Natural, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SigPattern: Full name: 'Signal Pattern'. Explanation: Pattern observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: Periodic, Random, Structured, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-DEF-5678'.
SignalDecoding.AnalysisDp: Full name: 'Analysis Depth'. Explanation: How thoroughly the signal was analyzed. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Comprehensive, Detailed, Preliminary.
SignalDecoding.CompResources: Full name: 'Computational Resources'. Explanation: Level of computing power used. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Extreme, High, Low, Medium.
SignalDecoding.CompressRatio: Full name: 'Compression Ratio'. Explanation: Factor by which the raw signal data was compressed. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.500'.
SignalDecoding.ConfirmStat: Full name: 'Confirmation Status'. Explanation: Whether the decoding results have been confirmed. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Confirmed, Pending, Rejected.
SignalDecoding.DecodeConf: Full name: 'Decoding Confidence (%)'. Explanation: Confidence level that the decoding is correct. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '88.75'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeIters: Full name: 'Decoding Iterations'. Explanation: Number of algorithmic passes attempted. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '7'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeMethod: Full name: 'Decoding Method'. Explanation: Method used to decode the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: FFT, Neural Network, Quantum, Wavelet.
SignalDecoding.DecodeStat: Full name: 'Decoding Status'. Explanation: Status of the decoding process. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Failed, In Progress.
SignalDecoding.EncodeType: Full name: 'Encoding Type'. Explanation: The type of signal encoding used (e.g., Binary). Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Binary, Complex, Tertiary, Unknown.
SignalDecoding.ErrCorrLvl: Full name: 'Error Correction Level'. Explanation: Degree of error correction applied. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, None.
SignalDecoding.ProcTimeHrs: Full name: 'Processing Time (hours)'. Explanation: Total hours spent decoding. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.50'.
SignalDecoding.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal entry. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-GHI-9012'.
SignalDecoding.VerifLvl: Full name: 'Verification Level'. Explanation: Extent to which decoding has been verified. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Partially, Unverified, Verified.
SignalDynamics.AmpStab: Full name: 'Amplitude Stability'. Explanation: Consistency of signal amplitude. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Unstable'.
SignalDynamics.FreqStab: Full name: 'Frequency Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal’s frequency is. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighlyStable'.
SignalDynamics.ModStab: Full name: 'Modulation Stability'. Explanation: Consistency in the signal’s modulation scheme. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'Consistent'.
SignalDynamics.PhaseStab: Full name: 'Phase Stability'. Explanation: Any variation in signal phase. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'VaryingPhase'.
SignalDynamics.SigCoherence: Full name: 'Signal Coherence'. Explanation: How coherent the signal remains over its duration. Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighCoherence'.
SignalDynamics.SigDisp: Full name: 'Signal Dispersion'. Explanation: The degree to which the signal is dispersed (time/frequency smearing). Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'SignificantDisp'.
SignalDynamics.SigEvolve: Full name: 'Signal Evolution'. Explanation: Indicates if the signal changes/evolves during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Dynamic, Static, Unknown.
SignalDynamics.SigIntegrity: Full name: 'Signal Integrity'. Explanation: Rating of how intact or uncorrupted the signal is. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighIntegrity'.
SignalDynamics.SigRecurr: Full name: 'Signal Recurrence'. Explanation: Whether the signal recurs over time. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: None, Regular, Sporadic.
SignalDynamics.SigScint: Full name: 'Signal Scintillation'. Explanation: Fluctuation in signal amplitude due to propagation effects. Data type: VARCHAR(45). If no fixed categories, example: 'MildScintillation'.
SignalDynamics.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-JKL-3456'.
SignalDynamics.SpatStab: Full name: 'Spatial Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal is spatially (e.g., consistent direction). Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Moderate'.
SignalDynamics.TempStab: Full name: 'Temporal Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal remains over time. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Stable'.
SignalProbabilities.AnomScore: Full name: 'Anomaly Score'. Explanation: How unusual or unexpected the signal is. Data type: FLOAT. Example: '1.23'.
SignalProbabilities.ArtSrcProb: Full name: 'Artificial Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from an artificial source. Data type: NUMERIC(3,1). Example: '3.4'.
SignalProbabilities.BioSigProb: Full name: 'Biosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal indicates a biological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '45.21'.
SignalProbabilities.CorrScore: Full name: 'Correlation Score'. Explanation: How well the signal aligns with expected patterns. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.9950'.
SignalProbabilities.FalsePosProb: Full name: 'False Positive Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is falsely detected. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.0135'.
SignalProbabilities.NatSrcProb: Full name: 'Natural Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from a natural source. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '98.761'.
SignalProbabilities.SigUnique: Full name: 'Signal Uniqueness'. Explanation: A measure of how unique the signal is compared to others. Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '99.1234'.
SignalProbabilities.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-XYZ-9876'.
SignalProbabilities.SimIndex: Full name: 'Similarity Index'. Explanation: Compares the signal to known references. Data type: NUMERIC(5,4). Example: '0.8222'.
SignalProbabilities.TechSigProb: Full name: 'Technosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is of artificial technological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.6789'.
Signals.AtmoInterf: Full name: 'Atmospheric Interference'. Explanation: Impact of atmospheric conditions on signal. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
Signals.BwHz: Full name: 'Bandwidth (Hz)'. Explanation: Signal’s bandwidth in Hertz. Data type: DECIMAL(10,3). Example: '500000.000'.
Signals.CarrierFreqMhz: Full name: 'Carrier Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Frequency of the carrier wave in MHz. Data type: DECIMAL(9,3). Example: '1000.000'.
Signals.CenterFreqMhz: Full name: 'Center Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Center frequency of the detected signal in MHz. Data type: NUMERIC(8,3). Example: '1420.500'.
Signals.DetectInstr: Full name: 'Detection Instrument'. Explanation: The instrument type employed for detecting the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Infrared Array, Optical Telescope, Quantum Detector, Radio Telescope.
Signals.DoppShiftHz: Full name: 'Doppler Shift (Hz)'. Explanation: Measured Doppler shift of the signal in Hertz. Data type: DOUBLE PRECISION. Example: '142.75'.
Signals.FreqDriftHzs: Full name: 'Frequency Drift (Hz/s)'. Explanation: How fast the signal drifts in frequency over time. Data type: NUMERIC(9,3). Example: '0.123'.
Signals.FreqMhz: Full name: 'Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Signal’s nominal frequency in MHz. Data type: DECIMAL(9,3). Example: '1420.405'.
Signals.InterfLvl: Full name: 'Interference Level'. Explanation: Degree of interference around the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, None.
Signals.ModIndex: Full name: 'Modulation Index'. Explanation: Numerical index describing modulation depth. Data type: DECIMAL(6,4). Example: '0.2875'.
Signals.ModType: Full name: 'Modulation Type'. Explanation: The method of signal modulation. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: AM, FM, PM, QAM, Unknown.
Signals.NoiseFloorDbm: Full name: 'Noise Floor (dBm)'. Explanation: Measured noise floor in dBm. Data type: DOUBLE PRECISION. Example: '-85.3'.
Signals.PhaseShiftDeg: Full name: 'Phase Shift (°)'. Explanation: Phase shift in degrees for the signal. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '45.00'.
Signals.PolarAngleDeg: Full name: 'Polarization Angle (°)'. Explanation: Angle of polarization in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(5,1). Example: '90.0'.
Signals.PolarMode: Full name: 'Polarization Mode'. Explanation: Type of signal polarization. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Circular, Elliptical, Linear, Unknown.
Signals.PulsePerSec: Full name: 'Pulse Rate (pulses/sec)'. Explanation: Rate of pulse repetition in the signal. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '4.500'.
Signals.PulseWidMs: Full name: 'Pulse Width (ms)'. Explanation: Duration of each pulse in milliseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '2.300'.
Signals.RfiStat: Full name: 'RFI Status'. Explanation: Radio Frequency Interference status. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Clean, Contaminated, Unknown.
Signals.SigDurSec: Full name: 'Signal Duration (s)'. Explanation: Total duration of the signal in seconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '12.50'.
Signals.SigStrDb: Full name: 'Signal Strength (dB)'. Explanation: Measured strength of the signal in decibels. Data type: NUMERIC(7,2). Example: '12.35'.
Signals.SignalClass: Full name: 'Signal Type'. Explanation: Broad classification of the detected signal. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Broadband, Continuous, Modulated, Narrowband, Pulsed.
Signals.SignalRegistry: Full name: 'Signal Registry'. Explanation: Unique ID for each signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-123E4567-E89B'.
Signals.SnrRatio: Full name: 'Signal-to-Noise Ratio'. Explanation: SNR measured for the signal. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '18.75'.
Signals.TelescRef: Full name: 'Telescope Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key to the telescope used for detection. Data type: CHAR(20). Example: 'TELESC_0001'.
Signals.TimeMark: Full name: 'Timestamp'. Explanation: The moment of signal detection. In some CSVs, it may be stored as an Excel serial date/time (e.g., '44302.55648' ≈ 2021-05-16 13:20:20 UTC). Data type: TIMESTAMPTZ. Example: '2025-08-01 13:45:00+00'.
SourceProperties.CelestObj: Full name: 'Celestial Object'. Explanation: Broad classification of the object. Data type: VARCHAR(75). Possible categories: Galaxy, Planet, Star, Unknown.
SourceProperties.GalLat: Full name: 'Galactic Latitude (°)'. Explanation: Galactic latitude of the source. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '-5.67'.
SourceProperties.GalLong: Full name: 'Galactic Longitude (°)'. Explanation: Galactic longitude of the source. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '12.34'.
SourceProperties.ObjAgeGyr: Full name: 'Object Age (Gyr)'. Explanation: Estimated age in billions of years. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '4.500'.
SourceProperties.ObjMag: Full name: 'Apparent Magnitude'. Explanation: Brightness of the object as seen from Earth. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '7.35'.
SourceProperties.ObjMassSol: Full name: 'Object Mass (solar)'. Explanation: Mass relative to the Sun. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '1.005'.
SourceProperties.ObjMetal: Full name: 'Metallicity'. Explanation: Ratio of elements heavier than helium in the object. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.012'.
SourceProperties.ObjPropMotion: Full name: 'Proper Motion (mas/yr)'. Explanation: Apparent motion across the sky in milliarcseconds/year. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '55.12'.
SourceProperties.ObjRadVel: Full name: 'Radial Velocity (km/s)'. Explanation: Speed at which the object is moving toward/away from us. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '-23.45'.
SourceProperties.ObjTempK: Full name: 'Object Temperature (K)'. Explanation: Approximate surface temperature in Kelvin. Data type: INTEGER. Example: '5800'.
SourceProperties.ObjType: Full name: 'Object Subtype'. Explanation: More specific object type. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Dwarf, Giant, Main Sequence, Unknown.
SourceProperties.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-STU-5432'.
SourceProperties.SourceDecDeg: Full name: 'Declination (°)'. Explanation: Declination of the source in degrees (-90 to +90). Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '-20.4567'.
SourceProperties.SourceDistLy: Full name: 'Distance (ly)'. Explanation: Approximate distance to the source in light-years. Data type: NUMERIC(10,2). Example: '26000.45'.
SourceProperties.SourceRaDeg: Full name: 'Right Ascension (°)'. Explanation: RA of the source in degrees (0 to 360). Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '123.4567'.
Telescopes.BandUsagePct: Full name: 'Bandwidth Usage (%)'. Explanation: Network bandwidth usage as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '73.25'.
Telescopes.CalibrStatus: Full name: 'Calibration Status'. Explanation: Status of telescope’s calibration. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Current, Due, Overdue.
Telescopes.CoolSysStatus: Full name: 'Cooling System Status'. Explanation: Status of the telescope’s cooling system. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Critical, Normal, Warning.
Telescopes.DataStorStatus: Full name: 'Data Storage Status'. Explanation: Capacity and status of local data storage. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Available, Critical, Low.
Telescopes.DetectTempK: Full name: 'Detector Temperature (K)'. Explanation: Temperature of the telescope’s primary detector in Kelvin. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '123.45'.
Telescopes.EquipStatus: Full name: 'Equipment Status'. Explanation: Operational state of the telescope. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Degraded, Maintenance, Operational.
Telescopes.FocusQuality: Full name: 'Focus Quality'. Explanation: Quality of the telescope’s focusing system. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
Telescopes.NetStatus: Full name: 'Network Status'. Explanation: Status of the network connection for telescope data transfer. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Connected, Disconnected, Limited.
Telescopes.ObservStation: Full name: 'Observatory Name Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key linking to the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
Telescopes.PointAccArc: Full name: 'Pointing Accuracy (arcsec)'. Explanation: How precise the telescope can point, in arcseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '0.45'.
Telescopes.PowerStatus: Full name: 'Power Supply Status'. Explanation: Indicates which power source or level is in use. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Backup, Critical, Main.
Telescopes.ProcQueueStatus: Full name: 'Processing Queue Status'. Explanation: Indicates how full the processing queue is. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Empty, Full, Normal.
Telescopes.TelescRegistry: Full name: 'Telescope Registry'. Explanation: A unique identifier for the telescope. Data type: CHAR(20). Example: 'TELESC_0001'.
Telescopes.TrackAccArc: Full name: 'Tracking Accuracy (arcsec)'. Explanation: How accurately the telescope can track a target, in arcseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '1.20'.

requests.specific_A: Group members by their major (`link_to_major`), with all members whose major is missing forming one extra group of their own that counts like any other group (in the total, in the average share, and in the comparison), and count the members in each group. Give each group a share: its count divided by the total count across all groups. Take the groups whose share is above the average share across groups, and return a single row with the total number of members in those groups, the average of their shares, and the average amount by which their shares exceed the average share. Do not round.
requests.specific_B: Group members by their major (`link_to_major`), first removing all members whose major is missing so they appear in no group, no total and no average, and count the members in each group. Give each group a share: its count divided by the total count across all groups. Take the groups whose share is above the average share across groups, and return a single row with the total number of members in those groups, the average of their shares, and the average amount by which their shares exceed the average share. Do not round.
requests.open: Group members by `link_to_major` and count the members in each group, then give each group its share of the total count. For the groups whose share is above the average share across groups, return one row with the total number of members in them, their average share, and on average how far their shares are above the average share. No rounding.

readings.A: Members without a major are treated as one extra group in every step.
readings.B: Only members who have a major are considered.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "member"."link_to_major" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "member" AS "member" GROUP BY "member"."link_to_major"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "member"."link_to_major" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "member" AS "member" WHERE "member"."link_to_major" IS NOT NULL GROUP BY "member"."link_to_major"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from `member` records and group them by `link_to_major`. Whether members with no major are included is the choice.

Count the members in each group. Each group's share is its count divided by the total count across all groups. The average share is the plain mean of the shares across groups. Keep only groups whose share is strictly above the average share.
Return exactly one row summarizing the kept groups, with no rounding.
Column 1: the total number of members in the kept groups.
Column 2: the average share of the kept groups.
Column 3: the average, over the kept groups, of share minus average share.

A.requirement: Members with a missing `link_to_major` form one group of their own. That group counts in the total and in the average share, and it can be one of the kept groups.

B.requirement: Members with a missing `link_to_major` are excluded before grouping. They are not in any group, the total or the average share.

requests.specific_A: For each constructor `nationality`, show the total points from constructor results (ignoring missing points) and the number of constructor result records, i.e. constructor-race entries. Also show how far that number is above or below the average number across all nationalities (unrounded).
requests.specific_B: For each constructor `nationality`, show the total points from constructor results (ignoring missing points) and the number of distinct constructors with constructor results. Also show how far that number is above or below the average number across all nationalities (unrounded).
requests.open: For each constructor nationality, what are the total points in the constructor results (ignoring missing points)? How many constructor entries does it have in the results, and how far is that above or below the average across nationalities?

readings.A: For each nationality, count every constructor result record (constructor-race entries). The baseline is the average of these record counts across nationalities.
readings.B: For each nationality, count the distinct constructors that appear in the results. The baseline is the average of these constructor counts across nationalities.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "constructors"."nationality" AS "g", SUM("constructorResults"."points") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "constructorResults" AS "constructorResults" INNER JOIN "constructors" AS "constructors" ON "constructors"."constructorId" = "constructorResults"."constructorId" GROUP BY "constructors"."nationality"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "constructors"."nationality" AS "g", SUM("constructorResults"."points") AS "m1", COUNT(DISTINCT "constructorResults"."constructorId") AS "m2" FROM "constructorResults" AS "constructorResults" INNER JOIN "constructors" AS "constructors" ON "constructors"."constructorId" = "constructorResults"."constructorId" GROUP BY "constructors"."nationality"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)

shared_requirements.requirement: Use the constructor result records (`constructorResults`).
Link the records to `constructors` on constructor id (inner join). Group by constructor nationality.
constructor nationality
total constructor result points: the sum of `constructorResults.points`, ignoring missing values
a count for the nationality (what is counted is the choice)
that count minus the average of the count across all nationalities, with no rounding. No ordering and no row limit.

A.requirement: Count the constructor result records for the nationality, i.e. constructor-race entries.

B.requirement: Count the distinct constructors of that nationality that have results.

requests.specific_A: Link each invoice line item to its product (by product id) and to that product's category (by production type code), dropping lines with no match. For each product type description, compute the average `product_quantity` and the average cost difference, where each line's cost difference is `derived_product_cost` minus `derived_total_cost` (ignore missing values). Then take the mean of those category averages and keep only the categories whose average cost difference is above that mean. Return one row with three values: the average of those categories' average quantity, the average of their average cost difference, and the average of how much their average cost difference exceeds the mean. Don't round anything.
requests.specific_B: Link each invoice line item to its product (by product id) and to that product's category (by production type code), dropping lines with no match. For each product type description, compute the average `product_quantity` and the average cost difference, where each line's cost difference is the absolute value of `derived_product_cost` minus `derived_total_cost` (ignore missing values). Then take the mean of those category averages and keep only the categories whose average cost difference is above that mean. Return one row with three values: the average of those categories' average quantity, the average of their average cost difference, and the average of how much their average cost difference exceeds the mean. Don't round anything.
requests.open: Link each invoice line item to its product (by product id) and to that product's category (by production type code), dropping lines with no match. For each product type description, compute the average `product_quantity` and the average difference between `derived_product_cost` and `derived_total_cost` per line (ignore missing values). Then keep only the categories whose average difference is above the mean of all the category averages. Return one row with three values: the average of those categories' average quantity, the average of their average difference, and the average of how much their average difference exceeds that mean. Don't round anything.

readings.A: The per-line difference is product cost minus total cost, keeping its sign.
readings.B: The per-line difference is the size of the gap between product cost and total cost, ignoring sign.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Product_Categories"."product_type_description" AS "g", AVG("Invoice_Line_Items"."product_quantity") AS "m1", AVG(("Invoice_Line_Items"."derived_product_cost" - "Invoice_Line_Items"."derived_total_cost")) AS "m2" FROM "Invoice_Line_Items" AS "Invoice_Line_Items" INNER JOIN "Products" AS "Products" ON "Products"."product_id" = "Invoice_Line_Items"."product_id" INNER JOIN "Product_Categories" AS "Product_Categories" ON "Product_Categories"."production_type_code" = "Products"."production_type_code" GROUP BY "Product_Categories"."product_type_description"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Product_Categories"."product_type_description" AS "g", AVG("Invoice_Line_Items"."product_quantity") AS "m1", AVG(ABS("Invoice_Line_Items"."derived_product_cost" - "Invoice_Line_Items"."derived_total_cost")) AS "m2" FROM "Invoice_Line_Items" AS "Invoice_Line_Items" INNER JOIN "Products" AS "Products" ON "Products"."product_id" = "Invoice_Line_Items"."product_id" INNER JOIN "Product_Categories" AS "Product_Categories" ON "Product_Categories"."production_type_code" = "Products"."production_type_code" GROUP BY "Product_Categories"."product_type_description"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v") SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s3"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s3"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from invoice line items. Inner-join them to Products on product_id, then to Product_Categories on production_type_code (compared as text). Drop unmatched lines.
Group by Product_Categories.product_type_description. Each category gets its average `product_quantity` and its average per-line cost difference, ignoring missing values.
Average the category-level average differences to get a mean. Keep only the categories whose average difference is strictly greater than that mean. If the mean is missing, keep nothing.
Collapse the kept categories into a single summary row.
The average, over the kept categories, of their average product_quantity. Missing values are ignored.
The average, over the kept categories, of their average cost difference.
The average, over the kept categories, of how far their average cost difference is above the mean (category value minus mean). No rounding on any output.

A.requirement: Each line's cost difference is the signed value derived_product_cost − derived_total_cost.

B.requirement: Each line's cost difference is the absolute value |derived_product_cost − derived_total_cost|.

requests.specific_A: Matching each scan to its site by site code (dropping scans with no matching site), group the scans by site code (`scans.zoneref`) and risk evaluation status (`riskeval`). For each group give the site code, the risk evaluation status, the average compression ratio (`pressratio`, ignoring missing values), the number of scans, and that number as a share of all matched scans. Sort by share from largest to smallest and keep exactly 10 rows; if several groups tie at the 10th place, any of them may fill the remaining spots. Don't round.
requests.specific_B: Matching each scan to its site by site code (dropping scans with no matching site), group the scans by site code (`scans.zoneref`) and risk evaluation status (`riskeval`). For each group give the site code, the risk evaluation status, the average compression ratio (`pressratio`, ignoring missing values), the number of scans, and that number as a share of all matched scans. Sort by share from largest to smallest and keep the top 10 rows plus every group whose share ties with the 10th one, even if that gives more than 10 rows. Don't round.
requests.open: Matching each scan to its site by site code (dropping scans with no matching site), group the scans by site code (`scans.zoneref`) and risk evaluation status (`riskeval`). For each group give the site code, the risk evaluation status, the average compression ratio (`pressratio`, ignoring missing values), the number of scans, and that number as a share of all matched scans. Show the top 10 by share, largest first. Don't round.

readings.A: Rank the site-and-risk-status groups by share of scans and return exactly 10. Ties at the cut are broken arbitrarily.
readings.B: Rank the site-and-risk-status groups by share of scans and return every group whose share reaches the 10th-ranked share, including all ties.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scans"."zoneref" AS "e", "sites"."riskeval" AS "g", AVG("scans"."pressratio") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "scans" AS "scans" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scans"."zoneref" GROUP BY "scans"."zoneref", "sites"."riskeval"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scans"."zoneref" AS "e", "sites"."riskeval" AS "g", AVG("scans"."pressratio") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "scans" AS "scans" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scans"."zoneref" GROUP BY "scans"."zoneref", "sites"."riskeval"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") >= (SELECT (CAST("t"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2b"."v") AS "cut" FROM "s1" AS "t" CROSS JOIN "s2" AS "s2b" ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 9) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from scans records.
Inner-join scans to sites on sites.zoneregistry = scans.zoneref. Drop unmatched scans.
Group by scans.zoneref and sites.riskeval.
Site code (scans.zoneref).
Risk evaluation status (sites.riskeval).
Average scans.pressratio in the group. Missing values are ignored.
Number of scans in the group.
Group count ÷ sum of all group counts (share of all matched scans). No rounding.
Order by share, descending.
Cut at the 10th-ranked row.

A.requirement: Return exactly 10 rows. Which rows tied at the cut are kept is arbitrary.

B.requirement: Return every row whose share is at least the 10th-ranked share, so all ties are included even beyond 10 rows.

requests.specific_A: In `Products`, compute each `production_type_code`'s average `unit_price` (ignoring missing prices). Compute an overall baseline by averaging those per-type averages, so each type counts once regardless of how many products it has. Proceed only if the baseline exists. Keep the types whose average is above this baseline. Next, take the simple mean of the kept types' averages, and keep only the types whose average is also above that mean. Return one row with three values, each averaged over the remaining types: their type average price, how far their type average is above the overall baseline, and how far it is above the mean of the kept types.
requests.specific_B: In `Products`, compute each `production_type_code`'s average `unit_price` (ignoring missing prices). Compute an overall baseline by averaging `unit_price` directly over all individual products (ignoring missing prices), so each product counts once and types with more products weigh more. Proceed only if the baseline exists. Keep the types whose average is above this baseline. Next, take the simple mean of the kept types' averages, and keep only the types whose average is also above that mean. Return one row with three values, each averaged over the remaining types: their type average price, how far their type average is above the overall baseline, and how far it is above the mean of the kept types.
requests.open: In `Products`, find each `production_type_code`'s average `unit_price` (ignoring missing prices) and keep the types whose average is above the overall average price, if that average exists. Next, take the simple mean of the kept types' averages, and keep only the types also above that mean. Return one row with three values, each averaged over the remaining types: their type average price, how far their type average is above the overall average price, and how far it is above the mean of the kept types.

readings.A: The overall baseline price is the mean of the per-type average prices.
readings.B: The overall baseline price is the mean unit price over all individual products.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Products"."production_type_code" AS "e", AVG("Products"."unit_price") AS "m1" FROM "Products" AS "Products" GROUP BY "Products"."production_type_code"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m1" > "s4"."v") SELECT AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Products"."production_type_code" AS "e", AVG("Products"."unit_price") AS "m1" FROM "Products" AS "Products" GROUP BY "Products"."production_type_code"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("Products"."unit_price") AS "v" FROM "Products" AS "Products"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS "e", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m1" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m1" > "s4"."v") SELECT AVG("s5"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s5"."m2") AS "m2", AVG("s5"."m3") AS "m3" FROM "s5" AS "s5"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every Products record, group by production_type_code, and compute each type's average unit_price (missing ignored). Keep the types whose average is above the overall baseline, which must exist. Then take the simple mean of the kept types' averages and keep only the types also above that mean
Return one row, averaging over the remaining types
the average of their type average prices
the average of how far each type average is above the mean of the above-baseline types

A.requirement: the average of each type average minus the baseline, where the baseline is the mean of the per-type averages (each type weighted equally); the same baseline is used for the first filter

B.requirement: the average of each type average minus the baseline, where the baseline is the mean unit_price over all products (each product weighted equally); the same baseline is used for the first filter

requests.specific_A: For each telescope reference (`telescref`) in the signals table, count its signals and compute that count as an unrounded fraction of all signals. Show the telescope reference, the signal count and the fraction, sorted by fraction from highest to lowest, and return exactly 10 rows, choosing arbitrarily among telescopes tied at the cutoff.
requests.specific_B: For each telescope reference (`telescref`) in the signals table, count its signals and compute that count as an unrounded fraction of all signals. Show the telescope reference, the signal count and the fraction, sorted by fraction from highest to lowest, and return the top 10, including every telescope tied with the 10th one even if that gives more than 10 rows.
requests.open: What are the top 10 telescopes by share of detected signals? For each telescope reference (`telescref`), show how many signals it detected and what fraction of all signals that is (unrounded), from the largest share down.

readings.A: Rank telescopes by their share of all signals and return exactly 10 rows, choosing arbitrarily among telescopes tied at the 10th place.
readings.B: Rank telescopes by their share of all signals and return every telescope whose share is at least the 10th-highest share, including all ties at the cut.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "signals"."telescref" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "signals" AS "signals" GROUP BY "signals"."telescref"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "signals"."telescref" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "signals" AS "signals" GROUP BY "signals"."telescref"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" >= (SELECT "t"."m1" FROM "s1" AS "t" ORDER BY "t"."m1" DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 9) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every `signals` record and group the records by telescope reference (`signals.telescref`). Each group gives one row with its record count.
Attach to every telescope row the total signal count (the sum of all per-telescope counts). Drop rows only if that total is missing.
First column: the telescope reference (`telescref`).
Second column: the telescope's signal count.
Third column: the telescope's count divided by the total signal count, as an unrounded fraction.
Sort rows by that fraction from highest to lowest, with missing values last.
The cut falls at 10 rows, counted by fraction rank.

A.requirement: Return exactly 10 rows. If telescopes are tied at the 10th place, pick among them arbitrarily.

B.requirement: Return every telescope whose fraction is at least the 10th-highest fraction. This keeps all ties at the cut, so there may be more than 10 rows.

context.documentation:
ObservationalConditions.ObsDate: Full name: 'Observation Date'. Explanation: Local date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD). Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-08-01'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsDurHrs: Full name: 'Observation Duration (hours)'. Explanation: How long the observation lasted in hours. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '2.50'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsTime: Full name: 'Observation Time'. Explanation: Local time of the observation in HH:MM:SS. Data type: TIME. Example: '13:45:59'.
ObservationalConditions.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-PQR-9876'.
Observatories.AirTempC: Full name: 'Air Temperature (°C)'. Explanation: Ambient temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '18.45'.
Observatories.AtmosTransparency: Full name: 'Atmospheric Transparency'. Explanation: A numeric measure of how transparent the atmosphere is. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.867'.
Observatories.GeomagStatus: Full name: 'Geomagnetic Activity'. Explanation: The level of geomagnetic activity during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Active, Quiet, Storm.
Observatories.HumidityRate: Full name: 'Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Relative humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '62.300'.
Observatories.LunarDistDeg: Full name: 'Moon Distance (Degrees)'. Explanation: Angular distance to the Moon in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '97.52'.
Observatories.LunarStage: Full name: 'Lunar Phase'. Explanation: The current phase of the Moon during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: First Quarter, Full, Last Quarter, New.
Observatories.ObservStation: Full name: 'Observatory Name'. Explanation: This field holds the name or unique identifier for the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
Observatories.PressHpa: Full name: 'Pressure (hPa)'. Explanation: Atmospheric pressure in hectopascals. Data type: DECIMAL(6,1). Example: '1013.2'.
Observatories.SeeingProfile: Full name: 'Seeing Profile'. Explanation: Assessment of sky seeing conditions (atmospheric steadiness). Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
Observatories.SiderealLocal: Full name: 'Local Sidereal Time'. Explanation: Sidereal time at the observatory in HH:MM:SS format. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: '12:34:56'.
Observatories.SolarStatus: Full name: 'Solar Activity'. Explanation: The level of solar activity at the time of observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Moderate.
Observatories.WeathProfile: Full name: 'Weather Profile'. Explanation: A short description of weather conditions during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Clear, Cloudy, Partially Cloudy.
Observatories.WindSpeedMs: Full name: 'Wind Speed (m/s)'. Explanation: Wind speed in meters per second. Data type: NUMERIC(4,2). Example: '3.45'.
ResearchProcess.AnalysisPrio: Full name: 'Analysis Priority'. Explanation: Priority assigned for analyzing this signal. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, Urgent.
ResearchProcess.CollabStat: Full name: 'Collaboration Status'. Explanation: The nature of collaboration on this signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: International, Solo, Team.
ResearchProcess.DiscStat: Full name: 'Disclosure Status'. Explanation: How much information about the signal is shared publicly. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Full, None, Partial.
ResearchProcess.FollowStat: Full name: 'Follow-up Status'. Explanation: Status of any follow-up observations. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Required, Scheduled.
ResearchProcess.FundStat: Full name: 'Funding Status'. Explanation: Funding situation for further study. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Funded, Pending, Unfunded.
ResearchProcess.NotesMemo: Full name: 'Research Notes'. Explanation: Any extra remarks or context by researchers. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Project requires further funding...'
ResearchProcess.PeerRevStat: Full name: 'Peer Review Status'. Explanation: Where this signal stands in peer review. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, In Progress, Pending.
ResearchProcess.PubStat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether findings about the signal have been published. Data type: CHAR(25). Possible categories: Draft, Published, Submitted.
ResearchProcess.ResPrio: Full name: 'Research Priority'. Explanation: How urgently this signal needs scientific attention. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium.
ResearchProcess.SecClass: Full name: 'Security Classification'. Explanation: Visibility and clearance level for the data. Data type: CHAR(35). Possible categories: Classified, Public, Restricted.
ResearchProcess.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-MNO-7890'.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.CultSig: Full name: 'Cultural Significance'. Explanation: The level of cultural impact or interest. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: High, Low, None.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.EncryptEvid: Full name: 'Encryption Evidence'. Explanation: Whether there is indication the signal is encrypted. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: None, Possible, Strong.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.GravLens: Full name: 'Gravitational Lensing'. Explanation: Whether the signal is affected by gravitational lensing. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: None, Strong, Weak.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.InterMedEffects: Full name: 'Interstellar Medium Effects'. Explanation: Impact of interstellar medium on the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.LangStruct: Full name: 'Language Structure'. Explanation: Presence of linguistic or structured patterns. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Complex, None, Simple.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.MsgContent: Full name: 'Message Content'. Explanation: Indicates whether an actual message was detected. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Identified, None, Possible.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.QuantEffects: Full name: 'Quantum Effects'. Explanation: Quantum-level phenomena observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(85). Possible categories: None, Observed, Significant.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SciImpact: Full name: 'Scientific Impact'. Explanation: Significance of the signal to scientific research. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Major, Minor, Moderate.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-ABC-1234'.

requests.specific_A: Link each advanced behaviour record to its transaction (`translink` = `transreg`), dropping any without a match, and group by order type mix (`ordertypedist`), keeping a separate group for records with no mix recorded. For each mix, count the behaviour records, and work out that count's share of the total across all mixes. Take the simple average of those shares across mixes as the baseline. Return only the mixes whose share is above the baseline, showing the order type mix, the count of behaviour records, the share, and how far the share is above the baseline average share, with no rounding.
requests.specific_B: Link each advanced behaviour record to its transaction (`translink` = `transreg`), dropping any without a match, and group by order type mix (`ordertypedist`), keeping a separate group for records with no mix recorded. For each mix, count the distinct transactions, and work out that count's share of the total across all mixes. Take the simple average of those shares across mixes as the baseline. Return only the mixes whose share is above the baseline, showing the order type mix, the count of distinct transactions, the share, and how far the share is above the baseline average share, with no rounding.
requests.open: Taking the advanced behaviour analyses that tie to a transaction (via `translink` → `transreg`), which order type mixes (`ordertypedist`, with a missing mix treated as its own group) make up an above-average share? For each mix, find how many there are and its share of the overall total. Compare that share with the plain average share across mixes, and list only the mixes above that average. Show the mix, its count, its share, and how far it sits above the average share, all unrounded.

readings.A: Each mix's count is the number of behaviour-analysis records linked to transactions with that mix, and shares are computed from those counts.
readings.B: Each mix's count is the number of distinct linked transactions with that mix, and shares are computed from those counts.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "transactionrecord"."ordertypedist" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "advancedbehavior" AS "advancedbehavior" INNER JOIN "transactionrecord" AS "transactionrecord" ON "transactionrecord"."transreg" = "advancedbehavior"."translink" GROUP BY "transactionrecord"."ordertypedist"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "transactionrecord"."ordertypedist" AS "g", COUNT(DISTINCT "transactionrecord"."transreg") AS "m1" FROM "advancedbehavior" AS "advancedbehavior" INNER JOIN "transactionrecord" AS "transactionrecord" ON "transactionrecord"."transreg" = "advancedbehavior"."translink" GROUP BY "transactionrecord"."ordertypedist"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s3" AS "s3") SELECT "s3"."g" AS "g", "s3"."m1" AS "m1", "s3"."m2" AS "m2", ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s3" AS "s3" INNER JOIN "s4" AS "s4" ON NOT ("s4"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from `advancedbehavior` records
Inner join to `transactionrecord` on `transreg` = `translink`; behaviour records with no matching transaction are dropped
Group by order type mix (`transactionrecord.ordertypedist`); records with no order type mix form their own group; return the mix value
Share = the mix's count ÷ the sum of counts across all mixes, not rounded
Baseline = simple average of the shares across mixes; keep only mixes whose share is strictly greater than that baseline
Return share − baseline average share, not rounded; output columns in the order mix, count, share, excess; no ordering is specified

A.requirement: The count per mix is the number of joined behaviour records, so a transaction linked from two behaviour records counts twice

B.requirement: The count per mix is the number of distinct transactions (`transreg`), so each transaction counts once

requests.specific_A: Match each scan to its project by project ID, dropping scans with no matching project, and group by project reference (`scans.arcref`) and funding source (`fundflux`). Compute each group's size-per-minute rate as the average, over its scans, of file size (`gbsize`) divided by scan duration (`spanmin`), ignoring scans where that ratio is missing. Use the simple average of these group rates as a benchmark. For groups whose rate is strictly above the benchmark, list the project reference, funding source, rate, and how much the rate exceeds the benchmark. Sort by that excess from largest to smallest and show only the top 10. Don't round.
requests.specific_B: Match each scan to its project by project ID, dropping scans with no matching project, and group by project reference (`scans.arcref`) and funding source (`fundflux`). Compute each group's size-per-minute rate as its total file size (`gbsize`) divided by its total scan duration (`spanmin`). Use the simple average of these group rates as a benchmark. For groups whose rate is strictly above the benchmark, list the project reference, funding source, rate, and how much the rate exceeds the benchmark. Sort by that excess from largest to smallest and show only the top 10. Don't round.
requests.open: Using only scans that match a project, what's each project's size-per-minute rate (`gbsize` per `spanmin`), grouped by project reference (`scans.arcref`) and funding source (`fundflux`)? Take the plain average of those project rates as a benchmark, with each project counting once. Show the 10 projects furthest above it, keeping only those strictly above, with project reference, funding source, rate and the gap above the benchmark, biggest gap first. Leave values unrounded.

readings.A: A project's rate is the mean of its per-scan gbsize/spanmin ratios.
readings.B: A project's rate is its total gbsize divided by its total spanmin.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scans"."arcref" AS "e", "projects"."fundflux" AS "g", AVG((CAST("scans"."gbsize" AS REAL) / "scans"."spanmin")) AS "m1" FROM "scans" AS "scans" INNER JOIN "projects" AS "projects" ON "projects"."arcregistry" = "scans"."arcref" GROUP BY "scans"."arcref", "projects"."fundflux"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v" ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scans"."arcref" AS "e", "projects"."fundflux" AS "g", (CAST(SUM("scans"."gbsize") AS REAL) / SUM("scans"."spanmin")) AS "m1" FROM "scans" AS "scans" INNER JOIN "projects" AS "projects" ON "projects"."arcregistry" = "scans"."arcref" GROUP BY "scans"."arcref", "projects"."fundflux"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v" ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from scan records
Inner-join to projects where projects.arcregistry = scans.arcref (text equality); scans with no matching project are dropped
Group by project reference (scans.arcref) and funding source (projects.fundflux), giving one rate per group
Benchmark = simple (unweighted) average of the group rates, with missing rates ignored; keep only groups whose rate is strictly greater than the benchmark (keep nothing if the benchmark is missing)
Project reference (scans.arcref)
Funding source (projects.fundflux)
The group's size-per-minute rate
Rate minus benchmark; no rounding
Order by (rate − benchmark) descending, with missing values last
Keep the first 10 rows

A.requirement: Rate = average over the group's scans of gbsize ÷ spanmin (scans where the ratio is missing are ignored)

B.requirement: Rate = SUM(gbsize) ÷ SUM(spanmin) over the group's scans

  CONSTRAINT "scanenvironment_zoneref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("zoneref") REFERENCES "sites" ("zoneregistry")

  "articount" integer(32),
  "structkind" text(15),
  "matkind" text(15),
  "huestudy" text(15),
  "texturestudy" text(15),
  "patternnote" text,
  CONSTRAINT "scanfeatures_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("traitregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanfeatures_equipref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("equipref") REFERENCES "equipment" ("equipregistry"),

  "geomdeltamm" real(6,3),
  CONSTRAINT "scanmesh_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("facetregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanmesh_equipref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("equipref") REFERENCES "equipment" ("equipregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanmesh_zoneref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("zoneref") REFERENCES "sites" ("zoneregistry")

CREATE TABLE "scanpointcloud" (

  "coverpct" real(4,1),
  "totalpts" integer(64),
  "clouddense" integer(32),
  "lappct" real(4,1),
  "noisedb" real(6,3),
  "refpct" real(4,1),
  CONSTRAINT "scanpointcloud_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("cloudregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanpointcloud_arcref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("arcref") REFERENCES "projects" ("arcregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanpointcloud_crewref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("crewref") REFERENCES "personnel" ("crewregistry")

CREATE TABLE "scanprocessing" (
  "flowregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "equipref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "zoneref" text(12) NOT NULL,
  "flowsoft" text(25),
  "flowhrs" real(5,2),
  "proccpu" integer(16),
  "memusagegb" real(6,2),
  "procgpu" integer(16),
  "stashloc" text(12),
  "safebak" text(50),
  "datalevel" text,
  "metabench" text(50),
  "coordframe" text(12),
  "elevref" text(16),
  "remaingb" real(7,2),
  "stationlink" text(50),
  "camcal" text,
  "lensdist" text(14),
  "colortune" text(50),
  "flowstage" text(18),
  "fmtver" text(3),
  CONSTRAINT "scanprocessing_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("flowregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanprocessing_equipref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("equipref") REFERENCES "equipment" ("equipregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanprocessing_zoneref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("zoneref") REFERENCES "sites" ("zoneregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanqc" (
  "qualregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "arcref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "crewref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "accucheck" text(22),
  "ctrlstate" text(50),
  "valimeth" text(18),
  "valistate" text,
  "archstat" text(50),
  "pubstat" text(24),
  "copystat" text(50),
  "refmention" text(60),
  "remark" text,
  CONSTRAINT "scanqc_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("qualregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanqc_arcref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("arcref") REFERENCES "projects" ("arcregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanqc_crewref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("crewref") REFERENCES "personnel" ("crewregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanregistration" (
  "logregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "crewref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "arcref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "logaccumm" real(5,3),
  "refmark" text(6),
  "ctrlpts" text(6),
  "logmethod" text(15),
  "transform" text(15),
  "errscale" text(20),
  "errvalmm" real(6,3),
  CONSTRAINT "scanregistration_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("logregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanregistration_arcref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("arcref") REFERENCES "projects" ("arcregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanregistration_crewref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("crewref") REFERENCES "personnel" ("crewregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scans" (
  "questregistry" text(16) NOT NULL,
  "chronotag" text(6),
  "arcref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "crewref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "zoneref" text(12) NOT NULL,
  "scancount" integer(16),
  "climtune" text(22),
  "huecatch" text(50),

  "spanmin" real(5,2),
  CONSTRAINT "scans_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("questregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scans_arcref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("arcref") REFERENCES "projects" ("arcregistry"),

  CONSTRAINT "scans_zoneref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("zoneref") REFERENCES "sites" ("zoneregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanspatial" (
  "domainregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "arcref" text(50) NOT NULL,

  "angleaz" integer(24),

CREATE TABLE "sites" (
  "zoneregistry" text(12) NOT NULL,

  "gridtrace" text(12),

  "geoy" real(8,5),
  "heightm" real(7,1),
  "depthc" real(7,1),
  "phasefactor" text(25),
  "guessdate" text(20),
  "typesite" text(25),
  "presstat" text(25),
  "guardhint" text(50),
  "entrystat" text(50),
  "saferank" text(15),
  "insurstat" text(15),
