requests.specific_A: Considering only budget lines whose `amount` is at least 75, group them by `category`. For each category, compute the average `remaining` and the total of `amount` minus `spent`, ignoring missing values (each is blank if a category has no values). Then average those per-category totals across all categories. If that average exists, list the categories whose total is strictly greater than it. For each one, show the category, its average remaining, its total, and how far its total is above the overall average, without rounding.
requests.specific_B: Considering only budget lines whose `amount` is more than 75, group them by `category`. For each category, compute the average `remaining` and the total of `amount` minus `spent`, ignoring missing values (each is blank if a category has no values). Then average those per-category totals across all categories. If that average exists, list the categories whose total is strictly greater than it. For each one, show the category, its average remaining, its total, and how far its total is above the overall average, without rounding.
requests.open: Looking only at budget lines whose budgeted `amount` passes the 75-dollar cutoff, group them by `category`. For each category, compute the average `remaining` and the total of `amount` minus `spent`, ignoring missing values (each is blank if a category has no values). Then average those per-category totals across all categories. If that average exists, list the categories whose total is strictly greater than it. For each one, show the category, its average remaining, its total, and how far its total is above the overall average, without rounding.

readings.A: Budget lines whose budgeted amount equals 75 are included along with those above 75.
readings.B: Only budget lines whose budgeted amount is strictly greater than 75 are included. Lines at exactly 75 are left out.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "budget"."category" AS "g", AVG("budget"."remaining") AS "m1", SUM(("budget"."amount" - "budget"."spent")) AS "m2" FROM "budget" AS "budget" WHERE "budget"."amount" >= 75 GROUP BY "budget"."category"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "budget"."category" AS "g", AVG("budget"."remaining") AS "m1", SUM(("budget"."amount" - "budget"."spent")) AS "m2" FROM "budget" AS "budget" WHERE "budget"."amount" > 75 GROUP BY "budget"."category"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m2" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m2" > "s2"."v"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the `budget` records (budget lines).
Filter on the budgeted amount `budget.amount` against the threshold 75. Whether 75 itself counts is the open choice.
Group the kept lines by `budget.category`, giving one row per category, and output the category.
For each category, output the average of `budget.remaining`. Missing values are ignored, and the result is missing if there are none.
For each category, output the sum of `amount` − `spent`. Missing values are ignored, and the result is missing if there are none.

Compute the overall average of the per-category totals (column 3) across all categories, ignoring missing ones. Attach it to every category row only when it is not missing; otherwise no rows are returned.

Keep only categories whose total (column 3) is strictly greater than that overall average. Output category, average remaining, total, and total minus the overall average, in that column order. No rounding.

A.requirement: Keep lines with `budget.amount` >= 75 (exactly 75 counts).

B.requirement: Keep lines with `budget.amount` > 75 (exactly 75 is excluded).

requests.specific_A: Considering only race results whose classification order (`positionOrder`) is 12 or greater, each matched to its race, show for each race (grouped by race ID and race name) the race ID, the race name, and the average number of laps completed (`laps`, ignoring missing values). List the 10 races with the highest average first, with any race lacking an average placed last.
requests.specific_B: Considering only race results whose classification order (`positionOrder`) is greater than 12, each matched to its race, show for each race (grouped by race ID and race name) the race ID, the race name, and the average number of laps completed (`laps`, ignoring missing values). List the 10 races with the highest average first, with any race lacking an average placed last.
requests.open: Looking only at back-of-the-field results, using 12 as the cutoff on classification order (`positionOrder`), and matching each result to its race: for each race (grouped by race ID and race name), show the race ID, the race name, and the average number of laps completed (`laps`, ignoring missing values). List the 10 races with the highest average first, with any race lacking an average placed last.

readings.A: Results classified exactly 12th are included in the filtered set, along with all later classifications.
readings.B: Only results classified after 12th (13th onward) are included. Results classified exactly 12th are excluded.

sql.A: SELECT "results"."raceId" AS "e", "races"."name" AS "g", AVG("results"."laps") AS "m1" FROM "results" AS "results" INNER JOIN "races" AS "races" ON "races"."raceId" = "results"."raceId" WHERE "results"."positionOrder" >= 12 GROUP BY "results"."raceId", "races"."name" ORDER BY AVG("results"."laps") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: SELECT "results"."raceId" AS "e", "races"."name" AS "g", AVG("results"."laps") AS "m1" FROM "results" AS "results" INNER JOIN "races" AS "races" ON "races"."raceId" = "results"."raceId" WHERE "results"."positionOrder" > 12 GROUP BY "results"."raceId", "races"."name" ORDER BY AVG("results"."laps") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from each `results` record.
Match each result to its race in `races` where `races.raceId` = `results.raceId`. There is one combined record per match, and results with no matching race are dropped.
Filter on classification order (`results.positionOrder`) using a threshold of 12, keeping results at the back of the order (numerically large values).
Group the kept records by race ID (`results.raceId`) and race name (`races.name`). Each group gives one result row.
Race ID (`results.raceId`).
Race name (`races.name`).
Average of laps completed (`results.laps`) in the group. Missing values are ignored, and the average is missing when there are none. No rounding.
Order rows by that average laps, descending, with missing averages last.
Keep only the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: Keep results whose `positionOrder` is at least 12 (12 included).

B.requirement: Keep results whose `positionOrder` is strictly more than 12 (12 excluded).

requests.specific_A: Looking only at processing runs whose RAM usage (`memusagegb`) is at least 60.8 GB and whose site code (`zoneref`) matches a site, first work out, for each site code and site access status (`entrystat`), the average RAM usage and the average GPU-to-CPU usage ratio (`procgpu` ÷ `proccpu`), ignoring missing values. Then, for each access status, give the access status, the average of those per-site average RAM usages, and the average of those per-site average GPU/CPU ratios, unrounded.
requests.specific_B: Looking only at processing runs whose RAM usage (`memusagegb`) is more than 60.8 GB and whose site code (`zoneref`) matches a site, first work out, for each site code and site access status (`entrystat`), the average RAM usage and the average GPU-to-CPU usage ratio (`procgpu` ÷ `proccpu`), ignoring missing values. Then, for each access status, give the access status, the average of those per-site average RAM usages, and the average of those per-site average GPU/CPU ratios, unrounded.
requests.open: For the memory-heavy processing runs, using 60.8 GB of RAM (`memusagegb`) as the cutoff and counting only runs whose site code (`zoneref`) matches a site: first get, for each site code and access status (`entrystat`), the average RAM usage and the average GPU-to-CPU usage ratio (`procgpu` ÷ `proccpu`), ignoring missing values. Then, for each access status, give the access status, the average of those per-site RAM averages, and the average of those per-site GPU/CPU ratios, unrounded.

readings.A: A processing record qualifies when its RAM usage is 60.8 GB or more, so 60.8 itself counts.
readings.B: A processing record qualifies only when its RAM usage is greater than 60.8 GB, so 60.8 itself does not count.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scanprocessing"."zoneref" AS "e", "sites"."entrystat" AS "g", AVG("scanprocessing"."memusagegb") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("scanprocessing"."procgpu" AS REAL) / "scanprocessing"."proccpu")) AS "m2" FROM "scanprocessing" AS "scanprocessing" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scanprocessing"."zoneref" WHERE "scanprocessing"."memusagegb" >= 60.8 GROUP BY "scanprocessing"."zoneref", "sites"."entrystat") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scanprocessing"."zoneref" AS "e", "sites"."entrystat" AS "g", AVG("scanprocessing"."memusagegb") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("scanprocessing"."procgpu" AS REAL) / "scanprocessing"."proccpu")) AS "m2" FROM "scanprocessing" AS "scanprocessing" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scanprocessing"."zoneref" WHERE "scanprocessing"."memusagegb" > 60.8 GROUP BY "scanprocessing"."zoneref", "sites"."entrystat") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from scanprocessing records, inner-joined to sites where sites.zoneregistry = scanprocessing.zoneref (text equality); processing records with no matching site are dropped
Keep only processing records that pass the RAM-usage (memusagegb) threshold of 60.8

Step 1: group the kept records by site code (scanprocessing.zoneref) and site access status (sites.entrystat). For each group, compute AVG(memusagegb) and AVG(procgpu / proccpu) as real division; missing values are ignored, and the result is missing when the group has none
Step 2: group the step-1 rows by access status only, so the final averages are averages of the per-(site, status) averages, not of the raw records
Access status (sites.entrystat)
Average over that status's step-1 rows of the per-site average RAM usage (missing values ignored)
Average over that status's step-1 rows of the per-site average GPU/CPU usage ratio (missing values ignored)
No rounding; no ordering or limit is required

A.requirement: memusagegb >= 60.8 (a value of exactly 60.8 is kept)

B.requirement: memusagegb > 60.8 (a value of exactly 60.8 is excluded)

requests.specific_A: Matching each driver standings entry to its race (`races.raceId` = `driverStandings.raceId`), keep only entries whose season-to-date driver points (`driverStandings.points`) are at least 1.0. For each race name (`races.name`), compute the average season-to-date points of the kept entries, ignoring missing values (missing if there are none). Then take the overall average of these per-race-name averages, ignoring missing values; return nothing if it is missing. List the race names whose average is strictly greater than the overall average, giving the race name, its average, and its average minus the overall average, without rounding.
requests.specific_B: Matching each driver standings entry to its race (`races.raceId` = `driverStandings.raceId`), keep only entries whose season-to-date driver points (`driverStandings.points`) are more than 1.0. For each race name (`races.name`), compute the average season-to-date points of the kept entries, ignoring missing values (missing if there are none). Then take the overall average of these per-race-name averages, ignoring missing values; return nothing if it is missing. List the race names whose average is strictly greater than the overall average, giving the race name, its average, and its average minus the overall average, without rounding.
requests.open: Matching each driver standings entry to its race (`races.raceId` = `driverStandings.raceId`), keep only entries whose season-to-date driver points (`driverStandings.points`) clear the 1.0-point threshold. For each race name (`races.name`), compute the average season-to-date points of the kept entries, ignoring missing values (missing if there are none). Then take the overall average of these per-race-name averages, ignoring missing values; return nothing if it is missing. List the race names whose average is strictly greater than the overall average, giving the race name, its average, and its average minus the overall average, without rounding.

readings.A: Driver standings entries with season-to-date points equal to 1.0 are included in the filter.
readings.B: Only driver standings entries with season-to-date points strictly greater than 1.0 are included in the filter.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "races"."name" AS "g", AVG("driverStandings"."points") AS "m1" FROM "driverStandings" AS "driverStandings" INNER JOIN "races" AS "races" ON "races"."raceId" = "driverStandings"."raceId" WHERE "driverStandings"."points" >= 1.0 GROUP BY "races"."name"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "races"."name" AS "g", AVG("driverStandings"."points") AS "m1" FROM "driverStandings" AS "driverStandings" INNER JOIN "races" AS "races" ON "races"."raceId" = "driverStandings"."raceId" WHERE "driverStandings"."points" > 1.0 GROUP BY "races"."name"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from driver standings entries (`driverStandings`). Keep only entries whose season-to-date driver points (`driverStandings.points`) meet the 1.0 threshold, keeping the higher values. Whether exactly 1.0 counts is the choice.
Match each entry to its race (`races.raceId` = `driverStandings.raceId`). Entries without a match are dropped. Group by race name (`races.name`).
Return the race name (`races.name`).
Return the average season-to-date driver points over the race name's kept entries, ignoring missing values. It is missing if there are none. Not rounded.
Compute the overall average of the per-race-name averages, ignoring missing values. Return nothing if it is missing. Keep only race names whose average is strictly greater than the overall average.
Return the race-name average minus the overall average. Not rounded.

A.requirement: Entries with exactly 1.0 points are kept (points >= 1.0).

B.requirement: Only entries with more than 1.0 points are kept (points > 1.0).

CREATE TABLE "circuits" (
"circuitId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "circuitRef" TEXT,
  "name" TEXT,
  "location" TEXT,
  "country" TEXT,
  "lat" REAL,
  "lng" REAL,
  "alt" TEXT,
  "url" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "races" (
"raceId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "year" INTEGER,
  "round" INTEGER,
  "circuitId" INTEGER,
  "name" TEXT,
  "date" TEXT,
  "time" TEXT,
  "url" TEXT,

requests.specific_A: Looking only at order executions whose expiry time (`expirespot`) falls between '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533', with both endpoints included (comparing the values as text), group them by order (`ordersmark`) and, for each order, compute the average unfilled quantity (`remaincount`, ignoring missing values) and the number of executions. Then give me one row with the average of those per-order averages (ignoring missing ones) and the total of the per-order execution counts, without rounding.
requests.specific_B: Looking only at order executions whose expiry time (`expirespot`) falls between '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533', with both endpoints excluded (comparing the values as text), group them by order (`ordersmark`) and, for each order, compute the average unfilled quantity (`remaincount`, ignoring missing values) and the number of executions. Then give me one row with the average of those per-order averages (ignoring missing ones) and the total of the per-order execution counts, without rounding.
requests.open: For order executions with an expiry time (`expirespot`) between '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' (comparing the values as text), group them by order (`ordersmark`) and work out each order's average unfilled quantity (`remaincount`, ignoring missing values) and its number of executions. Then give me one row with the average of those per-order averages (ignoring missing ones) and the total of the per-order execution counts, without rounding.

readings.A: Executions whose expiry time is exactly equal to either the start or the end bound of the window are included in the per-order groups.
readings.B: Executions whose expiry time is exactly equal to either the start or the end bound of the window are excluded, so only expiry times strictly between the two bounds count.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orderexecutions"."ordersmark" AS "e", AVG("orderexecutions"."remaincount") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "orderexecutions" AS "orderexecutions" WHERE ("orderexecutions"."expirespot" >= '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND "orderexecutions"."expirespot" <= '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533') GROUP BY "orderexecutions"."ordersmark") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", SUM("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orderexecutions"."ordersmark" AS "e", AVG("orderexecutions"."remaincount") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "orderexecutions" AS "orderexecutions" WHERE ("orderexecutions"."expirespot" > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND "orderexecutions"."expirespot" < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533') GROUP BY "orderexecutions"."ordersmark") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", SUM("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the order execution records (`orderexecutions`); no join to any other table
Keep only executions whose expiry time (`expirespot`) lies in the window from '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' to '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533', compared as text, character by character
Group the kept executions by order reference (`ordersmark`). Each group makes one intermediate row
For each group, compute the average unfilled quantity (`remaincount`), ignoring missing values (missing if the group has none), and count the executions in the group
Combine all per-order rows into a single summary row
First output column: the average of the per-order average unfilled quantities, ignoring missing ones (missing if there are none), not rounded
Second output column: the sum of the per-order execution counts (missing if there are none), not rounded

A.requirement: Both window endpoints are included: expirespot >= '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and expirespot <= '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533'

B.requirement: Both window endpoints are excluded: expirespot > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and expirespot < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533'

requests.specific_A: Join feature records (`scanfeatures`) to their sites on `scanfeatures.zoneref` = `sites.zoneregistry`, dropping unmatched records. Keep only records with a `traitcount` of at least 489. Then group by site code (`scanfeatures.zoneref`) and site access status (`sites.entrystat`). For each group, show the site code, the access status, the average `traitcount` (ignoring missing values), the number of records, and that record count as a fraction of the total record count across all groups (no rows if there is no total). Sort by the fraction, highest first with missing last, keep the top 10, and don't round.
requests.specific_B: Join feature records (`scanfeatures`) to their sites on `scanfeatures.zoneref` = `sites.zoneregistry`, dropping unmatched records. Keep only records with a `traitcount` greater than 489. Then group by site code (`scanfeatures.zoneref`) and site access status (`sites.entrystat`). For each group, show the site code, the access status, the average `traitcount` (ignoring missing values), the number of records, and that record count as a fraction of the total record count across all groups (no rows if there is no total). Sort by the fraction, highest first with missing last, keep the top 10, and don't round.
requests.open: Looking only at feature records whose `traitcount` passes the 489 threshold, and matching them to sites via `scanfeatures.zoneref` = `sites.zoneregistry` (unmatched ones left out), break them down by site code (`scanfeatures.zoneref`) and access status (`sites.entrystat`). For each combination, give the site code, the access status, the average `traitcount` (ignoring missing values), the record count, and that count's share of the overall total record count (no rows if there is no total). Sort by share, highest first with missing last, show the top 10, and don't round.

readings.A: Feature records with a count exactly equal to 489 are kept.
readings.B: Only feature records with a count strictly greater than 489 are kept.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scanfeatures"."zoneref" AS "e", "sites"."entrystat" AS "g", AVG("scanfeatures"."traitcount") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "scanfeatures" AS "scanfeatures" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scanfeatures"."zoneref" WHERE "scanfeatures"."traitcount" >= 489 GROUP BY "scanfeatures"."zoneref", "sites"."entrystat"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scanfeatures"."zoneref" AS "e", "sites"."entrystat" AS "g", AVG("scanfeatures"."traitcount") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "scanfeatures" AS "scanfeatures" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scanfeatures"."zoneref" WHERE "scanfeatures"."traitcount" > 489 GROUP BY "scanfeatures"."zoneref", "sites"."entrystat"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the `scanfeatures` records. Keep only those whose `traitcount` passes the threshold of 489.
Inner join to `sites` where `sites.zoneregistry` = `scanfeatures.zoneref`, compared as text. Unmatched records are dropped.
Group by `scanfeatures.zoneref` and `sites.entrystat`. First column: the site code (`scanfeatures.zoneref`).
Second column: the access status (`sites.entrystat`).
Third column: the average `traitcount` in the group, ignoring missing values.
Fourth column: the number of records in the group.
Fifth column: the group's record count divided by the total record count over all groups, unrounded. Rows appear only if that total is not missing.
Sort by that fraction, descending, with missing values last.
Keep the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: traitcount >= 489

B.requirement: traitcount > 489

requests.specific_A: Join each scan to its site (matching `scans.zoneref` to `sites.zoneregistry`, dropping scans with no matching site). Keep only scans whose `chronotag` lies between '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274' and '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797', including both endpoints, comparing the values as plain text. For each site risk evaluation status (`sites.riskeval`), what is the average file size per scan minute (`gbsize` ÷ `spanmin`), ignoring missing values and without rounding? Show the status and that average.
requests.specific_B: Join each scan to its site (matching `scans.zoneref` to `sites.zoneregistry`, dropping scans with no matching site). Keep only scans whose `chronotag` lies between '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274' and '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797', excluding both endpoints, comparing the values as plain text. For each site risk evaluation status (`sites.riskeval`), what is the average file size per scan minute (`gbsize` ÷ `spanmin`), ignoring missing values and without rounding? Show the status and that average.
requests.open: For scans taken between '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274' and '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797' (comparing `chronotag` as plain text), linked to their sites through `scans.zoneref` = `sites.zoneregistry` with unmatched scans left out, what is the average file size per scan minute (`gbsize` ÷ `spanmin`) for each site risk evaluation status (`sites.riskeval`)? Ignore missing values, don't round, and show the status next to its average.

readings.A: The timestamp range includes scans stamped exactly at either endpoint.
readings.B: The timestamp range excludes scans stamped exactly at either endpoint.

sql.A: SELECT "sites"."riskeval" AS "g", AVG((CAST("scans"."gbsize" AS REAL) / "scans"."spanmin")) AS "m1" FROM "scans" AS "scans" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scans"."zoneref" WHERE ("scans"."chronotag" >= '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274' AND "scans"."chronotag" <= '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797') GROUP BY "sites"."riskeval"
sql.B: SELECT "sites"."riskeval" AS "g", AVG((CAST("scans"."gbsize" AS REAL) / "scans"."spanmin")) AS "m1" FROM "scans" AS "scans" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scans"."zoneref" WHERE ("scans"."chronotag" > '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274' AND "scans"."chronotag" < '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797') GROUP BY "sites"."riskeval"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the `scans` records.
Inner join to `sites` where `sites.zoneregistry` = `scans.zoneref`, compared as text. A scan with no matching site is dropped.
Keep only scans whose `scans.chronotag` falls in the range from '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274' to '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797', compared as plain text.
Group by `sites.riskeval`. Each group gives one row.
First column: the risk evaluation status (`sites.riskeval`).
Second column: the average of `scans.gbsize` ÷ `scans.spanmin` in the group. Missing values are ignored, and the result is missing when there are none. No rounding.

A.requirement: Both endpoints count: chronotag >= start and chronotag <= end.

B.requirement: Both endpoints are excluded: chronotag > start and chronotag < end.

  "equiptune" text,
  "equipstatus" text(16),
  "powerlevel" integer(16),
  CONSTRAINT "equipment_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("equipregistry")
);

  "crewregistry" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "crewlabel" text(50),
  "leadregistry" text(50),
  "leadlabel" text(40),
  CONSTRAINT "personnel_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("crewregistry")
);

  "arcregistry" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "vesseltag" text(60),
  "fundflux" text,
  "authpin" text(50),
  "authhalt" text,
  CONSTRAINT "projects_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("arcregistry")
);

  "cureregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "arcref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "zoneref" text(12) NOT NULL,
  "harmassess" text(15),
  "curerank" text(15),
  "structstate" text(15),
  "intervhistory" text,

  CONSTRAINT "scanconservation_zoneref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("zoneref") REFERENCES "sites" ("zoneregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanenvironment" (
  "airregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "zoneref" text(12) NOT NULL,
  "equipref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "ambictemp" real(5,2),

  CONSTRAINT "scanfeatures_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("traitregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanfeatures_equipref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("equipref") REFERENCES "equipment" ("equipregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanfeatures_zoneref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("zoneref") REFERENCES "sites" ("zoneregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanmesh" (
  "facetregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "zoneref" text(12) NOT NULL,
  "equipref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "facetverts" integer(64),
  "facetfaces" integer(64),
  "facetresmm" real(5,2),
  "texdist" text(5),
  "texpix" integer(32),
  "uvmapqual" text(50),
  "geomdeltamm" real(6,3),
  CONSTRAINT "scanmesh_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("facetregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanmesh_equipref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("equipref") REFERENCES "equipment" ("equipregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanmesh_zoneref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("zoneref") REFERENCES "sites" ("zoneregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanpointcloud" (
  "cloudregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "crewref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "arcref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "scanresolmm" real(5,2),
  "pointdense" integer(32),
  "coverpct" real(4,1),
  "totalpts" integer(64),
  "clouddense" integer(32),
  "lappct" real(4,1),
  "noisedb" real(6,3),
  "refpct" real(4,1),
  CONSTRAINT "scanpointcloud_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("cloudregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanpointcloud_arcref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("arcref") REFERENCES "projects" ("arcregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanpointcloud_crewref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("crewref") REFERENCES "personnel" ("crewregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanprocessing" (
  "flowregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "equipref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "zoneref" text(12) NOT NULL,
  "flowsoft" text(25),
  "flowhrs" real(5,2),
  "proccpu" integer(16),
  "memusagegb" real(6,2),
  "procgpu" integer(16),
  "stashloc" text(12),
  "safebak" text(50),
  "datalevel" text,
  "metabench" text(50),
  "coordframe" text(12),
  "elevref" text(16),
  "remaingb" real(7,2),
  "stationlink" text(50),
  "camcal" text,
  "lensdist" text(14),
  "colortune" text(50),
  "flowstage" text(18),
  "fmtver" text(3),
  CONSTRAINT "scanprocessing_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("flowregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanprocessing_equipref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("equipref") REFERENCES "equipment" ("equipregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanprocessing_zoneref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("zoneref") REFERENCES "sites" ("zoneregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanqc" (
  "qualregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "arcref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "crewref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "accucheck" text(22),
  "ctrlstate" text(50),
  "valimeth" text(18),
  "valistate" text,
  "archstat" text(50),
  "pubstat" text(24),
  "copystat" text(50),
  "refmention" text(60),
  "remark" text,
  CONSTRAINT "scanqc_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("qualregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanqc_arcref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("arcref") REFERENCES "projects" ("arcregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanqc_crewref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("crewref") REFERENCES "personnel" ("crewregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanregistration" (
  "logregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "crewref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "arcref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "logaccumm" real(5,3),
  "refmark" text(6),
  "ctrlpts" text(6),
  "logmethod" text(15),
  "transform" text(15),
  "errscale" text(20),
  "errvalmm" real(6,3),
  CONSTRAINT "scanregistration_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("logregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanregistration_arcref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("arcref") REFERENCES "projects" ("arcregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanregistration_crewref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("crewref") REFERENCES "personnel" ("crewregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scans" (
  "questregistry" text(16) NOT NULL,
  "chronotag" text(6),
  "arcref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "crewref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "zoneref" text(12) NOT NULL,
  "scancount" integer(16),
  "climtune" text(22),
  "huecatch" text(50),
  "fmtfile" text(4),
  "gbsize" real(5,2),
  "pressratio" real(4,2),
  "spanmin" real(5,2),
  CONSTRAINT "scans_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("questregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scans_arcref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("arcref") REFERENCES "projects" ("arcregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scans_crewref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("crewref") REFERENCES "personnel" ("crewregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scans_zoneref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("zoneref") REFERENCES "sites" ("zoneregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanspatial" (
  "domainregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "arcref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "crewref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "aream2" real(8,3),
  "volm3" real(9,4),
  "boxx" real(8,2),
  "boxy" real(8,3),
  "boxz" real(9,2),
  "angleaz" integer(24),
  "angletilt" integer(53),
  "groundspan" real(6,3),
  CONSTRAINT "scanspatial_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("domainregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanspatial_arcref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("arcref") REFERENCES "projects" ("arcregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanspatial_crewref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("crewref") REFERENCES "personnel" ("crewregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "sites" (
  "zoneregistry" text(12) NOT NULL,
  "zonelabel" text,
  "digunit" text(50),
  "gridtrace" text(12),
  "geox" real(8,5),
  "geoy" real(8,5),
  "heightm" real(7,1),
  "depthc" real(7,1),
  "phasefactor" text(25),
  "guessdate" text(20),
  "typesite" text(25),
  "presstat" text(25),
  "guardhint" text(50),
  "entrystat" text(50),
  "saferank" text(15),
  "insurstat" text(15),
  "riskeval" text,
  "healtheval" text(12),
  "envhaz" text(50),
  CONSTRAINT "sites_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("zoneregistry")
);
context.documentation:
Equipment.EquipDesign: Full name: 'Equipment Model'. Explanation: Model name or identifier. Data type: VARCHAR(14). Example: 'Model-669'.
Equipment.EquipForm: Full name: 'Equipment Type'. Explanation: Type or category of scanning equipment. Data type: VARCHAR(28). Possible categories: LiDAR, Structured Light, Photogrammetry, Laser.
Equipment.EquipRegistry: Full name: 'Equipment ID'. Explanation: Primary key for equipment. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
Equipment.EquipStatus: Full name: 'Equipment Condition'. Explanation: Overall condition of the equipment. Data type: VARCHAR(16). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor.
Equipment.EquipTune: Full name: 'Calibration Date'. Explanation: Date the equipment was last calibrated. Data type: DATE. Example: '2024-11-01'.
Equipment.PowerLevel: Full name: 'Battery Level (%)'. Explanation: Battery level as an integer percentage. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 62.
Personnel.CrewLabel: Full name: 'Operator Name'. Explanation: Name or label for the operator. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Example: 'Joel Wallace'.
Personnel.CrewRegistry: Full name: 'Operator ID'. Explanation: Primary key for Personnel, representing an operator. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
Personnel.LeadLabel: Full name: 'Supervisor Name'. Explanation: Name of the supervisor. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Example: 'Michael Kaiser'.
Personnel.LeadRegistry: Full name: 'Supervisor ID'. Explanation: Identifies a supervisor. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'SV7658'.
Projects.ArcRegistry: Full name: 'Project ID'. Explanation: Primary key for Projects, a unique project identifier. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
Projects.AuthHalt: Full name: 'Permit Expiry Date'. Explanation: Date on which the permit expires. Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-12-05'.
Projects.AuthPin: Full name: 'Permit Number'. Explanation: Authorization or permit ID. Data type: CHAR(6). Example: 'PMT4719'.
Projects.FundFlux: Full name: 'Funding Source'. Explanation: Source of funds for the project. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Government'.
Projects.VesselTag: Full name: 'Project Name'. Explanation: Label or name for the project. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Example: 'Project Happy'.
ScanConservation.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Associates conservation data with a project. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanConservation.CureRank: Full name: 'Conservation Priority'. Explanation: Priority level for conservation efforts. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Critical, Low, High.
ScanConservation.CureRegistry: Full name: 'Conservation Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for conservation data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 6001.
ScanConservation.HarmAssess: Full name: 'Damage Assessment'. Explanation: Indicates severity of damage. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: None, Moderate, Severe.
ScanConservation.IntervHistory: Full name: 'Intervention History'. Explanation: Past restoration or intervention records. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: None, Major, Minor.
ScanConservation.PriorDocs: Full name: 'Previous Documentation'. Explanation: Level of existing documentation. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: None, Partial, Complete.
ScanConservation.StructState: Full name: 'Structural Stability'. Explanation: Stability level of the structure. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Stable, Moderate, Unstable.
ScanConservation.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Associates conservation data with a site code. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanEnvironment.AirRegistry: Full name: 'Environment Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for environment data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 1001.
ScanEnvironment.AmbicTemp: Full name: 'Ambient Temperature (C)'. Explanation: Air temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 25.3.
ScanEnvironment.EquipRef: Full name: 'Equipment Reference'. Explanation: Identifies which equipment these environment data refer to. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
ScanEnvironment.GeoSignal: Full name: 'GPS Signal Quality'. Explanation: Quality rating for GPS reception. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: None, Poor, Good, Excellent.
ScanEnvironment.HumePct: Full name: 'Relative Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 60.4.
ScanEnvironment.IllumeLux: Full name: 'Light Conditions (lux)'. Explanation: Measured illumination in lux. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 86054.
ScanEnvironment.ImgCount: Full name: 'Number of Images'. Explanation: How many images were taken for photogrammetry. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 248.
ScanEnvironment.LinkStatus: Full name: 'Network Status'. Explanation: Status of network connectivity. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Possible categories: Disconnected, Connected.
ScanEnvironment.PhotoMap: Full name: 'Photogrammetry Overlap'. Explanation: Percentage overlap for photogrammetry images. Data type: CHAR(4). Possible categories: 80%, 60%, 90%.
ScanEnvironment.TrackStatus: Full name: 'RTK Status'. Explanation: Real-Time Kinematic correction state. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Possible categories: None, Fixed.
ScanEnvironment.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Links environment conditions to a specific site code. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanFeatures.ArtiCount: Full name: 'Artifact Count'. Explanation: Number of artifacts recognized. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 71.
ScanFeatures.EquipRef: Full name: 'Equipment Reference'. Explanation: Equipment ID used to detect these features. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
ScanFeatures.HueStudy: Full name: 'Color Analysis'. Explanation: Status of color analysis (done or pending). Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Partial, Completed, Not Required.
ScanFeatures.MatKind: Full name: 'Material Type'. Explanation: Primary composition or material. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Organic, Metal, Mixed, Ceramic, Stone.
ScanFeatures.PatternNote: Full name: 'Pattern Recognition'. Explanation: Notes regarding detected patterns. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Not Required, None, Partial.
ScanFeatures.StructKind: Full name: 'Structure Type'. Explanation: Type of structural element. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Artifact, Complex, Wall, Foundation.
ScanFeatures.TextureStudy: Full name: 'Texture Analysis'. Explanation: Status of texture analysis. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Partial, Completed, Not Required.
ScanFeatures.TraitCount: Full name: 'Number of Detected Features'. Explanation: How many features were identified. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 516.
ScanFeatures.TraitExtract: Full name: 'Feature Extraction Method'. Explanation: Method used to extract features (manual or automated). Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Manual, Semi-automatic, Automatic.
ScanFeatures.TraitRegistry: Full name: 'Feature Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for feature data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 5001.
ScanFeatures.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Site code tied to these features. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanMesh.EquipRef: Full name: 'Equipment Reference'. Explanation: Identifies which equipment was used to generate the mesh. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
ScanMesh.FacetFaces: Full name: 'Mesh Faces'. Explanation: Count of triangular or polygonal faces. Data type: BIGINT. Example: 5997318.
ScanMesh.FacetRegistry: Full name: 'Mesh Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for mesh data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 3001.
ScanMesh.FacetResMm: Full name: 'Mesh Resolution (mm)'. Explanation: Mesh vertex spacing in mm. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 3.2.
ScanMesh.FacetVerts: Full name: 'Mesh Vertices'. Explanation: Count of mesh vertices. Data type: BIGINT. Example: 7234721.
ScanMesh.GeomDeltaMm: Full name: 'Geometric Accuracy (mm)'. Explanation: Estimated geometric deviation in millimeters. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: 2.74.
ScanMesh.TexDist: Full name: 'Texture Resolution Setting'. Explanation: Preset texture resolution. Data type: VARCHAR(5). Possible categories: 2K, 1K, 4K.
ScanMesh.TexPix: Full name: 'Texture Size (px)'. Explanation: Texture image dimension in pixels. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 2048.
ScanMesh.UVMapQual: Full name: 'UV Mapping Quality'. Explanation: Quality of the UV mapping process. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Possible categories: Medium, High, Low.
ScanMesh.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Associates mesh data with a site code. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanPointCloud.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Project ID associated with this point cloud. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanPointCloud.CloudDense: Full name: 'Point-Cloud Density Code'. Explanation: A numeric code classifying point density. Data type: INTEGER. Possible categories: 9449, 431, 7553, 1746.
ScanPointCloud.CloudRegistry: Full name: 'Point Cloud Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for point cloud data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 2001.
ScanPointCloud.CoverPct: Full name: 'Coverage (%)'. Explanation: Surface coverage percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(4,1). Example: 91.2.
ScanPointCloud.CrewRef: Full name: 'Operator Reference'. Explanation: Which operator is linked to this point cloud. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
ScanPointCloud.LapPct: Full name: 'Overlap (%)'. Explanation: Overlap percentage among multiple scans. Data type: NUMERIC(4,1). Example: 31.3.
ScanPointCloud.NoiseDb: Full name: 'Noise Level (dB)'. Explanation: Measured noise in decibels. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: 1.318.
ScanPointCloud.PointDense: Full name: 'Point Density (points/m²)'. Explanation: Density of points per square meter. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 42812.
ScanPointCloud.RefPct: Full name: 'Surface Reflectivity (%)'. Explanation: Reflectivity percentage of scanned surfaces. Data type: NUMERIC(4,1). Example: 65.4.
ScanPointCloud.ScanResolMm: Full name: 'Scan Resolution (mm)'. Explanation: Resolution of points in millimeters. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 2.4.
ScanPointCloud.TotalPts: Full name: 'Total Points'. Explanation: Overall number of points in the cloud. Data type: BIGINT. Example: 46562436.
ScanProcessing.CamCal: Full name: 'Camera Calibration Status'. Explanation: Whether camera calibration is completed or pending. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Required'.
ScanProcessing.ColorTune: Full name: 'Color Balance Status'. Explanation: Indicates color adjustment requirement. Data type: CHAR(10). Possible categories: Required, Adjusted.
ScanProcessing.CoordFrame: Full name: 'Coordinate System'. Explanation: Defines spatial reference frame. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Possible categories: Local, WGS84, Custom.
ScanProcessing.DataLevel: Full name: 'Data Access Level'. Explanation: Access restrictions or sharing level. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Confidential, Public, Restricted.
ScanProcessing.ElevRef: Full name: 'Elevation Reference'. Explanation: Reference for altitude or elevation. Data type: VARCHAR(16). Possible categories: Arbitrary, Sea Level, Local.
ScanProcessing.EquipRef: Full name: 'Equipment Reference'. Explanation: Equipment ID used for processing. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
ScanProcessing.FlowHrs: Full name: 'Processing Time (hours)'. Explanation: Time spent on processing. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 21.9.
ScanProcessing.FlowRegistry: Full name: 'Processing Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for processing workflow. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 8001.
ScanProcessing.FlowSoft: Full name: 'Processing Software'. Explanation: Name of the software used. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: RealityCapture, CloudCompare, Agisoft.
ScanProcessing.FlowStage: Full name: 'Processing Stage'. Explanation: Current stage of the processing workflow. Data type: VARCHAR(18). Possible categories: Aligned, Meshed, Final.
ScanProcessing.FmtVer: Full name: 'Export Format Version'. Explanation: Version tag for exported files. Data type: CHAR(3). Possible categories: 2.3, 2.7, 4.0, 1.1.
ScanProcessing.LensDist: Full name: 'Lens Distortion Status'. Explanation: Whether lens distortion is corrected or unknown. Data type: VARCHAR(14). Possible categories: Corrected, Unknown.
ScanProcessing.MemUsageGb: Full name: 'Memory Usage (GB)'. Explanation: RAM usage during processing. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: 70.3.
ScanProcessing.MetaBench: Full name: 'Metadata Standard'. Explanation: Which metadata framework is applied. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Possible categories: Dublin Core, CIDOC CRM, Custom.
ScanProcessing.ProcCPU: Full name: 'CPU Usage (%)'. Explanation: CPU usage as an integer percentage. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 81.
ScanProcessing.ProcGPU: Full name: 'GPU Usage (%)'. Explanation: GPU usage as an integer percentage. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 56.
ScanProcessing.RemainGb: Full name: 'Remaining Storage (GB)'. Explanation: Remaining disk or cloud space. Data type: NUMERIC(7,2). Example: 983.5.
ScanProcessing.SafeBak: Full name: 'Backup Status'. Explanation: Indicates progress of data backup. Data type: CHAR(8). Possible categories: In Progress, Completed, Pending.
ScanProcessing.StashLoc: Full name: 'Storage Location'. Explanation: Where processed data is stored. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Possible categories: Local, Network, Cloud.
ScanProcessing.StationLink: Full name: 'Total Station Integration'. Explanation: Indicates if total station integration is used. Data type: CHAR(6). Example: 'Yes'.
ScanProcessing.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Site code for which processing applies. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanQC.AccuCheck: Full name: 'Accuracy Assessment'. Explanation: Indicates if accuracy check was done. Data type: VARCHAR(22). Possible categories: Pending, Completed, Not Required.
ScanQC.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Points to a project for QC. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanQC.ArchStat: Full name: 'Archival Status'. Explanation: Indicates if data is archived. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Possible categories: Verified, Pending.
ScanQC.CopyStat: Full name: 'Copyright Status'. Explanation: Copyright or licensing restriction. Data type: CHAR(10). Possible categories: Reserved, Restricted, Open Access.
ScanQC.CrewRef: Full name: 'Operator Reference'. Explanation: Identifies the operator associated with QC. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
ScanQC.CtrlState: Full name: 'Quality Control Status'. Explanation: State of QC checks. Data type: CHAR(10). Possible categories: Failed, Pending.
ScanQC.PubStat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether data is published, drafted, etc. Data type: VARCHAR(24). Possible categories: Draft, Submitted.
ScanQC.QualRegistry: Full name: 'QC Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for quality control records. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 9001.
ScanQC.RefMention: Full name: 'Data Citation'. Explanation: Reference or citation code for the data. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: Citation-8447, Citation-6197, Citation-8090, Citation-2238.
ScanQC.Remark: Full name: 'Additional Notes'. Explanation: Any free-text remarks or comments. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Sell shoulder understand serious degree particular game.'
ScanQC.ValiMeth: Full name: 'Validation Method'. Explanation: How the data was validated (automated or manual). Data type: VARCHAR(18). Possible categories: Automated, Visual.
ScanQC.ValiState: Full name: 'Validation Status'. Explanation: Final status of validation. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Rejected, Approved.
ScanRegistration.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Project ID linked to registration data. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanRegistration.CrewRef: Full name: 'Operator Reference'. Explanation: Operator ID who performed registration. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
ScanRegistration.CtrlPts: Full name: 'Control Points'. Explanation: Numeric codes for control points. Data type: VARCHAR(6). Possible categories: 73, 99, 6, 84.
ScanRegistration.ErrScale: Full name: 'Error Metrics'. Explanation: Type of error measurement. Data type: VARCHAR(20). Possible categories: Cloud-to-Mesh, Cloud-to-Cloud, RMSE.
ScanRegistration.ErrValMm: Full name: 'Error Value (mm)'. Explanation: Measured error in millimeters. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: 6.962.
ScanRegistration.LogAccuMm: Full name: 'Registration Accuracy (mm)'. Explanation: Accuracy of the registration in mm. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: 0.84.
ScanRegistration.LogMethod: Full name: 'Registration Method'. Explanation: Method for aligning scans. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Target-based, Hybrid, Automatic.
ScanRegistration.LogRegistry: Full name: 'Registration Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for registration logs. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 7001.
ScanRegistration.RefMark: Full name: 'Reference Markers'. Explanation: Numeric codes for registration targets. Data type: VARCHAR(6). Possible categories: 40, 31, 25, 21.
ScanRegistration.TransForm: Full name: 'Transformation Matrix'. Explanation: Identifier for the transform matrix used. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Matrix-47, Matrix-113, Matrix-543.
ScanSpatial.AngleAz: Full name: 'Orientation (degrees)'. Explanation: Azimuth or rotation angle around vertical axis. Data type: REAL. Example: 342.4.
ScanSpatial.AngleTilt: Full name: 'Tilt Angle (degrees)'. Explanation: Inclination angle from horizontal. Data type: DOUBLE PRECISION. Example: 23.9.
ScanSpatial.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Project ID linking spatial data. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanSpatial.AreaM2: Full name: 'Surface Area (m²)'. Explanation: Calculated area in square meters. Data type: NUMERIC(8,3). Example: 78.01.
ScanSpatial.BoxX: Full name: 'Bounding Box X (m)'. Explanation: Size of bounding box along X-axis, in meters. Data type: NUMERIC(8,2). Example: 40.12.
ScanSpatial.BoxY: Full name: 'Bounding Box Y (m)'. Explanation: Size of bounding box along Y-axis, in meters. Data type: NUMERIC(8,3). Example: 1.06.
ScanSpatial.BoxZ: Full name: 'Bounding Box Z (m)'. Explanation: Size of bounding box along Z-axis, in meters. Data type: NUMERIC(9,2). Example: 16.41.
ScanSpatial.CrewRef: Full name: 'Operator Reference'. Explanation: Operator ID for these spatial records. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
ScanSpatial.DomainRegistry: Full name: 'Spatial Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for spatial data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 4001.
ScanSpatial.GroundSpan: Full name: 'Ground Sampling Distance (mm)'. Explanation: Effective resolution on the ground, in mm. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: 4.13.
ScanSpatial.VolM3: Full name: 'Volume (m³)'. Explanation: Computed volume in cubic meters. Data type: NUMERIC(9,4). Example: 76.7.
Scans.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Links a scan to a specific project. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
Scans.ChronoTag: Full name: 'Scan Timestamp'. Explanation: Timestamp representing the scan date/time. Data type: TIMESTAMP. If stored as a numeric like 44302.55648, it may be an Excel serial date/time (days since 1900-01-00). Example: 44302.55648.
Scans.ClimTune: Full name: 'Weather Conditions'. Explanation: Indicates the weather during scanning. Data type: VARCHAR(22). Possible categories: Windy, Rainy, Cloudy, Clear.
Scans.CrewRef: Full name: 'Operator Reference'. Explanation: Records which operator performed the scan. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
Scans.FmtFile: Full name: 'File Format'. Explanation: Format in which scan data is saved. Data type: CHAR(4). Possible categories: PTS, PLY, OBJ, LAS, E57.
Scans.GBSize: Full name: 'File Size (GB)'. Explanation: Size of the scan file in gigabytes. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 24.71.
Scans.HueCatch: Full name: 'Color Capture'. Explanation: Mode of color recording. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Possible categories: RGB, Grayscale, None.
Scans.PressRatio: Full name: 'Compression Ratio'. Explanation: Compression level applied to scan data. Data type: NUMERIC(4,2). Example: 3.22.
Scans.QuestRegistry: Full name: 'Scan ID'. Explanation: Primary key identifying a particular scan. Data type: VARCHAR(16). Example: 'ASD409481'.
Scans.ScanCount: Full name: 'Number of Scans'. Explanation: Numeric count of scans in a set. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 5.
Scans.SpanMin: Full name: 'Scan Duration (min)'. Explanation: Duration of the scanning process, in minutes. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 63.
Scans.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Associates the scan with a site code. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
Sites.DepthC: Full name: 'Depth (cm)'. Explanation: Depth measurement in centimeters. Data type: NUMERIC(7,1). Example: 329.9.
Sites.DigUnit: Full name: 'Excavation Unit'. Explanation: Designation of a specific trench or unit. Data type: VARCHAR(8). Example: 'Unit-C9'.
Sites.EntryStat: Full name: 'Site Access Status'. Explanation: Access restrictions or availability of the site. Data type: VARCHAR(8). Possible categories: Closed, Restricted, Open.
Sites.EnvHaz: Full name: 'Environmental Risk'. Explanation: Rating of environmental hazards. Data type: CHAR(6). Possible categories: Low, Medium, High.

requests.specific_A: Using only constructor results whose race points (`constructorResults.points`) are at least 1.0, matched to their races, find for each race (race ID and race name) the average constructor points and the number of such results. Then, for each race name, take the average of these per-race averages across all races sharing that name. List the race ID, race name, per-race average points, result count, and the ratio of the race's average to its race-name average. Show the 10 races with the highest ratio (missing ratios last), without rounding.
requests.specific_B: Using only constructor results whose race points (`constructorResults.points`) are more than 1.0, matched to their races, find for each race (race ID and race name) the average constructor points and the number of such results. Then, for each race name, take the average of these per-race averages across all races sharing that name. List the race ID, race name, per-race average points, result count, and the ratio of the race's average to its race-name average. Show the 10 races with the highest ratio (missing ratios last), without rounding.
requests.open: First filter the constructor results: split them by their race points (`constructorResults.points`) using 1.0 points as the dividing line, and keep only those on the higher side. Match the kept results to their races, then find for each race (race ID and race name) the average constructor points and the number of such results. Then, for each race name, take the average of these per-race averages across all races sharing that name. List the race ID, race name, per-race average points, result count, and the ratio of the race's average to its race-name average. Show the 10 races with the highest ratio (missing ratios last), without rounding.

readings.A: Only constructor results with points at least 1.0 are used, including results of exactly 1.0.
readings.B: Only constructor results with points strictly greater than 1.0 are used, leaving out results of exactly 1.0.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "constructorResults"."raceId" AS "e", "races"."name" AS "g", AVG("constructorResults"."points") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "constructorResults" AS "constructorResults" INNER JOIN "races" AS "races" ON "races"."raceId" = "constructorResults"."raceId" WHERE "constructorResults"."points" >= 1.0 GROUP BY "constructorResults"."raceId", "races"."name"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g" ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "constructorResults"."raceId" AS "e", "races"."name" AS "g", AVG("constructorResults"."points") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "constructorResults" AS "constructorResults" INNER JOIN "races" AS "races" ON "races"."raceId" = "constructorResults"."raceId" WHERE "constructorResults"."points" > 1.0 GROUP BY "constructorResults"."raceId", "races"."name"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g" ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from `constructorResults` records. Filter on `constructorResults.points` with 1.0 as the threshold, keeping the high side.

Inner-join `constructorResults` to `races` on raceId, dropping unmatched records. Group the kept records by race ID and race name (`races.name`). Then compute a per-race-name average of the per-race averages and attach it to each race by exact name match.
The race ID (`constructorResults.raceId`).
The race name (`races.name`).
The per-race average of `constructorResults.points` over the kept results. Missing values are ignored; the result is missing if there are none.
The number of kept results in the race.
The ratio of the race's average points to the average of per-race averages for its race name.
Order by the ratio, highest first, with missing ratios last.
Keep the first 10 rows. No rounding.

A.requirement: Constructor results with exactly 1.0 points are included (points >= 1.0).

B.requirement: Constructor results with exactly 1.0 points are excluded (points > 1.0).

context.schema:
CREATE TABLE "circuits" (
"circuitId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "circuitRef" TEXT,
  "name" TEXT,
  "location" TEXT,
  "country" TEXT,
  "lat" REAL,
  "lng" REAL,
  "alt" TEXT,
  "url" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "races" (
"raceId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "year" INTEGER,
  "round" INTEGER,
  "circuitId" INTEGER,
  "name" TEXT,
  "date" TEXT,
  "time" TEXT,
  "url" TEXT,
  FOREIGN KEY ("circuitId") REFERENCES "circuits"("circuitId")
);
CREATE TABLE "drivers" (
"driverId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "driverRef" TEXT,
  "number" TEXT,
  "code" TEXT,
  "forename" TEXT,
  "surname" TEXT,
  "dob" TEXT,
  "nationality" TEXT,
  "url" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "status" (
"statusId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "status" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "seasons" (
"year" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "url" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "constructors" (
	"constructorId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "constructorRef" TEXT,
  "name" TEXT,
  "nationality" TEXT,
  "url" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "constructorStandings" (
	"constructorStandingsId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "raceId" INTEGER,
  "constructorId" INTEGER,
  "points" REAL,
  "position" INTEGER,
  "positionText" TEXT,
  "wins" INTEGER,
  FOREIGN KEY("constructorId") REFERENCES "constructors"("constructorId"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId")
);
CREATE TABLE "results" (
"resultId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "raceId" INTEGER,
  "driverId" INTEGER,
  "constructorId" INTEGER,
  "number" INTEGER,
  "grid" INTEGER,
  "position" TEXT,
  "positionText" TEXT,
  "positionOrder" INTEGER,
  "points" REAL,
  "laps" TEXT,
  "time" TEXT,
  "milliseconds" TEXT,
  "fastestLap" TEXT,
  "rank" TEXT,
  "fastestLapTime" TEXT,
  "fastestLapSpeed" TEXT,
  "statusId" INTEGER,
  FOREIGN KEY("constructorId") REFERENCES "constructors"("constructorId"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("driverId") REFERENCES "drivers"("driverId")
);
CREATE TABLE "driverStandings" (
"driverStandingsId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "raceId" INTEGER,
  "driverId" INTEGER,
  "points" REAL,
  "position" INTEGER,
  "positionText" TEXT,
  "wins" INTEGER,
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("driverId") REFERENCES "drivers"("driverId")
);
CREATE TABLE "constructorResults" (
"constructorResultsId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "raceId" INTEGER,
  "constructorId" INTEGER,
  "points" REAL,
  "status" TEXT,
  FOREIGN KEY("constructorId") REFERENCES "constructors"("constructorId"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId")
);
CREATE TABLE "qualifying" (
"qualifyId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "raceId" INTEGER,
  "driverId" INTEGER,
  "constructorId" INTEGER,
  "number" INTEGER,
  "position" INTEGER,
  "q1" TEXT,
  "q2" TEXT,
  "q3" TEXT,
  FOREIGN KEY("constructorId") REFERENCES "constructors"("constructorId"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("driverId") REFERENCES "drivers"("driverId")
);
CREATE TABLE "pitStops" (
"raceId" INTEGER,
  "driverId" INTEGER,
  "stop" INTEGER,
  "lap" INTEGER,
  "time" TEXT,
  "duration" TEXT,
  "milliseconds" INTEGER,
  PRIMARY KEY ("raceId", "driverId", "stop"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("driverId") REFERENCES "drivers"("driverId")
);
CREATE TABLE "lapTimes" (
"raceId" INTEGER,
  "driverId" INTEGER,
  "lap" INTEGER,
  "position" INTEGER,
  "time" TEXT,
  "milliseconds" INTEGER,
  PRIMARY KEY("raceId", "driverId", "lap"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("driverId") REFERENCES "drivers"("driverId")
);

For each status, show the status, the total number of scans (sum of `scancount`) and the average file size per scan minute (`gbsize` ÷ `spanmin`), ignoring missing values. Also show how far each status's average ratio is from the mean of all the status-level average ratios (status average minus that mean), and return nothing if that mean can't be computed. Don't round.

requests.specific_A: Looking only at races dated from 1978-03-04 through 2003-03-09, with both of those dates included (comparing the `date` text directly), and only at races whose circuit appears in the circuits table: count the races held at each circuit, grouped by circuit ID and the circuit's country. Then, for each country, average these per-circuit race counts. For each circuit, give its circuit ID, its country, its race count, and its race count divided by its country's average (unrounded). Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest, with missing values last, and show the top 10.
requests.specific_B: Looking only at races dated strictly after 1978-03-04 and strictly before 2003-03-09, with both of those dates excluded (comparing the `date` text directly), and only at races whose circuit appears in the circuits table: count the races held at each circuit, grouped by circuit ID and the circuit's country. Then, for each country, average these per-circuit race counts. For each circuit, give its circuit ID, its country, its race count, and its race count divided by its country's average (unrounded). Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest, with missing values last, and show the top 10.
requests.open: For races held between 1978-03-04 and 2003-03-09 (comparing the `date` text directly), counting only races whose circuit is listed in the circuits table: how many races did each circuit host, grouped by circuit ID and country? For each circuit, show its circuit ID, its country, its race count, and that count divided by the average race count of circuits in the same country (unrounded). Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest, with missing values last, and give the top 10.

readings.A: Count races at each circuit using a date window that includes both end dates, 1978-03-04 and 2003-03-09. Then compare each circuit's count with its country's average count per circuit.
readings.B: Count races at each circuit using a date window that excludes both end dates, 1978-03-04 and 2003-03-09. Then compare each circuit's count with its country's average count per circuit.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "races"."circuitId" AS "e", "circuits"."country" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "races" AS "races" INNER JOIN "circuits" AS "circuits" ON "circuits"."circuitId" = "races"."circuitId" WHERE ("races"."date" >= '1978-03-04' AND "races"."date" <= '2003-03-09') GROUP BY "races"."circuitId", "circuits"."country"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g" ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "races"."circuitId" AS "e", "circuits"."country" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "races" AS "races" INNER JOIN "circuits" AS "circuits" ON "circuits"."circuitId" = "races"."circuitId" WHERE ("races"."date" > '1978-03-04' AND "races"."date" < '2003-03-09') GROUP BY "races"."circuitId", "circuits"."country"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g" ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from race records and keep only races whose `date`, compared as text, falls in the range from '1978-03-04' to '2003-03-09' (how the range ends are treated is the choice)
Match each race to its circuit on circuits.circuitId = races.circuitId (inner join, so a race with no matching circuit is dropped)
Circuit ID (races.circuitId); results are grouped by circuit ID together with circuit country
Circuit country (circuits.country)
Number of qualifying races at that circuit (count of records per circuitId+country group)

That circuit's race count divided by the average of the per-circuit race counts across all circuits in the same country (country averages are computed from the per-circuit counts and matched back to circuits by country as text). The ratio is not rounded
Sort by the ratio from highest to lowest, with missing values last
Keep only the first 10 rows

A.requirement: Races dated exactly 1978-03-04 or exactly 2003-03-09 are included (>= and <=)

B.requirement: Races dated exactly 1978-03-04 or exactly 2003-03-09 are excluded (> and <)

context.schema:
CREATE TABLE "circuits" (
"circuitId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "circuitRef" TEXT,
  "name" TEXT,
  "location" TEXT,
  "country" TEXT,
  "lat" REAL,
  "lng" REAL,
  "alt" TEXT,
  "url" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "races" (
"raceId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "year" INTEGER,
  "round" INTEGER,
  "circuitId" INTEGER,
  "name" TEXT,
  "date" TEXT,
  "time" TEXT,
  "url" TEXT,
  FOREIGN KEY ("circuitId") REFERENCES "circuits"("circuitId")
);
CREATE TABLE "drivers" (
"driverId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "driverRef" TEXT,
  "number" TEXT,
  "code" TEXT,
  "forename" TEXT,
  "surname" TEXT,
  "dob" TEXT,
  "nationality" TEXT,
  "url" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "status" (
"statusId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "status" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "seasons" (
"year" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "url" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "constructors" (
	"constructorId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "constructorRef" TEXT,
  "name" TEXT,
  "nationality" TEXT,
  "url" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE "constructorStandings" (
	"constructorStandingsId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "raceId" INTEGER,
  "constructorId" INTEGER,
  "points" REAL,
  "position" INTEGER,
  "positionText" TEXT,
  "wins" INTEGER,
  FOREIGN KEY("constructorId") REFERENCES "constructors"("constructorId"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId")
);
CREATE TABLE "results" (
"resultId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "raceId" INTEGER,
  "driverId" INTEGER,
  "constructorId" INTEGER,
  "number" INTEGER,
  "grid" INTEGER,
  "position" TEXT,
  "positionText" TEXT,
  "positionOrder" INTEGER,
  "points" REAL,
  "laps" TEXT,
  "time" TEXT,
  "milliseconds" TEXT,
  "fastestLap" TEXT,
  "rank" TEXT,
  "fastestLapTime" TEXT,
  "fastestLapSpeed" TEXT,
  "statusId" INTEGER,
  FOREIGN KEY("constructorId") REFERENCES "constructors"("constructorId"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("driverId") REFERENCES "drivers"("driverId")
);
CREATE TABLE "driverStandings" (
"driverStandingsId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "raceId" INTEGER,
  "driverId" INTEGER,
  "points" REAL,
  "position" INTEGER,
  "positionText" TEXT,
  "wins" INTEGER,
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("driverId") REFERENCES "drivers"("driverId")
);
CREATE TABLE "constructorResults" (
"constructorResultsId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "raceId" INTEGER,
  "constructorId" INTEGER,
  "points" REAL,
  "status" TEXT,
  FOREIGN KEY("constructorId") REFERENCES "constructors"("constructorId"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId")
);
CREATE TABLE "qualifying" (
"qualifyId" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  "raceId" INTEGER,
  "driverId" INTEGER,
  "constructorId" INTEGER,
  "number" INTEGER,
  "position" INTEGER,
  "q1" TEXT,
  "q2" TEXT,
  "q3" TEXT,
  FOREIGN KEY("constructorId") REFERENCES "constructors"("constructorId"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("driverId") REFERENCES "drivers"("driverId")
);
CREATE TABLE "pitStops" (
"raceId" INTEGER,
  "driverId" INTEGER,
  "stop" INTEGER,
  "lap" INTEGER,
  "time" TEXT,
  "duration" TEXT,
  "milliseconds" INTEGER,
  PRIMARY KEY ("raceId", "driverId", "stop"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("driverId") REFERENCES "drivers"("driverId")
);
CREATE TABLE "lapTimes" (
"raceId" INTEGER,
  "driverId" INTEGER,
  "lap" INTEGER,
  "position" INTEGER,
  "time" TEXT,
  "milliseconds" INTEGER,
  PRIMARY KEY("raceId", "driverId", "lap"),
  FOREIGN KEY("raceId") REFERENCES "races"("raceId"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("driverId") REFERENCES "drivers"("driverId")
);

requests.specific_A: Joining each track to its media type (dropping tracks with no matching media type) and keeping only tracks whose file size (`Track.Bytes`) is at least 10323804 bytes, for each media type name (`MediaType.Name`) give the media type name, the average list price per track (`Track.UnitPrice`), and the average of file size divided by track length (`Track.Bytes` ÷ `Track.Milliseconds`). Both averages should ignore missing values and be missing when there are none. Leave all values unrounded.
requests.specific_B: Joining each track to its media type (dropping tracks with no matching media type) and keeping only tracks whose file size (`Track.Bytes`) is more than 10323804 bytes, for each media type name (`MediaType.Name`) give the media type name, the average list price per track (`Track.UnitPrice`), and the average of file size divided by track length (`Track.Bytes` ÷ `Track.Milliseconds`). Both averages should ignore missing values and be missing when there are none. Leave all values unrounded.
requests.open: Joining each track to its media type (dropping tracks with no matching media type) and using 10323804 bytes as the file-size threshold (`Track.Bytes`) to keep only the large files, for each media type name (`MediaType.Name`) give the media type name, the average list price per track (`Track.UnitPrice`), and the average of file size divided by track length (`Track.Bytes` ÷ `Track.Milliseconds`). Both averages should ignore missing values and be missing when there are none. Leave all values unrounded.

readings.A: Tracks whose file size equals 10323804 bytes are kept along with larger ones.
readings.B: Only tracks whose file size is strictly greater than 10323804 bytes are kept.

sql.A: SELECT "MediaType"."Name" AS "g", AVG("Track"."UnitPrice") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("Track"."Bytes" AS REAL) / "Track"."Milliseconds")) AS "m2" FROM "Track" AS "Track" INNER JOIN "MediaType" AS "MediaType" ON "MediaType"."MediaTypeId" = "Track"."MediaTypeId" WHERE "Track"."Bytes" >= 10323804 GROUP BY "MediaType"."Name"
sql.B: SELECT "MediaType"."Name" AS "g", AVG("Track"."UnitPrice") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("Track"."Bytes" AS REAL) / "Track"."Milliseconds")) AS "m2" FROM "Track" AS "Track" INNER JOIN "MediaType" AS "MediaType" ON "MediaType"."MediaTypeId" = "Track"."MediaTypeId" WHERE "Track"."Bytes" > 10323804 GROUP BY "MediaType"."Name"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from each `Track` record.
Inner-join each track to the `MediaType` record with the same `MediaTypeId`, giving one combined record per match. Drop tracks that have no matching media type.
Keep tracks by comparing file size (`Track.Bytes`) with the threshold 10323804. Whether a value equal to the threshold is kept is the open choice.
Group the kept records by media type name (`MediaType.Name`). Each group gives one result row.
Column 1: the media type name (`MediaType.Name`).
Column 2: the average list price per track (`Track.UnitPrice`) in the group. Ignore missing values; the result is missing if there are none. Do not round.
Column 3: the average of file size divided by track length (`Track.Bytes` ÷ `Track.Milliseconds`) in the group. Ignore missing values; the result is missing if there are none. Do not round.

A.requirement: Keep tracks with `Track.Bytes` >= 10323804, so a value equal to the threshold counts.

B.requirement: Keep tracks with `Track.Bytes` > 10323804, so only values strictly above the threshold count.

requests.specific_A: Matching each telescope to its observatory by `observstation` (dropping telescopes with no matching observatory) and keeping only telescopes whose detector temperature (`detecttempk`) is at least 152.1, show for each weather profile (`weathprofile`) the average bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`, ignoring missing values), the number of telescopes, and how far that average sits from the mean of the per-weather-profile averages (the profile's average minus that mean, which ignores missing averages). Return nothing if that mean is missing, and leave all values unrounded.
requests.specific_B: Matching each telescope to its observatory by `observstation` (dropping telescopes with no matching observatory) and keeping only telescopes whose detector temperature (`detecttempk`) is strictly greater than 152.1, show for each weather profile (`weathprofile`) the average bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`, ignoring missing values), the number of telescopes, and how far that average sits from the mean of the per-weather-profile averages (the profile's average minus that mean, which ignores missing averages). Return nothing if that mean is missing, and leave all values unrounded.
requests.open: Matching each telescope to its observatory by `observstation` (dropping telescopes with no matching observatory) and keeping only telescopes on the high side of a 152.1 cutoff for detector temperature (`detecttempk`), show for each weather profile (`weathprofile`) the average bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`, ignoring missing values), the number of telescopes, and how far that average sits from the mean of the per-weather-profile averages (the profile's average minus that mean, which ignores missing averages). Return nothing if that mean is missing, and leave all values unrounded.

readings.A: Telescopes whose detector temperature is exactly 152.1 K are included, along with those above it.
readings.B: Only telescopes whose detector temperature is strictly greater than 152.1 K are included.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "observatories"."weathprofile" AS "g", AVG("telescopes"."bandusagepct") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" INNER JOIN "observatories" AS "observatories" ON "observatories"."observstation" = "telescopes"."observstation" WHERE "telescopes"."detecttempk" >= 152.1 GROUP BY "observatories"."weathprofile"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "observatories"."weathprofile" AS "g", AVG("telescopes"."bandusagepct") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" INNER JOIN "observatories" AS "observatories" ON "observatories"."observstation" = "telescopes"."observstation" WHERE "telescopes"."detecttempk" > 152.1 GROUP BY "observatories"."weathprofile"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from telescopes and keep only records on the high side of the detector temperature (`telescopes.detecttempk`) threshold of 152.1. How the boundary value is treated is the choice.
Inner-join each telescope to the observatories record with the same `observstation` (exact text match). Telescopes with no matching observatory are dropped.
Group by weather profile (`observatories.weathprofile`). Each weather profile gives one row.
The weather profile.
The average `bandusagepct` in the group (missing values ignored; missing if there are none).
The number of records in the group.
The group's average bandwidth usage minus the average of all the per-group averages (missing values ignored). Rows are returned only when that overall average is not missing. Nothing is rounded.

A.requirement: A `detecttempk` exactly equal to 152.1 is kept (>= 152.1).

B.requirement: Only a `detecttempk` strictly greater than 152.1 is kept (> 152.1).

ObservationalConditions.ObsDate: Full name: 'Observation Date'. Explanation: Local date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD). Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-08-01'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsDurHrs: Full name: 'Observation Duration (hours)'. Explanation: How long the observation lasted in hours. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '2.50'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsTime: Full name: 'Observation Time'. Explanation: Local time of the observation in HH:MM:SS. Data type: TIME. Example: '13:45:59'.
ObservationalConditions.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-PQR-9876'.
