SignalDynamics.SigCoherence: Full name: 'Signal Coherence'. Explanation: How coherent the signal remains over its duration. Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighCoherence'.
SignalDynamics.SigDisp: Full name: 'Signal Dispersion'. Explanation: The degree to which the signal is dispersed (time/frequency smearing). Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'SignificantDisp'.
SignalDynamics.SigEvolve: Full name: 'Signal Evolution'. Explanation: Indicates if the signal changes/evolves during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Dynamic, Static, Unknown.
SignalDynamics.SigIntegrity: Full name: 'Signal Integrity'. Explanation: Rating of how intact or uncorrupted the signal is. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighIntegrity'.
SignalDynamics.SigRecurr: Full name: 'Signal Recurrence'. Explanation: Whether the signal recurs over time. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: None, Regular, Sporadic.
SignalDynamics.SigScint: Full name: 'Signal Scintillation'. Explanation: Fluctuation in signal amplitude due to propagation effects. Data type: VARCHAR(45). If no fixed categories, example: 'MildScintillation'.

Signals.RfiStat: Full name: 'RFI Status'. Explanation: Radio Frequency Interference status. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Clean, Contaminated, Unknown.

Telescopes.ProcQueueStatus: Full name: 'Processing Queue Status'. Explanation: Indicates how full the processing queue is. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Empty, Full, Normal.
Telescopes.TelescRegistry: Full name: 'Telescope Registry'. Explanation: A unique identifier for the telescope. Data type: CHAR(20). Example: 'TELESC_0001'.
Telescopes.TrackAccArc: Full name: 'Tracking Accuracy (arcsec)'. Explanation: How accurately the telescope can track a target, in arcseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '1.20'.

requests.specific_A: For patients none of whose laboratory records has a urine protein (`U-PRO`) result of '-', first take each patient's average prothrombin time (`PT`) and average alkaline phosphatase-to-ALT ratio (`ALP` ÷ `GPT`, per record) across all their lab records. Then, for each sex (`SEX` from the Patient table, with a blank value as its own group), report the sex and the averages of those per-patient averages. Only lab records with a matching Patient record count. Averages ignore missing values. Don't round.
requests.specific_B: For patients with at least one laboratory record whose urine protein (`U-PRO`) result is recorded and is something other than '-', first take each patient's average prothrombin time (`PT`) and average alkaline phosphatase-to-ALT ratio (`ALP` ÷ `GPT`, per record) across all their lab records. Then, for each sex (`SEX` from the Patient table, with a blank value as its own group), report the sex and the averages of those per-patient averages. Only lab records with a matching Patient record count. Averages ignore missing values. Don't round.
requests.open: Looking only at patients without a urine protein (`U-PRO`) result of '-' in their lab tests, what are the average prothrombin time (`PT`) and the average alkaline phosphatase-to-ALT ratio (`ALP` ÷ `GPT`, per record) by sex? Compute each patient's averages over all their lab records first, then average those per-patient figures within each sex (`SEX` from the Patient table, with a blank value as its own group). Only count lab records that match a Patient record, ignore missing values in the averages and don't round.

readings.A: Patients none of whose lab records has a U-PRO result of '-'.
readings.B: Patients who have at least one lab record with a recorded U-PRO result other than '-'.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Laboratory"."ID" AS "e", "Patient"."SEX" AS "g", AVG("Laboratory"."PT") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("Laboratory"."ALP" AS REAL) / "Laboratory"."GPT")) AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" INNER JOIN "Patient" AS "Patient" ON "Patient"."ID" = "Laboratory"."ID" WHERE "Laboratory"."ID" NOT IN ((SELECT "x"."ID" FROM "Laboratory" AS "x" WHERE ("x"."U-PRO" = '-' AND NOT ("x"."ID" IS NULL)))) GROUP BY "Laboratory"."ID", "Patient"."SEX") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Laboratory"."ID" AS "e", "Patient"."SEX" AS "g", AVG("Laboratory"."PT") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("Laboratory"."ALP" AS REAL) / "Laboratory"."GPT")) AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" INNER JOIN "Patient" AS "Patient" ON "Patient"."ID" = "Laboratory"."ID" WHERE "Laboratory"."ID" IN ((SELECT "x"."ID" FROM "Laboratory" AS "x" WHERE ("x"."U-PRO" != '-' AND NOT ("x"."ID" IS NULL)))) GROUP BY "Laboratory"."ID", "Patient"."SEX") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"

shared_requirements.requirement: Use Laboratory records joined to Patient on `ID`. Drop lab records that have no matching patient. Choose patients by whether their lab records have a urine protein (`U-PRO`) result of exactly the text '-'. Once a patient qualifies, keep all of that patient's lab records.
First make one row per patient (`ID` and `SEX`). Then group those rows by `SEX`. A blank sex counts as its own group.
Show the sex (`SEX` from the Patient table).
Take each patient's average prothrombin time (`PT`), then average those values within the sex. Ignore missing values and do not round.
Compute `ALP` ÷ `GPT` for each record as a real number. Take each patient's average of that ratio, then average those values within the sex. Ignore missing values and do not round.

A.requirement: Keep a patient only if none of their lab records has `U-PRO` = '-'. Patients whose `U-PRO` is always missing still qualify.

B.requirement: Keep a patient only if at least one of their lab records has a `U-PRO` value that is recorded and is not '-'.

requests.specific_A: For each order item that appears in the invoice line items, take the average of `derived_product_cost` divided by `derived_total_cost` across its invoice line items (skipping missing ratios), and count its invoice line items. Then return one row with the average of those per-item average ratios (ignoring missing ones) and the average of those per-item line-item counts.
requests.specific_B: For every order item in `Order_Items`, including those with no invoice line items (which count as zero line items), take the average of `derived_product_cost` divided by `derived_total_cost` across its invoice line items (skipping missing ratios), and count its invoice line items. Then return one row with the average of those per-item average ratios (ignoring missing ones) and the average of those per-item line-item counts.
requests.open: Per order item, work out the average of `derived_product_cost` ÷ `derived_total_cost` over its invoice line items (skipping missing ratios) and how many invoice line items it has. In a single row, what are the overall average of those per-item ratios (ignoring missing ones) and the average number of invoice line items per order item?

readings.A: Average over only the order items that have invoice line items.
readings.B: Average over all order items. Those with no invoice line items contribute a count of zero and no ratio.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Invoice_Line_Items"."order_item_id" AS "e", AVG((CAST("Invoice_Line_Items"."derived_product_cost" AS REAL) / "Invoice_Line_Items"."derived_total_cost")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "Invoice_Line_Items" AS "Invoice_Line_Items" GROUP BY "Invoice_Line_Items"."order_item_id") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Order_Items"."order_item_id" AS "e", AVG((CAST("Invoice_Line_Items"."derived_product_cost" AS REAL) / "Invoice_Line_Items"."derived_total_cost")) AS "m1", COUNT("Invoice_Line_Items"."order_item_id") AS "m2" FROM "Order_Items" AS "Order_Items" LEFT JOIN "Invoice_Line_Items" AS "Invoice_Line_Items" ON "Invoice_Line_Items"."order_item_id" = "Order_Items"."order_item_id" GROUP BY "Order_Items"."order_item_id") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"

shared_requirements.requirement: Work per order item, using its `Invoice_Line_Items` rows (matched on `order_item_id`). For each order item, compute (a) the average of `derived_product_cost` ÷ `derived_total_cost` over its line items, ignoring missing ratios, and (b) the number of its line items.
Combine all the per-order-item rows into a single result row.
First column: the average of the per-order-item average ratios. Missing values are ignored.
Second column: the average of the per-order-item line-item counts.

A.requirement: Only order items that appear in `Invoice_Line_Items` are included.

B.requirement: Every order item in `Order_Items` is included. Those with no invoice line items count as 0 line items and have no ratio.

requests.specific_A: For each team that appears in `manager_half`, compute its average win rate (wins `w` divided by games managed `g` for each `manager_half` record, averaged and ignoring missing values) and its number of `manager_half` records. Then take the mean of those team averages across teams (ignoring missing ones), and, provided that mean exists, show each team's `team_id`, average win rate, record count, and its average minus that mean, sorted by the difference from highest to lowest with missing values last, top 10.
requests.specific_B: For every team in the `team` table, including teams with no `manager_half` records (which get a count of zero and no average), compute its average win rate (wins `w` divided by games managed `g` for each `manager_half` record, averaged and ignoring missing values) and its number of `manager_half` records. Then take the mean of those team averages across teams (ignoring missing ones), and, provided that mean exists, show each team's `team_id`, average win rate, record count, and its average minus that mean, sorted by the difference from highest to lowest with missing values last, top 10.
requests.open: For each team, what is its average half-season win rate (wins `w` divided by games managed `g` for each `manager_half` record, averaged and ignoring missing values) and how many `manager_half` records does it have? Also show how far its average is above the mean of all the team averages (ignoring missing ones, and only if that mean exists). List `team_id`, average win rate, record count and the difference, sorted by the difference from highest to lowest with missing values last, top 10.

readings.A: Only teams that have `manager_half` records are included.
readings.B: Every team is included. Teams without `manager_half` records get a zero count and no average.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "manager_half"."team_id" AS "e", AVG((CAST("manager_half"."w" AS REAL) / "manager_half"."g")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "manager_half" AS "manager_half" GROUP BY "manager_half"."team_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "team"."team_id" AS "e", AVG((CAST("manager_half"."w" AS REAL) / "manager_half"."g")) AS "m1", COUNT("manager_half"."player_id") AS "m2" FROM "team" AS "team" LEFT JOIN "manager_half" AS "manager_half" ON "manager_half"."team_id" = "team"."team_id" GROUP BY "team"."team_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

The team's `team_id`.
The team's average win rate (average of `w`/`g`). No rounding.
The team's number of `manager_half` records.
The team's average minus the cross-team mean.
Sort by the difference, descending, with missing values last.

requests.specific_A: For each player who has at least one manager award record, give the `player_id`, the number of `manager_award` records they have, and that number as a fraction of the total of those counts across all players (unrounded; return nothing if that total is missing). Sort by the fraction from highest to lowest, with missing values last, and show only the first 10 rows.
requests.specific_B: For every player in the `player` table, including those with no manager award records (counted as zero), give the `player_id`, the number of `manager_award` records they have, and that number as a fraction of the total of those counts across all players (unrounded; return nothing if that total is missing). Sort by the fraction from highest to lowest, with missing values last, and show only the first 10 rows.
requests.open: For each player, how many manager awards (`manager_award` records) do they have, and what fraction of the total of those counts across all players does that represent (unrounded; return nothing if that total is missing)? Show the `player_id`, the count and the fraction, sorted by the fraction from highest to lowest with missing values last, and keep only the top 10 rows.

readings.A: Only players who have at least one manager award record are counted and ranked.
readings.B: Every player in the player table is counted and ranked. Players without manager award records count as zero.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "manager_award"."player_id" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "manager_award" AS "manager_award" GROUP BY "manager_award"."player_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "player"."player_id" AS "e", COUNT("manager_award"."player_id") AS "m1" FROM "player" AS "player" LEFT JOIN "manager_award" AS "manager_award" ON "manager_award"."player_id" = "player"."player_id" GROUP BY "player"."player_id"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Count the `manager_award` records for each player, grouped by `player_id`. Every record counts.

Pair each player's count with one grand total: the sum of all the per-player counts, ignoring missing values. Rows are kept only when that total is not missing; if the total is missing, there are no rows.
First column: the player identifier (`player_id`).
Second column: the player's number of manager award records.
Third column: the player's count divided by the grand total, as a real number and not rounded.
Sort rows by the share (count ÷ total) from highest to lowest, with missing values last. No tie-breaker is given.
Keep only the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: The players are only those who appear in `manager_award`, so every player has at least one record.

B.requirement: The players are everyone in the `player` table, left-joined to `manager_award`. Players with no manager award records are included with a count of 0.

requests.specific_A: Using only fee records whose maker rebate rate (`rebrate`) is at least 0.0005, group them by order (`orderslink`) and, for each order, compute the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average of rebate rate divided by fee rate (`rebrate` / `feerate`), ignoring missing values. Then take the mean of those per-order average ratios across all orders and, provided that overall mean is not missing, divide each order's average ratio by it. Return the order link, the average total rebate, the average ratio and this relative ratio for the 10 orders with the highest relative ratio, sorted from highest to lowest with missing values last.
requests.specific_B: Using only fee records whose maker rebate rate (`rebrate`) is greater than 0.0005, group them by order (`orderslink`) and, for each order, compute the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average of rebate rate divided by fee rate (`rebrate` / `feerate`), ignoring missing values. Then take the mean of those per-order average ratios across all orders and, provided that overall mean is not missing, divide each order's average ratio by it. Return the order link, the average total rebate, the average ratio and this relative ratio for the 10 orders with the highest relative ratio, sorted from highest to lowest with missing values last.
requests.open: For fee records that clear the 0.0005 maker rebate rate (`rebrate`) threshold, group them by order (`orderslink`) and, for each order, work out the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average of rebate rate divided by fee rate (`rebrate` / `feerate`), ignoring missing values. Then take the mean of those per-order average ratios across all orders and, as long as that overall mean isn't missing, divide each order's average ratio by it. Show the order link, the average total rebate, the average ratio and the relative ratio for the top 10 orders by relative ratio, highest first, with missing values last.

readings.A: Fee records whose maker rebate rate is exactly 0.0005 are included, along with those above it.
readings.B: Only fee records whose maker rebate rate is strictly greater than 0.0005 are included.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "fees"."orderslink" AS "e", AVG("fees"."rebtotal") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("fees"."rebrate" AS REAL) / "fees"."feerate")) AS "m2" FROM "fees" AS "fees" WHERE "fees"."rebrate" >= 0.0005 GROUP BY "fees"."orderslink"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "fees"."orderslink" AS "e", AVG("fees"."rebtotal") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("fees"."rebrate" AS REAL) / "fees"."feerate")) AS "m2" FROM "fees" AS "fees" WHERE "fees"."rebrate" > 0.0005 GROUP BY "fees"."orderslink"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

requests.specific_A: What is the average debited amount (`order.amount`) of standing orders whose amount is at least 2802.0, unrounded?
requests.specific_B: What is the average debited amount (`order.amount`) of standing orders whose amount is more than 2802.0, unrounded?
requests.open: Applying a cutoff of 2802.0 to the debited amount (`order.amount`), what is the average debited amount of the large standing orders, unrounded?

readings.A: Orders of exactly 2802.0 are included.
readings.B: Only orders above 2802.0 are included.

sql.A: SELECT AVG("order"."amount") AS "m1" FROM "order" AS "order" WHERE "order"."amount" >= 2802.0
sql.B: SELECT AVG("order"."amount") AS "m1" FROM "order" AS "order" WHERE "order"."amount" > 2802.0

shared_requirements.requirement: Use standing-order (`order`) records.
Keep only orders whose debited amount (`order.amount`) passes the 2802.0 threshold. Whether exactly 2802.0 counts is the open choice.
All kept orders form one group, giving a single result row.
One column: the average `order.amount` of the kept orders, not rounded. It is missing if no orders are kept.

A.requirement: `order.amount` >= 2802.0.

B.requirement: `order.amount` > 2802.0.

requests.specific_A: Looking at individual lab records with a white blood cell count (`WBC`) of 6.5 or higher, group them by anti-centromere status (`CENTROMEA`), treating a missing status as its own group, and for each status work out the average AST minus ALT (`GOT` − `GPT`) and the average APTT minus PT (`APTT` − `PT`), skipping records where a difference can't be computed. Then give me a single row with two unrounded figures: the average of those per-status AST − ALT averages and the average of the per-status APTT − PT averages, with each status counting equally and missing per-status values ignored.
requests.specific_B: Looking at individual lab records with a white blood cell count (`WBC`) strictly greater than 6.5, group them by anti-centromere status (`CENTROMEA`), treating a missing status as its own group, and for each status work out the average AST minus ALT (`GOT` − `GPT`) and the average APTT minus PT (`APTT` − `PT`), skipping records where a difference can't be computed. Then give me a single row with two unrounded figures: the average of those per-status AST − ALT averages and the average of the per-status APTT − PT averages, with each status counting equally and missing per-status values ignored.
requests.open: Taking individual lab records and using 6.5 as the white blood cell count (`WBC`) cutoff, group them by anti-centromere status (`CENTROMEA`), treating a missing status as its own group, and for each status work out the average AST minus ALT (`GOT` − `GPT`) and the average APTT minus PT (`APTT` − `PT`), skipping records where a difference can't be computed. Then give me a single row with two unrounded figures: the average of those per-status AST − ALT averages and the average of the per-status APTT − PT averages, with each status counting equally and missing per-status values ignored.

readings.A: Laboratory records with WBC equal to 6.5 count as passing the filter (WBC at least 6.5).
readings.B: Only Laboratory records with WBC strictly above 6.5 pass the filter; records with exactly 6.5 are excluded.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Laboratory"."CENTROMEA" AS "g", AVG(("Laboratory"."GOT" - "Laboratory"."GPT")) AS "m1", AVG(("Laboratory"."APTT" - "Laboratory"."PT")) AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" WHERE "Laboratory"."WBC" >= 6.5 GROUP BY "Laboratory"."CENTROMEA") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Laboratory"."CENTROMEA" AS "g", AVG(("Laboratory"."GOT" - "Laboratory"."GPT")) AS "m1", AVG(("Laboratory"."APTT" - "Laboratory"."PT")) AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" WHERE "Laboratory"."WBC" > 6.5 GROUP BY "Laboratory"."CENTROMEA") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every individual Laboratory record (no join), filtered on its white blood cell value (`WBC`) against the threshold 6.5
Group the kept records by anti-centromere status (`CENTROMEA`); each distinct status value, including a missing status, forms one group
Per group, compute the average of (`GOT` − `GPT`) over records, ignoring records where the difference is missing; missing if none
Per group, compute the average of (`APTT` − `PT`) over records, ignoring records where the difference is missing; missing if none
Combine all the per-status groups into a single row: each figure is an unweighted average of the per-status averages (each status counts once), ignoring missing per-status values; missing if none
First output column: average across statuses of the per-status average AST − ALT difference (`GOT` − `GPT`), unrounded
Second output column: average across statuses of the per-status average APTT − PT difference (`APTT` − `PT`), unrounded
The status itself is not returned; the answer is exactly one row with those two columns in that order

A.requirement: Keep records whose `WBC` is 6.5 or higher (a value of exactly 6.5 is kept)

B.requirement: Keep only records whose `WBC` is strictly greater than 6.5 (a value of exactly 6.5 is excluded)

requests.specific_A: Looking only at driver standings records whose season-to-date championship points total (`driverStandings.points`) is at least 1.0, what is the single overall average of that points total across those records (ignoring missing values, unrounded)?
requests.specific_B: Looking only at driver standings records whose season-to-date championship points total (`driverStandings.points`) is more than 1.0, what is the single overall average of that points total across those records (ignoring missing values, unrounded)?
requests.open: Split driver standings records by their season-to-date championship points total (`driverStandings.points`), using 1.0 points as the dividing line, and keep only the records on the higher side. What is the single overall average of that points total across the kept records (ignoring missing values, unrounded)?

readings.A: Average the season-to-date points of driver standings records whose points are at least 1.0, counting records at exactly 1.0.
readings.B: Average the season-to-date points of driver standings records whose points are strictly greater than 1.0, leaving out records at exactly 1.0.

sql.A: SELECT AVG("driverStandings"."points") AS "m1" FROM "driverStandings" AS "driverStandings" WHERE "driverStandings"."points" >= 1.0
sql.B: SELECT AVG("driverStandings"."points") AS "m1" FROM "driverStandings" AS "driverStandings" WHERE "driverStandings"."points" > 1.0

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every `driverStandings` record (no joins).
Filter on `driverStandings.points` (season-to-date running total) with 1.0 as the threshold, keeping records on the high side of it.
All kept records form a single group, which gives exactly one result row.
One column: the average of `driverStandings.points` over the kept records. Missing values are ignored, the result is missing if there are none, and nothing is rounded.

A.requirement: Records whose points equal exactly 1.0 are kept (points >= 1.0).

B.requirement: Records whose points equal exactly 1.0 are dropped (points > 1.0).

requests.specific_A: Considering only films whose replacement cost is at least 20.99, group them by `original_language_id`, with films that have no original language forming their own group. For each group, show the original language id, the average of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` across its films (unrounded, ignoring missing values), and the number of films. Sort the groups from most films to fewest (any missing counts last) and show only the top 10.
requests.specific_B: Considering only films whose replacement cost is more than 20.99, group them by `original_language_id`, with films that have no original language forming their own group. For each group, show the original language id, the average of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` across its films (unrounded, ignoring missing values), and the number of films. Sort the groups from most films to fewest (any missing counts last) and show only the top 10.
requests.open: Using 20.99 as the replacement-cost cutoff for films, group the qualifying films by `original_language_id`, with films that have no original language forming their own group. For each group, show the original language id, the average of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` across its films (unrounded, ignoring missing values), and the number of films. Sort the groups from most films to fewest (any missing counts last) and show only the top 10.

readings.A: Films with a replacement cost equal to 20.99 are included along with those above it.
readings.B: Only films with a replacement cost above 20.99 are included. A cost of exactly 20.99 is left out.

sql.A: SELECT "film"."original_language_id" AS "e", AVG((CAST("film"."rental_rate" AS REAL) / "film"."rental_duration")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "film" AS "film" WHERE "film"."replacement_cost" >= 20.99 GROUP BY "film"."original_language_id" ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: SELECT "film"."original_language_id" AS "e", AVG((CAST("film"."rental_rate" AS REAL) / "film"."rental_duration")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "film" AS "film" WHERE "film"."replacement_cost" > 20.99 GROUP BY "film"."original_language_id" ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the films, one per `film` record.
Keep films by comparing `film.replacement_cost` with the value 20.99. Whether a cost of exactly 20.99 counts is the choice.
Group the kept films by `original_language_id`. Films with no original language (NULL) form their own group.
First column: the `original_language_id` of the group.
Second column: the average over the group's films of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration`, with no rounding. Missing values are ignored, and the result is missing if there are none.
Third column: the number of films in the group.
Sort the rows by number of films, highest first, with any missing counts last.
Return only the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: Keep films whose replacement cost is at least 20.99, so a cost of exactly 20.99 counts.

B.requirement: Keep only films whose replacement cost is more than 20.99, so a cost of exactly 20.99 is left out.

film.length: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified rating query already returns AVG(length) between 111.05 (G) and 120.44 (PG-13). The catalogue profile gives 140 distinct values from 46 to 185 minutes. So length is a continuous ratio-scale quantity whose group averages can be read directly. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(length) AS avg_minutes, MIN(length), MAX(length) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '120.4439461883408', '46', '185'], ['NC-17', '210', '113.22857142857143', '46', '184'], ['R', '195', '118.66153846153846', '49', '185'], ['PG', '194', '112.00515463917526', '46', '185'], ['G', '178', '111.0505617977528', '47', '185']]

The query shows how large and uniform the gap is. The auditor noted that the difference is always about −17 and the relative gap about −0.85, which fits two different quantities rather than one price seen two ways. requests.specific_A: How many advanced behaviour records have a peer correlation (`peercorr`) of at least 0.149?
requests.specific_B: How many advanced behaviour records have a peer correlation (`peercorr`) greater than 0.149?
requests.open: Using 0.149 as the cutoff, how many advanced behaviour records have high peer correlation (`peercorr`)? Give a single count.

readings.A: Peer correlation values equal to 0.149 are counted (at least 0.149).
readings.B: Only peer correlation values strictly greater than 0.149 are counted (more than 0.149).

sql.A: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "advancedbehavior" AS "advancedbehavior" WHERE "advancedbehavior"."peercorr" >= 0.149
sql.B: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "advancedbehavior" AS "advancedbehavior" WHERE "advancedbehavior"."peercorr" > 0.149

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from each `advancedbehavior` record (no joins)
Filter on peer correlation (`advancedbehavior.peercorr`) against the value 0.149, keeping the high side
All kept records form one group, so the result is one row
The only column is the number of kept records

A.requirement: A record whose `peercorr` is exactly 0.149 is kept (peercorr >= 0.149)

B.requirement: A record whose `peercorr` is exactly 0.149 is excluded (peercorr > 0.149)

requests.specific_A: Considering only tracks whose file size (`Track.Bytes`) is at least 10,323,804 bytes, work out for each media type (by name) the average bytes per millisecond (`Bytes` ÷ `Milliseconds`) of its tracks. What is the simple average of these per-media-type averages? Return just that single value, unrounded.
requests.specific_B: Considering only tracks whose file size (`Track.Bytes`) is more than 10,323,804 bytes, work out for each media type (by name) the average bytes per millisecond (`Bytes` ÷ `Milliseconds`) of its tracks. What is the simple average of these per-media-type averages? Return just that single value, unrounded.
requests.open: Considering only tracks that pass a file-size (`Track.Bytes`) cutoff of 10,323,804 bytes, work out for each media type (by name) the average bytes per millisecond (`Bytes` ÷ `Milliseconds`) of its tracks. What is the simple average of these per-media-type averages? Return just that single value, unrounded.

readings.A: Tracks whose file size is exactly 10,323,804 bytes are included along with larger ones.
readings.B: Only tracks whose file size is strictly greater than 10,323,804 bytes are included.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "MediaType"."Name" AS "g", AVG((CAST("Track"."Bytes" AS REAL) / "Track"."Milliseconds")) AS "m1" FROM "Track" AS "Track" INNER JOIN "MediaType" AS "MediaType" ON "MediaType"."MediaTypeId" = "Track"."MediaTypeId" WHERE "Track"."Bytes" >= 10323804 GROUP BY "MediaType"."Name") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1" FROM "s1" AS "s1"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "MediaType"."Name" AS "g", AVG((CAST("Track"."Bytes" AS REAL) / "Track"."Milliseconds")) AS "m1" FROM "Track" AS "Track" INNER JOIN "MediaType" AS "MediaType" ON "MediaType"."MediaTypeId" = "Track"."MediaTypeId" WHERE "Track"."Bytes" > 10323804 GROUP BY "MediaType"."Name") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1" FROM "s1" AS "s1"

shared_requirements.requirement: Use Track records matched to their MediaType by MediaTypeId (inner join, so tracks with no matching media type are dropped).
Only tracks that pass the file-size (`Track.Bytes`) cutoff of 10,323,804 count. Whether the cutoff value itself passes is the choice.
Group the kept tracks by media type name (`MediaType.Name`). For each group, compute the average of `Bytes` ÷ `Milliseconds`, ignoring missing values.
Combine all per-media-type averages into one group and take their simple, unweighted average, ignoring missing values. This gives a single row.
Return one column: that overall average, unrounded.

A.requirement: A track whose `Bytes` equals 10,323,804 is kept (Bytes >= 10323804).

B.requirement: A track whose `Bytes` equals 10,323,804 is excluded (Bytes > 10323804).

requests.specific_A: Consider patients who have at least one laboratory record on which the urine protein (`U-PRO`) result is exactly '-' and the rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result is also exactly '-'. For each such patient, use all of their laboratory records to compute the average prothrombin time (`PT`) and the average of `TAT` minus `TAT2`. Across these patients, what are the average of the per-patient PT averages and the average of the per-patient TAT − TAT2 averages? Give them as a single row with these two values, unrounded, and ignore missing values at every step.
requests.specific_B: Consider patients who have at least one laboratory record with a urine protein (`U-PRO`) result of exactly '-' and at least one laboratory record, not necessarily the same one, with a rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result of exactly '-'. For each such patient, use all of their laboratory records to compute the average prothrombin time (`PT`) and the average of `TAT` minus `TAT2`. Across these patients, what are the average of the per-patient PT averages and the average of the per-patient TAT − TAT2 averages? Give them as a single row with these two values, unrounded, and ignore missing values at every step.
requests.open: Consider patients whose laboratory results include a urine protein (`U-PRO`) result of exactly '-' and a rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result of exactly '-'. For each such patient, use all of their laboratory records to compute the average prothrombin time (`PT`) and the average of `TAT` minus `TAT2`. Across these patients, what are the average of the per-patient PT averages and the average of the per-patient TAT − TAT2 averages? Give them as a single row with these two values, unrounded, and ignore missing values at every step.

readings.A: Patients qualify only if one laboratory record shows both a urine protein result of '-' and a rheumatoid factor result of '-'.
readings.B: Patients qualify if they have a record with a urine protein result of '-' and a record with a rheumatoid factor result of '-'. These can be different records.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Laboratory"."ID" AS "e", AVG("Laboratory"."PT") AS "m1", AVG(("Laboratory"."TAT" - "Laboratory"."TAT2")) AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" WHERE "Laboratory"."ID" IN ((SELECT "x"."ID" FROM "Laboratory" AS "x" WHERE ("x"."U-PRO" = '-' AND "x"."RA" = '-' AND NOT ("x"."ID" IS NULL)))) GROUP BY "Laboratory"."ID") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Laboratory"."ID" AS "e", AVG("Laboratory"."PT") AS "m1", AVG(("Laboratory"."TAT" - "Laboratory"."TAT2")) AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" WHERE ("Laboratory"."ID" IN ((SELECT "x"."ID" FROM "Laboratory" AS "x" WHERE ("x"."U-PRO" = '-' AND NOT ("x"."ID" IS NULL)))) AND "Laboratory"."ID" IN ((SELECT "x"."ID" FROM "Laboratory" AS "x" WHERE ("x"."RA" = '-' AND NOT ("x"."ID" IS NULL))))) GROUP BY "Laboratory"."ID") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"

shared_requirements.requirement: Use `Laboratory` records only. Once a patient qualifies, use all of that patient's laboratory records, not only the records that meet the conditions.

A patient qualifies through their laboratory results for urine protein (`U-PRO`) and rheumatoid factor (`RA`). Each must equal the text '-' exactly, so values such as '+-' do not count. Records with a missing patient ID cannot qualify a patient.

Group the qualifying patients' records by patient (`Laboratory.ID`). For each patient, compute the average prothrombin time (`PT`) and the average of `TAT` minus `TAT2`. Ignore missing values. If a patient has no usable values, their average is missing.
Combine all qualifying patients into one group. Return a single row that averages the per-patient values, ignoring missing per-patient averages.
The first column is the average, across patients, of the per-patient average PT. It is not rounded.
The second column is the average, across patients, of the per-patient average of TAT − TAT2. It is not rounded.

A.requirement: A patient qualifies only if a single laboratory record has both `U-PRO` = '-' and `RA` = '-'.

B.requirement: A patient qualifies if some record has `U-PRO` = '-' and some record, possibly a different one, has `RA` = '-'.

requests.specific_A: Considering only standing orders (the `order` table) whose `amount` is at least 2802, compute the average `amount` for each payment purpose code (`k_symbol`), treating the blank purpose code as a group of its own. Then take the simple average of those per-purpose averages. Which purposes have an average above that overall figure? For each, list the `k_symbol`, its average amount, and how far it exceeds the overall figure (purpose average minus overall figure), without rounding.
requests.specific_B: Considering only standing orders (the `order` table) whose `amount` is greater than 2802, compute the average `amount` for each payment purpose code (`k_symbol`), treating the blank purpose code as a group of its own. Then take the simple average of those per-purpose averages. Which purposes have an average above that overall figure? For each, list the `k_symbol`, its average amount, and how far it exceeds the overall figure (purpose average minus overall figure), without rounding.
requests.open: Using an `amount` of 2802 as the cutoff for a large standing order (the `order` table), compute the average `amount` of the large orders for each payment purpose code (`k_symbol`), treating the blank purpose code as a group of its own. Then take the simple average of those per-purpose averages. Which purposes have an average above that overall figure? For each, list the `k_symbol`, its average amount, and how far it exceeds the overall figure (purpose average minus overall figure), without rounding.

readings.A: Standing orders with an amount of 2802 or more are used in the per-purpose averages and in the overall average.
readings.B: Only standing orders with an amount strictly greater than 2802 are used in the per-purpose averages and in the overall average.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "order"."k_symbol" AS "g", AVG("order"."amount") AS "m1" FROM "order" AS "order" WHERE "order"."amount" >= 2802.0 GROUP BY "order"."k_symbol"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "order"."k_symbol" AS "g", AVG("order"."amount") AS "m1" FROM "order" AS "order" WHERE "order"."amount" > 2802.0 GROUP BY "order"."k_symbol"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"

shared_requirements.requirement: Population is the standing orders in the `order` table, kept only if `order.amount` passes the 2802 threshold. The threshold's inclusiveness is the open choice.
Group the kept orders by payment purpose code `order.k_symbol`. The empty-string code is its own group and is kept as an empty string, not turned into NULL.
Compare each group's average order amount with the overall average, which is the plain (unweighted) mean of the per-purpose averages. Each purpose row is paired with that single overall value.
Keep only the purposes whose average is strictly greater than the overall average of per-purpose averages.
First column: the payment purpose code `k_symbol`.
Second column: the purpose's average `order.amount`, not rounded.
Third column: the purpose's average minus the overall average of per-purpose averages, not rounded.

A.requirement: An order whose amount is exactly 2802 is included (amount >= 2802).

B.requirement: An order whose amount is exactly 2802 is excluded (amount > 2802).

requests.specific_A: How many disposition records (each `disp` row, not distinct accounts) belong to accounts that have no disposition at all with `type` 'DISPONENT'?
requests.specific_B: How many disposition records (each `disp` row, not distinct accounts) belong to accounts that have at least one disposition whose `type` is not 'DISPONENT'?
requests.open: How many disposition records belong to non-disponent accounts? Count each disposition row, not each account.

readings.A: Count the disposition records belonging to accounts that have no 'DISPONENT' disposition at all.
readings.B: Count the disposition records belonging to accounts that have at least one disposition whose type is not 'DISPONENT'.

sql.A: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "disp" AS "disp" WHERE "disp"."account_id" NOT IN ((SELECT "x"."account_id" FROM "disp" AS "x" WHERE ("x"."type" = 'DISPONENT' AND NOT ("x"."account_id" IS NULL))))
sql.B: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "disp" AS "disp" WHERE "disp"."account_id" IN ((SELECT "x"."account_id" FROM "disp" AS "x" WHERE ("x"."type" != 'DISPONENT' AND NOT ("x"."account_id" IS NULL))))

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from disposition records (`disp`). Count disposition rows, not distinct accounts.

Keep a disposition based on how its account (`disp.account_id`) relates to the 'DISPONENT' disposition type (`disp.type`), looking across all dispositions of that account and ignoring rows with a missing account id.
All kept dispositions form one group, so the result is a single row.
One column: the number of kept disposition records.

A.requirement: Keep dispositions whose account has no disposition at all with type 'DISPONENT' (NOT IN the set of accounts that have a DISPONENT disposition).

B.requirement: Keep dispositions whose account has at least one disposition with a type other than 'DISPONENT' (IN the set of accounts that have a non-DISPONENT disposition).

requests.specific_A: Looking only at films whose running time (`film.length`) is at least 112 minutes, for each language (`film.language_id`) give the language id, the average replacement cost (`replacement_cost`), and the average running time, ignoring missing values in each average (missing if none remain). Sort by average running time from highest to lowest, with missing averages last, show the top 10, and don't round.
requests.specific_B: Looking only at films whose running time (`film.length`) is more than 112 minutes, for each language (`film.language_id`) give the language id, the average replacement cost (`replacement_cost`), and the average running time, ignoring missing values in each average (missing if none remain). Sort by average running time from highest to lowest, with missing averages last, show the top 10, and don't round.
requests.open: Using 112 minutes (`film.length`) as the cutoff for a long film and considering only the long films, for each language (`film.language_id`) give the language id, the average replacement cost (`replacement_cost`), and the average running time, ignoring missing values in each average (missing if none remain). Sort by average running time from highest to lowest, with missing averages last, show the top 10, and don't round.

readings.A: Films whose running time is 112 minutes or more are included; a film of exactly 112 minutes counts.
readings.B: Only films whose running time is strictly more than 112 minutes are included; a film of exactly 112 minutes does not count.

sql.A: SELECT "film"."language_id" AS "e", AVG("film"."replacement_cost") AS "m1", AVG("film"."length") AS "m2" FROM "film" AS "film" WHERE "film"."length" >= 112 GROUP BY "film"."language_id" ORDER BY AVG("film"."length") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: SELECT "film"."language_id" AS "e", AVG("film"."replacement_cost") AS "m1", AVG("film"."length") AS "m2" FROM "film" AS "film" WHERE "film"."length" > 112 GROUP BY "film"."language_id" ORDER BY AVG("film"."length") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the film table, one record per film; no joins.
Keep films according to how their running time (`film.length`) compares with the threshold 112 minutes; films with missing length are not kept.
Group the kept films by `film.language_id`; one result row per language.
First column: the language id (`film.language_id`).
Second column: average replacement cost (`film.replacement_cost`) in the group, ignoring missing values (missing if none); not rounded.
Third column: average running time (`film.length`) in the group, ignoring missing values (missing if none); not rounded.
Order rows by the average running time, highest first, with missing averages last.
Return only the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: A film whose length is exactly 112 is kept (length >= 112).

B.requirement: A film whose length is exactly 112 is excluded (length > 112).

);

);

  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (country_id)
);
CREATE TABLE customer (
  customer_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  store_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  first_name VARCHAR(45) NOT NULL,
  last_name VARCHAR(45) NOT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  address_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
  create_date DATETIME NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (customer_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (address_id) REFERENCES address (address_id),

);
CREATE TABLE film (
  film_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  title VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  description TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  release_year YEAR DEFAULT NULL,
  language_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  original_language_id TINYINT UNSIGNED DEFAULT NULL,
  rental_duration TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 3,
  rental_rate DECIMAL(4,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 4.99,
  length SMALLINT UNSIGNED DEFAULT NULL,
  replacement_cost DECIMAL(5,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 19.99,
  rating DEFAULT 'G',
  special_features DEFAULT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (film_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (language_id) REFERENCES language (language_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (original_language_id) REFERENCES language (language_id)
);
CREATE TABLE film_actor (
  actor_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  film_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (actor_id,film_id),
 FOREIGN KEY (actor_id) REFERENCES actor (actor_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (film_id) REFERENCES film (film_id)
);
CREATE TABLE film_category (
  film_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  category_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (film_id, category_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (film_id) REFERENCES film (film_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES category (category_id)
);
CREATE TABLE film_text (
  film_id SMALLINT NOT NULL,
  title VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  description TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY  (film_id)
);
CREATE TABLE inventory (
  inventory_id MEDIUMINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  film_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  store_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (inventory_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES store (store_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (film_id) REFERENCES film (film_id)
);
CREATE TABLE language (
  language_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  name CHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (language_id)
);
CREATE TABLE payment (

  staff_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,

film.rental_duration: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows 5 values from 3 to 7 days, all well above zero, so the column is a ratio-scale number of days per film. The query shows how many films fall at each value. Evidence: SELECT rental_duration, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate) AS avg_rate FROM film GROUP BY rental_duration ORDER BY rental_duration -> [['3', '203', '2.8323645320197115'], ['4', '203', '2.97029556650247'], ['5', '191', '3.19942408376964'], ['6', '212', '2.895660377358497'], ['7', '191', '3.021413612565451']]
film.rental_rate: desc (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows rental_rate takes only 0.99, 2.99 and 4.99, while replacement_cost runs from 9.99 to 29.99. The query shows how large and uniform the gap is. The auditor noted that the difference is always about −17 and the relative gap about −0.85, which fits two different quantities rather than one price seen two ways. Evidence: SELECT MIN(replacement_cost - rental_rate), MAX(replacement_cost - rental_rate), AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) FROM film -> [['5.0', '29.0', '0.16651517608314595']]
film.replacement_cost: quantity (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The column holds a per-copy value that becomes meaningful when summed over physical copies in inventory, for example as stock value. That is the reading of an asset value, not of a price charged per rental. Evidence: SELECT f.rating, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copies, SUM(f.replacement_cost) AS stock_value FROM inventory i JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating -> [['G', '791', '16185.089999999853'], ['NC-17', '944', '19128.56000000009'], ['PG', '924', '17755.759999999962'], ['PG-13', '1018', '21052.82000000024'], ['R', '904', '18498.960000000006']]
payment.staff_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows only 2 distinct values (1 and 2) across 16,049 payments. Each value is therefore shared by thousands of rows, which makes it a grouping label rather than a record identifier. Evidence: SELECT staff_id, COUNT(*) AS payments, SUM(amount) AS revenue, AVG(amount) FROM payment GROUP BY staff_id -> [['1', '8057', '33489.470000005174', '4.156568201564499'], ['2', '7992', '33927.04000000482', '4.245125125125728']]
rental.staff_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows only 2 distinct values across 16,044 rentals, so each staff value covers thousands of rentals and works as a grouping class. Evidence: SELECT staff_id, COUNT(*) AS rentals, SUM(CASE WHEN return_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unreturned FROM rental GROUP BY staff_id -> [['1', '8040', '85'], ['2', '8004', '98']]

requests.specific_A: For each observatory station that has at least one telescope, show the station (`observstation`), the average bandwidth usage of its telescopes (`bandusagepct`, ignoring missing values), the number of telescopes, and that number divided by the average telescope count across those stations. Sort by the ratio, largest first, and show the top 10.
requests.specific_B: For every observatory station in `observatories`, including stations with no telescopes (which count as 0 telescopes and have no average bandwidth), show the station (`observstation`), the average bandwidth usage of its telescopes (`bandusagepct`, ignoring missing values), the number of telescopes, and that number divided by the average telescope count across all those stations. Sort by the ratio, largest first, and show the top 10.
requests.open: Per observatory station (`observstation`), show the average bandwidth usage of its telescopes (`bandusagepct`, ignoring missing values), the number of telescopes, and that number divided by the average telescope count per station. Sort by the ratio, largest first, and show the top 10.

readings.A: Only stations that appear among the telescopes are listed and averaged.
readings.B: Every observatory station is listed and averaged, and stations without telescopes count as 0.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", AVG("telescopes"."bandusagepct") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "observatories"."observstation" AS "e", AVG("telescopes"."bandusagepct") AS "m1", COUNT("telescopes"."telescregistry") AS "m2" FROM "observatories" AS "observatories" LEFT JOIN "telescopes" AS "telescopes" ON "telescopes"."observstation" = "observatories"."observstation" GROUP BY "observatories"."observstation"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Count telescopes per observatory station. Average bandwidth usage (`telescopes.bandusagepct`) per station, ignoring missing values.
Pair every station row with the single overall average of the per-station telescope counts, taken across all listed stations. Drop rows if that average is missing.
Station (`observstation`)
Average bandwidth usage at the station. No rounding.
The station's telescope count
The station's count divided by the average count per station. No rounding.
Sort by that ratio, largest first (missing values last)
Return only the first 10 rows

A.requirement: Include only stations that have at least one telescope. The average count is taken over these stations only.

B.requirement: Include every station in `observatories`. Stations with no telescopes get a count of 0 and a missing average bandwidth, and these zeros enter the average count.

context.schema:
CREATE TABLE "observationalconditions" (

  "obstime" text(6),
  "obsdate" text,
  "obsdurhrs" real(5,2),
  CONSTRAINT "observationalconditions_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalref"),

);
CREATE TABLE "observatories" (
  "observstation" text(60) NOT NULL,

context.documentation:
ObservationalConditions.ObsDate: Full name: 'Observation Date'. Explanation: Local date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD). Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-08-01'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsDurHrs: Full name: 'Observation Duration (hours)'. Explanation: How long the observation lasted in hours. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '2.50'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsTime: Full name: 'Observation Time'. Explanation: Local time of the observation in HH:MM:SS. Data type: TIME. Example: '13:45:59'.
ObservationalConditions.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-PQR-9876'.
Observatories.AirTempC: Full name: 'Air Temperature (°C)'. Explanation: Ambient temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '18.45'.
Observatories.AtmosTransparency: Full name: 'Atmospheric Transparency'. Explanation: A numeric measure of how transparent the atmosphere is. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.867'.
Observatories.GeomagStatus: Full name: 'Geomagnetic Activity'. Explanation: The level of geomagnetic activity during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Active, Quiet, Storm.
Observatories.HumidityRate: Full name: 'Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Relative humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '62.300'.
Observatories.LunarDistDeg: Full name: 'Moon Distance (Degrees)'. Explanation: Angular distance to the Moon in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '97.52'.
Observatories.LunarStage: Full name: 'Lunar Phase'. Explanation: The current phase of the Moon during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: First Quarter, Full, Last Quarter, New.
Observatories.ObservStation: Full name: 'Observatory Name'. Explanation: This field holds the name or unique identifier for the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
Observatories.PressHpa: Full name: 'Pressure (hPa)'. Explanation: Atmospheric pressure in hectopascals. Data type: DECIMAL(6,1). Example: '1013.2'.
Observatories.SeeingProfile: Full name: 'Seeing Profile'. Explanation: Assessment of sky seeing conditions (atmospheric steadiness). Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
Observatories.SiderealLocal: Full name: 'Local Sidereal Time'. Explanation: Sidereal time at the observatory in HH:MM:SS format. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: '12:34:56'.
Observatories.SolarStatus: Full name: 'Solar Activity'. Explanation: The level of solar activity at the time of observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Moderate.
Observatories.WeathProfile: Full name: 'Weather Profile'. Explanation: A short description of weather conditions during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Clear, Cloudy, Partially Cloudy.
Observatories.WindSpeedMs: Full name: 'Wind Speed (m/s)'. Explanation: Wind speed in meters per second. Data type: NUMERIC(4,2). Example: '3.45'.
ResearchProcess.AnalysisPrio: Full name: 'Analysis Priority'. Explanation: Priority assigned for analyzing this signal. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, Urgent.
ResearchProcess.CollabStat: Full name: 'Collaboration Status'. Explanation: The nature of collaboration on this signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: International, Solo, Team.
ResearchProcess.DiscStat: Full name: 'Disclosure Status'. Explanation: How much information about the signal is shared publicly. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Full, None, Partial.
ResearchProcess.FollowStat: Full name: 'Follow-up Status'. Explanation: Status of any follow-up observations. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Required, Scheduled.
ResearchProcess.FundStat: Full name: 'Funding Status'. Explanation: Funding situation for further study. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Funded, Pending, Unfunded.
ResearchProcess.NotesMemo: Full name: 'Research Notes'. Explanation: Any extra remarks or context by researchers. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Project requires further funding...'
ResearchProcess.PeerRevStat: Full name: 'Peer Review Status'. Explanation: Where this signal stands in peer review. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, In Progress, Pending.
ResearchProcess.PubStat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether findings about the signal have been published. Data type: CHAR(25). Possible categories: Draft, Published, Submitted.
ResearchProcess.ResPrio: Full name: 'Research Priority'. Explanation: How urgently this signal needs scientific attention. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium.
ResearchProcess.SecClass: Full name: 'Security Classification'. Explanation: Visibility and clearance level for the data. Data type: CHAR(35). Possible categories: Classified, Public, Restricted.
ResearchProcess.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-MNO-7890'.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.CultSig: Full name: 'Cultural Significance'. Explanation: The level of cultural impact or interest. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: High, Low, None.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.EncryptEvid: Full name: 'Encryption Evidence'. Explanation: Whether there is indication the signal is encrypted. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: None, Possible, Strong.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.GravLens: Full name: 'Gravitational Lensing'. Explanation: Whether the signal is affected by gravitational lensing. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: None, Strong, Weak.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.InterMedEffects: Full name: 'Interstellar Medium Effects'. Explanation: Impact of interstellar medium on the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.LangStruct: Full name: 'Language Structure'. Explanation: Presence of linguistic or structured patterns. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Complex, None, Simple.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.MsgContent: Full name: 'Message Content'. Explanation: Indicates whether an actual message was detected. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Identified, None, Possible.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.QuantEffects: Full name: 'Quantum Effects'. Explanation: Quantum-level phenomena observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(85). Possible categories: None, Observed, Significant.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SciImpact: Full name: 'Scientific Impact'. Explanation: Significance of the signal to scientific research. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Major, Minor, Moderate.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-ABC-1234'.
SignalClassification.ClassConf: Full name: 'Classification Confidence (%)'. Explanation: How confident we are in the assigned signal class. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '92.50'.
SignalClassification.ComplexIdx: Full name: 'Complexity Index'. Explanation: Numeric measure of the signal’s complexity. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '5.678'.
SignalClassification.EntropyVal: Full name: 'Entropy'. Explanation: Entropy measurement of the signal. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.45'.
SignalClassification.InfoDense: Full name: 'Information Density'. Explanation: Estimated information per unit time/frequency. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.345'.
SignalClassification.PeriodSec: Full name: 'Period (s)'. Explanation: Duration of each cycle if periodic. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '12.345'.
SignalClassification.RepeatCount: Full name: 'Repetition Count'. Explanation: Number of times the signal has repeated. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '3'.
SignalClassification.SigClassType: Full name: 'Classification Type'. Explanation: High-level category for the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Artificial, Candidate, Natural, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SigPattern: Full name: 'Signal Pattern'. Explanation: Pattern observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: Periodic, Random, Structured, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-DEF-5678'.
SignalDecoding.AnalysisDp: Full name: 'Analysis Depth'. Explanation: How thoroughly the signal was analyzed. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Comprehensive, Detailed, Preliminary.
SignalDecoding.CompResources: Full name: 'Computational Resources'. Explanation: Level of computing power used. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Extreme, High, Low, Medium.
SignalDecoding.CompressRatio: Full name: 'Compression Ratio'. Explanation: Factor by which the raw signal data was compressed. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.500'.
SignalDecoding.ConfirmStat: Full name: 'Confirmation Status'. Explanation: Whether the decoding results have been confirmed. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Confirmed, Pending, Rejected.
SignalDecoding.DecodeConf: Full name: 'Decoding Confidence (%)'. Explanation: Confidence level that the decoding is correct. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '88.75'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeIters: Full name: 'Decoding Iterations'. Explanation: Number of algorithmic passes attempted. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '7'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeMethod: Full name: 'Decoding Method'. Explanation: Method used to decode the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: FFT, Neural Network, Quantum, Wavelet.
SignalDecoding.DecodeStat: Full name: 'Decoding Status'. Explanation: Status of the decoding process. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Failed, In Progress.
SignalDecoding.EncodeType: Full name: 'Encoding Type'. Explanation: The type of signal encoding used (e.g., Binary). Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Binary, Complex, Tertiary, Unknown.
SignalDecoding.ErrCorrLvl: Full name: 'Error Correction Level'. Explanation: Degree of error correction applied. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, None.
SignalDecoding.ProcTimeHrs: Full name: 'Processing Time (hours)'. Explanation: Total hours spent decoding. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.50'.
SignalDecoding.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal entry. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-GHI-9012'.
SignalDecoding.VerifLvl: Full name: 'Verification Level'. Explanation: Extent to which decoding has been verified. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Partially, Unverified, Verified.
SignalDynamics.AmpStab: Full name: 'Amplitude Stability'. Explanation: Consistency of signal amplitude. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Unstable'.
SignalDynamics.FreqStab: Full name: 'Frequency Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal’s frequency is. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighlyStable'.
SignalDynamics.ModStab: Full name: 'Modulation Stability'. Explanation: Consistency in the signal’s modulation scheme. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'Consistent'.
SignalDynamics.PhaseStab: Full name: 'Phase Stability'. Explanation: Any variation in signal phase. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'VaryingPhase'.
SignalDynamics.SigCoherence: Full name: 'Signal Coherence'. Explanation: How coherent the signal remains over its duration. Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighCoherence'.
SignalDynamics.SigDisp: Full name: 'Signal Dispersion'. Explanation: The degree to which the signal is dispersed (time/frequency smearing). Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'SignificantDisp'.
SignalDynamics.SigEvolve: Full name: 'Signal Evolution'. Explanation: Indicates if the signal changes/evolves during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Dynamic, Static, Unknown.
SignalDynamics.SigIntegrity: Full name: 'Signal Integrity'. Explanation: Rating of how intact or uncorrupted the signal is. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighIntegrity'.
SignalDynamics.SigRecurr: Full name: 'Signal Recurrence'. Explanation: Whether the signal recurs over time. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: None, Regular, Sporadic.
SignalDynamics.SigScint: Full name: 'Signal Scintillation'. Explanation: Fluctuation in signal amplitude due to propagation effects. Data type: VARCHAR(45). If no fixed categories, example: 'MildScintillation'.
SignalDynamics.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-JKL-3456'.
SignalDynamics.SpatStab: Full name: 'Spatial Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal is spatially (e.g., consistent direction). Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Moderate'.
SignalDynamics.TempStab: Full name: 'Temporal Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal remains over time. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Stable'.
SignalProbabilities.AnomScore: Full name: 'Anomaly Score'. Explanation: How unusual or unexpected the signal is. Data type: FLOAT. Example: '1.23'.
SignalProbabilities.ArtSrcProb: Full name: 'Artificial Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from an artificial source. Data type: NUMERIC(3,1). Example: '3.4'.
SignalProbabilities.BioSigProb: Full name: 'Biosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal indicates a biological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '45.21'.
SignalProbabilities.CorrScore: Full name: 'Correlation Score'. Explanation: How well the signal aligns with expected patterns. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.9950'.
SignalProbabilities.FalsePosProb: Full name: 'False Positive Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is falsely detected. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.0135'.
SignalProbabilities.NatSrcProb: Full name: 'Natural Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from a natural source. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '98.761'.
SignalProbabilities.SigUnique: Full name: 'Signal Uniqueness'. Explanation: A measure of how unique the signal is compared to others. Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '99.1234'.

SignalProbabilities.SimIndex: Full name: 'Similarity Index'. Explanation: Compares the signal to known references. Data type: NUMERIC(5,4). Example: '0.8222'.

requests.specific_A: Match each telescope to its observatory by station name (`observstation`), dropping telescopes with no matching observatory. Keep only stations where none of the telescopes has equipment status (`equipstatus`) 'Maintenance'. For each combination of station (`telescopes.observstation`) and moon phase (`observatories.lunarstage`), report the station, the moon phase, the average bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`, ignoring missing values) and the number of telescopes. Sort by that count, largest first, and show the top 10.
requests.specific_B: Match each telescope to its observatory by station name (`observstation`), dropping telescopes with no matching observatory. Keep only stations that have at least one telescope whose equipment status (`equipstatus`) is recorded and is something other than 'Maintenance'. For each combination of station (`telescopes.observstation`) and moon phase (`observatories.lunarstage`), report the station, the moon phase, the average bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`, ignoring missing values) and the number of telescopes. Sort by that count, largest first, and show the top 10.
requests.open: Match each telescope to its observatory by station name (`observstation`), dropping telescopes with no matching observatory. Looking only at stations with telescopes that aren't in 'Maintenance' equipment status (`equipstatus`), give each combination of station (`telescopes.observstation`) and moon phase (`observatories.lunarstage`). For each one, show the station, the moon phase, the average bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`, ignoring missing values) and the number of telescopes. Sort by that count, largest first, and show the top 10.

readings.A: A station counts as 'without Maintenance' when none of its telescopes is in Maintenance status.
readings.B: A station counts when at least one of its telescopes has a recorded status other than Maintenance, even if other telescopes there are in Maintenance.

sql.A: SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", "observatories"."lunarstage" AS "g", AVG("telescopes"."bandusagepct") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" INNER JOIN "observatories" AS "observatories" ON "observatories"."observstation" = "telescopes"."observstation" WHERE "telescopes"."observstation" NOT IN ((SELECT "x"."observstation" FROM "telescopes" AS "x" WHERE ("x"."equipstatus" = 'Maintenance' AND NOT ("x"."observstation" IS NULL)))) GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation", "observatories"."lunarstage" ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", "observatories"."lunarstage" AS "g", AVG("telescopes"."bandusagepct") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" INNER JOIN "observatories" AS "observatories" ON "observatories"."observstation" = "telescopes"."observstation" WHERE "telescopes"."observstation" IN ((SELECT "x"."observstation" FROM "telescopes" AS "x" WHERE ("x"."equipstatus" != 'Maintenance' AND NOT ("x"."observstation" IS NULL)))) GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation", "observatories"."lunarstage" ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the telescope records (`telescopes`).
Pair each telescope with the observatory record (`observatories`) whose `observstation` matches the telescope's `observstation` exactly. Drop telescopes that have no matching observatory.
Keep only the telescopes whose station passes the station-level condition about equipment status 'Maintenance' (`telescopes.equipstatus`). The condition is judged over all telescopes at that station.
Group by station (`telescopes.observstation`) and moon phase (`observatories.lunarstage`). A missing moon phase forms its own group.
Station (`telescopes.observstation`)
Moon phase (`observatories.lunarstage`)
Average bandwidth usage (`telescopes.bandusagepct`), ignoring missing values. No rounding.
Number of telescope records in the group
Sort by the count, largest first
Return only the first 10 rows

A.requirement: Keep a station only if none of its telescopes has equipment status 'Maintenance'

B.requirement: Keep a station if at least one of its telescopes has a recorded equipment status other than 'Maintenance'
