  "atmointerf" text(30),
  CONSTRAINT "signals_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_signals_telescopesref" FOREIGN KEY ("telescref") REFERENCES "telescopes" ("telescregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "sourceproperties" (
  "signalref" text(36) NOT NULL,
  "sourceradeg" real(7,4),
  "sourcedecdeg" real(7,4),
  "sourcedistly" real(10,2),
  "gallong" real(6,2),
  "gallat" real(6,2),
  "celestobj" text(75),
  "objtype" text(50),
  "objmag" real(5,2),
  "objtempk" integer(32),
  "objmasssol" real(6,3),
  "objagegyr" real(6,3),
  "objmetal" real(5,3),
  "objpropmotion" real(7,2),
  "objradvel" real(7,2),
  CONSTRAINT "sourceproperties_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("signalref"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_source_signal" FOREIGN KEY ("signalref") REFERENCES "signals" ("signalregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "telescopes" (
  "telescregistry" text(20) NOT NULL,
  "observstation" text(60) NOT NULL,
  "equipstatus" text(35),
  "calibrstatus" text(50),
  "pointaccarc" real(6,2),
  "trackaccarc" real(6,2),
  "focusquality" text(25),
  "detecttempk" real(7,2),
  "coolsysstatus" text(35),
  "powerstatus" text(30),
  "datastorstatus" text(35),
  "netstatus" text(40),
  "bandusagepct" real(5,2),
  "procqueuestatus" text(40),
  CONSTRAINT "telescopes_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("telescregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "fk_telescopes_observatoriesref" FOREIGN KEY ("observstation") REFERENCES "observatories" ("observstation")
);
context.documentation:
ObservationalConditions.ObsDate: Full name: 'Observation Date'. Explanation: Local date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD). Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-08-01'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsDurHrs: Full name: 'Observation Duration (hours)'. Explanation: How long the observation lasted in hours. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '2.50'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsTime: Full name: 'Observation Time'. Explanation: Local time of the observation in HH:MM:SS. Data type: TIME. Example: '13:45:59'.
ObservationalConditions.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-PQR-9876'.
Observatories.AirTempC: Full name: 'Air Temperature (°C)'. Explanation: Ambient temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '18.45'.
Observatories.AtmosTransparency: Full name: 'Atmospheric Transparency'. Explanation: A numeric measure of how transparent the atmosphere is. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.867'.
Observatories.GeomagStatus: Full name: 'Geomagnetic Activity'. Explanation: The level of geomagnetic activity during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Active, Quiet, Storm.
Observatories.HumidityRate: Full name: 'Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Relative humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '62.300'.
Observatories.LunarDistDeg: Full name: 'Moon Distance (Degrees)'. Explanation: Angular distance to the Moon in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '97.52'.
Observatories.LunarStage: Full name: 'Lunar Phase'. Explanation: The current phase of the Moon during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: First Quarter, Full, Last Quarter, New.
Observatories.ObservStation: Full name: 'Observatory Name'. Explanation: This field holds the name or unique identifier for the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
Observatories.PressHpa: Full name: 'Pressure (hPa)'. Explanation: Atmospheric pressure in hectopascals. Data type: DECIMAL(6,1). Example: '1013.2'.
Observatories.SeeingProfile: Full name: 'Seeing Profile'. Explanation: Assessment of sky seeing conditions (atmospheric steadiness). Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
Observatories.SiderealLocal: Full name: 'Local Sidereal Time'. Explanation: Sidereal time at the observatory in HH:MM:SS format. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: '12:34:56'.
Observatories.SolarStatus: Full name: 'Solar Activity'. Explanation: The level of solar activity at the time of observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Moderate.
Observatories.WeathProfile: Full name: 'Weather Profile'. Explanation: A short description of weather conditions during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Clear, Cloudy, Partially Cloudy.
Observatories.WindSpeedMs: Full name: 'Wind Speed (m/s)'. Explanation: Wind speed in meters per second. Data type: NUMERIC(4,2). Example: '3.45'.
ResearchProcess.AnalysisPrio: Full name: 'Analysis Priority'. Explanation: Priority assigned for analyzing this signal. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, Urgent.
ResearchProcess.CollabStat: Full name: 'Collaboration Status'. Explanation: The nature of collaboration on this signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: International, Solo, Team.
ResearchProcess.DiscStat: Full name: 'Disclosure Status'. Explanation: How much information about the signal is shared publicly. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Full, None, Partial.
ResearchProcess.FollowStat: Full name: 'Follow-up Status'. Explanation: Status of any follow-up observations. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Required, Scheduled.
ResearchProcess.FundStat: Full name: 'Funding Status'. Explanation: Funding situation for further study. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Funded, Pending, Unfunded.
ResearchProcess.NotesMemo: Full name: 'Research Notes'. Explanation: Any extra remarks or context by researchers. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Project requires further funding...'
ResearchProcess.PeerRevStat: Full name: 'Peer Review Status'. Explanation: Where this signal stands in peer review. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, In Progress, Pending.
ResearchProcess.PubStat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether findings about the signal have been published. Data type: CHAR(25). Possible categories: Draft, Published, Submitted.
ResearchProcess.ResPrio: Full name: 'Research Priority'. Explanation: How urgently this signal needs scientific attention. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium.
ResearchProcess.SecClass: Full name: 'Security Classification'. Explanation: Visibility and clearance level for the data. Data type: CHAR(35). Possible categories: Classified, Public, Restricted.
ResearchProcess.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-MNO-7890'.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.CultSig: Full name: 'Cultural Significance'. Explanation: The level of cultural impact or interest. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: High, Low, None.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.EncryptEvid: Full name: 'Encryption Evidence'. Explanation: Whether there is indication the signal is encrypted. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: None, Possible, Strong.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.GravLens: Full name: 'Gravitational Lensing'. Explanation: Whether the signal is affected by gravitational lensing. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: None, Strong, Weak.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.InterMedEffects: Full name: 'Interstellar Medium Effects'. Explanation: Impact of interstellar medium on the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.LangStruct: Full name: 'Language Structure'. Explanation: Presence of linguistic or structured patterns. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Complex, None, Simple.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.MsgContent: Full name: 'Message Content'. Explanation: Indicates whether an actual message was detected. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Identified, None, Possible.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.QuantEffects: Full name: 'Quantum Effects'. Explanation: Quantum-level phenomena observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(85). Possible categories: None, Observed, Significant.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SciImpact: Full name: 'Scientific Impact'. Explanation: Significance of the signal to scientific research. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Major, Minor, Moderate.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-ABC-1234'.
SignalClassification.ClassConf: Full name: 'Classification Confidence (%)'. Explanation: How confident we are in the assigned signal class. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '92.50'.
SignalClassification.ComplexIdx: Full name: 'Complexity Index'. Explanation: Numeric measure of the signal’s complexity. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '5.678'.
SignalClassification.EntropyVal: Full name: 'Entropy'. Explanation: Entropy measurement of the signal. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.45'.
SignalClassification.InfoDense: Full name: 'Information Density'. Explanation: Estimated information per unit time/frequency. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.345'.
SignalClassification.PeriodSec: Full name: 'Period (s)'. Explanation: Duration of each cycle if periodic. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '12.345'.
SignalClassification.RepeatCount: Full name: 'Repetition Count'. Explanation: Number of times the signal has repeated. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '3'.
SignalClassification.SigClassType: Full name: 'Classification Type'. Explanation: High-level category for the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Artificial, Candidate, Natural, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SigPattern: Full name: 'Signal Pattern'. Explanation: Pattern observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: Periodic, Random, Structured, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-DEF-5678'.
SignalDecoding.AnalysisDp: Full name: 'Analysis Depth'. Explanation: How thoroughly the signal was analyzed. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Comprehensive, Detailed, Preliminary.
SignalDecoding.CompResources: Full name: 'Computational Resources'. Explanation: Level of computing power used. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Extreme, High, Low, Medium.
SignalDecoding.CompressRatio: Full name: 'Compression Ratio'. Explanation: Factor by which the raw signal data was compressed. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.500'.
SignalDecoding.ConfirmStat: Full name: 'Confirmation Status'. Explanation: Whether the decoding results have been confirmed. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Confirmed, Pending, Rejected.
SignalDecoding.DecodeConf: Full name: 'Decoding Confidence (%)'. Explanation: Confidence level that the decoding is correct. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '88.75'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeIters: Full name: 'Decoding Iterations'. Explanation: Number of algorithmic passes attempted. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '7'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeMethod: Full name: 'Decoding Method'. Explanation: Method used to decode the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: FFT, Neural Network, Quantum, Wavelet.
SignalDecoding.DecodeStat: Full name: 'Decoding Status'. Explanation: Status of the decoding process. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Failed, In Progress.
SignalDecoding.EncodeType: Full name: 'Encoding Type'. Explanation: The type of signal encoding used (e.g., Binary). Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Binary, Complex, Tertiary, Unknown.
SignalDecoding.ErrCorrLvl: Full name: 'Error Correction Level'. Explanation: Degree of error correction applied. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, None.
SignalDecoding.ProcTimeHrs: Full name: 'Processing Time (hours)'. Explanation: Total hours spent decoding. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.50'.
SignalDecoding.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal entry. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-GHI-9012'.
SignalDecoding.VerifLvl: Full name: 'Verification Level'. Explanation: Extent to which decoding has been verified. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Partially, Unverified, Verified.
SignalDynamics.AmpStab: Full name: 'Amplitude Stability'. Explanation: Consistency of signal amplitude. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Unstable'.
SignalDynamics.FreqStab: Full name: 'Frequency Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal’s frequency is. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighlyStable'.
SignalDynamics.ModStab: Full name: 'Modulation Stability'. Explanation: Consistency in the signal’s modulation scheme. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'Consistent'.
SignalDynamics.PhaseStab: Full name: 'Phase Stability'. Explanation: Any variation in signal phase. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'VaryingPhase'.
SignalDynamics.SigCoherence: Full name: 'Signal Coherence'. Explanation: How coherent the signal remains over its duration. Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighCoherence'.
SignalDynamics.SigDisp: Full name: 'Signal Dispersion'. Explanation: The degree to which the signal is dispersed (time/frequency smearing). Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'SignificantDisp'.
SignalDynamics.SigEvolve: Full name: 'Signal Evolution'. Explanation: Indicates if the signal changes/evolves during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Dynamic, Static, Unknown.
SignalDynamics.SigIntegrity: Full name: 'Signal Integrity'. Explanation: Rating of how intact or uncorrupted the signal is. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighIntegrity'.
SignalDynamics.SigRecurr: Full name: 'Signal Recurrence'. Explanation: Whether the signal recurs over time. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: None, Regular, Sporadic.
SignalDynamics.SigScint: Full name: 'Signal Scintillation'. Explanation: Fluctuation in signal amplitude due to propagation effects. Data type: VARCHAR(45). If no fixed categories, example: 'MildScintillation'.
SignalDynamics.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-JKL-3456'.
SignalDynamics.SpatStab: Full name: 'Spatial Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal is spatially (e.g., consistent direction). Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Moderate'.
SignalDynamics.TempStab: Full name: 'Temporal Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal remains over time. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Stable'.
SignalProbabilities.AnomScore: Full name: 'Anomaly Score'. Explanation: How unusual or unexpected the signal is. Data type: FLOAT. Example: '1.23'.
SignalProbabilities.ArtSrcProb: Full name: 'Artificial Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from an artificial source. Data type: NUMERIC(3,1). Example: '3.4'.
SignalProbabilities.BioSigProb: Full name: 'Biosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal indicates a biological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '45.21'.
SignalProbabilities.CorrScore: Full name: 'Correlation Score'. Explanation: How well the signal aligns with expected patterns. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.9950'.
SignalProbabilities.FalsePosProb: Full name: 'False Positive Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is falsely detected. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.0135'.
SignalProbabilities.NatSrcProb: Full name: 'Natural Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from a natural source. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '98.761'.
SignalProbabilities.SigUnique: Full name: 'Signal Uniqueness'. Explanation: A measure of how unique the signal is compared to others. Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '99.1234'.
SignalProbabilities.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-XYZ-9876'.
SignalProbabilities.SimIndex: Full name: 'Similarity Index'. Explanation: Compares the signal to known references. Data type: NUMERIC(5,4). Example: '0.8222'.
SignalProbabilities.TechSigProb: Full name: 'Technosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is of artificial technological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.6789'.
Signals.AtmoInterf: Full name: 'Atmospheric Interference'. Explanation: Impact of atmospheric conditions on signal. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
Signals.BwHz: Full name: 'Bandwidth (Hz)'. Explanation: Signal’s bandwidth in Hertz. Data type: DECIMAL(10,3). Example: '500000.000'.
Signals.CarrierFreqMhz: Full name: 'Carrier Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Frequency of the carrier wave in MHz. Data type: DECIMAL(9,3). Example: '1000.000'.
Signals.CenterFreqMhz: Full name: 'Center Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Center frequency of the detected signal in MHz. Data type: NUMERIC(8,3). Example: '1420.500'.
Signals.DetectInstr: Full name: 'Detection Instrument'. Explanation: The instrument type employed for detecting the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Infrared Array, Optical Telescope, Quantum Detector, Radio Telescope.
Signals.DoppShiftHz: Full name: 'Doppler Shift (Hz)'. Explanation: Measured Doppler shift of the signal in Hertz. Data type: DOUBLE PRECISION. Example: '142.75'.
Signals.FreqDriftHzs: Full name: 'Frequency Drift (Hz/s)'. Explanation: How fast the signal drifts in frequency over time. Data type: NUMERIC(9,3). Example: '0.123'.
Signals.FreqMhz: Full name: 'Frequency (MHz)'. Explanation: Signal’s nominal frequency in MHz. Data type: DECIMAL(9,3). Example: '1420.405'.
Signals.InterfLvl: Full name: 'Interference Level'. Explanation: Degree of interference around the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, None.
Signals.ModIndex: Full name: 'Modulation Index'. Explanation: Numerical index describing modulation depth. Data type: DECIMAL(6,4). Example: '0.2875'.
Signals.ModType: Full name: 'Modulation Type'. Explanation: The method of signal modulation. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: AM, FM, PM, QAM, Unknown.
Signals.NoiseFloorDbm: Full name: 'Noise Floor (dBm)'. Explanation: Measured noise floor in dBm. Data type: DOUBLE PRECISION. Example: '-85.3'.
Signals.PhaseShiftDeg: Full name: 'Phase Shift (°)'. Explanation: Phase shift in degrees for the signal. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '45.00'.
Signals.PolarAngleDeg: Full name: 'Polarization Angle (°)'. Explanation: Angle of polarization in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(5,1). Example: '90.0'.
Signals.PolarMode: Full name: 'Polarization Mode'. Explanation: Type of signal polarization. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Circular, Elliptical, Linear, Unknown.
Signals.PulsePerSec: Full name: 'Pulse Rate (pulses/sec)'. Explanation: Rate of pulse repetition in the signal. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '4.500'.
Signals.PulseWidMs: Full name: 'Pulse Width (ms)'. Explanation: Duration of each pulse in milliseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '2.300'.
Signals.RfiStat: Full name: 'RFI Status'. Explanation: Radio Frequency Interference status. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Clean, Contaminated, Unknown.
Signals.SigDurSec: Full name: 'Signal Duration (s)'. Explanation: Total duration of the signal in seconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '12.50'.
Signals.SigStrDb: Full name: 'Signal Strength (dB)'. Explanation: Measured strength of the signal in decibels. Data type: NUMERIC(7,2). Example: '12.35'.
Signals.SignalClass: Full name: 'Signal Type'. Explanation: Broad classification of the detected signal. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Broadband, Continuous, Modulated, Narrowband, Pulsed.
Signals.SignalRegistry: Full name: 'Signal Registry'. Explanation: Unique ID for each signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-123E4567-E89B'.
Signals.SnrRatio: Full name: 'Signal-to-Noise Ratio'. Explanation: SNR measured for the signal. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '18.75'.
Signals.TelescRef: Full name: 'Telescope Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key to the telescope used for detection. Data type: CHAR(20). Example: 'TELESC_0001'.
Signals.TimeMark: Full name: 'Timestamp'. Explanation: The moment of signal detection. In some CSVs, it may be stored as an Excel serial date/time (e.g., '44302.55648' ≈ 2021-05-16 13:20:20 UTC). Data type: TIMESTAMPTZ. Example: '2025-08-01 13:45:00+00'.
SourceProperties.CelestObj: Full name: 'Celestial Object'. Explanation: Broad classification of the object. Data type: VARCHAR(75). Possible categories: Galaxy, Planet, Star, Unknown.
SourceProperties.GalLat: Full name: 'Galactic Latitude (°)'. Explanation: Galactic latitude of the source. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '-5.67'.
SourceProperties.GalLong: Full name: 'Galactic Longitude (°)'. Explanation: Galactic longitude of the source. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '12.34'.
SourceProperties.ObjAgeGyr: Full name: 'Object Age (Gyr)'. Explanation: Estimated age in billions of years. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '4.500'.
SourceProperties.ObjMag: Full name: 'Apparent Magnitude'. Explanation: Brightness of the object as seen from Earth. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '7.35'.
SourceProperties.ObjMassSol: Full name: 'Object Mass (solar)'. Explanation: Mass relative to the Sun. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '1.005'.
SourceProperties.ObjMetal: Full name: 'Metallicity'. Explanation: Ratio of elements heavier than helium in the object. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.012'.
SourceProperties.ObjPropMotion: Full name: 'Proper Motion (mas/yr)'. Explanation: Apparent motion across the sky in milliarcseconds/year. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '55.12'.
SourceProperties.ObjRadVel: Full name: 'Radial Velocity (km/s)'. Explanation: Speed at which the object is moving toward/away from us. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '-23.45'.
SourceProperties.ObjTempK: Full name: 'Object Temperature (K)'. Explanation: Approximate surface temperature in Kelvin. Data type: INTEGER. Example: '5800'.
SourceProperties.ObjType: Full name: 'Object Subtype'. Explanation: More specific object type. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Dwarf, Giant, Main Sequence, Unknown.
SourceProperties.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-STU-5432'.
SourceProperties.SourceDecDeg: Full name: 'Declination (°)'. Explanation: Declination of the source in degrees (-90 to +90). Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '-20.4567'.
SourceProperties.SourceDistLy: Full name: 'Distance (ly)'. Explanation: Approximate distance to the source in light-years. Data type: NUMERIC(10,2). Example: '26000.45'.
SourceProperties.SourceRaDeg: Full name: 'Right Ascension (°)'. Explanation: RA of the source in degrees (0 to 360). Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '123.4567'.
Telescopes.BandUsagePct: Full name: 'Bandwidth Usage (%)'. Explanation: Network bandwidth usage as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '73.25'.
Telescopes.CalibrStatus: Full name: 'Calibration Status'. Explanation: Status of telescope’s calibration. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Current, Due, Overdue.
Telescopes.CoolSysStatus: Full name: 'Cooling System Status'. Explanation: Status of the telescope’s cooling system. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Critical, Normal, Warning.
Telescopes.DataStorStatus: Full name: 'Data Storage Status'. Explanation: Capacity and status of local data storage. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Available, Critical, Low.
Telescopes.DetectTempK: Full name: 'Detector Temperature (K)'. Explanation: Temperature of the telescope’s primary detector in Kelvin. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '123.45'.
Telescopes.EquipStatus: Full name: 'Equipment Status'. Explanation: Operational state of the telescope. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Degraded, Maintenance, Operational.
Telescopes.FocusQuality: Full name: 'Focus Quality'. Explanation: Quality of the telescope’s focusing system. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
Telescopes.NetStatus: Full name: 'Network Status'. Explanation: Status of the network connection for telescope data transfer. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Connected, Disconnected, Limited.
Telescopes.ObservStation: Full name: 'Observatory Name Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key linking to the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
Telescopes.PointAccArc: Full name: 'Pointing Accuracy (arcsec)'. Explanation: How precise the telescope can point, in arcseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '0.45'.
Telescopes.PowerStatus: Full name: 'Power Supply Status'. Explanation: Indicates which power source or level is in use. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Backup, Critical, Main.
Telescopes.ProcQueueStatus: Full name: 'Processing Queue Status'. Explanation: Indicates how full the processing queue is. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Empty, Full, Normal.
Telescopes.TelescRegistry: Full name: 'Telescope Registry'. Explanation: A unique identifier for the telescope. Data type: CHAR(20). Example: 'TELESC_0001'.
Telescopes.TrackAccArc: Full name: 'Tracking Accuracy (arcsec)'. Explanation: How accurately the telescope can track a target, in arcseconds. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: '1.20'.

requests.specific_A: Among players who have at least one postseason batting record that is both in the NL (`league_id` = 'NL') and in the World Series (`round` = 'WS'), list each player's `player_id` and their total triples (`triple`) across all of their postseason batting records (ignoring missing values), sorted by that total from highest to lowest with missing totals last, and show the top 10.
requests.specific_B: Among players who have at least one postseason batting record in the NL (`league_id` = 'NL') and at least one postseason batting record in the World Series (`round` = 'WS'), not necessarily the same record, list each player's `player_id` and their total triples (`triple`) across all of their postseason batting records (ignoring missing values), sorted by that total from highest to lowest with missing totals last, and show the top 10.
requests.open: Which players with NL and World Series postseason batting records have the most postseason triples? Show each player's `player_id` and their total `triple` across all of their postseason batting records (ignoring missing values), highest first with missing totals last, top 10.

readings.A: Players with at least one postseason batting record that is both NL and World Series.
readings.B: Players with an NL postseason batting record and a World Series postseason batting record, which may be different records.

sql.A: SELECT "batting_postseason"."player_id" AS "e", SUM("batting_postseason"."triple") AS "m1" FROM "batting_postseason" AS "batting_postseason" WHERE "batting_postseason"."player_id" IN ((SELECT "x"."player_id" FROM "batting_postseason" AS "x" WHERE ("x"."league_id" = 'NL' AND "x"."round" = 'WS' AND NOT ("x"."player_id" IS NULL)))) GROUP BY "batting_postseason"."player_id" ORDER BY SUM("batting_postseason"."triple") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: SELECT "batting_postseason"."player_id" AS "e", SUM("batting_postseason"."triple") AS "m1" FROM "batting_postseason" AS "batting_postseason" WHERE ("batting_postseason"."player_id" IN ((SELECT "x"."player_id" FROM "batting_postseason" AS "x" WHERE ("x"."league_id" = 'NL' AND NOT ("x"."player_id" IS NULL)))) AND "batting_postseason"."player_id" IN ((SELECT "x"."player_id" FROM "batting_postseason" AS "x" WHERE ("x"."round" = 'WS' AND NOT ("x"."player_id" IS NULL))))) GROUP BY "batting_postseason"."player_id" ORDER BY SUM("batting_postseason"."triple") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Use `batting_postseason` records. A player's triples total covers all of that player's postseason batting records, not only the ones that qualify the player.

Keep a player only if their `player_id` is not missing and they have postseason batting with `league_id` = 'NL' (exact text match) and with `round` = 'WS' (exact text match). How these two conditions combine is the open choice.
One result row per player (`player_id`).
The player's `player_id`.
The sum of `triple` over all of the player's postseason batting records. Missing values are ignored, and the sum is missing if every value is missing. No rounding.
Sort by the triples total, highest first, with missing totals last.
Keep only the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: At least one single record has both `league_id` = 'NL' and `round` = 'WS'.

B.requirement: The player has some record with `league_id` = 'NL' and some record with `round` = 'WS'. These can be different records.

requests.specific_A: Counting customers per `SupportRepId` value that appears on customer records (with customers that have no rep forming one group), what is the average number of customers per value? Don't round.
requests.specific_B: Counting, for every employee, the customers whose `SupportRepId` is that employee (zero for employees with none), what is the average number of customers per employee? Don't round.
requests.open: On average, how many customers does each support rep look after? Don't round.

readings.A: Average the customer counts over only the support-rep values that actually appear on customer records.
readings.B: Average the customer counts over every employee, with employees who have no customers counted as zero.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Customer"."SupportRepId" AS "e", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "Customer" AS "Customer" GROUP BY "Customer"."SupportRepId") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1" FROM "s1" AS "s1"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Employee"."EmployeeId" AS "e", COUNT("Customer"."CustomerId") AS "m1" FROM "Employee" AS "Employee" LEFT JOIN "Customer" AS "Customer" ON "Customer"."SupportRepId" = "Employee"."EmployeeId" GROUP BY "Employee"."EmployeeId") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1" FROM "s1" AS "s1"

shared_requirements.requirement: Count customers by the support rep assigned to them (`Customer.SupportRepId`).
Combine the per-rep counts into a single result row.
The only output: the average of the per-rep customer counts, not rounded.

A.requirement: Make one group per distinct `SupportRepId` value found among customers (a missing value forms its own group). Employees with no customers do not appear.

B.requirement: Make one group per employee, counting the customers whose `SupportRepId` equals that `EmployeeId`. Employees with no customers count as 0.

For each driver, show the driver ID, the average points, the average wins, and the driver's average wins minus that overall mean. Return the 10 drivers with the largest difference, largest first, with missing differences last, unrounded.

readings.A: Per-driver averages are computed over standings records with points at least 1.0, counting records at exactly 1.0.

Ignore missing values in every average, return nothing if that overall mean is missing, and don't round.
requests.specific_B: Using laboratory tests dated strictly after 1985-04-22 and strictly before 1994-03-14 (comparing the `Date` text as stored), for each anti-centromere status (`CENTROMEA`, with a missing status as its own group), give the status, the average hemoglobin (`HGB`), the average of each test's total bilirubin-to-creatinine ratio (`T-BIL` ÷ `CRE`), and that average ratio divided by the plain mean of all the statuses' average ratios. Ignore missing values in every average, return nothing if that overall mean is missing, and don't round.
requests.open: For laboratory tests between 1985-04-22 and 1994-03-14 (comparing the `Date` text as stored), what is the average hemoglobin (`HGB`) and the average total bilirubin-to-creatinine ratio (`T-BIL` ÷ `CRE`, per test) for each anti-centromere status (`CENTROMEA`, with a missing status as its own group)? Also give each status's average ratio divided by the plain mean of all the statuses' average ratios. Ignore missing values in the averages, return nothing if that overall mean is missing, and don't round.

readings.A: Lab tests dated on 1985-04-22 or on 1994-03-14 are included in the range, along with every test between them.
readings.B: Only lab tests dated strictly after 1985-04-22 and strictly before 1994-03-14 are used. Tests on either end date are left out.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Laboratory"."CENTROMEA" AS "g", AVG("Laboratory"."HGB") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("Laboratory"."T-BIL" AS REAL) / "Laboratory"."CRE")) AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" WHERE ("Laboratory"."Date" >= '1985-04-22' AND "Laboratory"."Date" <= '1994-03-14') GROUP BY "Laboratory"."CENTROMEA"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Laboratory"."CENTROMEA" AS "g", AVG("Laboratory"."HGB") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("Laboratory"."T-BIL" AS REAL) / "Laboratory"."CRE")) AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" WHERE ("Laboratory"."Date" > '1985-04-22' AND "Laboratory"."Date" < '1994-03-14') GROUP BY "Laboratory"."CENTROMEA"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)

Then return one row with the average of those per-item average ratios (ignoring missing ones) and the average of those per-item line-item counts.
requests.specific_B: For every order item in `Order_Items`, including those with no invoice line items (which count as zero line items), take the average of `product_price` divided by `derived_total_cost` across its invoice line items (skipping missing ratios), and count its invoice line items. Then return one row with the average of those per-item average ratios (ignoring missing ones) and the average of those per-item line-item counts.
requests.open: Per order item, work out the average of `product_price` ÷ `derived_total_cost` over its invoice line items (skipping missing ratios) and how many invoice line items it has. In a single row, what are the overall average of those per-item ratios (ignoring missing ones) and the average number of invoice line items per order item?

readings.A: Average over only the order items that have invoice line items.
readings.B: Average over all order items. Those with no invoice line items contribute a count of zero and no ratio.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Invoice_Line_Items"."order_item_id" AS "e", AVG((CAST("Invoice_Line_Items"."product_price" AS REAL) / "Invoice_Line_Items"."derived_total_cost")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "Invoice_Line_Items" AS "Invoice_Line_Items" GROUP BY "Invoice_Line_Items"."order_item_id") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Order_Items"."order_item_id" AS "e", AVG((CAST("Invoice_Line_Items"."product_price" AS REAL) / "Invoice_Line_Items"."derived_total_cost")) AS "m1", COUNT("Invoice_Line_Items"."order_item_id") AS "m2" FROM "Order_Items" AS "Order_Items" LEFT JOIN "Invoice_Line_Items" AS "Invoice_Line_Items" ON "Invoice_Line_Items"."order_item_id" = "Order_Items"."order_item_id" GROUP BY "Order_Items"."order_item_id") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"

Combine all the per-order-item rows into a single result row.
First column: the average of the per-order-item average ratios. Missing values are ignored.

requests.specific_A: Considering only transactions whose amount (`trans.amount`) is at least 2400, group them by operation (`trans.operation`), with transactions that have no operation forming their own group. For each group, show the operation; the average signed amount, where the amount counts as positive for credits (`trans.type` = 'PRIJEM'), as negative for withdrawals (`trans.type` = 'VYDAJ'), and is left out of the average for any other type; and the total number of transactions in the group, of any type.
requests.specific_B: Considering only transactions whose amount (`trans.amount`) is greater than 2400, group them by operation (`trans.operation`), with transactions that have no operation forming their own group. For each group, show the operation; the average signed amount, where the amount counts as positive for credits (`trans.type` = 'PRIJEM'), as negative for withdrawals (`trans.type` = 'VYDAJ'), and is left out of the average for any other type; and the total number of transactions in the group, of any type.
requests.open: Treating 2400 as the cutoff for a large transaction amount (`trans.amount`), break the large transactions down by operation (`trans.operation`), with transactions that have no operation as their own group. For each group, show the operation; the average signed amount, positive for credits (`trans.type` = 'PRIJEM') and negative for withdrawals ('VYDAJ'), with any other type left out of the average; and how many large transactions the group has in total, of any type.

readings.A: Only transactions with an amount of 2400 or more count, so an amount of exactly 2400 is included.
readings.B: Only transactions with an amount strictly greater than 2400 count, so an amount of exactly 2400 is excluded.

sql.A: SELECT "trans"."operation" AS "g", AVG(CASE WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('PRIJEM') THEN "trans"."amount" WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('VYDAJ') THEN (0 - "trans"."amount") END) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "trans" AS "trans" WHERE "trans"."amount" >= 2400 GROUP BY "trans"."operation"
sql.B: SELECT "trans"."operation" AS "g", AVG(CASE WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('PRIJEM') THEN "trans"."amount" WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('VYDAJ') THEN (0 - "trans"."amount") END) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "trans" AS "trans" WHERE "trans"."amount" > 2400 GROUP BY "trans"."operation"

shared_requirements.requirement: start from individual transaction records in `trans`
group the kept transactions by `trans.operation`; transactions with a missing operation form their own group
first column: the operation (`trans.operation`)

second column: average signed amount, not rounded: +amount when `trans.type` = 'PRIJEM', −amount when `trans.type` = 'VYDAJ', and any other type (e.g. VYBER or missing) left out of the average; missing if no such values
third column: the number of kept transactions in the group, of any type

A.requirement: keep transactions with `trans.amount` >= 2400 (amounts of exactly 2400 count)

B.requirement: keep transactions with `trans.amount` > 2400 (amounts of exactly 2400 are excluded)

Show patient `ID`, average uric acid (`UA`) and average hematocrit, highest hematocrit first, with patients who have no hematocrit values last. Averages ignore missing values. Don't round.

requests.open: Looking only at patients without a rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result of '-' in their lab tests, which 10 have the highest average hematocrit (`HCT`) across all their lab records? Show patient `ID`, average uric acid (`UA`) and average hematocrit, highest first, with patients who have no hematocrit values last. Ignore missing values in the averages and don't round.

readings.A: Patients none of whose lab records has an RA result of '-'.
readings.B: Patients who have at least one lab record with a recorded RA result other than '-'.

sql.A: SELECT "Laboratory"."ID" AS "e", AVG("Laboratory"."UA") AS "m1", AVG("Laboratory"."HCT") AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" WHERE "Laboratory"."ID" NOT IN ((SELECT "x"."ID" FROM "Laboratory" AS "x" WHERE ("x"."RA" = '-' AND NOT ("x"."ID" IS NULL)))) GROUP BY "Laboratory"."ID" ORDER BY AVG("Laboratory"."HCT") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: SELECT "Laboratory"."ID" AS "e", AVG("Laboratory"."UA") AS "m1", AVG("Laboratory"."HCT") AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" WHERE "Laboratory"."ID" IN ((SELECT "x"."ID" FROM "Laboratory" AS "x" WHERE ("x"."RA" != '-' AND NOT ("x"."ID" IS NULL)))) GROUP BY "Laboratory"."ID" ORDER BY AVG("Laboratory"."HCT") DESC LIMIT 10

Choose patients by whether their lab records have a rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result of exactly the text '-'. Once a patient qualifies, keep all of that patient's lab records for the averages.
Make one result row per patient (`Laboratory.ID`).
Show the patient `ID`.
Show the average uric acid (`UA`) over the patient's kept records. Ignore missing values and do not round.
Show the average hematocrit (`HCT`) over the patient's kept records. Ignore missing values and do not round.
Sort by average hematocrit, highest first. Put patients with no hematocrit values last.
Keep only the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: Keep a patient only if none of their lab records has `RA` = '-'. Patients whose `RA` is always missing still qualify.

B.requirement: Keep a patient only if at least one of their lab records has an `RA` value that is recorded and is not '-'.

requests.specific_A: Match each order execution to its order (where the order's `recordvault` equals the execution's `ordersmark`, and executions without a matching order are dropped). Keep only executions whose expiry time (`expirespot`) falls between '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533', with both endpoints included (comparing the values as text). Group them by order reference (`ordersmark`) and order status (`orderflow`), and compute each group's average filled quantity (`fillcount`, ignoring missing values). Then give me a single value: the average of those per-group averages (ignoring missing ones), without rounding.
requests.specific_B: Match each order execution to its order (where the order's `recordvault` equals the execution's `ordersmark`, and executions without a matching order are dropped). Keep only executions whose expiry time (`expirespot`) falls between '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533', with both endpoints excluded (comparing the values as text). Group them by order reference (`ordersmark`) and order status (`orderflow`), and compute each group's average filled quantity (`fillcount`, ignoring missing values). Then give me a single value: the average of those per-group averages (ignoring missing ones), without rounding.
requests.open: For order executions that have a matching order (where the order's `recordvault` equals the execution's `ordersmark`; drop executions with no match) and an expiry time (`expirespot`) between '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' (comparing the values as text), group them by order reference (`ordersmark`) and order status (`orderflow`), and work out each group's average filled quantity (`fillcount`, ignoring missing values). What is the average of those per-group averages (ignoring missing ones), without rounding?

readings.A: Executions whose expiry time is exactly equal to either the start or the end bound of the window are included before grouping by order and status.
readings.B: Executions whose expiry time is exactly equal to either the start or the end bound of the window are excluded, so only expiry times strictly between the two bounds count.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orderexecutions"."ordersmark" AS "e", "orders"."orderflow" AS "g", AVG("orderexecutions"."fillcount") AS "m1" FROM "orderexecutions" AS "orderexecutions" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "orderexecutions"."ordersmark" WHERE ("orderexecutions"."expirespot" >= '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND "orderexecutions"."expirespot" <= '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533') GROUP BY "orderexecutions"."ordersmark", "orders"."orderflow") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1" FROM "s1" AS "s1"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "orderexecutions"."ordersmark" AS "e", "orders"."orderflow" AS "g", AVG("orderexecutions"."fillcount") AS "m1" FROM "orderexecutions" AS "orderexecutions" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "orderexecutions"."ordersmark" WHERE ("orderexecutions"."expirespot" > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND "orderexecutions"."expirespot" < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533') GROUP BY "orderexecutions"."ordersmark", "orders"."orderflow") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1" FROM "s1" AS "s1"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the order execution records (`orderexecutions`) and match each one to its order in `orders`, where `orders.recordvault` equals `orderexecutions.ordersmark` (compared as text). Each match gives one combined record, and executions with no matching order are dropped (inner join)
Keep only combined records whose execution expiry time (`expirespot`) lies in the window from '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' to '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533', compared as text, character by character
Group the kept records by order reference (`ordersmark`) and order status (`orders.orderflow`). Each group makes one intermediate row
For each group, compute the average filled quantity (`fillcount`), ignoring missing values (missing if the group has none)
Combine all intermediate rows into a single summary row
Only output column: the average of the per-group average filled quantities, ignoring missing ones (missing if there are none), not rounded

A.requirement: Both window endpoints are included: expirespot >= '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and expirespot <= '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533'

B.requirement: Both window endpoints are excluded: expirespot > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and expirespot < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533'

requests.specific_A: Across the invoices that have at least one line item, what is the average of each invoice's mean line-item `product_price` (missing prices ignored; an invoice with no non-missing price has no mean and is skipped), and what is the average number of line items per invoice? Return a single row with these two values, unrounded.
requests.specific_B: Across all invoices, including those with no line items, what is the average of each invoice's mean line-item `product_price` (missing prices ignored; an invoice with no non-missing price has no mean and is skipped), and what is the average number of line items per invoice, with an invoice that has no line items counting as zero? Return a single row with these two values, unrounded.
requests.open: Per invoice, what is the average of the invoice's mean line-item `product_price` (missing prices ignored; an invoice with no non-missing price has no mean and is skipped), and what is the average number of line items on an invoice? Return a single row with these two values, unrounded.

readings.A: Only invoices that have line items are averaged over.
readings.B: All invoices are averaged over. Invoices without line items count as having zero line items and have no mean price.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Invoice_Line_Items"."invoice_number" AS "e", AVG("Invoice_Line_Items"."product_price") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "Invoice_Line_Items" AS "Invoice_Line_Items" GROUP BY "Invoice_Line_Items"."invoice_number") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Invoices"."invoice_number" AS "e", AVG("Invoice_Line_Items"."product_price") AS "m1", COUNT("Invoice_Line_Items"."order_item_id") AS "m2" FROM "Invoices" AS "Invoices" LEFT JOIN "Invoice_Line_Items" AS "Invoice_Line_Items" ON "Invoice_Line_Items"."invoice_number" = "Invoices"."invoice_number" GROUP BY "Invoices"."invoice_number") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"

shared_requirements.requirement: Invoice line items (`Invoice_Line_Items` rows) are the records, grouped per invoice by `invoice_number`.
Each invoice gets two figures: the mean of its line items' `product_price` and its number of line items.
Missing `product_price` values are left out of an invoice's mean. If an invoice has no non-missing price, its mean is missing.
All the per-invoice figures are combined into one result row.
First column: the average, across invoices, of the per-invoice mean `product_price`. Invoices whose mean is missing are skipped. Not rounded.
Second column: the average, across invoices, of the per-invoice line-item count. Not rounded.

A.requirement: Only invoices that have at least one line item count, i.e. invoice numbers that appear in `Invoice_Line_Items`.
The line-item count is averaged only over invoices that have line items.

B.requirement: Every invoice in `Invoices` counts, including invoices with no line items.
An invoice with no line items counts as 0 and is included in the average count. It has no mean price, so it is skipped for output 1.

requests.specific_A: Take the payments of at least 4.99 that can be linked to a rental and, through that rental, to an inventory item (leave out payments without such a match). For each rental and store (`inventory.store_id`), total the payment amounts and count the payments. Then for each store, show the store id, the average of those per-rental totals, and the average number of payments per rental (both unrounded, ignoring missing values).
requests.specific_B: Take the payments of more than 4.99 that can be linked to a rental and, through that rental, to an inventory item (leave out payments without such a match). For each rental and store (`inventory.store_id`), total the payment amounts and count the payments. Then for each store, show the store id, the average of those per-rental totals, and the average number of payments per rental (both unrounded, ignoring missing values).
requests.open: Applying a 4.99 cutoff on the payment amount, take the qualifying payments that can be linked to a rental and, through that rental, to an inventory item (leave out payments without such a match). For each rental and store (`inventory.store_id`), total the payment amounts and count the payments. Then for each store, show the store id, the average of those per-rental totals, and the average number of payments per rental (both unrounded, ignoring missing values).

readings.A: Payments of exactly 4.99 are included along with larger ones.
readings.B: Only payments larger than 4.99 are included. Payments of exactly 4.99 are left out.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "payment"."rental_id" AS "e", "inventory"."store_id" AS "g", SUM("payment"."amount") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "payment" AS "payment" INNER JOIN "rental" AS "rental" ON "rental"."rental_id" = "payment"."rental_id" INNER JOIN "inventory" AS "inventory" ON "inventory"."inventory_id" = "rental"."inventory_id" WHERE "payment"."amount" >= 4.99 GROUP BY "payment"."rental_id", "inventory"."store_id") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "payment"."rental_id" AS "e", "inventory"."store_id" AS "g", SUM("payment"."amount") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "payment" AS "payment" INNER JOIN "rental" AS "rental" ON "rental"."rental_id" = "payment"."rental_id" INNER JOIN "inventory" AS "inventory" ON "inventory"."inventory_id" = "rental"."inventory_id" WHERE "payment"."amount" > 4.99 GROUP BY "payment"."rental_id", "inventory"."store_id") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from payments. Link each payment to its rental (`rental.rental_id` = `payment.rental_id`) and then to that rental's inventory item (`inventory.inventory_id` = `rental.inventory_id`). Drop any payment that has no matching rental or inventory item.
Keep payments by comparing `payment.amount` with the value 4.99. Whether an amount of exactly 4.99 counts is the choice.

Intermediate step: for each combination of rental (`payment.rental_id`) and store (`inventory.store_id`), compute the sum of the kept payment amounts (ignoring missing values) and the number of kept payments.
Group those per-rental rows by store id.
First column: the store id.
Second column: the average of the per-rental summed amounts, unrounded and ignoring missing values.
Third column: the average of the per-rental payment counts, unrounded and ignoring missing values.

A.requirement: Keep payments with an amount of at least 4.99, so an amount of exactly 4.99 counts.

B.requirement: Keep only payments with an amount above 4.99, so an amount of exactly 4.99 is left out.

Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate), AVG(length), AVG(replacement_cost) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '3.0348430493273613', '120.4439461883408', '20.402556053811544'], ['NC-17', '210', '2.970952380952388', '113.22857142857143', '20.137619047618937'], ['R', '195', '2.9387179487179553', '118.66153846153846', '20.23102564102554'], ['PG', '194', '3.051855670103099', '112.00515463917526', '18.959072164948356'], ['G', '178', '2.888876404494388', '111.0505617977528', '20.12483146067407']] scale (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows exactly 5 levels: G, PG, PG-13, R and NC-17. These are the standard MPAA bands, which are ordered by audience restriction, so the column is an ordinal class. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY rating -> [['G', '178'], ['NC-17', '210'], ['PG', '194'], ['PG-13', '223'], ['R', '195']]
category.name: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 16 genres, each shared by many films (about 50-75 each), so the column is a grouping label and does not identify single records. Evidence: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film_category fc JOIN category c ON c.category_id = fc.category_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY films DESC -> [['Sports', '74'], ['Foreign', '73'], ['Family', '69'], ['Documentary', '68'], ['Animation', '66'], ['Action', '64']]
customer.store_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 2 stores with about 300 customers each, so the column is a grouping label shared by many rows. inventory.store_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 2 store values over 4581 copies, about 2270 per store, so the column is a grouping label. Evidence: SELECT co.country, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customer cu JOIN address a ON a.address_id = cu.address_id JOIN city ci ON ci.city_id = a.city_id JOIN country co ON co.country_id = ci.country_id GROUP BY co.country ORDER BY customers DESC LIMIT 10 -> [['India', '60'], ['China', '53'], ['United States', '36'], ['Japan', '31'], ['Mexico', '30'], ['Russian Federation', '28']]

The column is a set, not a single category. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']] semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows 15 distinct values, all combinations of the same 4 feature names, such as 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes' and 'Trailers,Commentaries'. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']]

The catalogue profile gives 140 distinct values from 46 to 185 minutes. So length is a continuous ratio-scale quantity whose group averages can be read directly. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(length) AS avg_minutes, MIN(length), MAX(length) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '120.4439461883408', '46', '185'], ['NC-17', '210', '113.22857142857143', '46', '184'], ['R', '195', '118.66153846153846', '49', '185'], ['PG', '194', '112.00515463917526', '46', '185'], ['G', '178', '111.0505617977528', '47', '185']]

requests.specific_A: Take the scans whose timestamp (`chronotag`, compared as text) is from '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274' through '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797', with both endpoints included, and keep only scans that match a site by site code. Group them by scan zone reference (`zoneref`) and site type (`typesite`). For each group, work out the average compression ratio (`pressratio`) and the average of file size divided by scan duration (`gbsize` / `spanmin`), ignoring missing values. Then give me one row with two unrounded values: the average of those per-group compression-ratio averages and the average of the per-group size-per-minute averages.
requests.specific_B: Take the scans whose timestamp (`chronotag`, compared as text) is strictly after '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274' and strictly before '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797', with both endpoints excluded, and keep only scans that match a site by site code. Group them by scan zone reference (`zoneref`) and site type (`typesite`). For each group, work out the average compression ratio (`pressratio`) and the average of file size divided by scan duration (`gbsize` / `spanmin`), ignoring missing values. Then give me one row with two unrounded values: the average of those per-group compression-ratio averages and the average of the per-group size-per-minute averages.
requests.open: For scans taken between '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274' and '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797' (comparing the `chronotag` text), and only those linked to a site by site code, group by zone reference (`zoneref`) and site type (`typesite`). For each group, get the average compression ratio (`pressratio`) and the average of file size divided by scan duration (`gbsize` / `spanmin`), ignoring missing values. Then give me one row with two unrounded values: the average of the per-group compression-ratio averages and the average of the per-group size-per-minute averages.

readings.A: Scans whose timestamp equals either boundary value are counted.
readings.B: Scans whose timestamp equals either boundary value are left out. Only scans strictly between the two bounds count.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scans"."zoneref" AS "e", "sites"."typesite" AS "g", AVG("scans"."pressratio") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("scans"."gbsize" AS REAL) / "scans"."spanmin")) AS "m2" FROM "scans" AS "scans" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scans"."zoneref" WHERE ("scans"."chronotag" >= '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274' AND "scans"."chronotag" <= '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797') GROUP BY "scans"."zoneref", "sites"."typesite") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "scans"."zoneref" AS "e", "sites"."typesite" AS "g", AVG("scans"."pressratio") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("scans"."gbsize" AS REAL) / "scans"."spanmin")) AS "m2" FROM "scans" AS "scans" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scans"."zoneref" WHERE ("scans"."chronotag" > '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274' AND "scans"."chronotag" < '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797') GROUP BY "scans"."zoneref", "sites"."typesite") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from scans records and inner-join sites where sites.zoneregistry = scans.zoneref (text comparison). Scans with no matching site are dropped.
Filter on scans.chronotag against the bounds '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274' and '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797', comparing the values as text, character by character.

Group the kept records by scans.zoneref and sites.typesite. For each group, compute the average of scans.pressratio and the average of scans.gbsize ÷ scans.spanmin. Missing values are ignored, and the result is missing when a group has no values.
Combine all of the per-group rows into a single result row.
Column 1 is the average, across groups, of the per-group average compression ratio. Missing values are ignored. No rounding.
Column 2 is the average, across groups, of the per-group average of file size per minute of scan duration (gbsize/spanmin). Missing values are ignored. No rounding.

A.requirement: Both bounds are inclusive: chronotag >= start and chronotag <= end.

B.requirement: Both bounds are exclusive: chronotag > start and chronotag < end.
