  "crewlabel" text(50),
  "leadregistry" text(50),
  "leadlabel" text(40),
  CONSTRAINT "personnel_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("crewregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "projects" (
  "arcregistry" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "vesseltag" text(60),
  "fundflux" text,
  "authpin" text(50),
  "authhalt" text,
  CONSTRAINT "projects_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("arcregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanconservation" (
  "cureregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "arcref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "zoneref" text(12) NOT NULL,
  "harmassess" text(15),
  "curerank" text(15),
  "structstate" text(15),
  "intervhistory" text,
  "priordocs" text,
  CONSTRAINT "scanconservation_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("cureregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanconservation_arcref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("arcref") REFERENCES "projects" ("arcregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanconservation_zoneref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("zoneref") REFERENCES "sites" ("zoneregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanenvironment" (
  "airregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "zoneref" text(12) NOT NULL,
  "equipref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "ambictemp" real(5,2),
  "humepct" real(5,2),
  "illumelux" integer(32),
  "geosignal" text(15),
  "trackstatus" text(12),
  "linkstatus" text(12),
  "photomap" text(4),
  "imgcount" integer(16),
  CONSTRAINT "scanenvironment_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("airregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanenvironment_equipref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("equipref") REFERENCES "equipment" ("equipregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanenvironment_zoneref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("zoneref") REFERENCES "sites" ("zoneregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanfeatures" (
  "traitregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "zoneref" text(12) NOT NULL,
  "equipref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "traitextract" text(25),
  "traitcount" integer(32),
  "articount" integer(32),
  "structkind" text(15),
  "matkind" text(15),
  "huestudy" text(15),
  "texturestudy" text(15),
  "patternnote" text,
  CONSTRAINT "scanfeatures_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("traitregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanfeatures_equipref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("equipref") REFERENCES "equipment" ("equipregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanfeatures_zoneref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("zoneref") REFERENCES "sites" ("zoneregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanmesh" (
  "facetregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "zoneref" text(12) NOT NULL,
  "equipref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "facetverts" integer(64),
  "facetfaces" integer(64),
  "facetresmm" real(5,2),
  "texdist" text(5),
  "texpix" integer(32),
  "uvmapqual" text(50),
  "geomdeltamm" real(6,3),
  CONSTRAINT "scanmesh_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("facetregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanmesh_equipref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("equipref") REFERENCES "equipment" ("equipregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanmesh_zoneref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("zoneref") REFERENCES "sites" ("zoneregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanpointcloud" (
  "cloudregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "crewref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "arcref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "scanresolmm" real(5,2),
  "pointdense" integer(32),
  "coverpct" real(4,1),
  "totalpts" integer(64),
  "clouddense" integer(32),
  "lappct" real(4,1),
  "noisedb" real(6,3),
  "refpct" real(4,1),
  CONSTRAINT "scanpointcloud_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("cloudregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanpointcloud_arcref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("arcref") REFERENCES "projects" ("arcregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanpointcloud_crewref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("crewref") REFERENCES "personnel" ("crewregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanprocessing" (
  "flowregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "equipref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "zoneref" text(12) NOT NULL,
  "flowsoft" text(25),
  "flowhrs" real(5,2),
  "proccpu" integer(16),
  "memusagegb" real(6,2),
  "procgpu" integer(16),
  "stashloc" text(12),
  "safebak" text(50),
  "datalevel" text,
  "metabench" text(50),
  "coordframe" text(12),
  "elevref" text(16),
  "remaingb" real(7,2),
  "stationlink" text(50),
  "camcal" text,
  "lensdist" text(14),
  "colortune" text(50),
  "flowstage" text(18),
  "fmtver" text(3),
  CONSTRAINT "scanprocessing_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("flowregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanprocessing_equipref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("equipref") REFERENCES "equipment" ("equipregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanprocessing_zoneref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("zoneref") REFERENCES "sites" ("zoneregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanqc" (
  "qualregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "arcref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "crewref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "accucheck" text(22),
  "ctrlstate" text(50),
  "valimeth" text(18),
  "valistate" text,
  "archstat" text(50),
  "pubstat" text(24),
  "copystat" text(50),
  "refmention" text(60),
  "remark" text,
  CONSTRAINT "scanqc_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("qualregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanqc_arcref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("arcref") REFERENCES "projects" ("arcregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanqc_crewref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("crewref") REFERENCES "personnel" ("crewregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanregistration" (
  "logregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "crewref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "arcref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "logaccumm" real(5,3),
  "refmark" text(6),
  "ctrlpts" text(6),
  "logmethod" text(15),
  "transform" text(15),
  "errscale" text(20),
  "errvalmm" real(6,3),
  CONSTRAINT "scanregistration_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("logregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanregistration_arcref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("arcref") REFERENCES "projects" ("arcregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanregistration_crewref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("crewref") REFERENCES "personnel" ("crewregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scans" (
  "questregistry" text(16) NOT NULL,
  "chronotag" text(6),
  "arcref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "crewref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "zoneref" text(12) NOT NULL,
  "scancount" integer(16),
  "climtune" text(22),
  "huecatch" text(50),
  "fmtfile" text(4),
  "gbsize" real(5,2),
  "pressratio" real(4,2),
  "spanmin" real(5,2),
  CONSTRAINT "scans_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("questregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scans_arcref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("arcref") REFERENCES "projects" ("arcregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scans_crewref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("crewref") REFERENCES "personnel" ("crewregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scans_zoneref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("zoneref") REFERENCES "sites" ("zoneregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "scanspatial" (
  "domainregistry" integer(64) NOT NULL,
  "arcref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "crewref" text(50) NOT NULL,
  "aream2" real(8,3),
  "volm3" real(9,4),
  "boxx" real(8,2),
  "boxy" real(8,3),
  "boxz" real(9,2),
  "angleaz" integer(24),
  "angletilt" integer(53),
  "groundspan" real(6,3),
  CONSTRAINT "scanspatial_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("domainregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanspatial_arcref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("arcref") REFERENCES "projects" ("arcregistry"),
  CONSTRAINT "scanspatial_crewref_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("crewref") REFERENCES "personnel" ("crewregistry")
);
CREATE TABLE "sites" (
  "zoneregistry" text(12) NOT NULL,
  "zonelabel" text,
  "digunit" text(50),
  "gridtrace" text(12),
  "geox" real(8,5),
  "geoy" real(8,5),
  "heightm" real(7,1),
  "depthc" real(7,1),
  "phasefactor" text(25),
  "guessdate" text(20),
  "typesite" text(25),
  "presstat" text(25),
  "guardhint" text(50),
  "entrystat" text(50),
  "saferank" text(15),
  "insurstat" text(15),
  "riskeval" text,
  "healtheval" text(12),
  "envhaz" text(50),
  CONSTRAINT "sites_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("zoneregistry")
);
context.documentation:
Equipment.EquipDesign: Full name: 'Equipment Model'. Explanation: Model name or identifier. Data type: VARCHAR(14). Example: 'Model-669'.
Equipment.EquipForm: Full name: 'Equipment Type'. Explanation: Type or category of scanning equipment. Data type: VARCHAR(28). Possible categories: LiDAR, Structured Light, Photogrammetry, Laser.
Equipment.EquipRegistry: Full name: 'Equipment ID'. Explanation: Primary key for equipment. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
Equipment.EquipStatus: Full name: 'Equipment Condition'. Explanation: Overall condition of the equipment. Data type: VARCHAR(16). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor.
Equipment.EquipTune: Full name: 'Calibration Date'. Explanation: Date the equipment was last calibrated. Data type: DATE. Example: '2024-11-01'.
Equipment.PowerLevel: Full name: 'Battery Level (%)'. Explanation: Battery level as an integer percentage. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 62.
Personnel.CrewLabel: Full name: 'Operator Name'. Explanation: Name or label for the operator. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Example: 'Joel Wallace'.
Personnel.CrewRegistry: Full name: 'Operator ID'. Explanation: Primary key for Personnel, representing an operator. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
Personnel.LeadLabel: Full name: 'Supervisor Name'. Explanation: Name of the supervisor. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Example: 'Michael Kaiser'.
Personnel.LeadRegistry: Full name: 'Supervisor ID'. Explanation: Identifies a supervisor. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'SV7658'.
Projects.ArcRegistry: Full name: 'Project ID'. Explanation: Primary key for Projects, a unique project identifier. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
Projects.AuthHalt: Full name: 'Permit Expiry Date'. Explanation: Date on which the permit expires. Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-12-05'.
Projects.AuthPin: Full name: 'Permit Number'. Explanation: Authorization or permit ID. Data type: CHAR(6). Example: 'PMT4719'.
Projects.FundFlux: Full name: 'Funding Source'. Explanation: Source of funds for the project. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Government'.
Projects.VesselTag: Full name: 'Project Name'. Explanation: Label or name for the project. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Example: 'Project Happy'.
ScanConservation.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Associates conservation data with a project. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanConservation.CureRank: Full name: 'Conservation Priority'. Explanation: Priority level for conservation efforts. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Critical, Low, High.
ScanConservation.CureRegistry: Full name: 'Conservation Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for conservation data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 6001.
ScanConservation.HarmAssess: Full name: 'Damage Assessment'. Explanation: Indicates severity of damage. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: None, Moderate, Severe.
ScanConservation.IntervHistory: Full name: 'Intervention History'. Explanation: Past restoration or intervention records. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: None, Major, Minor.
ScanConservation.PriorDocs: Full name: 'Previous Documentation'. Explanation: Level of existing documentation. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: None, Partial, Complete.
ScanConservation.StructState: Full name: 'Structural Stability'. Explanation: Stability level of the structure. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Stable, Moderate, Unstable.
ScanConservation.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Associates conservation data with a site code. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanEnvironment.AirRegistry: Full name: 'Environment Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for environment data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 1001.
ScanEnvironment.AmbicTemp: Full name: 'Ambient Temperature (C)'. Explanation: Air temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 25.3.
ScanEnvironment.EquipRef: Full name: 'Equipment Reference'. Explanation: Identifies which equipment these environment data refer to. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
ScanEnvironment.GeoSignal: Full name: 'GPS Signal Quality'. Explanation: Quality rating for GPS reception. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: None, Poor, Good, Excellent.
ScanEnvironment.HumePct: Full name: 'Relative Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 60.4.
ScanEnvironment.IllumeLux: Full name: 'Light Conditions (lux)'. Explanation: Measured illumination in lux. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 86054.
ScanEnvironment.ImgCount: Full name: 'Number of Images'. Explanation: How many images were taken for photogrammetry. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 248.
ScanEnvironment.LinkStatus: Full name: 'Network Status'. Explanation: Status of network connectivity. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Possible categories: Disconnected, Connected.
ScanEnvironment.PhotoMap: Full name: 'Photogrammetry Overlap'. Explanation: Percentage overlap for photogrammetry images. Data type: CHAR(4). Possible categories: 80%, 60%, 90%.
ScanEnvironment.TrackStatus: Full name: 'RTK Status'. Explanation: Real-Time Kinematic correction state. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Possible categories: None, Fixed.
ScanEnvironment.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Links environment conditions to a specific site code. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanFeatures.ArtiCount: Full name: 'Artifact Count'. Explanation: Number of artifacts recognized. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 71.
ScanFeatures.EquipRef: Full name: 'Equipment Reference'. Explanation: Equipment ID used to detect these features. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
ScanFeatures.HueStudy: Full name: 'Color Analysis'. Explanation: Status of color analysis (done or pending). Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Partial, Completed, Not Required.
ScanFeatures.MatKind: Full name: 'Material Type'. Explanation: Primary composition or material. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Organic, Metal, Mixed, Ceramic, Stone.
ScanFeatures.PatternNote: Full name: 'Pattern Recognition'. Explanation: Notes regarding detected patterns. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Not Required, None, Partial.
ScanFeatures.StructKind: Full name: 'Structure Type'. Explanation: Type of structural element. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Artifact, Complex, Wall, Foundation.
ScanFeatures.TextureStudy: Full name: 'Texture Analysis'. Explanation: Status of texture analysis. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Partial, Completed, Not Required.
ScanFeatures.TraitCount: Full name: 'Number of Detected Features'. Explanation: How many features were identified. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 516.
ScanFeatures.TraitExtract: Full name: 'Feature Extraction Method'. Explanation: Method used to extract features (manual or automated). Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Manual, Semi-automatic, Automatic.
ScanFeatures.TraitRegistry: Full name: 'Feature Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for feature data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 5001.
ScanFeatures.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Site code tied to these features. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanMesh.EquipRef: Full name: 'Equipment Reference'. Explanation: Identifies which equipment was used to generate the mesh. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
ScanMesh.FacetFaces: Full name: 'Mesh Faces'. Explanation: Count of triangular or polygonal faces. Data type: BIGINT. Example: 5997318.
ScanMesh.FacetRegistry: Full name: 'Mesh Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for mesh data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 3001.
ScanMesh.FacetResMm: Full name: 'Mesh Resolution (mm)'. Explanation: Mesh vertex spacing in mm. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 3.2.
ScanMesh.FacetVerts: Full name: 'Mesh Vertices'. Explanation: Count of mesh vertices. Data type: BIGINT. Example: 7234721.
ScanMesh.GeomDeltaMm: Full name: 'Geometric Accuracy (mm)'. Explanation: Estimated geometric deviation in millimeters. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: 2.74.
ScanMesh.TexDist: Full name: 'Texture Resolution Setting'. Explanation: Preset texture resolution. Data type: VARCHAR(5). Possible categories: 2K, 1K, 4K.
ScanMesh.TexPix: Full name: 'Texture Size (px)'. Explanation: Texture image dimension in pixels. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 2048.
ScanMesh.UVMapQual: Full name: 'UV Mapping Quality'. Explanation: Quality of the UV mapping process. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Possible categories: Medium, High, Low.
ScanMesh.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Associates mesh data with a site code. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanPointCloud.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Project ID associated with this point cloud. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanPointCloud.CloudDense: Full name: 'Point-Cloud Density Code'. Explanation: A numeric code classifying point density. Data type: INTEGER. Possible categories: 9449, 431, 7553, 1746.
ScanPointCloud.CloudRegistry: Full name: 'Point Cloud Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for point cloud data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 2001.
ScanPointCloud.CoverPct: Full name: 'Coverage (%)'. Explanation: Surface coverage percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(4,1). Example: 91.2.
ScanPointCloud.CrewRef: Full name: 'Operator Reference'. Explanation: Which operator is linked to this point cloud. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
ScanPointCloud.LapPct: Full name: 'Overlap (%)'. Explanation: Overlap percentage among multiple scans. Data type: NUMERIC(4,1). Example: 31.3.
ScanPointCloud.NoiseDb: Full name: 'Noise Level (dB)'. Explanation: Measured noise in decibels. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: 1.318.
ScanPointCloud.PointDense: Full name: 'Point Density (points/m²)'. Explanation: Density of points per square meter. Data type: INTEGER. Example: 42812.
ScanPointCloud.RefPct: Full name: 'Surface Reflectivity (%)'. Explanation: Reflectivity percentage of scanned surfaces. Data type: NUMERIC(4,1). Example: 65.4.
ScanPointCloud.ScanResolMm: Full name: 'Scan Resolution (mm)'. Explanation: Resolution of points in millimeters. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 2.4.
ScanPointCloud.TotalPts: Full name: 'Total Points'. Explanation: Overall number of points in the cloud. Data type: BIGINT. Example: 46562436.
ScanProcessing.CamCal: Full name: 'Camera Calibration Status'. Explanation: Whether camera calibration is completed or pending. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Required'.
ScanProcessing.ColorTune: Full name: 'Color Balance Status'. Explanation: Indicates color adjustment requirement. Data type: CHAR(10). Possible categories: Required, Adjusted.
ScanProcessing.CoordFrame: Full name: 'Coordinate System'. Explanation: Defines spatial reference frame. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Possible categories: Local, WGS84, Custom.
ScanProcessing.DataLevel: Full name: 'Data Access Level'. Explanation: Access restrictions or sharing level. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Confidential, Public, Restricted.
ScanProcessing.ElevRef: Full name: 'Elevation Reference'. Explanation: Reference for altitude or elevation. Data type: VARCHAR(16). Possible categories: Arbitrary, Sea Level, Local.
ScanProcessing.EquipRef: Full name: 'Equipment Reference'. Explanation: Equipment ID used for processing. Data type: CHAR(10). Example: 'SN20065'.
ScanProcessing.FlowHrs: Full name: 'Processing Time (hours)'. Explanation: Time spent on processing. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: 21.9.
ScanProcessing.FlowRegistry: Full name: 'Processing Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for processing workflow. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 8001.
ScanProcessing.FlowSoft: Full name: 'Processing Software'. Explanation: Name of the software used. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: RealityCapture, CloudCompare, Agisoft.
ScanProcessing.FlowStage: Full name: 'Processing Stage'. Explanation: Current stage of the processing workflow. Data type: VARCHAR(18). Possible categories: Aligned, Meshed, Final.
ScanProcessing.FmtVer: Full name: 'Export Format Version'. Explanation: Version tag for exported files. Data type: CHAR(3). Possible categories: 2.3, 2.7, 4.0, 1.1.
ScanProcessing.LensDist: Full name: 'Lens Distortion Status'. Explanation: Whether lens distortion is corrected or unknown. Data type: VARCHAR(14). Possible categories: Corrected, Unknown.
ScanProcessing.MemUsageGb: Full name: 'Memory Usage (GB)'. Explanation: RAM usage during processing. Data type: NUMERIC(6,2). Example: 70.3.
ScanProcessing.MetaBench: Full name: 'Metadata Standard'. Explanation: Which metadata framework is applied. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Possible categories: Dublin Core, CIDOC CRM, Custom.
ScanProcessing.ProcCPU: Full name: 'CPU Usage (%)'. Explanation: CPU usage as an integer percentage. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 81.
ScanProcessing.ProcGPU: Full name: 'GPU Usage (%)'. Explanation: GPU usage as an integer percentage. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: 56.
ScanProcessing.RemainGb: Full name: 'Remaining Storage (GB)'. Explanation: Remaining disk or cloud space. Data type: NUMERIC(7,2). Example: 983.5.
ScanProcessing.SafeBak: Full name: 'Backup Status'. Explanation: Indicates progress of data backup. Data type: CHAR(8). Possible categories: In Progress, Completed, Pending.
ScanProcessing.StashLoc: Full name: 'Storage Location'. Explanation: Where processed data is stored. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Possible categories: Local, Network, Cloud.
ScanProcessing.StationLink: Full name: 'Total Station Integration'. Explanation: Indicates if total station integration is used. Data type: CHAR(6). Example: 'Yes'.
ScanProcessing.ZoneRef: Full name: 'Site Reference'. Explanation: Site code for which processing applies. Data type: VARCHAR(12). Example: 'SC9016'.
ScanQC.AccuCheck: Full name: 'Accuracy Assessment'. Explanation: Indicates if accuracy check was done. Data type: VARCHAR(22). Possible categories: Pending, Completed, Not Required.
ScanQC.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Points to a project for QC. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanQC.ArchStat: Full name: 'Archival Status'. Explanation: Indicates if data is archived. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Possible categories: Verified, Pending.
ScanQC.CopyStat: Full name: 'Copyright Status'. Explanation: Copyright or licensing restriction. Data type: CHAR(10). Possible categories: Reserved, Restricted, Open Access.
ScanQC.CrewRef: Full name: 'Operator Reference'. Explanation: Identifies the operator associated with QC. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
ScanQC.CtrlState: Full name: 'Quality Control Status'. Explanation: State of QC checks. Data type: CHAR(10). Possible categories: Failed, Pending.
ScanQC.PubStat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether data is published, drafted, etc. Data type: VARCHAR(24). Possible categories: Draft, Submitted.
ScanQC.QualRegistry: Full name: 'QC Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for quality control records. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 9001.
ScanQC.RefMention: Full name: 'Data Citation'. Explanation: Reference or citation code for the data. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: Citation-8447, Citation-6197, Citation-8090, Citation-2238.
ScanQC.Remark: Full name: 'Additional Notes'. Explanation: Any free-text remarks or comments. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Sell shoulder understand serious degree particular game.'
ScanQC.ValiMeth: Full name: 'Validation Method'. Explanation: How the data was validated (automated or manual). Data type: VARCHAR(18). Possible categories: Automated, Visual.
ScanQC.ValiState: Full name: 'Validation Status'. Explanation: Final status of validation. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Rejected, Approved.
ScanRegistration.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Project ID linked to registration data. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanRegistration.CrewRef: Full name: 'Operator Reference'. Explanation: Operator ID who performed registration. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
ScanRegistration.CtrlPts: Full name: 'Control Points'. Explanation: Numeric codes for control points. Data type: VARCHAR(6). Possible categories: 73, 99, 6, 84.
ScanRegistration.ErrScale: Full name: 'Error Metrics'. Explanation: Type of error measurement. Data type: VARCHAR(20). Possible categories: Cloud-to-Mesh, Cloud-to-Cloud, RMSE.
ScanRegistration.ErrValMm: Full name: 'Error Value (mm)'. Explanation: Measured error in millimeters. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: 6.962.
ScanRegistration.LogAccuMm: Full name: 'Registration Accuracy (mm)'. Explanation: Accuracy of the registration in mm. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: 0.84.
ScanRegistration.LogMethod: Full name: 'Registration Method'. Explanation: Method for aligning scans. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Target-based, Hybrid, Automatic.
ScanRegistration.LogRegistry: Full name: 'Registration Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for registration logs. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 7001.
ScanRegistration.RefMark: Full name: 'Reference Markers'. Explanation: Numeric codes for registration targets. Data type: VARCHAR(6). Possible categories: 40, 31, 25, 21.
ScanRegistration.TransForm: Full name: 'Transformation Matrix'. Explanation: Identifier for the transform matrix used. Data type: VARCHAR(15). Possible categories: Matrix-47, Matrix-113, Matrix-543.
ScanSpatial.AngleAz: Full name: 'Orientation (degrees)'. Explanation: Azimuth or rotation angle around vertical axis. Data type: REAL. Example: 342.4.
ScanSpatial.AngleTilt: Full name: 'Tilt Angle (degrees)'. Explanation: Inclination angle from horizontal. Data type: DOUBLE PRECISION. Example: 23.9.
ScanSpatial.ArcRef: Full name: 'Project Reference'. Explanation: Project ID linking spatial data. Data type: VARCHAR(10). Example: 'PR7509'.
ScanSpatial.AreaM2: Full name: 'Surface Area (m²)'. Explanation: Calculated area in square meters. Data type: NUMERIC(8,3). Example: 78.01.
ScanSpatial.BoxX: Full name: 'Bounding Box X (m)'. Explanation: Size of bounding box along X-axis, in meters. Data type: NUMERIC(8,2). Example: 40.12.
ScanSpatial.BoxY: Full name: 'Bounding Box Y (m)'. Explanation: Size of bounding box along Y-axis, in meters. Data type: NUMERIC(8,3). Example: 1.06.
ScanSpatial.BoxZ: Full name: 'Bounding Box Z (m)'. Explanation: Size of bounding box along Z-axis, in meters. Data type: NUMERIC(9,2). Example: 16.41.
ScanSpatial.CrewRef: Full name: 'Operator Reference'. Explanation: Operator ID for these spatial records. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: 'OP4641'.
ScanSpatial.DomainRegistry: Full name: 'Spatial Record ID'. Explanation: Primary key for spatial data. Data type: BIGSERIAL. Example: 4001.
ScanSpatial.GroundSpan: Full name: 'Ground Sampling Distance (mm)'. Explanation: Effective resolution on the ground, in mm. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: 4.13.

requests.specific_A: Only looking at accounts whose opening date (`account.date`, compared as text) is on or after 1994-06-17 and on or before 1996-09-02, how many such accounts are there in each region (`district.A3`) of the account's district? Count only accounts whose district appears in the district table, and show each region with its number of accounts.
requests.specific_B: Only looking at accounts whose opening date (`account.date`, compared as text) is strictly after 1994-06-17 and strictly before 1996-09-02, how many such accounts are there in each region (`district.A3`) of the account's district? Count only accounts whose district appears in the district table, and show each region with its number of accounts.
requests.open: Only looking at accounts whose opening date (`account.date`, compared as text) falls between 1994-06-17 and 1996-09-02, how many such accounts are there in each region (`district.A3`) of the account's district? Count only accounts whose district appears in the district table, and show each region with its number of accounts.

readings.A: Count accounts per region for accounts opened on any date from 1994-06-17 to 1996-09-02, with both end dates included.
readings.B: Count accounts per region for accounts opened strictly after 1994-06-17 and strictly before 1996-09-02, with both end dates excluded.

sql.A: SELECT "district"."A3" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "account" AS "account" INNER JOIN "district" AS "district" ON "district"."district_id" = "account"."district_id" WHERE ("account"."date" >= '1994-06-17' AND "account"."date" <= '1996-09-02') GROUP BY "district"."A3"
sql.B: SELECT "district"."A3" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "account" AS "account" INNER JOIN "district" AS "district" ON "district"."district_id" = "account"."district_id" WHERE ("account"."date" > '1994-06-17' AND "account"."date" < '1996-09-02') GROUP BY "district"."A3"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from account records; each account is one record.
Match each account to the district record whose `district.district_id` equals `account.district_id`. Drop accounts with no matching district (inner join).
Keep only accounts whose opening date (`account.date`) falls in the date window from 1994-06-17 to 1996-09-02. Compare the dates as text, character by character. This filter is required.
Group the kept records by region name (`district.A3`), one result row per region.
First output column: the region name (`district.A3`).
Second output column: the number of kept records (accounts) in the region, not rounded.

A.requirement: Both end dates are included: `account.date` >= '1994-06-17' and `account.date` <= '1996-09-02'.

B.requirement: Both end dates are excluded: `account.date` > '1994-06-17' and `account.date` < '1996-09-02'.

requests.specific_A: Looking only at standing orders (the `order` table) whose `amount` is at least 2802, and linking each order to its account and the account's district (dropping orders with no matching account or district), compute the average order `amount` for each combination of account (`order.account_id`) and region (`district.A3`). Then take the simple average of all those group averages. Show the 10 groups whose average exceeds that overall figure by the most: give the account id, the region, the group's average amount, and the difference (group average minus overall figure), sorted by that difference from largest to smallest, without rounding.
requests.specific_B: Looking only at standing orders (the `order` table) whose `amount` is greater than 2802, and linking each order to its account and the account's district (dropping orders with no matching account or district), compute the average order `amount` for each combination of account (`order.account_id`) and region (`district.A3`). Then take the simple average of all those group averages. Show the 10 groups whose average exceeds that overall figure by the most: give the account id, the region, the group's average amount, and the difference (group average minus overall figure), sorted by that difference from largest to smallest, without rounding.
requests.open: Treating an `amount` of 2802 as the cutoff for a large standing order (the `order` table), link each large order to its account and the account's district (dropping orders with no matching account or district), and compute the average order `amount` for each combination of account (`order.account_id`) and region (`district.A3`). Then take the simple average of all those group averages. Show the 10 groups whose average exceeds that overall figure by the most: give the account id, the region, the group's average amount, and the difference (group average minus overall figure), sorted by that difference from largest to smallest, without rounding.

readings.A: Standing orders with an amount of 2802 or more are used in the per-account averages and in the overall average.
readings.B: Only standing orders with an amount strictly greater than 2802 are used in the per-account averages and in the overall average.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "order"."account_id" AS "e", "district"."A3" AS "g", AVG("order"."amount") AS "m1" FROM "order" AS "order" INNER JOIN "account" AS "account" ON "account"."account_id" = "order"."account_id" INNER JOIN "district" AS "district" ON "district"."district_id" = "account"."district_id" WHERE "order"."amount" >= 2802.0 GROUP BY "order"."account_id", "district"."A3"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "order"."account_id" AS "e", "district"."A3" AS "g", AVG("order"."amount") AS "m1" FROM "order" AS "order" INNER JOIN "account" AS "account" ON "account"."account_id" = "order"."account_id" INNER JOIN "district" AS "district" ON "district"."district_id" = "account"."district_id" WHERE "order"."amount" > 2802.0 GROUP BY "order"."account_id", "district"."A3"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) ORDER BY ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Population is the standing orders in the `order` table, kept only if `order.amount` passes the 2802 threshold. The threshold's inclusiveness is the open choice.
Link each order to its account (`account.account_id` = `order.account_id`) and that account's district (`district.district_id` = `account.district_id`). Orders without a match are dropped.
First column: the account id `order.account_id`. Groups are formed by account id and region together.
Second column: the region `district.A3`.
Third column: the group's average `order.amount`, not rounded.
Fourth column: the group's average minus the overall average, which is the plain (unweighted) mean of all the group averages. Not rounded.
Sort by that difference, largest first.
Return only the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: An order whose amount is exactly 2802 is included (amount >= 2802).

B.requirement: An order whose amount is exactly 2802 is excluded (amount > 2802).

requests.specific_A: For transactions dated from 1996-05-09 through 1998-01-06, both dates included (comparing `trans.date` as text), link each transaction to its account and each account to its branch's district. Then give one row per region (`district.A3`) with four columns. First, the region. Second, the average signed transaction amount, where credits ('PRIJEM') count as +`amount`, withdrawals ('VYDAJ') count as −`amount`, and transactions of any other or missing type are left out of the average. Third, the number of the region's transactions in that date range, counting every type. Fourth, the ratio of the region's average signed amount to the average of these regional averages across all regions; return no rows if that overall average is missing. Do not round anything.
requests.specific_B: For transactions dated strictly after 1996-05-09 and strictly before 1998-01-06, both dates excluded (comparing `trans.date` as text), link each transaction to its account and each account to its branch's district. Then give one row per region (`district.A3`) with four columns. First, the region. Second, the average signed transaction amount, where credits ('PRIJEM') count as +`amount`, withdrawals ('VYDAJ') count as −`amount`, and transactions of any other or missing type are left out of the average. Third, the number of the region's transactions in that date range, counting every type. Fourth, the ratio of the region's average signed amount to the average of these regional averages across all regions; return no rows if that overall average is missing. Do not round anything.

Then give one row per region (`district.A3`) with four columns. First, the region. Second, the average signed transaction amount, where credits ('PRIJEM') count as +`amount`, withdrawals ('VYDAJ') count as −`amount`, and transactions of any other or missing type are left out of the average. Third, the number of the region's transactions in that period, counting every type. shared_requirements.requirement: Use transaction (`trans`) records, keeping only those whose date (`trans.date`, compared as text) falls in the range from 1996-05-09 to 1998-01-06. Whether the two end dates count is the open choice.

Link each transaction to its account (`account.account_id` = `trans.account_id`), then link the account to its branch district (`district.district_id` = `account.district_id`). Use inner joins, so rows with no match are dropped. Group the results by region (`district.A3`), one row per region.
First column: the region name (`district.A3`).

Second column: the region's average signed transaction amount. A credit ('PRIJEM') counts as +`trans.amount`. A withdrawal ('VYDAJ') counts as −`trans.amount`. Transactions of any other type, or with no type, are left out of this average. The result is missing if no transactions remain.
Third column: the number of transactions in the range for the region, counting every type.

Fourth column: the region's average signed amount divided by the average of all the regional averages, with missing regional averages ignored. If that overall average is missing, return no rows. No output is rounded. Columns appear in the order region, average signed amount, count, ratio.

A.requirement: The range includes both end dates: `trans.date` >= '1996-05-09' and <= '1998-01-06'.

B.requirement: The range excludes both end dates: `trans.date` > '1996-05-09' and < '1998-01-06'.

Then take the simple mean of these per-rating averages, ignoring missing ones. If that overall mean exists, list each rating whose average is strictly greater than it, showing the rating, its average, and how far its average is above the overall mean (all unrounded).
requests.specific_B: Among films whose replacement cost is more than 20.99, compute for each rating the average of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` (ignoring missing values). Then take the simple mean of these per-rating averages, ignoring missing ones. If that overall mean exists, list each rating whose average is strictly greater than it, showing the rating, its average, and how far its average is above the overall mean (all unrounded).

Then take the simple mean of these per-rating averages, ignoring missing ones. If that overall mean exists, list each rating whose average is strictly greater than it, showing the rating, its average, and how far its average is above the overall mean (all unrounded).

readings.A: Films with a replacement cost equal to 20.99 are included along with those above it.
readings.B: Only films with a replacement cost above 20.99 are included. A cost of exactly 20.99 is left out.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "film"."rating" AS "g", AVG((CAST("film"."rental_rate" AS REAL) / "film"."rental_duration")) AS "m1" FROM "film" AS "film" WHERE "film"."replacement_cost" >= 20.99 GROUP BY "film"."rating"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "film"."rating" AS "g", AVG((CAST("film"."rental_rate" AS REAL) / "film"."rental_duration")) AS "m1" FROM "film" AS "film" WHERE "film"."replacement_cost" > 20.99 GROUP BY "film"."rating"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"

Keep films by comparing `film.replacement_cost` with the value 20.99. Whether a cost of exactly 20.99 counts is the choice.
Compute the overall mean as the simple average of the per-rating averages, ignoring missing ones. Compare each rating against it only if the overall mean exists (is not missing).
Keep only the ratings whose average is strictly greater than the overall mean.

Second column: the rating's average, unrounded.

requests.specific_A: Considering only transactions whose amount (`trans.amount`) is at least 2400, work out two figures for each account (`trans.account_id`). The first is its average signed transaction amount, where credits ('PRIJEM') count as +amount, withdrawals ('VYDAJ') count as −amount, and other or missing types are left out. The second is its average balance after transaction (`trans.balance`). Then return a single row giving the average across accounts of each of these two figures, in that order, without rounding; accounts with no signed amount are skipped for the first figure.
requests.specific_B: Considering only transactions whose amount (`trans.amount`) is more than 2400, work out two figures for each account (`trans.account_id`). The first is its average signed transaction amount, where credits ('PRIJEM') count as +amount, withdrawals ('VYDAJ') count as −amount, and other or missing types are left out. The second is its average balance after transaction (`trans.balance`). Then return a single row giving the average across accounts of each of these two figures, in that order, without rounding; accounts with no signed amount are skipped for the first figure.
requests.open: Looking only at large transactions, with the cutoff at an amount (`trans.amount`) of 2400, work out two figures for each account (`trans.account_id`). The first is its average signed transaction amount, where credits ('PRIJEM') count as +amount, withdrawals ('VYDAJ') count as −amount, and other or missing types are left out. The second is its average balance after transaction (`trans.balance`). Then return a single row giving the average across accounts of each of these two figures, in that order, without rounding; accounts with no signed amount are skipped for the first figure.

readings.A: Transactions of exactly 2400 are kept.
readings.B: Only transactions above 2400 are kept.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "trans"."account_id" AS "e", AVG(CASE WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('PRIJEM') THEN "trans"."amount" WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('VYDAJ') THEN (0 - "trans"."amount") END) AS "m1", AVG("trans"."balance") AS "m2" FROM "trans" AS "trans" WHERE "trans"."amount" >= 2400 GROUP BY "trans"."account_id") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "trans"."account_id" AS "e", AVG(CASE WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('PRIJEM') THEN "trans"."amount" WHEN "trans"."type" IN ('VYDAJ') THEN (0 - "trans"."amount") END) AS "m1", AVG("trans"."balance") AS "m2" FROM "trans" AS "trans" WHERE "trans"."amount" > 2400 GROUP BY "trans"."account_id") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"

shared_requirements.requirement: Use transaction (`trans`) records, keeping only those whose `trans.amount` passes the 2400 threshold. Whether exactly 2400 counts is the open choice. Group the kept transactions by account (`trans.account_id`).
Combine the per-account rows into one group, which gives a single result row.

First column: the average over accounts of each account's average signed amount. A credit ('PRIJEM') counts as +`amount`. A withdrawal ('VYDAJ') counts as −`amount`. Other or missing types are left out. Accounts whose signed average is missing are ignored. Not rounded.
Second column: the average over accounts of each account's average balance after transaction (`trans.balance`). Not rounded. Columns appear in this order.

A.requirement: `trans.amount` >= 2400.

B.requirement: `trans.amount` > 2400.

Account id (`trans.account_id`).

Average balance after transaction (`trans.balance`) over the group's kept transactions. Not rounded.
Sort by the average balance, highest first (missing values last).
Return only the top 10 rows.

requests.specific_A: Linking each budget line to its event (`event.event_id` = `budget.link_to_event`, exact text match; lines without a matching event are dropped), and considering only lines whose `spent` is at least 6.0, show for each event `status`: the status, the average of `amount` minus `spent` (ignoring missing values; blank if there are none), and the number of such budget lines. Leave the results unrounded.
requests.specific_B: Linking each budget line to its event (`event.event_id` = `budget.link_to_event`, exact text match; lines without a matching event are dropped), and considering only lines whose `spent` is more than 6.0, show for each event `status`: the status, the average of `amount` minus `spent` (ignoring missing values; blank if there are none), and the number of such budget lines. Leave the results unrounded.
requests.open: Linking each budget line to its event (`event.event_id` = `budget.link_to_event`, exact text match; lines without a matching event are dropped), and using 6.0 as the cutoff on `spent` so that only the higher-spending budget lines are considered, show for each event `status`: the status, the average of `amount` minus `spent` (ignoring missing values; blank if there are none), and the number of such budget lines. Leave the results unrounded.

readings.A: Keep budget lines whose spent is 6.0 or more, including lines at exactly 6.0.
readings.B: Keep only budget lines whose spent is strictly greater than 6.0. A line at exactly 6.0 is excluded.

sql.A: SELECT "event"."status" AS "g", AVG(("budget"."amount" - "budget"."spent")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "budget" AS "budget" INNER JOIN "event" AS "event" ON "event"."event_id" = "budget"."link_to_event" WHERE "budget"."spent" >= 6.0 GROUP BY "event"."status"
sql.B: SELECT "event"."status" AS "g", AVG(("budget"."amount" - "budget"."spent")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "budget" AS "budget" INNER JOIN "event" AS "event" ON "event"."event_id" = "budget"."link_to_event" WHERE "budget"."spent" > 6.0 GROUP BY "event"."status"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the budget lines (`budget` records).
Join each budget line to the event where `event.event_id` = `budget.link_to_event`, using an exact text match. Each match gives one combined record. Budget lines with no matching event are dropped.
Filter on `budget.spent` against the threshold 6.0. Lines below 6.0 are always excluded.
Group the kept records by `event.status`. Each group gives one result row.
First column: the event `status`.
Second column: the average of `budget.amount` − `budget.spent` in the group. Missing values are ignored, and the result is missing (blank) when there are no values. The result is not rounded.
Third column: the number of records in the group.

A.requirement: A line whose `spent` is exactly 6.0 is kept, so the filter is spent >= 6.0.

B.requirement: A line whose `spent` is exactly 6.0 is excluded, so the filter is spent > 6.0.

requests.specific_A: Matching each telescope to its observatory by `observstation` (dropping telescopes with no matching observatory) and keeping only telescopes whose bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`) is at least 47.6, count the telescopes for each combination of observatory station and moon phase (`lunarstage`). List the station, the moon phase and the count, ordered by count from highest to lowest, and show only the top 10.
requests.specific_B: Matching each telescope to its observatory by `observstation` (dropping telescopes with no matching observatory) and keeping only telescopes whose bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`) is strictly greater than 47.6, count the telescopes for each combination of observatory station and moon phase (`lunarstage`). List the station, the moon phase and the count, ordered by count from highest to lowest, and show only the top 10.
requests.open: Matching each telescope to its observatory by `observstation` (dropping telescopes with no matching observatory) and keeping only telescopes on the high side of a 47.6 cutoff for bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`), count the telescopes for each combination of observatory station and moon phase (`lunarstage`). List the station, the moon phase and the count, ordered by count from highest to lowest, and show only the top 10.

readings.A: Telescopes whose bandwidth usage is exactly 47.6 are included, along with those above it.
readings.B: Only telescopes whose bandwidth usage is strictly greater than 47.6 are included.

sql.A: SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", "observatories"."lunarstage" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" INNER JOIN "observatories" AS "observatories" ON "observatories"."observstation" = "telescopes"."observstation" WHERE "telescopes"."bandusagepct" >= 47.6 GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation", "observatories"."lunarstage" ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", "observatories"."lunarstage" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" INNER JOIN "observatories" AS "observatories" ON "observatories"."observstation" = "telescopes"."observstation" WHERE "telescopes"."bandusagepct" > 47.6 GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation", "observatories"."lunarstage" ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from telescope records.
Inner-join each telescope to the observatories record with the same `observstation` (exact text match). Telescopes with no matching observatory are dropped.
Keep only records on the high side of the bandwidth usage (`telescopes.bandusagepct`) threshold of 47.6. How the boundary value is treated is the choice.
Group by observatory station (`telescopes.observstation`) and moon phase (`observatories.lunarstage`). Each group gives one row.
The observatory station (`observstation`).
The moon phase (`lunarstage`).
The number of records in the group.
Order by the record count, highest first (missing last). No tie-break is specified.
Keep only the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: A `bandusagepct` exactly equal to 47.6 is kept (>= 47.6).

B.requirement: Only a `bandusagepct` strictly greater than 47.6 is kept (> 47.6).

context.documentation:
ObservationalConditions.ObsDate: Full name: 'Observation Date'. Explanation: Local date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD). Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-08-01'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsDurHrs: Full name: 'Observation Duration (hours)'. Explanation: How long the observation lasted in hours. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '2.50'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsTime: Full name: 'Observation Time'. Explanation: Local time of the observation in HH:MM:SS. Data type: TIME. Example: '13:45:59'.
ObservationalConditions.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-PQR-9876'.
Observatories.AirTempC: Full name: 'Air Temperature (°C)'. Explanation: Ambient temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '18.45'.
Observatories.AtmosTransparency: Full name: 'Atmospheric Transparency'. Explanation: A numeric measure of how transparent the atmosphere is. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.867'.
Observatories.GeomagStatus: Full name: 'Geomagnetic Activity'. Explanation: The level of geomagnetic activity during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Active, Quiet, Storm.
Observatories.HumidityRate: Full name: 'Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Relative humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '62.300'.
Observatories.LunarDistDeg: Full name: 'Moon Distance (Degrees)'. Explanation: Angular distance to the Moon in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '97.52'.
Observatories.LunarStage: Full name: 'Lunar Phase'. Explanation: The current phase of the Moon during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: First Quarter, Full, Last Quarter, New.
Observatories.ObservStation: Full name: 'Observatory Name'. Explanation: This field holds the name or unique identifier for the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
Observatories.PressHpa: Full name: 'Pressure (hPa)'. Explanation: Atmospheric pressure in hectopascals. Data type: DECIMAL(6,1). Example: '1013.2'.
Observatories.SeeingProfile: Full name: 'Seeing Profile'. Explanation: Assessment of sky seeing conditions (atmospheric steadiness). Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
Observatories.SiderealLocal: Full name: 'Local Sidereal Time'. Explanation: Sidereal time at the observatory in HH:MM:SS format. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: '12:34:56'.
Observatories.SolarStatus: Full name: 'Solar Activity'. Explanation: The level of solar activity at the time of observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Moderate.
Observatories.WeathProfile: Full name: 'Weather Profile'. Explanation: A short description of weather conditions during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Clear, Cloudy, Partially Cloudy.
Observatories.WindSpeedMs: Full name: 'Wind Speed (m/s)'. Explanation: Wind speed in meters per second. Data type: NUMERIC(4,2). Example: '3.45'.
ResearchProcess.AnalysisPrio: Full name: 'Analysis Priority'. Explanation: Priority assigned for analyzing this signal. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, Urgent.
ResearchProcess.CollabStat: Full name: 'Collaboration Status'. Explanation: The nature of collaboration on this signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: International, Solo, Team.
ResearchProcess.DiscStat: Full name: 'Disclosure Status'. Explanation: How much information about the signal is shared publicly. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Full, None, Partial.
ResearchProcess.FollowStat: Full name: 'Follow-up Status'. Explanation: Status of any follow-up observations. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Required, Scheduled.
ResearchProcess.FundStat: Full name: 'Funding Status'. Explanation: Funding situation for further study. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Funded, Pending, Unfunded.
ResearchProcess.NotesMemo: Full name: 'Research Notes'. Explanation: Any extra remarks or context by researchers. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Project requires further funding...'
ResearchProcess.PeerRevStat: Full name: 'Peer Review Status'. Explanation: Where this signal stands in peer review. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, In Progress, Pending.
ResearchProcess.PubStat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether findings about the signal have been published. Data type: CHAR(25). Possible categories: Draft, Published, Submitted.
ResearchProcess.ResPrio: Full name: 'Research Priority'. Explanation: How urgently this signal needs scientific attention. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium.
ResearchProcess.SecClass: Full name: 'Security Classification'. Explanation: Visibility and clearance level for the data. Data type: CHAR(35). Possible categories: Classified, Public, Restricted.
ResearchProcess.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-MNO-7890'.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.CultSig: Full name: 'Cultural Significance'. Explanation: The level of cultural impact or interest. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: High, Low, None.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.EncryptEvid: Full name: 'Encryption Evidence'. Explanation: Whether there is indication the signal is encrypted. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: None, Possible, Strong.

requests.specific_A: Across all `manager_half` records with at least 26 wins (`w`), what is the total of games managed minus losses (`g` − `l`, ignoring missing values), and how many such records are there?
requests.specific_B: Across all `manager_half` records with more than 26 wins (`w`), what is the total of games managed minus losses (`g` − `l`, ignoring missing values), and how many such records are there?
requests.open: Across all `manager_half` records whose wins (`w`) pass the 26-win mark, what is the total of games managed minus losses (`g` − `l`, ignoring missing values), and how many such records are there?

readings.A: Records with 26 wins or more.
readings.B: Records with more than 26 wins.

sql.A: SELECT SUM(("manager_half"."g" - "manager_half"."l")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "manager_half" AS "manager_half" WHERE "manager_half"."w" >= 26
sql.B: SELECT SUM(("manager_half"."g" - "manager_half"."l")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "manager_half" AS "manager_half" WHERE "manager_half"."w" > 26

shared_requirements.requirement: Use `manager_half` records.
Keep records by comparing wins (`w`) with 26. Whether exactly 26 counts is the open choice.
All kept records form one group, giving a single result row.
The sum of `g` − `l` over the kept records. Missing values are ignored, and the sum is missing if there are none. No rounding.
The number of kept records.

A.requirement: `w` >= 26 (exactly 26 counts).

B.requirement: `w` > 26 (exactly 26 does not count).

requests.specific_A: Looking at invoices with an `InvoiceDate` from '2010-06-22 00:00:00' through '2012-06-26 00:00:00' inclusive (comparing the dates as text), each matched to its customer, work out per customer `State` the total of invoice `Total` and the number of invoices, with customers that have no state counted as one group. Then give, as a single row, the sum of those state totals and the average number of invoices per state, both unrounded.
requests.specific_B: Looking at invoices with an `InvoiceDate` strictly after '2010-06-22 00:00:00' and strictly before '2012-06-26 00:00:00' (comparing the dates as text), each matched to its customer, work out per customer `State` the total of invoice `Total` and the number of invoices, with customers that have no state counted as one group. Then give, as a single row, the sum of those state totals and the average number of invoices per state, both unrounded.
requests.open: For invoices dated between '2010-06-22 00:00:00' and '2012-06-26 00:00:00' (comparing `InvoiceDate` as text), each matched to its customer, work out per customer `State` the total of invoice `Total` and the number of invoices, with customers that have no state counted as one group. Then give, as a single row, the sum of those state totals and the average number of invoices per state, both unrounded.

readings.A: Invoices dated exactly on either boundary timestamp are included in the date range.
readings.B: Invoices dated exactly on either boundary timestamp are excluded from the date range.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Customer"."State" AS "g", SUM("Invoice"."Total") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "Invoice" AS "Invoice" INNER JOIN "Customer" AS "Customer" ON "Customer"."CustomerId" = "Invoice"."CustomerId" WHERE ("Invoice"."InvoiceDate" >= '2010-06-22 00:00:00' AND "Invoice"."InvoiceDate" <= '2012-06-26 00:00:00') GROUP BY "Customer"."State") SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Customer"."State" AS "g", SUM("Invoice"."Total") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "Invoice" AS "Invoice" INNER JOIN "Customer" AS "Customer" ON "Customer"."CustomerId" = "Invoice"."CustomerId" WHERE ("Invoice"."InvoiceDate" > '2010-06-22 00:00:00' AND "Invoice"."InvoiceDate" < '2012-06-26 00:00:00') GROUP BY "Customer"."State") SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from invoices and attach each invoice's customer by matching `Invoice.CustomerId` to `Customer.CustomerId`; drop invoices with no matching customer.
Filter on `Invoice.InvoiceDate` against the bounds '2010-06-22 00:00:00' and '2012-06-26 00:00:00', comparing the dates as text.

Group the kept invoices by customer `State`. Customers with no state form one group of their own. For each state, compute the sum of `Invoice.Total` (missing values ignored) and the number of invoices.
Combine all the state rows into a single result row.
First output: the sum of the per-state invoice totals (missing values ignored), not rounded.
Second output: the average of the per-state invoice counts, not rounded.

A.requirement: Both bounds are inclusive: InvoiceDate >= '2010-06-22 00:00:00' and <= '2012-06-26 00:00:00'.

B.requirement: Both bounds are exclusive: InvoiceDate > '2010-06-22 00:00:00' and < '2012-06-26 00:00:00'.

requests.specific_A: Looking at examinations with an `Examination Date` on or after 1995-11-09 and on or before 1997-03-17 (comparing the dates as text), what is the average `ANA` value (ignoring missing values) and how many examination records are there in total? Give the answer as a single row with the unrounded average first and the record count second.
requests.specific_B: Looking at examinations with an `Examination Date` strictly after 1995-11-09 and strictly before 1997-03-17 (comparing the dates as text), what is the average `ANA` value (ignoring missing values) and how many examination records are there in total? Give the answer as a single row with the unrounded average first and the record count second.
requests.open: For examinations held between 1995-11-09 and 1997-03-17 (comparing the `Examination Date` as text), what is the average `ANA` value (ignoring missing values) and how many examination records are there in total? Give one row with the unrounded average first and the record count second.

readings.A: Examinations dated on either end date are counted together with those dated in between.
readings.B: Only examinations dated strictly between the two end dates are counted. Those dated exactly on either end date are left out.

sql.A: SELECT AVG("Examination"."ANA") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "Examination" AS "Examination" WHERE ("Examination"."Examination Date" >= '1995-11-09' AND "Examination"."Examination Date" <= '1997-03-17')
sql.B: SELECT AVG("Examination"."ANA") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "Examination" AS "Examination" WHERE ("Examination"."Examination Date" > '1995-11-09' AND "Examination"."Examination Date" < '1997-03-17')

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every record in the `Examination` table; no joins.
Keep examinations whose `Examination Date` falls in the range from 1995-11-09 to 1997-03-17, comparing the date as text, character by character.
All kept records form one group and the result is exactly one row.
First column: the average of `ANA` over the kept records, ignoring missing values. It is missing when no values are present. No rounding.
Second column: the number of kept examination records, counting every row whether or not its `ANA` is missing.

A.requirement: Both end dates are included: `Examination Date` >= '1995-11-09' and <= '1997-03-17'.

B.requirement: Both end dates are excluded: `Examination Date` > '1995-11-09' and < '1997-03-17'.

requests.specific_A: Matching each telescope to its observatory by `observstation` (dropping telescopes with no matching observatory) and keeping only telescopes whose pointing accuracy (`pointaccarc`) is at least 4.86, group them by observatory station and weather profile (`weathprofile`). For each group, find the average bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`, ignoring missing values) and the number of telescopes. Then return a single row with the average of those group averages (ignoring missing ones) and the average of those group counts, unrounded.
requests.specific_B: Matching each telescope to its observatory by `observstation` (dropping telescopes with no matching observatory) and keeping only telescopes whose pointing accuracy (`pointaccarc`) is strictly greater than 4.86, group them by observatory station and weather profile (`weathprofile`). For each group, find the average bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`, ignoring missing values) and the number of telescopes. Then return a single row with the average of those group averages (ignoring missing ones) and the average of those group counts, unrounded.
requests.open: Matching each telescope to its observatory by `observstation` (dropping telescopes with no matching observatory) and keeping only telescopes on the high side of a 4.86 cutoff for pointing accuracy (`pointaccarc`), group them by observatory station and weather profile (`weathprofile`). For each group, find the average bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`, ignoring missing values) and the number of telescopes. Then return a single row with the average of those group averages (ignoring missing ones) and the average of those group counts, unrounded.

readings.A: Telescopes whose pointing accuracy is exactly 4.86 are included, along with those above it.
readings.B: Only telescopes whose pointing accuracy is strictly greater than 4.86 are included.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", "observatories"."weathprofile" AS "g", AVG("telescopes"."bandusagepct") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" INNER JOIN "observatories" AS "observatories" ON "observatories"."observstation" = "telescopes"."observstation" WHERE "telescopes"."pointaccarc" >= 4.86 GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation", "observatories"."weathprofile") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "telescopes"."observstation" AS "e", "observatories"."weathprofile" AS "g", AVG("telescopes"."bandusagepct") AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "telescopes" AS "telescopes" INNER JOIN "observatories" AS "observatories" ON "observatories"."observstation" = "telescopes"."observstation" WHERE "telescopes"."pointaccarc" > 4.86 GROUP BY "telescopes"."observstation", "observatories"."weathprofile") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from telescopes and inner-join each one to the observatories record with the same `observstation` (exact text match). Telescopes with no matching observatory are dropped.
Keep only records on the high side of the pointing accuracy (`telescopes.pointaccarc`) threshold of 4.86. How the boundary value is treated is the choice.

Group the kept records by observatory station (`telescopes.observstation`) and weather profile (`observatories.weathprofile`). For each group, compute the average `bandusagepct` (missing values ignored; missing if there are none) and the number of records.
Combine all of these per-group rows into one result row.
The average of the per-group average bandwidth usage values (missing values ignored; missing if there are none), not rounded.
The average of the per-group record counts, not rounded.

A.requirement: A `pointaccarc` exactly equal to 4.86 is kept (>= 4.86).

B.requirement: Only a `pointaccarc` strictly greater than 4.86 is kept (> 4.86).

context.documentation:
ObservationalConditions.ObsDate: Full name: 'Observation Date'. Explanation: Local date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD). Data type: DATE. Example: '2025-08-01'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsDurHrs: Full name: 'Observation Duration (hours)'. Explanation: How long the observation lasted in hours. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '2.50'.
ObservationalConditions.ObsTime: Full name: 'Observation Time'. Explanation: Local time of the observation in HH:MM:SS. Data type: TIME. Example: '13:45:59'.
ObservationalConditions.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-PQR-9876'.
Observatories.AirTempC: Full name: 'Air Temperature (°C)'. Explanation: Ambient temperature in Celsius. Data type: NUMERIC(5,2). Example: '18.45'.
Observatories.AtmosTransparency: Full name: 'Atmospheric Transparency'. Explanation: A numeric measure of how transparent the atmosphere is. Data type: NUMERIC(5,3). Example: '0.867'.
Observatories.GeomagStatus: Full name: 'Geomagnetic Activity'. Explanation: The level of geomagnetic activity during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: Active, Quiet, Storm.
Observatories.HumidityRate: Full name: 'Humidity (%)'. Explanation: Relative humidity as a percentage. Data type: NUMERIC(6,3). Example: '62.300'.
Observatories.LunarDistDeg: Full name: 'Moon Distance (Degrees)'. Explanation: Angular distance to the Moon in degrees. Data type: DECIMAL(7,2). Example: '97.52'.
Observatories.LunarStage: Full name: 'Lunar Phase'. Explanation: The current phase of the Moon during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: First Quarter, Full, Last Quarter, New.
Observatories.ObservStation: Full name: 'Observatory Name'. Explanation: This field holds the name or unique identifier for the observatory station. Data type: CHAR(60). Example: 'OBS_STATION_ALPHA'.
Observatories.PressHpa: Full name: 'Pressure (hPa)'. Explanation: Atmospheric pressure in hectopascals. Data type: DECIMAL(6,1). Example: '1013.2'.
Observatories.SeeingProfile: Full name: 'Seeing Profile'. Explanation: Assessment of sky seeing conditions (atmospheric steadiness). Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Excellent, Good, Poor.
Observatories.SiderealLocal: Full name: 'Local Sidereal Time'. Explanation: Sidereal time at the observatory in HH:MM:SS format. Data type: CHAR(8). Example: '12:34:56'.
Observatories.SolarStatus: Full name: 'Solar Activity'. Explanation: The level of solar activity at the time of observation. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Moderate.
Observatories.WeathProfile: Full name: 'Weather Profile'. Explanation: A short description of weather conditions during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Clear, Cloudy, Partially Cloudy.
Observatories.WindSpeedMs: Full name: 'Wind Speed (m/s)'. Explanation: Wind speed in meters per second. Data type: NUMERIC(4,2). Example: '3.45'.
ResearchProcess.AnalysisPrio: Full name: 'Analysis Priority'. Explanation: Priority assigned for analyzing this signal. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, Urgent.
ResearchProcess.CollabStat: Full name: 'Collaboration Status'. Explanation: The nature of collaboration on this signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: International, Solo, Team.
ResearchProcess.DiscStat: Full name: 'Disclosure Status'. Explanation: How much information about the signal is shared publicly. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Full, None, Partial.
ResearchProcess.FollowStat: Full name: 'Follow-up Status'. Explanation: Status of any follow-up observations. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Required, Scheduled.
ResearchProcess.FundStat: Full name: 'Funding Status'. Explanation: Funding situation for further study. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Funded, Pending, Unfunded.
ResearchProcess.NotesMemo: Full name: 'Research Notes'. Explanation: Any extra remarks or context by researchers. Data type: TEXT. Example: 'Project requires further funding...'
ResearchProcess.PeerRevStat: Full name: 'Peer Review Status'. Explanation: Where this signal stands in peer review. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, In Progress, Pending.
ResearchProcess.PubStat: Full name: 'Publication Status'. Explanation: Whether findings about the signal have been published. Data type: CHAR(25). Possible categories: Draft, Published, Submitted.
ResearchProcess.ResPrio: Full name: 'Research Priority'. Explanation: How urgently this signal needs scientific attention. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium.
ResearchProcess.SecClass: Full name: 'Security Classification'. Explanation: Visibility and clearance level for the data. Data type: CHAR(35). Possible categories: Classified, Public, Restricted.
ResearchProcess.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-MNO-7890'.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.CultSig: Full name: 'Cultural Significance'. Explanation: The level of cultural impact or interest. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: High, Low, None.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.EncryptEvid: Full name: 'Encryption Evidence'. Explanation: Whether there is indication the signal is encrypted. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: None, Possible, Strong.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.GravLens: Full name: 'Gravitational Lensing'. Explanation: Whether the signal is affected by gravitational lensing. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: None, Strong, Weak.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.InterMedEffects: Full name: 'Interstellar Medium Effects'. Explanation: Impact of interstellar medium on the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Minimal, Moderate, Severe.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.LangStruct: Full name: 'Language Structure'. Explanation: Presence of linguistic or structured patterns. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Complex, None, Simple.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.MsgContent: Full name: 'Message Content'. Explanation: Indicates whether an actual message was detected. Data type: TEXT. Possible categories: Identified, None, Possible.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.QuantEffects: Full name: 'Quantum Effects'. Explanation: Quantum-level phenomena observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(85). Possible categories: None, Observed, Significant.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SciImpact: Full name: 'Scientific Impact'. Explanation: Significance of the signal to scientific research. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Major, Minor, Moderate.
SignalAdvancedPhenomena.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-ABC-1234'.
SignalClassification.ClassConf: Full name: 'Classification Confidence (%)'. Explanation: How confident we are in the assigned signal class. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '92.50'.
SignalClassification.ComplexIdx: Full name: 'Complexity Index'. Explanation: Numeric measure of the signal’s complexity. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '5.678'.
SignalClassification.EntropyVal: Full name: 'Entropy'. Explanation: Entropy measurement of the signal. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.45'.
SignalClassification.InfoDense: Full name: 'Information Density'. Explanation: Estimated information per unit time/frequency. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.345'.
SignalClassification.PeriodSec: Full name: 'Period (s)'. Explanation: Duration of each cycle if periodic. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '12.345'.
SignalClassification.RepeatCount: Full name: 'Repetition Count'. Explanation: Number of times the signal has repeated. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '3'.
SignalClassification.SigClassType: Full name: 'Classification Type'. Explanation: High-level category for the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Artificial, Candidate, Natural, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SigPattern: Full name: 'Signal Pattern'. Explanation: Pattern observed in the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(60). Possible categories: Periodic, Random, Structured, Unknown.
SignalClassification.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-DEF-5678'.
SignalDecoding.AnalysisDp: Full name: 'Analysis Depth'. Explanation: How thoroughly the signal was analyzed. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Comprehensive, Detailed, Preliminary.
SignalDecoding.CompResources: Full name: 'Computational Resources'. Explanation: Level of computing power used. Data type: VARCHAR(50). Possible categories: Extreme, High, Low, Medium.
SignalDecoding.CompressRatio: Full name: 'Compression Ratio'. Explanation: Factor by which the raw signal data was compressed. Data type: DECIMAL(6,3). Example: '2.500'.
SignalDecoding.ConfirmStat: Full name: 'Confirmation Status'. Explanation: Whether the decoding results have been confirmed. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Confirmed, Pending, Rejected.
SignalDecoding.DecodeConf: Full name: 'Decoding Confidence (%)'. Explanation: Confidence level that the decoding is correct. Data type: DECIMAL(5,2). Example: '88.75'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeIters: Full name: 'Decoding Iterations'. Explanation: Number of algorithmic passes attempted. Data type: SMALLINT. Example: '7'.
SignalDecoding.DecodeMethod: Full name: 'Decoding Method'. Explanation: Method used to decode the signal. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: FFT, Neural Network, Quantum, Wavelet.
SignalDecoding.DecodeStat: Full name: 'Decoding Status'. Explanation: Status of the decoding process. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Completed, Failed, In Progress.
SignalDecoding.EncodeType: Full name: 'Encoding Type'. Explanation: The type of signal encoding used (e.g., Binary). Data type: VARCHAR(40). Possible categories: Binary, Complex, Tertiary, Unknown.
SignalDecoding.ErrCorrLvl: Full name: 'Error Correction Level'. Explanation: Degree of error correction applied. Data type: VARCHAR(35). Possible categories: High, Low, Medium, None.
SignalDecoding.ProcTimeHrs: Full name: 'Processing Time (hours)'. Explanation: Total hours spent decoding. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '3.50'.
SignalDecoding.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal entry. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-GHI-9012'.
SignalDecoding.VerifLvl: Full name: 'Verification Level'. Explanation: Extent to which decoding has been verified. Data type: VARCHAR(30). Possible categories: Partially, Unverified, Verified.
SignalDynamics.AmpStab: Full name: 'Amplitude Stability'. Explanation: Consistency of signal amplitude. Data type: VARCHAR(20). If no fixed categories, example: 'Unstable'.
SignalDynamics.FreqStab: Full name: 'Frequency Stability'. Explanation: How stable the signal’s frequency is. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighlyStable'.
SignalDynamics.ModStab: Full name: 'Modulation Stability'. Explanation: Consistency in the signal’s modulation scheme. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'Consistent'.
SignalDynamics.PhaseStab: Full name: 'Phase Stability'. Explanation: Any variation in signal phase. Data type: VARCHAR(35). If no fixed categories, example: 'VaryingPhase'.
SignalDynamics.SigCoherence: Full name: 'Signal Coherence'. Explanation: How coherent the signal remains over its duration. Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighCoherence'.
SignalDynamics.SigDisp: Full name: 'Signal Dispersion'. Explanation: The degree to which the signal is dispersed (time/frequency smearing). Data type: VARCHAR(25). If no fixed categories, example: 'SignificantDisp'.
SignalDynamics.SigEvolve: Full name: 'Signal Evolution'. Explanation: Indicates if the signal changes/evolves during observation. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: Dynamic, Static, Unknown.
SignalDynamics.SigIntegrity: Full name: 'Signal Integrity'. Explanation: Rating of how intact or uncorrupted the signal is. Data type: VARCHAR(30). If no fixed categories, example: 'HighIntegrity'.
SignalDynamics.SigRecurr: Full name: 'Signal Recurrence'. Explanation: Whether the signal recurs over time. Data type: VARCHAR(25). Possible categories: None, Regular, Sporadic.
SignalDynamics.SigScint: Full name: 'Signal Scintillation'. Explanation: Fluctuation in signal amplitude due to propagation effects. Data type: VARCHAR(45). If no fixed categories, example: 'MildScintillation'.
SignalDynamics.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Foreign key referencing the main signal. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-JKL-3456'.

SignalProbabilities.ArtSrcProb: Full name: 'Artificial Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from an artificial source. Data type: NUMERIC(3,1). Example: '3.4'.
SignalProbabilities.BioSigProb: Full name: 'Biosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal indicates a biological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(6,2). Example: '45.21'.
SignalProbabilities.CorrScore: Full name: 'Correlation Score'. Explanation: How well the signal aligns with expected patterns. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.9950'.
SignalProbabilities.FalsePosProb: Full name: 'False Positive Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is falsely detected. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.0135'.
SignalProbabilities.NatSrcProb: Full name: 'Natural Source Probability'. Explanation: Probability the signal is from a natural source. Data type: NUMERIC(7,3). Example: '98.761'.
SignalProbabilities.SigUnique: Full name: 'Signal Uniqueness'. Explanation: A measure of how unique the signal is compared to others. Data type: DECIMAL(7,4). Example: '99.1234'.
SignalProbabilities.SignalRef: Full name: 'Signal Registry Reference'. Explanation: Primary key referencing the main signal record. Data type: CHAR(36). Example: 'SIG-XYZ-9876'.
SignalProbabilities.SimIndex: Full name: 'Similarity Index'. Explanation: Compares the signal to known references. Data type: NUMERIC(5,4). Example: '0.8222'.
SignalProbabilities.TechSigProb: Full name: 'Technosignature Probability'. Explanation: Probability that the signal is of artificial technological origin. Data type: DECIMAL(5,4). Example: '0.6789'.
