requests.specific_A: For films whose `replacement_cost` is at least 20.99, group by `rating` and show, for each rating, the rating, the average `length` (ignoring missing values), and the average per film of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` (ignoring missing values). Leave all values unrounded.
requests.specific_B: For films whose `replacement_cost` is more than 20.99, group by `rating` and show, for each rating, the rating, the average `length` (ignoring missing values), and the average per film of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` (ignoring missing values). Leave all values unrounded.
requests.open: Taking 20.99 as the cutoff for a film being expensive to replace (`replacement_cost`), look only at the expensive films and group them by `rating`. For each rating, show the rating, the average `length` (ignoring missing values), and the average per film of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` (ignoring missing values). Leave all values unrounded.

readings.A: Keep films whose replacement cost is 20.99 or more, so films costing exactly 20.99 count.
readings.B: Keep only films whose replacement cost is strictly more than 20.99, so films costing exactly 20.99 are left out.

sql.A: SELECT "film"."rating" AS "g", AVG("film"."length") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("film"."rental_rate" AS REAL) / "film"."rental_duration")) AS "m2" FROM "film" AS "film" WHERE "film"."replacement_cost" >= 20.99 GROUP BY "film"."rating"
sql.B: SELECT "film"."rating" AS "g", AVG("film"."length") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("film"."rental_rate" AS REAL) / "film"."rental_duration")) AS "m2" FROM "film" AS "film" WHERE "film"."replacement_cost" > 20.99 GROUP BY "film"."rating"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the `film` table, one record per film.
Keep films whose `replacement_cost` passes the 20.99 threshold (the inclusive/exclusive part is the choice).
Group the kept films by `rating`, one result row per rating.
Column 1 is the film's `rating`.
Column 2 is the average `length` of the films in the group. Missing values are ignored, and the result is missing if there are none.
Column 3 is the average, over the films in the group, of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` for each film. Missing values are ignored, and the result is missing if there are none.
Output columns appear in this order: rating, average length, average rate per day. Nothing is rounded, and no ordering or limit is required.

A.requirement: Films with `replacement_cost` exactly 20.99 are included (replacement_cost >= 20.99).

B.requirement: Films with `replacement_cost` exactly 20.99 are excluded (replacement_cost > 20.99).

context.schema:
CREATE TABLE actor (
  actor_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  first_name VARCHAR(45) NOT NULL,
  last_name VARCHAR(45) NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (actor_id)
);
CREATE TABLE address (
  address_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  address VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
  address2 VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  district VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  city_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  postal_code VARCHAR(10) DEFAULT NULL,
  phone VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (address_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (city_id) REFERENCES city (city_id)
);
CREATE TABLE category (
  category_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  name VARCHAR(25) NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (category_id)
);
CREATE TABLE city (
  city_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  city VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
  country_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (city_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (country_id) REFERENCES country (country_id)
);
CREATE TABLE country (
  country_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  country VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (country_id)
);
CREATE TABLE customer (
  customer_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  store_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  first_name VARCHAR(45) NOT NULL,
  last_name VARCHAR(45) NOT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  address_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
  create_date DATETIME NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (customer_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (address_id) REFERENCES address (address_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES store (store_id)
);
CREATE TABLE film (
  film_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  title VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  description TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  release_year YEAR DEFAULT NULL,
  language_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  original_language_id TINYINT UNSIGNED DEFAULT NULL,
  rental_duration TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 3,
  rental_rate DECIMAL(4,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 4.99,
  length SMALLINT UNSIGNED DEFAULT NULL,
  replacement_cost DECIMAL(5,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 19.99,
  rating DEFAULT 'G',
  special_features DEFAULT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (film_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (language_id) REFERENCES language (language_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (original_language_id) REFERENCES language (language_id)
);
CREATE TABLE film_actor (
  actor_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  film_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (actor_id,film_id),
 FOREIGN KEY (actor_id) REFERENCES actor (actor_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (film_id) REFERENCES film (film_id)
);
CREATE TABLE film_category (
  film_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  category_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (film_id, category_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (film_id) REFERENCES film (film_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES category (category_id)
);
CREATE TABLE film_text (
  film_id SMALLINT NOT NULL,
  title VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  description TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY  (film_id)
);
CREATE TABLE inventory (
  inventory_id MEDIUMINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  film_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  store_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (inventory_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES store (store_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (film_id) REFERENCES film (film_id)
);
CREATE TABLE language (
  language_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  name CHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (language_id)
);
CREATE TABLE payment (
  payment_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  customer_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  staff_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  rental_id INT DEFAULT NULL,
  amount DECIMAL(5,2) NOT NULL,
  payment_date DATETIME NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (payment_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (rental_id) REFERENCES rental (rental_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customer (customer_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (staff_id) REFERENCES staff (staff_id)
);
CREATE TABLE rental (
  rental_id INT NOT NULL,
  rental_date DATETIME NOT NULL,
  inventory_id MEDIUMINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  customer_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  return_date DATETIME DEFAULT NULL,
  staff_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (rental_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (staff_id) REFERENCES staff (staff_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (inventory_id) REFERENCES inventory (inventory_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customer (customer_id)
);
CREATE TABLE staff (
  staff_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  first_name VARCHAR(45) NOT NULL,
  last_name VARCHAR(45) NOT NULL,
  address_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  picture BLOB DEFAULT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  store_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
  username VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL,
  password VARCHAR(40) DEFAULT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (staff_id),
  --FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES store (store_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (address_id) REFERENCES address (address_id)
);
CREATE TABLE store (
  store_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  manager_staff_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  address_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  last_update TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY  (store_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (manager_staff_id) REFERENCES staff (staff_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (address_id) REFERENCES address (address_id)
);

category.name: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 16 genres, each shared by many films (about 50-75 each), so the column is a grouping label and does not identify single records. Evidence: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film_category fc JOIN category c ON c.category_id = fc.category_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY films DESC -> [['Sports', '74'], ['Foreign', '73'], ['Family', '69'], ['Documentary', '68'], ['Animation', '66'], ['Action', '64']]
customer.store_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 2 stores with about 300 customers each, so the column is a grouping label shared by many rows. Evidence: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS customers, SUM(active) AS active_customers FROM customer GROUP BY store_id -> [['1', '326', '318'], ['2', '273', '266']]
inventory.store_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 2 store values over 4581 copies, about 2270 per store, so the column is a grouping label. Evidence: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS copies, COUNT(DISTINCT film_id) AS titles FROM inventory GROUP BY store_id -> [['1', '2270', '759'], ['2', '2311', '762']]
country.country: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Many customers share a country (the top countries have dozens of customers each), so country works as a grouping attribute for customers. Evidence: SELECT co.country, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customer cu JOIN address a ON a.address_id = cu.address_id JOIN city ci ON ci.city_id = a.city_id JOIN country co ON co.country_id = ci.country_id GROUP BY co.country ORDER BY customers DESC LIMIT 10 -> [['India', '60'], ['China', '53'], ['United States', '36'], ['Japan', '31'], ['Mexico', '30'], ['Russian Federation', '28']]
film.special_features: desc (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 15 distinct values, all of them combinations of the same 4 feature names (for example 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes'). The column is a set, not a single category. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']] semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows 15 distinct values, all combinations of the same 4 feature names, such as 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes' and 'Trailers,Commentaries'. The column is a set, not a single class, so it should not be offered as a grouping. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']]
film.length: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified rating query already returns AVG(length) between 111.05 (G) and 120.44 (PG-13). The catalogue profile gives 140 distinct values from 46 to 185 minutes. So length is a continuous ratio-scale quantity whose group averages can be read directly. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(length) AS avg_minutes, MIN(length), MAX(length) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '120.4439461883408', '46', '185'], ['NC-17', '210', '113.22857142857143', '46', '184'], ['R', '195', '118.66153846153846', '49', '185'], ['PG', '194', '112.00515463917526', '46', '185'], ['G', '178', '111.0505617977528', '47', '185']]
film.rental_duration: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows 5 values from 3 to 7 days, all well above zero, so the column is a ratio-scale number of days per film. The query shows how many films fall at each value. Evidence: SELECT rental_duration, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate) AS avg_rate FROM film GROUP BY rental_duration ORDER BY rental_duration -> [['3', '203', '2.8323645320197115'], ['4', '203', '2.97029556650247'], ['5', '191', '3.19942408376964'], ['6', '212', '2.895660377358497'], ['7', '191', '3.021413612565451']]
film.rental_rate: desc (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows rental_rate takes only 0.99, 2.99 and 4.99, while replacement_cost runs from 9.99 to 29.99. The query shows how large and uniform the gap is. The auditor noted that the difference is always about −17 and the relative gap about −0.85, which fits two different quantities rather than one price seen two ways. Evidence: SELECT MIN(replacement_cost - rental_rate), MAX(replacement_cost - rental_rate), AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) FROM film -> [['5.0', '29.0', '0.16651517608314595']]
film.replacement_cost: quantity (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The column holds a per-copy value that becomes meaningful when summed over physical copies in inventory, for example as stock value. That is the reading of an asset value, not of a price charged per rental. Evidence: SELECT f.rating, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copies, SUM(f.replacement_cost) AS stock_value FROM inventory i JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating -> [['G', '791', '16185.089999999853'], ['NC-17', '944', '19128.56000000009'], ['PG', '924', '17755.759999999962'], ['PG-13', '1018', '21052.82000000024'], ['R', '904', '18498.960000000006']]
payment.staff_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows only 2 distinct values (1 and 2) across 16,049 payments. Each value is therefore shared by thousands of rows, which makes it a grouping label rather than a record identifier. Evidence: SELECT staff_id, COUNT(*) AS payments, SUM(amount) AS revenue, AVG(amount) FROM payment GROUP BY staff_id -> [['1', '8057', '33489.470000005174', '4.156568201564499'], ['2', '7992', '33927.04000000482', '4.245125125125728']]
rental.staff_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows only 2 distinct values across 16,044 rentals, so each staff value covers thousands of rentals and works as a grouping class. Evidence: SELECT staff_id, COUNT(*) AS rentals, SUM(CASE WHEN return_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unreturned FROM rental GROUP BY staff_id -> [['1', '8040', '85'], ['2', '8004', '98']]

requests.specific_A: For laboratory records with a white blood cell count (`WBC`) of at least 6.5, what are the average triglyceride level (`TG`) and the average `WBC`? Give them as a single unrounded row and ignore missing values.
requests.specific_B: For laboratory records with a white blood cell count (`WBC`) strictly above 6.5, what are the average triglyceride level (`TG`) and the average `WBC`? Give them as a single unrounded row and ignore missing values.
requests.open: Using 6.5 as the cutoff for a high white blood cell count (`WBC`), what are the average triglyceride level (`TG`) and the average `WBC` across the laboratory records with a high count? Give them as a single unrounded row and ignore missing values.

readings.A: Records with a white blood cell count equal to 6.5 or greater are included.
readings.B: Only records with a white blood cell count strictly greater than 6.5 are included.

sql.A: SELECT AVG("Laboratory"."TG") AS "m1", AVG("Laboratory"."WBC") AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" WHERE "Laboratory"."WBC" >= 6.5
sql.B: SELECT AVG("Laboratory"."TG") AS "m1", AVG("Laboratory"."WBC") AS "m2" FROM "Laboratory" AS "Laboratory" WHERE "Laboratory"."WBC" > 6.5

shared_requirements.requirement: Use individual `Laboratory` records.
Filter the records by white blood cell count (`WBC`) against the threshold 6.5. Records with a missing WBC are excluded.
All kept records form one group, which gives a single result row.
The first column is the average triglyceride (`TG`), ignoring missing values. It is not rounded.
The second column is the average `WBC`, ignoring missing values. It is not rounded.

A.requirement: Keep records with WBC ≥ 6.5, so a value of exactly 6.5 counts.

B.requirement: Keep records with WBC > 6.5, so a value of exactly 6.5 does not count.

requests.specific_A: Across all fee records whose fee rate (`feerate`) is at least 0.0009, what is the average ratio of maker rebate rate to fee rate (`rebrate` / `feerate`), ignoring missing values, and how many such fee records are there?
requests.specific_B: Across all fee records whose fee rate (`feerate`) is greater than 0.0009, what is the average ratio of maker rebate rate to fee rate (`rebrate` / `feerate`), ignoring missing values, and how many such fee records are there?
requests.open: For fee records in the high fee-rate band, using 0.0009 as the `feerate` cutoff, what's the average ratio of maker rebate rate to fee rate (`rebrate` / `feerate`), ignoring missing values, and how many such records are there?

readings.A: Fee records with a fee rate of exactly 0.0009 are included, along with those above it.
readings.B: Only fee records with a fee rate strictly greater than 0.0009 are included.

sql.A: SELECT AVG((CAST("fees"."rebrate" AS REAL) / "fees"."feerate")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "fees" AS "fees" WHERE "fees"."feerate" >= 0.0009
sql.B: SELECT AVG((CAST("fees"."rebrate" AS REAL) / "fees"."feerate")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "fees" AS "fees" WHERE "fees"."feerate" > 0.0009

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from each `fees` record
filter on fee rate (`fees.feerate`) against the 0.0009 threshold
all kept records form a single group giving one result row
average of `rebrate` / `feerate` over the kept records, missing values ignored (missing when there are none); no rounding
number of kept records (COUNT(*))

A.requirement: `feerate` >= 0.0009 (equal to the threshold counts)

B.requirement: `feerate` > 0.0009 (equal to the threshold excluded)

requests.specific_A: Join scans to their sites on `scans.zoneref` = `sites.zoneregistry`, dropping unmatched scans. Keep only scans whose `scancount` is at least 11. Group by site code (`scans.zoneref`) and historical phase (`sites.phasefactor`). For each group, give the site code, the phase, the average `scancount` and the average compression ratio (`pressratio`), each ignoring missing values. Sort by average compression ratio, highest first with missing last, keep the first 10 rows, and don't round.
requests.specific_B: Join scans to their sites on `scans.zoneref` = `sites.zoneregistry`, dropping unmatched scans. Keep only scans whose `scancount` is more than 11. Group by site code (`scans.zoneref`) and historical phase (`sites.phasefactor`). For each group, give the site code, the phase, the average `scancount` and the average compression ratio (`pressratio`), each ignoring missing values. Sort by average compression ratio, highest first with missing last, keep the first 10 rows, and don't round.
requests.open: For scans whose `scancount` clears the 11-scan mark, linked to their sites through `scans.zoneref` = `sites.zoneregistry` (scans without a site left out), what are the average `scancount` and the average compression ratio (`pressratio`) for each site code (`scans.zoneref`) and historical phase (`sites.phasefactor`)? Ignore missing values and don't round. Show the site code, the phase and both averages for the 10 combinations with the highest average compression ratio, with missing values last.

readings.A: Scans with a scan count of exactly 11 are kept.
readings.B: Only scans with a scan count strictly greater than 11 are kept.

sql.A: SELECT "scans"."zoneref" AS "e", "sites"."phasefactor" AS "g", AVG("scans"."scancount") AS "m1", AVG("scans"."pressratio") AS "m2" FROM "scans" AS "scans" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scans"."zoneref" WHERE "scans"."scancount" >= 11 GROUP BY "scans"."zoneref", "sites"."phasefactor" ORDER BY AVG("scans"."pressratio") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: SELECT "scans"."zoneref" AS "e", "sites"."phasefactor" AS "g", AVG("scans"."scancount") AS "m1", AVG("scans"."pressratio") AS "m2" FROM "scans" AS "scans" INNER JOIN "sites" AS "sites" ON "sites"."zoneregistry" = "scans"."zoneref" WHERE "scans"."scancount" > 11 GROUP BY "scans"."zoneref", "sites"."phasefactor" ORDER BY AVG("scans"."pressratio") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the `scans` records.
Inner join to `sites` where `sites.zoneregistry` = `scans.zoneref`, compared as text. Unmatched scans are dropped.
Keep only scans whose `scancount` meets the threshold of 11.
Group by `scans.zoneref` and `sites.phasefactor`.
First column: the site code (`scans.zoneref`).
Second column: the historical phase (`sites.phasefactor`).
Third column: the average `scancount`, ignoring missing values, unrounded.
Fourth column: the average `pressratio`, ignoring missing values, unrounded.
Sort by the average `pressratio`, descending, with missing values last.
Keep the first 10 rows. No tie rule is stated.

A.requirement: scancount >= 11

B.requirement: scancount > 11

requests.specific_A: Considering only tracks whose file size (`Track.Bytes`) is at least 10,323,804 bytes, work out for each media type (by name) the average bytes per millisecond (`Bytes` ÷ `Milliseconds`) of its tracks. Which media types have an average strictly higher than the simple average of all these per-media-type averages? Show the media type name, its average, and how far it is above that overall average (its average minus the overall average). Leave all values unrounded.
requests.specific_B: Considering only tracks whose file size (`Track.Bytes`) is more than 10,323,804 bytes, work out for each media type (by name) the average bytes per millisecond (`Bytes` ÷ `Milliseconds`) of its tracks. Which media types have an average strictly higher than the simple average of all these per-media-type averages? Show the media type name, its average, and how far it is above that overall average (its average minus the overall average). Leave all values unrounded.
requests.open: Considering only tracks that pass a file-size (`Track.Bytes`) cutoff of 10,323,804 bytes, work out for each media type (by name) the average bytes per millisecond (`Bytes` ÷ `Milliseconds`) of its tracks. Which media types have an average strictly higher than the simple average of all these per-media-type averages? Show the media type name, its average, and how far it is above that overall average (its average minus the overall average). Leave all values unrounded.

readings.A: Tracks whose file size is exactly 10,323,804 bytes are included along with larger ones.
readings.B: Only tracks whose file size is strictly greater than 10,323,804 bytes are included.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "MediaType"."Name" AS "g", AVG((CAST("Track"."Bytes" AS REAL) / "Track"."Milliseconds")) AS "m1" FROM "Track" AS "Track" INNER JOIN "MediaType" AS "MediaType" ON "MediaType"."MediaTypeId" = "Track"."MediaTypeId" WHERE "Track"."Bytes" >= 10323804 GROUP BY "MediaType"."Name"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "MediaType"."Name" AS "g", AVG((CAST("Track"."Bytes" AS REAL) / "Track"."Milliseconds")) AS "m1" FROM "Track" AS "Track" INNER JOIN "MediaType" AS "MediaType" ON "MediaType"."MediaTypeId" = "Track"."MediaTypeId" WHERE "Track"."Bytes" > 10323804 GROUP BY "MediaType"."Name"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL) WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from Track records. Group them by media type name (`MediaType.Name`). For each group, compute the average of `Bytes` ÷ `Milliseconds`, ignoring missing values.
Match each track to its MediaType by MediaTypeId (inner join, so tracks with no match are dropped).
Only tracks that pass the file-size (`Track.Bytes`) cutoff of 10,323,804 count. Whether the cutoff value itself passes is the choice.

Compute the overall value as the simple average of the per-media-type averages. Keep only media types whose average is strictly greater than that overall value (if the overall value is missing, return no rows).
Column 1: media type name.
Column 2: that media type's average bytes per millisecond, unrounded.
Column 3: its average minus the overall average, unrounded.

A.requirement: A track whose `Bytes` equals 10,323,804 is kept (Bytes >= 10323804).

B.requirement: A track whose `Bytes` equals 10,323,804 is excluded (Bytes > 10323804).

requests.specific_A: Considering only films whose `replacement_cost` is at least 20.99, work out for each `rating` the average `rental_duration` and the average ratio of `rental_rate` to `replacement_cost` (ignoring missing values). Then return a single row with the average of those per-rating average durations and the average of those per-rating average ratios, in that order and unrounded.
requests.specific_B: Considering only films whose `replacement_cost` is more than 20.99, work out for each `rating` the average `rental_duration` and the average ratio of `rental_rate` to `replacement_cost` (ignoring missing values). Then return a single row with the average of those per-rating average durations and the average of those per-rating average ratios, in that order and unrounded.
requests.open: For the pricier-to-replace films, with 20.99 as the `replacement_cost` cutoff, what are the average `rental_duration` and the average `rental_rate`-to-`replacement_cost` ratio for each `rating` (ignoring missing values)? Then give me one row with the average of those per-rating durations and the average of those per-rating ratios, in that order and unrounded.

readings.A: Only films whose replacement cost is 20.99 or higher are used. Films costing exactly 20.99 are included.
readings.B: Only films whose replacement cost is strictly higher than 20.99 are used. Films costing exactly 20.99 are excluded.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "film"."rating" AS "g", AVG("film"."rental_duration") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("film"."rental_rate" AS REAL) / "film"."replacement_cost")) AS "m2" FROM "film" AS "film" WHERE "film"."replacement_cost" >= 20.99 GROUP BY "film"."rating") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "film"."rating" AS "g", AVG("film"."rental_duration") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("film"."rental_rate" AS REAL) / "film"."replacement_cost")) AS "m2" FROM "film" AS "film" WHERE "film"."replacement_cost" > 20.99 GROUP BY "film"."rating") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the `film` table, one record per film; no joins.
Filter films on `replacement_cost` against the threshold 20.99.
Group the kept films by `rating`, giving one intermediate row per rating.
For each rating, take the average `rental_duration`, ignoring missing values.
For each rating, take the average of the per-film ratio `rental_rate` ÷ `replacement_cost`, ignoring missing values.
Collapse all per-rating rows into a single result row. Each rating counts equally, so the result is an average of averages.
First output column: the average of the per-rating average rental durations.
Second output column: the average of the per-rating average rental-rate-to-replacement-cost ratios.
No rounding. Exactly two output columns, in the order (duration, ratio).

A.requirement: Keep films with `replacement_cost` >= 20.99, so films costing exactly 20.99 are included.

B.requirement: Keep films with `replacement_cost` > 20.99, so films costing exactly 20.99 are excluded.

requests.specific_A: For films whose running time (`film.length`) is at least 112 minutes, taken together as one group, what is the average running time, and what is the average of each film's replacement cost divided by its rental rate (`replacement_cost` / `rental_rate`, computed per film, then averaged)? Ignore missing values in each average (giving a missing value if none remain), return the two figures in that order as a single row, and don't round.
requests.specific_B: For films whose running time (`film.length`) is more than 112 minutes, taken together as one group, what is the average running time, and what is the average of each film's replacement cost divided by its rental rate (`replacement_cost` / `rental_rate`, computed per film, then averaged)? Ignore missing values in each average (giving a missing value if none remain), return the two figures in that order as a single row, and don't round.
requests.open: Using 112 minutes (`film.length`) as the cutoff for a long film, take all the long films together as one group. What is their average running time, and what is the average of each film's replacement cost divided by its rental rate (`replacement_cost` / `rental_rate`, computed per film, then averaged)? Ignore missing values in each average (giving a missing value if none remain), return the two figures in that order as a single row, and don't round.

readings.A: Films whose running time is 112 minutes or more are included; a film of exactly 112 minutes counts.
readings.B: Only films whose running time is strictly more than 112 minutes are included; a film of exactly 112 minutes does not count.

sql.A: SELECT AVG("film"."length") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("film"."replacement_cost" AS REAL) / "film"."rental_rate")) AS "m2" FROM "film" AS "film" WHERE "film"."length" >= 112
sql.B: SELECT AVG("film"."length") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("film"."replacement_cost" AS REAL) / "film"."rental_rate")) AS "m2" FROM "film" AS "film" WHERE "film"."length" > 112

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from the film table, one record per film; no joins.
Keep films according to how their running time (`film.length`) compares with the threshold 112 minutes; films with missing length are not kept.
All kept films form a single group, which gives exactly one result row.
First column: average running time (`film.length`) over the kept films, ignoring missing values (missing if there are none); not rounded.

Second column: the average over the kept films of each film's replacement cost divided by its rental rate (`film.replacement_cost` / `film.rental_rate`), computed per film and then averaged, ignoring missing values (missing if there are none); not rounded.

A.requirement: A film whose length is exactly 112 is kept (length >= 112).

B.requirement: A film whose length is exactly 112 is excluded (length > 112).

film.rating: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns exactly 5 rating levels, each covering roughly 180-225 films, so every group is well populated and rating works as a grouping class. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate), AVG(length), AVG(replacement_cost) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '3.0348430493273613', '120.4439461883408', '20.402556053811544'], ['NC-17', '210', '2.970952380952388', '113.22857142857143', '20.137619047618937'], ['R', '195', '2.9387179487179553', '118.66153846153846', '20.23102564102554'], ['PG', '194', '3.051855670103099', '112.00515463917526', '18.959072164948356'], ['G', '178', '2.888876404494388', '111.0505617977528', '20.12483146067407']] scale (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows exactly 5 levels: G, PG, PG-13, R and NC-17. These are the standard MPAA bands, which are ordered by audience restriction, so the column is an ordinal class. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY rating -> [['G', '178'], ['NC-17', '210'], ['PG', '194'], ['PG-13', '223'], ['R', '195']]
category.name: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 16 genres, each shared by many films (about 50-75 each), so the column is a grouping label and does not identify single records. Evidence: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film_category fc JOIN category c ON c.category_id = fc.category_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY films DESC -> [['Sports', '74'], ['Foreign', '73'], ['Family', '69'], ['Documentary', '68'], ['Animation', '66'], ['Action', '64']]
customer.store_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 2 stores with about 300 customers each, so the column is a grouping label shared by many rows. Evidence: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS customers, SUM(active) AS active_customers FROM customer GROUP BY store_id -> [['1', '326', '318'], ['2', '273', '266']]
inventory.store_id: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 2 store values over 4581 copies, about 2270 per store, so the column is a grouping label. Evidence: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS copies, COUNT(DISTINCT film_id) AS titles FROM inventory GROUP BY store_id -> [['1', '2270', '759'], ['2', '2311', '762']]
country.country: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Many customers share a country (the top countries have dozens of customers each), so country works as a grouping attribute for customers. film.special_features: desc (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 15 distinct values, all of them combinations of the same 4 feature names (for example 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes'). The column is a set, not a single category. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']] semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows 15 distinct values, all combinations of the same 4 feature names, such as 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes' and 'Trailers,Commentaries'. The column is a set, not a single class, so it should not be offered as a grouping. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']]
film.length: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified rating query already returns AVG(length) between 111.05 (G) and 120.44 (PG-13). The catalogue profile gives 140 distinct values from 46 to 185 minutes. So length is a continuous ratio-scale quantity whose group averages can be read directly. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(length) AS avg_minutes, MIN(length), MAX(length) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '120.4439461883408', '46', '185'], ['NC-17', '210', '113.22857142857143', '46', '184'], ['R', '195', '118.66153846153846', '49', '185'], ['PG', '194', '112.00515463917526', '46', '185'], ['G', '178', '111.0505617977528', '47', '185']]
film.rental_duration: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows 5 values from 3 to 7 days, all well above zero, so the column is a ratio-scale number of days per film. The query shows how many films fall at each value. Evidence: SELECT rental_duration, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate) AS avg_rate FROM film GROUP BY rental_duration ORDER BY rental_duration -> [['3', '203', '2.8323645320197115'], ['4', '203', '2.97029556650247'], ['5', '191', '3.19942408376964'], ['6', '212', '2.895660377358497'], ['7', '191', '3.021413612565451']]

The query shows how large and uniform the gap is. The auditor noted that the difference is always about −17 and the relative gap about −0.85, which fits two different quantities rather than one price seen two ways. Evidence: SELECT MIN(replacement_cost - rental_rate), MAX(replacement_cost - rental_rate), AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) FROM film -> [['5.0', '29.0', '0.16651517608314595']]

requests.specific_A: For patients none of whose examination records has an `ANA Pattern` of 'S', list each patient's ID, their sex (from the Patient table, only patients present there), and the average `aCL IgM` across all of their examinations (ignoring missing values, unrounded). Group by patient ID and sex, sort by that average from highest to lowest with missing averages last, and show the top 10.
requests.specific_B: For patients with at least one examination record whose `ANA Pattern` is recorded and is something other than 'S', list each patient's ID, their sex (from the Patient table, only patients present there), and the average `aCL IgM` across all of their examinations (ignoring missing values, unrounded). Group by patient ID and sex, sort by that average from highest to lowest with missing averages last, and show the top 10.
requests.open: Among patients whose examinations don't show an `ANA Pattern` of 'S', list each patient's ID, their sex (from the Patient table, only patients present there), and the average `aCL IgM` across all of their examinations (ignoring missing values, unrounded). Group by patient ID and sex, sort by that average from highest to lowest with missing averages last, and show the top 10.

readings.A: Patients who never have an examination with ANA pattern S.
readings.B: Patients who have at least one examination whose recorded ANA pattern is something other than S.

sql.A: SELECT "Examination"."ID" AS "e", "Patient"."SEX" AS "g", AVG("Examination"."aCL IgM") AS "m1" FROM "Examination" AS "Examination" INNER JOIN "Patient" AS "Patient" ON "Patient"."ID" = "Examination"."ID" WHERE "Examination"."ID" NOT IN ((SELECT "x"."ID" FROM "Examination" AS "x" WHERE ("x"."ANA Pattern" = 'S' AND NOT ("x"."ID" IS NULL)))) GROUP BY "Examination"."ID", "Patient"."SEX" ORDER BY AVG("Examination"."aCL IgM") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: SELECT "Examination"."ID" AS "e", "Patient"."SEX" AS "g", AVG("Examination"."aCL IgM") AS "m1" FROM "Examination" AS "Examination" INNER JOIN "Patient" AS "Patient" ON "Patient"."ID" = "Examination"."ID" WHERE "Examination"."ID" IN ((SELECT "x"."ID" FROM "Examination" AS "x" WHERE ("x"."ANA Pattern" != 'S' AND NOT ("x"."ID" IS NULL)))) GROUP BY "Examination"."ID", "Patient"."SEX" ORDER BY AVG("Examination"."aCL IgM") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every `Examination` record.
Inner join to `Patient` on `Patient.ID` = `Examination.ID`, so examinations without a matching patient are dropped.

Keep all examination records of qualifying patients, decided at patient (ID) level by the patient's `ANA Pattern` values relative to 'S' (text comparison). Only non-missing IDs are considered in the subquery.
Group by `Examination.ID` and `Patient.SEX`, giving one row per group.
Patient ID (`Examination.ID`).
Patient sex (`Patient.SEX`).
Average `aCL IgM` over the group's examination records, ignoring missing values. It is missing when no values are present. No rounding.
Sort by that average, highest first, with missing averages last.
Keep only the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: A patient qualifies only if none of their examination records has `ANA Pattern` = 'S' (NOT IN the set of IDs with a pattern-'S' record).

B.requirement: A patient qualifies if at least one of their examination records has a recorded `ANA Pattern` other than 'S' (IN the set of IDs with a pattern != 'S' record), even if other records do show 'S'.

requests.specific_A: Considering only tracks whose file size (`Bytes`) is at least 10,323,804 bytes, group them by `MediaTypeId`. For each media type, compute the average bytes per millisecond (`Bytes` ÷ `Milliseconds`, ignoring missing values) and the number of tracks. Then return a single row with (1) the average of those per-media-type bytes-per-millisecond averages and (2) the average of those per-media-type track counts, both unrounded.
requests.specific_B: Considering only tracks whose file size (`Bytes`) is strictly greater than 10,323,804 bytes, group them by `MediaTypeId`. For each media type, compute the average bytes per millisecond (`Bytes` ÷ `Milliseconds`, ignoring missing values) and the number of tracks. Then return a single row with (1) the average of those per-media-type bytes-per-millisecond averages and (2) the average of those per-media-type track counts, both unrounded.
requests.open: For the large track files, using 10,323,804 bytes (`Bytes`) as the size cutoff, group the tracks by `MediaTypeId`. For each media type, work out the average bytes per millisecond (`Bytes` ÷ `Milliseconds`, ignoring missing values) and how many tracks there are. Then give me one summary row with (1) the average of those per-media-type bytes-per-millisecond averages and (2) the average of those per-media-type track counts, both unrounded.

readings.A: Tracks whose file size is at least 10323804 bytes count, including any track of exactly that size.
readings.B: Only tracks whose file size is strictly greater than 10323804 bytes count; a track of exactly that size is excluded.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Track"."MediaTypeId" AS "e", AVG((CAST("Track"."Bytes" AS REAL) / "Track"."Milliseconds")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "Track" AS "Track" WHERE "Track"."Bytes" >= 10323804 GROUP BY "Track"."MediaTypeId") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Track"."MediaTypeId" AS "e", AVG((CAST("Track"."Bytes" AS REAL) / "Track"."Milliseconds")) AS "m1", COUNT(*) AS "m2" FROM "Track" AS "Track" WHERE "Track"."Bytes" > 10323804 GROUP BY "Track"."MediaTypeId") SELECT AVG("s1"."m1") AS "m1", AVG("s1"."m2") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1"

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from every `Track` record and keep only those that pass a file-size (`Track.Bytes`) threshold of 10323804.
Group the kept tracks by `Track.MediaTypeId`, so each media type gives one intermediate row.

For each media type, compute the average of `Bytes` ÷ `Milliseconds` per track (real division). Missing values are ignored, and the average is missing if there are none. Also count the tracks in the group.
Collapse all per-media-type rows into one group that gives exactly one result row.
First output column: the average, across media types, of the per-media-type average bytes-per-millisecond. Missing values are ignored, and the result is missing if there are none. No rounding.
Second output column: the average, across media types, of the per-media-type track counts. Missing values are ignored. No rounding.

A.requirement: A track whose `Bytes` equals 10323804 exactly is kept, so the condition is Bytes >= 10323804.

B.requirement: A track whose `Bytes` equals 10323804 exactly is excluded, so the condition is Bytes > 10323804.

requests.specific_A: Take fee records with a fee rate (`feerate`) of at least 0.0009 and match each to its order (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`, exact text match; drop fees with no matching order). For each combination of `orderslink` and trading pair (`mktnote`), show `orderslink`, the trading pair, the average maker rebate rate (`rebrate`), and the total rebate (the sum of `rebtotal`), ignoring missing values. Sort by total rebate from highest to lowest (missing last), keep the top 10, and don't round.
requests.specific_B: Take fee records with a fee rate (`feerate`) strictly greater than 0.0009 and match each to its order (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`, exact text match; drop fees with no matching order). For each combination of `orderslink` and trading pair (`mktnote`), show `orderslink`, the trading pair, the average maker rebate rate (`rebrate`), and the total rebate (the sum of `rebtotal`), ignoring missing values. Sort by total rebate from highest to lowest (missing last), keep the top 10, and don't round.
requests.open: Using only high-rate fee records, with 0.0009 on the fee rate (`feerate`) as the cutoff, match each fee to its order (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`, exact text match; drop fees with no matching order). For each combination of `orderslink` and trading pair (`mktnote`), show `orderslink`, the trading pair, the average maker rebate rate (`rebrate`), and the total rebate (the sum of `rebtotal`), ignoring missing values. Sort by total rebate from highest to lowest (missing last), keep the top 10, and don't round.

readings.A: Fee records with a fee rate of exactly 0.0009 are included along with those above it.
readings.B: Only fee records with a fee rate strictly above 0.0009 are included; exactly 0.0009 is excluded.

sql.A: SELECT "fees"."orderslink" AS "e", "orders"."mktnote" AS "g", AVG("fees"."rebrate") AS "m1", SUM("fees"."rebtotal") AS "m2" FROM "fees" AS "fees" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "fees"."orderslink" WHERE "fees"."feerate" >= 0.0009 GROUP BY "fees"."orderslink", "orders"."mktnote" ORDER BY SUM("fees"."rebtotal") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: SELECT "fees"."orderslink" AS "e", "orders"."mktnote" AS "g", AVG("fees"."rebrate") AS "m1", SUM("fees"."rebtotal") AS "m2" FROM "fees" AS "fees" INNER JOIN "orders" AS "orders" ON "orders"."recordvault" = "fees"."orderslink" WHERE "fees"."feerate" > 0.0009 GROUP BY "fees"."orderslink", "orders"."mktnote" ORDER BY SUM("fees"."rebtotal") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from each `fees` record.
Inner-join each fee to `orders` where `orders.recordvault` = `fees.orderslink` (exact text match), one combined record per match; fees without a matching order are dropped.
Filter on fee rate (`fees.feerate`) against the threshold 0.0009 before grouping.
Group by `fees.orderslink` and trading pair (`orders.mktnote`); one row per group.
Return `orderslink`.
Return trading pair (`mktnote`).
Return the average maker rebate rate (`rebrate`) in the group (missing ignored; missing if none); not rounded.
Return the sum of total rebate (`rebtotal`) in the group (missing ignored; missing if none); not rounded.
Order by the group's total rebate sum descending, with missing values last.
Keep only the first 10 rows.

A.requirement: Keep records with `feerate` >= 0.0009 (exactly 0.0009 is kept).

B.requirement: Keep records with `feerate` > 0.0009 (exactly 0.0009 is dropped).

requests.specific_A: Take the advanced behaviour records with a peer correlation (`peercorr`) of at least 0.149 and match each one to its transaction record(s), where `transactionrecord.transreg` equals `advancedbehavior.translink`; drop records with no match. For each combination of `translink` and order type mix (`ordertypedist`), count the matched records. For each combination, show the `translink`, the order type mix, the count, and the count as an unrounded fraction of the total count across all combinations with that same order type mix. Leave out combinations where the order type mix is missing. Sort by that fraction from highest to lowest and return the top 10.
requests.specific_B: Take the advanced behaviour records with a peer correlation (`peercorr`) greater than 0.149 and match each one to its transaction record(s), where `transactionrecord.transreg` equals `advancedbehavior.translink`; drop records with no match. For each combination of `translink` and order type mix (`ordertypedist`), count the matched records. For each combination, show the `translink`, the order type mix, the count, and the count as an unrounded fraction of the total count across all combinations with that same order type mix. Leave out combinations where the order type mix is missing. Sort by that fraction from highest to lowest and return the top 10.
requests.open: Using 0.149 as the peer correlation (`peercorr`) cutoff, take the advanced behaviour records with high peer correlation and match each one to its transaction record(s), where `transactionrecord.transreg` equals `advancedbehavior.translink`; drop records with no match. For each combination of `translink` and order type mix (`ordertypedist`), count the matched records. For each combination, show the `translink`, the order type mix, the count, and the count as an unrounded fraction of the total count across all combinations with that same order type mix. Leave out combinations where the order type mix is missing. Sort by that fraction from highest to lowest and return the top 10.

readings.A: Peer correlation values equal to 0.149 pass the filter (at least 0.149).
readings.B: Only peer correlation values strictly greater than 0.149 pass the filter (more than 0.149).

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "advancedbehavior"."translink" AS "e", "transactionrecord"."ordertypedist" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "advancedbehavior" AS "advancedbehavior" INNER JOIN "transactionrecord" AS "transactionrecord" ON "transactionrecord"."transreg" = "advancedbehavior"."translink" WHERE "advancedbehavior"."peercorr" >= 0.149 GROUP BY "advancedbehavior"."translink", "transactionrecord"."ordertypedist"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g" ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "advancedbehavior"."translink" AS "e", "transactionrecord"."ordertypedist" AS "g", COUNT(*) AS "m1" FROM "advancedbehavior" AS "advancedbehavior" INNER JOIN "transactionrecord" AS "transactionrecord" ON "transactionrecord"."transreg" = "advancedbehavior"."translink" WHERE "advancedbehavior"."peercorr" > 0.149 GROUP BY "advancedbehavior"."translink", "transactionrecord"."ordertypedist"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", SUM("s1"."m1") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g") SELECT "s1"."e" AS "e", "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m2" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g" ORDER BY (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") DESC LIMIT 10

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from each `advancedbehavior` record and filter on peer correlation (`advancedbehavior.peercorr`) against the value 0.149, keeping the high side
Pair each `advancedbehavior` record with every `transactionrecord` whose `transreg` equals its `translink` (exact text match), one row per match; drop advanced-behaviour records that have no match
Group the kept matched records by (`advancedbehavior.translink`, `transactionrecord.ordertypedist`), giving one row per combination; the first column is `translink`
The second column is the order type mix (`ordertypedist`). Leave out combinations whose order type mix is missing, because they have no matching per-mix total
The third column is the number of matched records in the combination

The fourth column is the combination's count divided by the total count for its order type mix, where the total is the sum of the counts of all kept combinations with that mix. Give it as an unrounded decimal fraction
Sort the rows by that fraction from highest to lowest
Return only the first 10 rows

A.requirement: A record whose `peercorr` is exactly 0.149 is kept (peercorr >= 0.149)

B.requirement: A record whose `peercorr` is exactly 0.149 is excluded (peercorr > 0.149)

requests.specific_A: Joining each track to its media type (dropping tracks with no matching media type) and keeping only tracks whose file size (`Track.Bytes`) is at least 10323804 bytes, for each media type name (`MediaType.Name`) give the media type name, the average list price per track (`Track.UnitPrice`), and the average of file size divided by track length (`Track.Bytes` ÷ `Track.Milliseconds`). Also give that last average divided by the plain average of it across all the media types. All averages should ignore missing values and be missing when there are none. Return no rows if the across-media-type average is missing. Leave all values unrounded.
requests.specific_B: Joining each track to its media type (dropping tracks with no matching media type) and keeping only tracks whose file size (`Track.Bytes`) is more than 10323804 bytes, for each media type name (`MediaType.Name`) give the media type name, the average list price per track (`Track.UnitPrice`), and the average of file size divided by track length (`Track.Bytes` ÷ `Track.Milliseconds`). Also give that last average divided by the plain average of it across all the media types. All averages should ignore missing values and be missing when there are none. Return no rows if the across-media-type average is missing. Leave all values unrounded.
requests.open: Joining each track to its media type (dropping tracks with no matching media type) and using 10323804 bytes as the file-size threshold (`Track.Bytes`) to keep only the large files, for each media type name (`MediaType.Name`) give the media type name, the average list price per track (`Track.UnitPrice`), and the average of file size divided by track length (`Track.Bytes` ÷ `Track.Milliseconds`). Also give that last average divided by the plain average of it across all the media types. All averages should ignore missing values and be missing when there are none. Return no rows if the across-media-type average is missing. Leave all values unrounded.

readings.A: Tracks whose file size equals 10323804 bytes are kept along with larger ones.
readings.B: Only tracks whose file size is strictly greater than 10323804 bytes are kept.

sql.A: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "MediaType"."Name" AS "g", AVG("Track"."UnitPrice") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("Track"."Bytes" AS REAL) / "Track"."Milliseconds")) AS "m2" FROM "Track" AS "Track" INNER JOIN "MediaType" AS "MediaType" ON "MediaType"."MediaTypeId" = "Track"."MediaTypeId" WHERE "Track"."Bytes" >= 10323804 GROUP BY "MediaType"."Name"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)
sql.B: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "MediaType"."Name" AS "g", AVG("Track"."UnitPrice") AS "m1", AVG((CAST("Track"."Bytes" AS REAL) / "Track"."Milliseconds")) AS "m2" FROM "Track" AS "Track" INNER JOIN "MediaType" AS "MediaType" ON "MediaType"."MediaTypeId" = "Track"."MediaTypeId" WHERE "Track"."Bytes" > 10323804 GROUP BY "MediaType"."Name"), "s2" AS (SELECT AVG("s1"."m2") AS "v" FROM "s1" AS "s1") SELECT "s1"."g" AS "g", "s1"."m1" AS "m1", "s1"."m2" AS "m2", (CAST("s1"."m2" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS "m3" FROM "s1" AS "s1" INNER JOIN "s2" AS "s2" ON NOT ("s2"."v" IS NULL)

shared_requirements.requirement: Start from each `Track` record and keep tracks by comparing file size (`Track.Bytes`) with the threshold 10323804. Whether a value equal to the threshold is kept is the open choice.

Inner-join each track to the `MediaType` record with the same `MediaTypeId`, dropping tracks with no match. Group the kept tracks by media type name (`MediaType.Name`), one row per name. Then compute one overall figure: the unweighted average of the per-media-type column 3 values, ignoring missing values. Attach that figure to every per-media-type row only when it is not missing; otherwise there are no rows.
Column 1: the media type name (`MediaType.Name`).
Column 2: the average `Track.UnitPrice` in the group. Ignore missing values; the result is missing if there are none. Do not round.
Column 3: the average of `Track.Bytes` ÷ `Track.Milliseconds` in the group. Ignore missing values; the result is missing if there are none. Do not round.
Column 4: column 3 divided by the overall average of column 3 across all media types. Do not round.
